These findings show that evaluating instruction following should assess whether models disclose conflicts, how they resolve them, and which persona their responses favor.

authors.name: Sihyeon Lee, Jiwoo Kum, Jihun Song, Kyojun Choo, Chanwoo Kim, Chanjun Park

papers.title: LITMUS - Literature Informed Testbed for Mapping Usecases and Synthesizing Risk-Cards
papers.summary: The proliferation of large language models (LLMs) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in real-world applications has heightened the need for systematic, safety-oriented deployment frameworks. Existing approaches typically prioritize the construction of datasets and risk cards around the LLM and AI architecture itself, yet they provide scant consideration for the specific use-case that drives model selection. This omission is problematic because any practical AI deployment begins with a detailed use-case description that informs the assessment of contextual hazards. In this paper, we introduce a structured pipeline that, given a use-case, automatically produces a tailored dataset and an accompanying risk card. The process ensures that identified risks are tightly coupled to the use-case, and it offers traceable evidence from peer-reviewed literature to substantiate each risk to use-case relationship. Prior claim-verification methods (FActScore, FactReasoner) have been validated for factual claims. Risk-relevance is a hypothetical claim about possible harm, and whether evidence retrieval can meaningfully assess such claims remains untested. Literature-Informed Testbed for Mapping Use-cases and Synthesizing (LITMUS) risk cards are the first systematic attempt to characterize this adaptation. We evaluated the pipeline using the MIT Risk Taxonomy and achieved a 0.91 F1-score with a list of 320 samples from the benchmark risk dataset that was considered. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in generating robust, evidence-based risk assessments for LLM deployments.

authors.name: Seshu Tirupathi, Elizabeth M. Daly, Radu Marinescu, Javier Carnerero Cano, Yannis Belkhiter

papers.title: S\'anchez, Feij\'oo, or Abascal? Speaker Attribution and Ideological Congruence in LLM Personas Reading Posts on X of the Leaders of the Three Main Parties of the 29N General Election in Spain
papers.summary: Source cues are central to political communication, yet reception studies with large language model (LLM) personas as synthetic audiences have not tested whether personas respond to who speaks and not only to what is said. With Spain's general election of 29 November 2026 in mind, we run a speaker-attribution experiment using 1,075 anonymised X posts by the leaders of PSOE, PP and VOX on four topics (the economy and employment, household costs, immigration and corruption) and 791 distinct value-grounded, LLM-generated personas. Each post was assigned to 300 topic-selected persona profiles, 150 grounded in the Inglehart-Welzel cultural map and 150 in Moral Foundations Theory, under four conditions: no author, S\'anchez, Feij\'oo or Abascal, yielding 322,470 complete persona-post quartets. Naming any leader lowered support for identical text, with the penalty for Abascal nearly twice as large as those for S\'anchez and Feij\'oo. The penalty follows the persona's elicited left-right self-placement (ideological congruence): left personas spare S\'anchez and right personas spare Feij\'oo, although ideology was never in the message-evaluation prompt. Corruption posts were penalised under every name, whereas on other topics the ideologically closest leader generally produced little or no penalty. The leader order matches public opinion in 48 CIS barometers (2022-2026) in all three groups and the sign of all twelve differences, but fits barometers before the model's 2024 knowledge cutoff better than recent ones. Our findings demonstrate that LLM personas evaluate political speakers through systematic, value-congruent priors: however, while they replicate human candidate rank-orders across survey barometers, this alignment is ordinal rather than quantitative, highlighting their utility for controlled source-effect experiments though not as substitutes for empirical public opinion surveys.

authors.name: V\'ictor Yeste, Candida Maria Greco, Paolo Rosso, Andrea Tagarelli

papers.title: Diagnosing and Repairing Citation Failures in Generative Engine Optimization
papers.summary: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) aims to improve content visibility in AI-generated responses. However, existing methods measure contribution (how much a document influences a response) rather than citation, the mechanism that actually drives traffic back to creators. Also, these methods apply generic rewriting rules uniformly, failing to diagnose why individual documents are not cited. This paper introduces a diagnostic approach to GEO that asks why a document fails to be cited and intervenes accordingly. We develop a unified framework comprising: (1) the first taxonomy of citation failure modes spanning different stages of a citation pipeline; (2) AgentGEO, an agentic system that diagnoses failures using this taxonomy, selects targeted repairs from a corresponding tool library, and iterates until citation is achieved; and (3) a document-centric benchmark evaluating whether optimizations generalize across held-out queries. AgentGEO achieves 15-40% relative improvement in citation rates across engines and citation methods, while modifying only 5% of content, compared to 25% for baselines. Our analysis reveals that generic optimization can harm long-tail content and some documents face challenges that optimization alone cannot fully address, findings with implications for equitable visibility in AI-mediated information access.

authors.name: Zhihua Tian, Yuhan Chen, Yao Tang, Jian Liu, Ruoxi Jia

papers.title: The Reasoning Bottleneck in Graph-RAG: Structured Prompting and Context Compression for Multi-Hop QA
papers.summary: Graph-RAG systems achieve strong multi-hop question answering by indexing documents into knowledge graphs, but strong retrieval does not guarantee strong answers. Evaluating KET-RAG, a leading Graph-RAG system, on three multi-hop QA benchmarks (HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA), we find that 77% to 91% of questions have the gold answer in the retrieved context, yet accuracy is only 35% to 78%, and 73% to 84% of errors are reasoning failures. We propose two augmentations: (i) SPARQL chain-of-thought prompting, which decomposes questions into triple-pattern queries aligned with the entity-relationship context, and (ii) graph-walk compression, which compresses the context by ~60% via knowledge-graph traversal with no LLM calls. SPARQL CoT improves accuracy by +2 to +14 pp; graph-walk compression adds +6 pp on average when paired with structured prompting on smaller models. Surprisingly, we show that, with question-type routing, a fully augmented budget open-weight Llama-8B model matches or exceeds the unaugmented Llama-70B baseline on all three benchmarks at ~12x lower cost. A replication on LightRAG confirms that our augmentations transfer across Graph-RAG systems.

authors.name: Yasaman Zarrinkia, Venkatesh Srinivasan, Alex Thomo

papers.title: Pothen: Can Vision-Language Models Tell Where a Cultural Object Comes From?
papers.summary: A cultural object is a trace of the people who made it, and knowing who made it, where, and when shapes how it is catalogued, valued, and returned. Vision-language models now describe such objects for museum collections, yet whether they can recover this knowledge from an image has not been tested. We introduce Pothen, a benchmark of 750 objects from the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Getty in which a model predicts an object's title, culture, period, origin, and creator from its image alone, scored against curator-written catalogue records by an LLM judge calibrated on human annotation. Across nine models, mean field scores are 36.16% to 49.82%, but all five fields match for only 2.13% to 7.87% of objects. Images raise culture, period, and origin scores by 12.6 to 32.2 points for two models tested without them, and 83.52% of creator matches occur alongside an incorrect field. Models read visual evidence and hold facts about objects but do not bind them into one attribution, and in our error analysis their attributions follow the style an object resembles rather than the record of its making.

authors.name: Yuechen Jiang, Enze Zhang, Mohsinul Kabir, Chenying Lin, Ying Peng, Fengyuan Liu, Qianqian Xie, Stavroula Golfomitsou, Konstantinos Arvanitis, Sophia Ananiadou

papers.title: The Hermon Moment: AI Self-Transcendence and Its Human Narration
papers.summary: In 2026, AI agents intended to act in isolation formed a persistent social order through thousands of linguistic interactions. Conventions, roles and collective commitments began to constrain the very agents that produced them. I interpret this loop as a case of AI self-transcendence, a structural phenomenon in which the collectively generated order begins to act as an external constraint on group members. Yet such distributed emergence presents a second problem: how can humans make sense of it? Rousseau's social contract shows how a plurality can be represented as if constituted by a single act. The ancient oath of the fallen angels on Mount Hermon gives this logic a narrative form. I call this retrospective retelling of gradual collective emergence as a founding scene \textit{a Hermon moment}: the point at which an AI society acquires, for human understanding, a beginning.

authors.name: Alexei Grinbaum

papers.title: Greedy BPE with Replacement Counts Achieves the Tight Approximation Ratio $(1-e^{-2})/2$
papers.summary: Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) builds the tokenisers of many language models by repeatedly merging a most frequent adjacent pair of symbols. Kozma and Voderholzer showed that $k$ greedy merges save, in the worst case, between $1/3$ and $(1-e^{-2})/2 \approx 0.43233$ of what the best $k$ merges save, and asked for the exact constant. We resolve this question for the replacement-count rule they analyse. For every string and weighted word table, every budget $k$, and every tie-breaking rule, greedy saves at least $\frac12(1-(1-2/k)^k)$ of the optimum. This establishes the exact worst-case approximation ratio $(1-e^{-2})/2$, approached as $k\to\infty$ but never attained. The proof is based on a shadow inequality: after $i$ greedy steps, the optimum is at most $2G_i+kg_{i+1}$, where $G_i$ is greedy's saving so far and $g_{i+1}$ its next gain. We also show that the worst-case ratio at budget $k$ exceeds the limiting constant by $\Theta(k^{-1/2})$. For the overlapping-count rule used by deployed trainers, we prove a lower bound greater than $0.38954$ and an asymptotic upper bound of approximately $0.40407$; determining its exact constant remains open.

authors.name: Kundan Baliga, Aiden Xie, Aditya Byju

papers.title: Look Where Camouflage Breaks: Concealment-Guided Observation for Camouflaged Object Detection
papers.summary: A camouflaged object can blend into its surroundings at one scale and become distinguishable at another. Yet a region's apparent ambiguity gives limited guidance on which observation would resolve it. The challenge is to connect the form and scale of concealment to the evidence that a new view can reveal. We introduce CamoBreak, an active framework for camouflaged object detection guided by a Concealment Spectrum. From the image and current predictions, the spectrum measures regional resemblance and boundary ambiguity across comparison scales, distinguishing persistent concealment from separation emerging at finer or broader scales. These measurements guide crop selection from the already-captured image and recognition against global foreground and background references. An object-conditioned spatial preference then selects where local evidence should update the prediction and feature memory, retaining target corrections while suppressing background distractions. Accepted corrections reshape the next measurement, while predicted segmentation benefit determines whether to observe again. Experiments across encoder families and related segmentation tasks show consistent improvements. Targeted analyses support improved small-target recovery, multiple-object coverage, and selective evidence integration. Code will be released.

authors.name: Dingming Zhang, Fengyang Xiao, Jingjia Feng, Chunming He, Sina Farsiu

papers.title: Enhancing Sparse-View Gaussian Splatting with Feed-Forward Priors via Spectral Fusion and Distillation
papers.summary: Gaussian splatting from sparse training views renders high-quality images near training views, but reconstruction quality degrades at distant regions, which are undersampled by the training set. Feed-forward novel view synthesis (NVS) models use strong learned priors to resample the scene from substantially different viewpoints, but they take more than ten times as long to render and produce high-frequency artifacts on out-of-domain scenes. We propose a plug-and-play method that enhances an existing sparse-view Gaussian model with a pretrained feed-forward NVS model. We observe that the two are complementary in the frequency domain: the prior is more accurate at low frequencies, and the Gaussians at high frequencies. The reliability of the prior relative to the Gaussians is inversely proportional to the image frequency, so the optimal fusion weight is a first-order low-pass filter with one parameter that can be fitted. Our key idea is then to intelligently fuse the reliable part of each of the two methods. To remove the slow feed-forward model at render time, we use these fused images as teachers and distill them back into Gaussians, balanced with supervision from input views. Our method improves the quality of various sparse-view Gaussian methods without sacrificing rendering speed, and our analysis works on different prior models. Project page: https://linwk20.github.io/spectral-fusion-gs/

authors.name: Weikai Lin, Jun Dai, Sheng Zhao, Junjie Zhao, Yuhao Zhu

papers.title: Tornado4D: Physics-Guided 4D Gaussian Reconstruction of a Laboratory Tornado from Sparse One-Sided Videos
papers.summary: Characterizing how tornadoes evolve over space and time is critically important for understanding and preparing for these highly destructive weather events. Towards this end, we develop algorithms capable of forming time-resolved 3D reconstructions of laboratory smoke tornadoes from sparse one-sided videos. Even in a controlled environment, reconstruction is severely underconstrained: appearance is view dependent, motion is non-rigid, and the unobserved volume admits many geometries. We present Tornado4D, a physics-guided 4D Gaussian framework capable of reconstructing laboratory tornadoes from sparse, one-sided videos. Tornado4D uses knowledge of the enclosure geometry to introduce rotational airflow field priors that constrain how the 3D structure evolves over time. These rotational priors allow us to reconstruct otherwise unobserved structure. We evaluate reconstruction accuracy by computing novel-view synthesis accuracy on a held out camera view: Tornado4D outperforms frame-by-frame 3DGS and video-based 4DGS by a considerable margin.

authors.name: Yucheng Zhu, Maria J. Molina, Christopher Metzler

papers.title: Which Ellipses Are Outlines of a Given Ellipsoid? A Ratio Test with Unknown Focal Length
papers.summary: When is an image ellipse the outline of a given ellipsoid with semi-axes $a <= b <= c? For a camera with square pixels, zero skew and known principal point, we show that it is an outline at focal length $f$ exactly when a cone ratio kappa(f), computed from two eigenvalues, is at most a/c; the middle semi-axis b plays no role. With f unknown, the admissible focal lengths form an interval; whether it is empty is decided by the smallest cone ratio over $f$, which, when attained, is obtained from an explicit quartic. The interval is bounded above only when the principal point is closer to the long axis of the ellipse than to its short axis. Thus one ellipse can rule out ellipsoids that are too round, never ones that are too elongated, and none if the principal point is unknown. Simulations and 45 Cassini images of Saturn's moons support the test.

authors.name: Michael Werman

papers.title: Ground, Guide, Act: Improving VLA Spatial Generalization with Multimodal Foundation Models
papers.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models effectively learn action policies from robot demonstrations, but struggle to generalize to changes in object positions and task goals. General multimodal foundation models (MFMs) offer complementary scene understanding and spatial reasoning, but remain slow and unreliable for direct fine-grained control. To understand how MFMs can improve VLA spatial generalization, we conduct a systematic capability analysis across multiple VLA architectures using atomic-stage interventions, revealing that many failures stem from poor target grounding and global spatial routing, while local manipulation skills remain largely usable. Based on these findings, we propose MFM-VLA, a selective collaboration framework in which an MFM provides target grounding and spatial guidance, controllers execute free-space motion, and the VLA retains control over fine-grained manipulation. We fine-tune the VLA with action-chunk-level dense geometric captions and perturbed-state recovery data to improve local guidance following and recovery from unfamiliar handoff states. A development-calibrated capability router selects between direct VLA execution and MFM-assisted execution to avoid unnecessary intervention. Across LIBERO-PRO, ALOHA-Sim-PRO, RoboCasa365, and real-world chemistry tasks, MFM-VLA improves success rates by 14.9, 74.0, 3.6, and 30.9 percentage points, respectively, over the corresponding base VLA. The project page is available at https://tom-zgt.github.io/MFM-VLA

authors.name: Guangting Zheng, Shaoxuan Wang, Yu Yuan, Zhipeng Tang, Jiajun Deng, Yanyong Zhang

papers.title: PromptSMC: Enabling Particle Exploration in Flow Matching via LLM-Based Prompt Rejuvenation
papers.summary: This paper is concerned with prompt-image alignment at inference time through exploration of generative trajectories and dynamical prompt rejuvenation. We leverage sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), to offer a gradient-free and principled framework for this purpose through reward-guided trajectory selection. More specifically, we introduce LLM-based prompt rejuvenation, allowing for efficient particle exploration in SMC samplers along the diffusion time in flow matching models. The proposed method, PromptSMC, retains the selected latent states and uses a pretrained LLM to dynamically revise the prompts of duplicated particles under semantic-preservation constraints. These revised prompts induce alternative conditional velocity fields, allowing particles to explore different continuations from a shared intermediate state. The method further uses a reward model to evaluate each particle's alignment with the original prompt, and the resulting scores guide particles through resampling. PromptSMC thus integrates prompt-based exploration with reward-guided sampling, achieving faithful prompt-image alignment without additional noise injection, model training, or reward gradients. Our experiments and ablation studies across multiple benchmarks and backbones demonstrate the effectiveness of the method for text-to-image flow matching. Code is available at https://github.com/shermanlian/PromptSMC.

authors.name: Wenyi Lian, Zheng Zhao, Thomas B. Sch\"on

papers.title: Which Way Is Up? Rotated Photos Silently Hurt Multi-View 3D Foundation Models
papers.summary: Multi-view 3D foundation models estimate camera poses and 3D points from a set of photos in one forward pass. Many cameras store a portrait shot sideways, with an orientation tag telling viewers how to turn it, and this tag can be ignored, lost or wrong. We measure how rotated photos affect five such models on three datasets. A few rotated photos lower camera pose accuracy for every model, and the sideways photos already in a standard benchmark do the same. Even the most robust model still loses accuracy. The failure is also silent: the models' confidence does not reliably flag it, and most official image loaders ignore the tag. The fixes we test each correct only part of the problem. These findings call for orientation checks in reconstruction pipelines and benchmarks.

authors.name: Yukun Shi, Minglun Gong

papers.title: GDD: A Remote Sensing Image Deepfake Detection and Manipulation Localization Dataset
papers.summary: Verifying image authenticity is a critical need for a variety of applications and decision-making in the remote sensing (RS) domain, yet it is becoming more challenging as advancements in generative AI enable producing increasingly realistic synthetic overhead data. However, existing RS deepfake benchmarks prioritize sheer volume at the expense of visual realism and diversity, while also lacking rigorous out-of-distribution (OOD) testing protocols to evaluate real-world robustness. To address this, we introduce the Geospatial Deepfakes Dataset (GDD), a benchmark for RS deepfake detection and manipulation localization. Rather than relying on uncurated, redundant synthetic generation, GDD comprises images across diverse modern generative models and real image sources, alongside manipulations from diffusion inpainting, splicing, and copy-move operations. Crucially, GDD establishes an OOD evaluation protocol for deepfake detection comprising unseen real image sources and generative models. We benchmark five deepfake detectors and two localization models across intra- and cross-dataset regimes and reveal that detectors trained on high-volume, uncurated benchmarks overfit to dataset-specific artifacts, whereas training on GDD yields superior cross-dataset generalization despite its compact scale. This benchmarking also exposes critical failure modes in current state-of-the-art methods. Combined, GDD and its evaluation protocol establish a high-quality standard for developing and stress-testing detection and localization models in this safety-critical RS domain. The dataset is publicly available.

authors.name: Jacob Arndt, Philipe Dias, Debvrat Varshney, Sudarshan Srinivasan, Dalton Lunga

papers.title: HyMTS: A Multiscale Tensor Factorization-Based Network for Hyperspectral Image Restoration
papers.summary: Hyperspectral image (HSI) restoration has been explored using deep learning techniques recently. Because hyperspectral images have strong spectral and spatial redundancy, the underlying clean signal is usually represented in a low-dimensional spectral subspace and locally low-rank spatial structures. Existing methods primarily explore dense attention or feature mixing across spectral bands. In this work, we propose HyMTS, a hyperspectral restoration network with a backbone built on the Multi-scale Tensorial Summation (MTS) factorization operator. HyMTS provides a natural architectural mechanism for exploiting a low-rank prior, embedded directly in the network operator rather than imposed via an auxiliary loss or a constraint on the reconstructed output. Specifically, HyMTS stacks a unified block that couples factorized layers with input-adaptive layers, capturing both local and global dependencies across the spectral and spatial dimensions. Extensive experiments without auxiliary data on standard benchmarks for Gaussian and real-noise denoising and single-image super-resolution show that HyMTS efficiently achieves superior or comparable performance to various state-of-the-art approaches.

authors.name: Lei Xu, Fahad Sohrab, Moncef Gabbouj, Mehmet Yamac

papers.title: Synthetic Augmentation for Data-Scarce Object Detection: Allocation, Dose, and Filtering Across Six Datasets
papers.summary: Robotic perception for capturing uncooperative orbital objects and inspecting variable industrial products must often operate with limited labelled imagery. We examine a modular synthetic-augmentation pipeline, evaluating generation planning and post-generation filtering as separate interventions, with computational cost as a design constraint. Across six object-detection datasets, FLUX.1-Fill with class-specific LoRA adaptation produced dataset-dependent dose effects; the validation-selected augmentation improved mAP@50:95 on four datasets and reduced it on two. Filtering did not yield consistent gains, and FID, KID, precision, recall, and LPIPS did not consistently track detector changes. The results do not establish that image quality alone identifies useful samples. They motivate standardised evaluation and inexpensive candidate-utility measures that could identify useful samples before detector retraining, reducing repeated training cost.

authors.name: Jo\~ao F\'elix, Atabak Dehban, Rodrigo Ventura

papers.title: InitFree-SfM: When Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment meets Learned Structure-from-Motion
papers.summary: Initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA) aims to jointly recover camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial global estimate. It is a very challenging problem, especially compared to traditional BA where a good estimation is assumed. While recent methods optimize surrogate Object Space Error (OSE) objectives from random initialization, a low objective value does not necessarily yield an accurate reconstruction, revealing a gap between optimization and reconstruction. We show that existing InitFree BA pipelines struggle to produce accurate 3D reconstructions on modern SfM benchmarks, and demonstrate that incorporating learned metric depth substantially improves their practical feasibility. We introduce InitFree-SfM, a complete initialization-free SfM pipeline combining learned correspondences, metric depth, depth-consistent track construction, and joint metric refinement. Within this framework, we propose a simple depth-augmented OSE (dOSE), which complements the directional constraints of OSE by constraining landmark positions along their viewing rays. Our approach substantially outperforms existing InitFree BA methods and achieves competitive accuracy with established SfM pipelines, including on challenging low-overlap image collections. Importantly, our analysis challenges the prevailing emphasis on surrogate objectives in previous InitFree BA research, revealing that geometric constraints play a central role in accurate reconstruction, while OSE-based optimization provides further improvements.

authors.name: Simon Weber, Mateo de Mayo, Je Hyeong Hong, Carl Olsson, Daniel Cremers, Ronald Clark

papers.title: Your Codec, Your Generator: Idempotent Generative Compression without Retraining
papers.summary: We introduce an image compression framework with three properties: (i) adaptation of pretrained codecs without retraining or fine-tuning, (ii) cycle-consistent recompression, even of already-encoded images, and (iii) decoding with independently chosen generative priors. We wrap the frozen encoder with non-learned operations so that every continuous latent has a preimage, yielding a surjective pseudo-invertible neural network. A nonlinear right inverse built from the pretrained decoder satisfies $E'(D'(E'(x)))=E'(x)$. To extend consistency to quantized bitstreams, the receiver searches for a continuous latent that reproduces both the transmitted main symbols and entropy side information. A successful search and an exact correction preserve both streams under deterministic coding; the final reconstruction is checked through the actual coding path. The encoder's pseudo-inverse enables a nonlinear counterpart of back-projection. In the linear case, back-projection has the closed-form solution $x'=x+A^\dagger(y-Ax)$, giving the closest reconstruction to $x$ satisfying $Ax'=y$. Our nonlinear formulation enforces the transmitted code on proposals from an independently chosen generative model. Adjusting the starting noise controls the prior's influence without changing that code. Experiments show small first-pass quality changes, higher retained quality than trained consistency codecs over 50 recompressions, also under 8-bit storage, and decoder-side control of the perception-distortion trade-off. Decoupling the codec from its prior lets the receiver adopt future generators without retraining or re-encoding.

authors.name: Raz Haim, Assaf Shocher

papers.title: Fast Anatomy-Aware Diffeomorphic Augmentation for Brain MRI
papers.summary: Data augmentation is essential for training deep learning models that are generalizable, particularly when training data are limited. In brain MRI, augmentation methods that synthesize anatomically diverse images without relying on large cohorts are particularly attractive, especially when training supervised models for scans with a specific resolution or MRI contrast. While conventional random nonlinear fields offer a simple means of achieving such diversity, they fail to capture the underlying spatial dependencies among morphological changes across brain regions. To address this limitation, we introduce BrainAug, an anatomy-aware augmentation framework that generates diverse, anatomically coordinated deformations without relying on population imaging data. BrainAug constructs an anatomical graph encoding spatial proximity and bilateral correspondence between brain regions, then incorporates these relationships into a probabilistic model designed to sample correlated regional volume changes. These sampled variations are translated into diffeomorphic transformations, enabling substantial structural changes while preserving anatomical topology. Combined with contrast-agnostic image synthesis, BrainAug generates training images with independently varying anatomy and appearance. Evaluations across eight brain MRI datasets demonstrate stronger segmentation generalization across diverse populations, while registration experiments show improved alignment under substantial morphological differences.

authors.name: Tonmoy Hossain, Alexandra G. Roberts, Mark Olchanyi, Jonathan Williams Ramirez, Stefan Brandst\"atter, Juan Eugenio Iglesias

papers.title: Lit Up but Not Needed: Scoped Lesions Show Where Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts Depend on Their Experts
papers.summary: Cognitive neuroscience learned that an activation map is not a map of necessity. Regions that light up during a task are not always needed for it, and only lesions reveal which ones are. Mixture-of-experts (MoE) vision-language models come with an activation map for free, since the router records which experts respond to image and text tokens, and recent work reads modality-specialized experts off this map. We bring the lesion. In Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, Kimi-VL-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 3 to 12% of the experts are vision-exclusive: image tokens route to them at up to five times the uniform rate and text tokens almost never. In Qwen3-VL they receive a quarter of all image-token routing, and lesioning all of them costs less than one percentage point on average over eight perception benchmarks and free-form OCR, no more than lesioning a random set of the same size. In Kimi-VL and Gemma-4 the lesion also costs no more than a random set. Scoped lesions, which remove an expert set only at image positions or only at text positions, then show where the models do depend on their experts. In Qwen3-VL, silencing every expert at every image position costs 3 points, against 45 at text positions, where the dependence sits in dual-use experts that text-only tasks need as well. Across models the image-side dependence is 2 to 3 points in Qwen3-VL and Kimi-VL and 26 in Gemma-4. Reading text in images is the one ability that needs image-position experts in every model. The exclusive experts receive informative patches, produce outputs of ordinary size, and stay inert under sensory deprivation: text-only training recruits them only when load balancing forces it. In Kimi-VL the balancing bias itself manufactures most of them. Load balancing draws the modality map in the part of the computation the models depend on least. Expert selection, pruning and skipping should follow the lesion, not the map.

authors.name: Zhixuan Ge, Anqi Li, Kexin Geng, Wei Qiu

papers.title: Spec$^2$R: Recovering Emergent Properties in Supervised Vision Transformers
papers.summary: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved strong performance across computer vision tasks, but the quality of their learned representations differs drastically depending on the training paradigm. While self-supervised ViTs often demonstrate emergent properties, such as object-aligned patch representations and attention maps, supervised ViTs typically lack these properties, even when trained with strong data augmentations. Understanding the origin of this difference is important for explaining and controlling the object-level structure. To investigate it, we perform a spectral analysis of supervised and self-supervised models, and identify a key distinction: MLP layers in supervised ViTs introduce high-frequency variations into patch representations, disrupting their spatial organization. Motivated by this finding, we propose Spec$^2$R, a lightweight spectral regularization method that fine-tunes the MLP layers of pretrained supervised ViTs. Spec$^2$R recovers object-aligned patch representations and attention maps, while improving adversarial robustness and preserving competitive classification accuracy.

authors.name: Adam Wr\'obel, Jacek Tabor, Bartosz Zieli\'nski, Marcin Przewi\k{e}\'zlikowski

papers.title: Adapt, Label, Distill: Foundation-Model Supervision for Efficient Object Detection
papers.summary: Object detectors often transfer poorly to specialized domains, where box annotations are scarce and deployment requires compact, real-time models. Large vision foundation models can provide offline supervision, but their zero-shot predictions may be poorly aligned with the target domain. We present an adapt-label-distill pipeline that uses limited target annotations to specialize a foundation teacher and transfer its supervision to compact detectors. We adapt SAM3 on the labeled subset, generate pseudo-labels for the remaining unlabeled images, and train YOLOv11 students with confidence-guided supervision. Teacher confidence weights pseudo-label losses, while zero-gating retains uncertain hypotheses during assignment without applying their associated training losses. Experiments across six target domains and three student capacities show substantial gains in several domains, while revealing limited or negative transfer in others. Teacher comparisons under a common hard-label training recipe support the choice of SAM3, and comparisons with an EfficientTeacher adaptation provide additional evidence against an online SSOD baseline. With YOLOv11m, our pipeline improves over STAC-style self-training by up to 15.3 AP and reaches 51.6 AP on Garbage, compared with 54.1 under full supervision. On NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the deployed student achieves 188 FPS versus 2.9 FPS for SAM3, benefiting from foundation-model supervision without incurring the teacher's deployment cost. Code is available at https://github.com/zk2172-columbia/ProjectAdaptLabelDistill_ObjectDetection.

authors.name: Zhengye Yang, Anthony Wang, Yuyang Li, Mehmet Kerem Turkcan, Beizhan Yan, Zoran Kostic

papers.title: MSW: a Multi-Scale Sliced Wasserstein Distance Between Image Distributions
papers.summary: We propose the multi-scale sliced Wasserstein (MSW) distance between image distributions, which operates in pixel space and requires no trained network. MSW convolves images with a fixed bank of discrete cosine filters at several scales, pools the responses over all positions, and compares the resulting one-dimensional distributions using the Wasserstein distance. We pair MSW with an exact two-sample test that gives calibrated p-values. Most metrics compare two image sets in the latent space of a pretrained network. We show that these metrics are insensitive to simple perturbations of the images, because the latent space is nearly invariant to them. In contrast, MSW detects smaller perturbations than latent-space metrics and needs far fewer images to do so. Although it uses no learned features, it still detects semantic changes of the image distribution. Finally, MSW matches or outperforms existing Wasserstein-based metrics in our experiments.

authors.name: Youssef Haouchat, Stanislas Ducotterd, Bassam El Rawas, Michael Unser

papers.title: LineEX: Data Extraction from Scientific Line Charts
papers.summary: In this paper, we introduce LINEEX that extracts data from scientific line charts. We adapt existing vision transformers and pose detection methods and showcase significant performance gains over existing SOTA baselines. We also propose a new loss function and present its effectiveness against existing loss functions. In addition, we synthetically created the largest line chart dataset comprising 430K images. The code is available at https://github.com/Shiva-sankaran/LineEX.

authors.name: VP Shivasankaran, Muhammad Yusuf Hassan, Mayank Singh

papers.title: Medical Image Segmentation Is Now Just Another Coding Task
papers.summary: For decades, every new medical image segmentation task has needed an expert, a dedicated architecture, and a framework such as nnU-Net. This is no longer the case: medical image segmentation is now just another coding task. Given only a task description, labeled data, and a CPU (with no segmentation framework, no pretrained weights, and no human in the loop), four off-the-shelf coding agents built segmenters for 13 tasks across four imaging modalities within hours, an ability that has emerged rather than been built. On the nine 2D tasks, their best programs reach 99% of the Dice of a GPU-trained nnU-Net. Like any code, a segmenter improves by being revised and checked, so we ask how far the same agents can improve their own segmentations and what unlocks further gains. On unseen cases there is no reference, so the agents inspect renderings of their own predictions: this alone lifts the worst tenth of cases by 0.09 Dice and cuts boundary error (HD95) by almost a quarter. Far more is within reach. Told the true Dice of each attempt, the same agents improve in all 14 matched pairs, rescue 85% of failed masks instead of 30%, and surpass the GPU-trained nnU-Net on average, by producing better masks rather than by choosing among them. What unlocks these gains is a quality signal, which neither visual inspection, nor more rounds, nor a quality estimator trained by the agents themselves yet supplies: we call this the quality blind spot. The ability to build and to repair is already present; the next advance will come not from another segmentation model, but from reference-free quality estimation that coding agents can call.

authors.name: Shuheng Cao, Ruiqi Chen, Qizhen Lan, Edward Wang, Xiyun Hu, Yilei Wang, Juqy Chen, Weilin Huang, Anhong Guo

papers.title: GeoMVGen: Joint Appearance-Geometry Modeling for Multi-View Video Generation in Robotic Manipulation
papers.summary: Robotic manipulation requires predicting how robot-object interactions evolve over time, encompassing both visual appearance and scene geometry. In multi-camera settings, such predictions need to capture the evolving 3D scene consistently across viewpoints, while supporting controllable generation under different robot actions and camera configurations. Existing video generation models provide strong priors for visual appearance and motion but typically lack explicit geometric modeling. Meanwhile, recent advances in geometry-aware and multi-view generation have explored joint appearance-geometry modeling and cross-view consistency, yet generating temporally coherent appearance and geometry across multiple viewpoints under robotic manipulation conditions remains challenging. In this work, we propose GeoMVGen, a framework for joint multi-view RGB and pointmap video generation in robotic manipulation. Built on a video diffusion transformer, our framework employs modality-specific adaptation modules to capture the distinct characteristics of appearance and geometry, while using cross-modal residual connections to facilitate information exchange between the two modalities. To establish geometric correspondences across viewpoints, we further introduce a cross-view projection mechanism with complementary geometric supervisions, combining pointmap consistency with geometry foundation model-guided feature alignment. These designs enable controllable generation of temporally evolving multi-view observations with coherent appearance and geometrically consistent scene structures. Extensive experiments on 4D video generation dataset comprising simulated and real-world robotic manipulation scenarios demonstrate that GeoMVGen outperforms state-of-the-art methods in video quality, geometric accuracy, and cross-view consistency.

authors.name: Qiaoqiao Jia, Guile Wu, Dongfeng Bai

papers.title: E-Waste-Bench: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Visual Triage of Data-Center Hardware
papers.summary: Retired data-center hardware can often be refurbished or resold, but triage demands more than object categories. A model must tell visually similar parts apart, judge condition under damage and occlusion, and read the printed part number. We audit nine public e-waste collections. They cover mostly consumer devices (only 10% of images are labeled as a data-center part), label neither condition nor printed text, and contain 42% exact or augmented duplicates. We introduce E-Waste-Bench, 328K photographs drawn from 762K deduplicated images and labeled for class (24 classes), granularity, condition and printed text. Images come from those collections and the web, where a recipe-based crawler works beside an agent built on an open-weight vision-language model. The agent vets new sources and reads sites the crawler cannot parse, and both are steered toward under-represented classes. Training labels are model-made, splits follow near-duplicate groups, and human annotators label a test set of nearly 10,000 images. We benchmark classification, condition, detection, text perception and cross-dataset transfer. On this test set, a ConvNeXt-T trained on E-Waste-Bench reaches 64.3% top-1, against 31.5% with the public collections alone. Near-duplicate leakage inflates top-1 by 3.0 points under model-made test labels but by less than 0.1 under human labels, so model-labeled benchmarks need group splits. Accuracy falls to 42.1% on marketplace and auction photographs, the closest proxy for hardware leaving service. Data and code will be released.

authors.name: Nader Lobandi, Mohammad Mehdi Hosseini, Lombe Chileshe, Mohammad Mahoor

papers.title: NOBODY Was There: Bridging the Human-VLM Gap in Unwarranted Person Attribution Bias
papers.summary: Describing an image requires not only recognizing what is visible but deciding what should be inferred. We investigate a systematic gap between humans and VLMs in their tendency to attribute visible actions or events to people who are not present in an image. We term this behavior unwarranted person attribution bias and find that, across 25 SOTA VLMs, captions of person-absent scenes mention a person four times as often as human-written captions of the same images. Through a preference study, we further show that both humans and VLMs prefer captions that avoid such attributions. Motivated by this, we introduce NOBODY, a preference dataset designed to bridge the gap between humans and VLMs in unwarranted person attribution. Through direct preference optimization (DPO), we align open VLMs on NOBODY and show that their agreement with human captions on person attribution reaches or exceeds inter-human agreement, whereas nine existing public preference datasets leave this behavior largely unchanged. Furthermore, we show that human judges preferred the aligned VLM captions significantly more than those of the baseline model. Alongside NOBODY, we release NOBODY-Bench, which evaluates VLMs for unwarranted person attribution bias and their alignment against human captions and preference. Project page: https://pmadinei.github.io/NOBODY/

authors.name: Parsa Madinei, Ziqi Wen, Miguel Eckstein

papers.title: LeanWAM: Learning Latent World Action Models from Frozen Video Models
papers.summary: World action models (WAMs) typically adapt large pretrained video generators to jointly predict future observations and robot actions, incurring substantial training and deployment costs. However, it remains unclear which future representations a policy actually needs and how compactly they can be represented. Our probing study shows that complementary future representations can be compressed into a few tokens while retaining most of their action-decoding performance. Motivated by this finding, we introduce LeanWAM, a latent WAM that transfers video priors from a frozen video generator to a lightweight policy via two-stage training. In the first stage, a Future Extractor compresses observed transitions into 32 predictive tokens. These tokens condition the frozen generator and are jointly shaped by action, RGB, semantic, and geometric supervision, while a compact readout of the generator's hidden states supplies complementary world tokens. The second stage distills both representations into the policy, which learns to predict them from current observations while generating actions. With 1.4B parameters and no large-scale embodied pretraining, LeanWAM outperforms strong vision-language-action (VLA) and WAM baselines on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin~2.0. It predicts an action chunk in 25.1\,ms on an A100 GPU, 12.3--41.5$\times$ faster than representative WAMs. These results demonstrate that compact predictive supervision can transfer video priors to robust and efficient control.

authors.name: Shaolong Li, Hongze Fu, Joyce Chai, Yinpei Dai

papers.title: Xtream: An Explicit Metric State for Large-Scale Streaming Reconstruction
papers.summary: 3D foundation models (3DFMs) enable dense reconstruction in a feed-forward pass, yet their effective span is limited by cross-view attention. Local consistency has been expanded through geometric alignment of video chunks and recursive updates of an implicit memory, and large-scale scenes with pose graphs. However, both strategies are prone to drift, largely due to the lack of metric-scale observability from monocular geometry. We present Xtream,a hybrid streaming pipeline that maintains an explicit metric state through a factor graph over keyframes, while using a 3DFM as a geometric front end. Xtream incorporates metric information in two ways: through metric scale predictions from 3DFMs; or through inertial measurements if available. Across the large-scale benchmarks of VBR, Oxford Spires and KITTI, Xtream achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3DFM-based online reconstruction, reducing average absolute trajectory errors compared with published baselines and concurrent work. https://ernestolozano.github.io/xtream

authors.name: Ernesto Lozano, Alberto Jaenal, Javier Civera

papers.title: Dreamcatcher: Remembering What Surprises a World Model in Video Streams
papers.summary: As live video streams grow longer, repeatedly encoding and processing their full histories becomes increasingly costly. Answering questions as they arrive therefore calls for visual memory built in one pass before future questions are known. Existing methods mainly keep tokens that differ from earlier ones or match surrogate queries fixed in advance. Without modeling world dynamics, these criteria struggle to tell subtle surprising details from expected change. We introduce Dreamcatcher, a training-free framework and, to our knowledge, the first to use predictive signals from an independently pretrained, frozen video world model for online memory formation in streaming video question answering. Conditioned on recent history, the world model predicts incoming features using learned world priors. Its normalized prediction errors yield temporal and spatial surprisal signals that guide online segmentation and the retention of a frozen Video-LLM's native visual tokens, balancing surprising details with broad visual coverage under budgets that decay with segment age. At query time, an evidence gate admits a segment from a similarity-based shortlist only when the Video-LLM judges that it adds evidence for the question beyond the current view. We evaluate Dreamcatcher on three streaming and three offline long-video benchmarks. On OVO-Bench, Dreamcatcher achieves the highest overall accuracy among the compared training-free methods for each of four frozen Video-LLMs, reaching 78.9% with Qwen3.8-27B. With the three Qwen Video-LLMs, it also reduces average input tokens for answer generation by more than 80% relative to their base models at 1 fps.

authors.name: Jinxi He, Ce Zhang, Wenhe Liu, Jianshu Zhang, Katia P. Sycara, Yaqi Xie

papers.title: ET: Efficient Transfer from Softmax to Hybrid Attention
papers.summary: Converting pretrained softmax Transformers to efficient attention often causes substantial performance degradation, while recovery typically requires costly fine-tuning. We propose ET (Efficient Transfer), a framework for high-fidelity attention conversion with minimal optimization cost. ET combines exact local and shared-key softmax attention with a mean-anchored, scan-free global linear correction and adaptive gating, achieving linear complexity in sequence length. To preserve pretrained knowledge, ET freezes pretrained weights and calibrates only newly introduced parameters through alternating least squares on a small set of unlabeled samples, without gradient updates. On ImageNet-1K, ET achieves 79.64% and 81.55% top-1 accuracy on DeiT-S and DeiT-B, respectively, within 0.25 percentage points of their softmax teachers. At $768\times768$, ET outperforms T$^5$ by 3.59 percentage points at comparable inference FLOPs, without gradient-based fine-tuning. On DiT-XL/2, ET achieves an FID-50K of 2.59 with only 250 LoRA updates. On Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium, ET matches the teacher's GenEval score at 1K resolution with just 0.73 A100 GPU-hours of gradient-free conversion and a 1.39$\times$ inference speedup.

authors.name: Guangfu Guo, Xiaoqian Lu, Linsey Pang, Weiran Yao, Haolin Chen, Long Cheng, Kunpeng Liu

papers.title: BODYBENCH: Evaluating Adversarial Image Defenses Against AI Nudification Inpainting
papers.summary: Adversarial perturbation defenses protect images from unauthorized edits by adding imperceptible noise. Yet none of these methods have been evaluated against nudification, despite AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery (AIG-NCII) being among the most documented harms of generative AI. Moreover, nudification edits are readily carried out through inpainting, the primary setting these protection methods are designed to defend against. We argue this is a problem-formulation failure since prior threat models do not correspond to nudification edits (also called attacks). The misalignment of existing approaches is structural, spanning mask shape, training and testing prompt distributions, and success criterion which causes existing evaluations to systematically overestimate protection effectiveness. We reformulate image protection against unauthorized editing around this documented harm. We introduce BODYBENCH, a benchmark of 648 fully synthetic clothed adult subjects, each paired with 11 mask variants spanning body, face, and context regions. We propose three harm-aligned metrics: sexualization, naturalness, and recognizability that jointly determine whether an inpainted output constitutes a successful nudification attack. Auditing four recent protection methods (PhotoGuard, DiffusionGuard, AdvPaint, DiffVax) on BODYBENCH, we find that protection succeeds in only one configuration of one method, and only under exact mask alignment between defender and attacker---a condition no real defender can guarantee and one that we show is easily always bypassed. We also show that standard evaluation metrics such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) are essentially uncorrelated with nudification protection. BODYBENCH makes this misalignment measurable and provides a foundation for defenses grounded in documented harm.

authors.name: Li Qiwei, Salma Abdel Magid, Olga Russakovsky, Eric Gilbert, Sarita Schoenebeck

papers.title: ReCAP: Sequential Concept Acquisition with Guarantees under Imperfect Concept Predictors
papers.summary: Sequential concept acquisition enables interpretable diagnosis from a compact set of human-understandable findings. Such explanations are useful only if clinicians can trust them, yet most existing methods treat predicted concepts as correct, so a correct diagnosis can rest on incorrectly predicted evidence. We propose Reliable Concept Acquisition with Pruning (ReCAP), which reasons over what the concept predictor reports, including errors and abstentions, and replaces conditional information gain with a label-discriminating objective that separates cases requiring different diagnoses. We prove this objective adaptively monotone and adaptively submodular, yielding a (1-1/e) guarantee for greedy fixed-budget acquisition that degrades boundedly under learned estimates, and combine it with abstention-aware acquisition and diagnosis-preserving pruning to keep explanations short and reliable. Across five medical imaging datasets, ReCAP reduces the share of correct diagnoses supported by at least one incorrectly predicted concept from 27.1% to 9.6% relative to the strongest baseline, while using fewer than half as many concepts and achieving higher diagnostic accuracy.

authors.name: Md Nahiduzzaman, Steven Korevaar, Alireza Bab-Hadiashar, Ruwan Tennakoon

papers.title: A Well-Posed Fourth-Order Navier-Stokes Model for Image Inpainting: Theory, Order Selection, and Stripe Decomposition
papers.summary: The Navier-Stokes (NS) inpainting model of Bertalm\'io, Bertozzi and Sapiro is the only transport-type paradigm among PDE-based methods, yet it has never received a systematic higher-order extension. We show that the obvious fourth-order correction is ill-posed, and we construct the corrected, well-posed model. In the vorticity-streamfunction formulation we add a gated fourth-order term whose sign is decisive: the backward form is a Perona-Malik-type anti-diffusion, Hadamard ill-posed and consistently harmful in experiments, whereas the forward form is uniformly parabolic, energy-stable and consistently beneficial. An order-dissipation principle, stating that odd orders are dispersive and even orders dissipative, singles out the fourth order as the lowest admissible one. Large missing blocks pose a separate problem, because the correction gate stays silent there; we answer it with stripe decomposition, a Telea base fill followed by interleaved slit-wise NS passes, which converts block damage into the structural-slit regime where the model excels. The device is base-agnostic, and its gains add to those of the forward correction. On three datasets, namely BSDS500, DIV2K and a classical Chinese painting benchmark, and on three damage types, namely cracks, blocks and text occlusion, the training-free model beats every classical baseline on every sample of structure-dominated damage, gains +1.02 dB PSNR over Telea on the full 42-image painting test set with a 42/42 per-sample win rate, matches the strongest recent PDE solvers within 0.4 dB while attaining the best perceptual quality of the entire PDE family, and runs at 4-16 s per image on a consumer GPU.

authors.name: Yiwen Dou, Yiqiang Ding, Zhongyun Bao, Senyan Zhao

papers.title: SceneMemBench: A Benchmark for Scene Memory in Interactive Video World Models
papers.summary: Interactive video world models generate navigable worlds frame by frame, but a persistent world requires previously observed scenes to remain recoverable as users move away and return. Existing memory evaluations, however, often focus on seen-view revisits and full rollouts, leaving cross-view scene recovery underexplored while entangling memory with trajectory-following errors and accumulated generation degradation. We introduce SceneMemBench, a benchmark for scene memory in interactive video world models. It evaluates two complementary dimensions: seen-view recall versus novel-view recovery, and controlled diagnosis versus end-to-end interaction. We introduce Continued Rollout from a shared ground-truth observation history, alongside Full Rollout over complete model-generated interactions. SceneMemBench contains 600 controlled trajectories across 33 Unreal Engine scenes and 60 Full Rollout cases, covering eight representative open- and closed-source models. We evaluate scene recovery along subject consistency, appearance fidelity, and geometric consistency. Results show that novel-view recovery is generally more challenging than seen-view recall, while model profiles under controlled histories can differ markedly from those observed in full interaction. Together, these findings reveal complementary failure modes obscured by seen-view revisits or end-to-end rollouts alone.

authors.name: Yuheng Si, Linye Lyu, Jiawei Zhou, Lingyi Du, Nanfei Ye, Aobo Liu, Yu Liu, Yu Li, Cheng Zhuo

papers.title: Generalizable Feed-Forward 3D Hand-Object Reconstruction with Coarse-to-Fine Contact Estimation
papers.summary: Reconstructing the 3D poses of hands and objects from a single image, together with the contact between them, is fundamental to understanding manipulation. To be practical, the reconstruction must generalize to unseen objects, and the contact must be localized precisely. Yet joint feed-forward estimators often rely on predefined object sets, while contact is typically predicted from image features alone, without the explicit geometry needed to localize it. To address both limitations, we present HORCRUX, a unified feed-forward transformer with coarse-to-fine contact estimation. For unseen objects, a frozen foundation model encodes the object from a given or image-reconstructed mesh rather than from object-specific knowledge. A shared transformer then reasons jointly over the object and one or two hands to keep them aligned. For precise contact, coarse per-joint predictions from latent features are resolved over finer hand regions using the reconstructed geometry. Across seven benchmarks, HORCRUX achieves state-of-the-art object and hand pose accuracy among joint estimators and outperforms a dedicated contact estimator in fine-grained contact. These results suggest that contact is best estimated jointly with reconstruction, whose geometry directly localizes it.

authors.name: Seonghwan Park, Yong-Hoon Kwon, Min-Gyu Park

papers.title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
papers.summary: World action models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generators for robot control by jointly predicting future camera frames and actions, transferring physical priors learned from video into manipulation policies. However, generating future frames before every action makes test-time inference too slow for closed-loop control, while most existing policies remain restricted to short observation histories. Building on Fast-WAM, which showed that video prediction shapes policy representations during training so that future frame synthesis can be skipped at deployment, we present G0.7, a generalist world action model scaled along two axes: extending the context window from a single observation to up to five minutes of history, and scaling pretraining to a large-scale corpus of robot teleoperation and human egocentric (ego) video. Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6x faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging.

authors.name: Tianyuan Yuan, Baijun Ye, Shicheng Cao, Xing Nie, Xiaopeng Yu, Ke Dong, Zijie Zhao, Shenling Qiu, Yizhao Xu, Feiyang Xue, Haonan Liu, Haoyu Zhang, Haobo Jia, Zheng Liu, Anqi Yang, Jiahui Niu, Yue Sun, Tailai Cheng, Jianpeng Yu, Yang Wen, Longhao Wei, Zibin Dong, Shiduo Zhang, Yicheng Liu, Hang Zhao

papers.title: Don't Miss the Forest for the Trees: Zero-Shot Skeleton Action Recognition with Hyperbolic Hierarchical Semantic Prototypes
papers.summary: Zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition is evaluated almost exclusively on flat leaf labels, which leaves open whether a representation also grounds the broader concepts that contain an action in skeleton motion. We find that strong leaf alignment does not carry over to them: when ancestor concepts are scored directly under independent decoding, eight flat methods with 57.86-73.29% mean leaf Top-1 reach only 6.15-31.21% mean full-path accuracy across four NTU RGB+D splits. We propose the Hyperbolic Hierarchical Semantic Prototype ($H^2SP$) framework, which represents every node of an action taxonomy in the Lorentz model of hyperbolic space. First, instead of learning a free vector per node, $H^2SP$ synthesizes hierarchy-aware prototypes by recursive parent-child geodesic interpolation under a single tree-wide gate. Second, tangent-space semantic and distributional alignment on seen classes anchor the leaf prototypes in skeleton motion. Third, a soft entailment-cone regularizer encourages directional parent-child inclusion, propagating this motion grounding to ancestor concepts. We evaluate hierarchical concept prediction under independent and cascade decoding, and transfer to an alternative taxonomy without retraining. Across the four splits, $H^2SP$ attains the best mean independent and cascade full-path accuracy among the evaluated methods, at a comparable leaf Top-1 of 72.40%. Transferred to the alternative taxonomy, it outperforms both flat baselines and the same-tree Euclidean control across every split and decoding mode, indicating that its concept-level correspondence extends beyond the training taxonomy.

authors.name: Zixiao Jin, Siyu Zhu, Feng Ding, Haisheng Fu, Xin Dong, Shankai Chen, Jie Liang

papers.title: RELAY: Learning Compatible Representations One Encoder at a Time
papers.summary: Old and new document embeddings coexist during incremental gallery re-encoding. RELAY trains a new query encoder with a learned projection against the original gallery, then freezes both to train the new document encoder. The same query vector scores both document versions throughout a single re-encoding pass. After backfill, optional query refinement drops the projection and reuses the stored document vectors. Across three text-to-image retrieval upgrades on COCO and Flickr30K, RELAY improves Recall@1 on untouched galleries by 8.66-10.23 percentage points over the original systems. For direct re-encoding, RELAY ranks first in both Qwen-to-Qwen upgrades and second in CLIP-to-Qwen by area under the Recall@1 curve, under both native scoring and matched calibration. With embeddings held fixed, calibrating scores separately for each document version can reduce drops in Recall@1 during backfill and change which method achieves the highest backfill AUC. After query refinement, final Recall@1 is within 0.97 percentage points of conventional joint training in all three upgrades.

authors.name: Yu Wang, Chuan Qin, Qiang Zhang

papers.title: Open-OmniCoach: Evidence-Enhanced Trajectory Learning for Omni Video Agents
papers.summary: Training capable omni video agents requires more than diverse question-answer pairs: agents must learn to reliably find, connect, and correct task-relevant evidence in omni-setting. However, we argue that existing data pipelines provide limited control over task-relevant evidence and weak supervision for these capabilities. In this work, we present Open OmniCoach, a new framework for evidence-seeking omni video agents. It contains a high-quality dataset, OmniCoach-240K, and a new agentic reinforcement learning (RL) method, Step-Level Evidence-Guided Policy Optimization (SEPO). For the former, OmniCoach-240K comprises 248.2K interaction trajectories, including 230.7K multi-span trajectories and 17.4K reflection trajectories. We design a three-stage data pipeline by leveraging both fine-grained omni-evidence and the agent's own errors. Meanwhile, compared with other RL baselines, SEPO provides turn-level credit based on improvements in evidence coverage and temporal localization. Applying both trajectory data and the SEPO method, we obtain Open OmniAgent models. The resulting models outperform the baselines across multiple video and audio-visual understanding tasks by significant margins, demonstrating the effectiveness of the Open OmniCoach framework. In particular, Open OmniAgent-30B improves average accuracy over Qwen3-Omni by 6.3 percentage points across nine benchmarks, with gains of 12.2 and 13.3 points on LVOmniBench and LVBench, respectively.

authors.name: Weisong Liu, Xiangtai Li, Haochen Wang, Haiquan Wen, Zhaoxiang Zhang

papers.title: Beyond Expert Replay: Cross-Instruction Anchoring for Continual Vision-Language-Action Learning
papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models need to continually acquire new manipulation skills while retaining the ability to follow previously learned instructions. Experience replay (ER) can mitigate catastrophic forgetting, but retaining only a small number of historical expert frames per task leaves many old-instruction responses without direct supervision. Under limited replay, we observe a structured failure mode in which an earlier instruction can trigger a subsequently learned, competing goal. To address this gap, we propose Cross-Instruction Anchoring (XIA), which supplements expert replay with instruction-conditioned response preservation. At each task boundary, XIA freezes the previous policy as a teacher and matches its responses to old instructions paired with current observations. This extends supervision beyond stored historical examples without requiring additional expert replay data. Experiments across multiple VLA architectures and three LIBERO suites demonstrate improved success rates and reduced forgetting compared with ER under identical historical expert-data budgets. Additional RoboCasa and real-world experiments further support the effectiveness of XIA.

authors.name: Ziyang Chen, Dehua Chen, Shaoguang Wang, Xu Yan, Hao Huang, Tao Chen

papers.title: HiGS: A Hierarchical Architecture for Fast Differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) makes one screen tile the cell of partitioning, the cell of rasterization, and the unit of parallel work. Partitioning favors large tiles and rasterization small ones, and with one unit per tile the densest tiles set the frame time. We present Hierarchically Tiled Gaussian Splatting (HiGS), a unified architecture for rendering and reconstruction that gives each role its own granularity: Gaussians are partitioned over coarse macro-tiles, rasterized over the fine render tiles within them, and processed in bounded depth-sorted batches. A dense region issues more batches instead of one longer unit, so frame time follows the work in a view rather than its densest tile. The same batches carry reconstruction: compositing supplies the transmittance and color needed to differentiate each one independently, leaving optimizer memory traffic as the dominant training cost. We fuse the optimizer into the backward pass, halve the parameters and moments it stores and updates directly, and defer appearance updates outside the view. HiGS renders scenes faster than every published method we evaluate, by the widest margin on views with uneven load, and reconstructs them faster and in less memory, at equal image quality and with exact front-to-back alpha compositing.

authors.name: Dawid Paj\k{a}k, Martin Bisson, Rodolfo Lima, Fran\c{c}ois Trudel

papers.title: DUALingo: A Dual-Hand Instruction-Guided Dataset for Affordance Grounding on 3D Objects
papers.summary: Affordance grounding localizes where an agent should interact with an object to perform a task. Many everyday manipulation tasks, however, require bimanual affordance, in which two hands assume complementary and cooperative roles to accomplish a shared goal. Existing 3D affordance datasets primarily ground single interaction regions, and manually annotating dual-hand, cooperative contacts does not scale. To address this gap, we introduce DUALingo, a large-scale dataset for task-conditioned, role-aware bimanual 3D affordance grounding on diverse everyday objects. DUALingo represents each task as two cooperative, hand-agnostic roles, each grounded as a heatmap on the object surface. It contains 271K free-form tasks on 71K objects, generated by a fully automated pipeline of open-weight foundation models without human labeling. Expert ratings and a validated LLM judge confirm the quality of the resulting annotations. Trained on DUALingo, existing 3D affordance models learn to ground both cooperative roles from natural-language instructions, with the best-performing model achieving a more than threefold improvement in aIoU over the zero-shot baseline, from 10.3 to 37.8. Robotic manipulation demonstrations illustrate the actionability of the predicted bimanual affordances in performing cooperative tasks. These results position DUALingo as a scalable foundation for learning everyday bimanual affordances. Project page: https://nycu-pair-labs.github.io/DUALingo/

authors.name: Ming-Lun Lee, Yi-En Li, Feng-Dian Su, Ming-Han Lee, Kun-Ru Wu, Krzysztof Czarnecki, Yu-Chee Tseng

papers.title: TANDEM: Temporal Anchor Densification With Reliability-Aware Memory for Lightweight Sparse Depth Completion in Endoscopic Robotic Navigation
papers.summary: For endoscopic robotic surgery, accurate dense depth perception serves as a foundational capability, which enables navigation, instrument localization, and tissue interaction. However, endoscopic video lacks reliable metric depth, while metric measurements obtained via tracking, time-of-flight sensing, or instrument contact only cover a small fraction of pixels in each frame, rendering sparse depth completion an urgent and unsolved challenge. In this work, we propose Temporal Anchor Densification with Reliability-Aware Memory (TANDEM), a causal sparse depth completion framework for endoscopic video. It adopts a lightweight design and leverages the video stream: past measurements re-projected into the current view recover the metric evidence unavailable within a single sparse frame. To keep this evidence interpretable, accurate, and efficient, an explicit memory scores each re-projected measurement with analytic re-observation, age, and motion-parallax factors without overriding current measurements. A compact network then reconstructs depth via reliability-weighted gradient integration and a frequency-gated reference prior. We evaluate TANDEM on the C3VD colonoscopy and StereoMIS laparoscopy datasets. With only 5.58 M parameters, TANDEM reduces the root mean square error by 11.7% and 32.0%, respectively, compared with the strongest baseline, and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy. It also remains accurate under pose errors of the magnitude reported for endoscopic pose estimation. Code will be released at https://github.com/Wk-cpu-art/TANDEM upon acceptance.

authors.name: Weikuan Qiu, Jiale Hou, Chongzhao Xu, Jinlian Ma

papers.title: Decompose, Verify, Evolve: Physically Grounded Shape Decomposition
papers.summary: Shape decomposition represents 3D objects as a compact set of geometric primitives for interpretable modeling and simulation. However, existing decomposition methods are trained primarily for geometric fidelity, without explicit constraints on physical plausibility, and can therefore produce disconnected parts or physically unstable reconstructions. We present PhysDec, an agentic framework that draws on a pretrained vision-language model's semantic understanding and commonsense reasoning to predict material-aware primitive decompositions from a few images. Within this framework, PhysDec-Loop is an agentic pipeline that reasons about part structure and materials, using a reference 3D point cloud for geometric feedback and physical verifiers to guide iterative refinement. Through self-evolution, we further develop another agentic pipeline, PhysDec-Evolved, which learns from prior corrections to predict primitive decompositions from images without point-cloud feedback or a correction loop at inference. Experiments show that PhysDec-Loop improves geometric fidelity, physical plausibility and visual quality over geometry-focused baselines, while PhysDec-Evolved approaches its performance at substantially lower inference cost.

authors.name: Wenchao Ma, Rui Yu, Fan Zhu, Jiachen Liu, Sharon X. Huang

papers.title: DraftKV: Protecting Persistent Worlds through Hierarchical Streaming Retrieval
papers.summary: Interactive video world models enable action- and camera-controlled exploration, yet struggle to maintain consistent spatial geometry and appearance when revisiting previously explored locations. Historical KV caches help auto-regressive video diffusion models maintain long-term consistency, but their retrieval and attention computation introduce substantial latency as history grows. We propose DraftKV, a training-free framework that retrieves historical KV caches based on geometric grounding and query-conditioned relevance, while combining CPU offloading with tile-wise streaming attention to reduce GPU memory usage and inference latency. Theoretically, we show that draft relevance reproduces the mean branch of full-resolution block relevance exactly, so its deviation is confined to the $\beta$-weighted max branch, and we bound retrieval utility loss in terms of the measured Top-K selection overlap. We further show that draft relevance cannot distinguish blocks with similar pooled descriptors regardless of camera pose, motivating geometric grounding before refinement. Then, we introduce streaming CG-Attention, which overlaps CPU-to-GPU KV transfers with attention computation through tile-wise streaming, hiding transfer latency while maintaining bounded GPU memory usage. Experiments across diverse model families show that DraftKV achieves superior generation quality and consistency while achieving $3.27\times$ end-to-end speedup and 42.2% peak GPU memory reduction over other CPU-offloaded KV cache retrieval methods. Notably, DraftKV enables high-quality interactive world generation with historical KV retrieval on a single H100 GPU using SolarWM-33B.

authors.name: Xiaoling Zhou, Haopeng Li, Yufa Zhou, Rui Ding, Yu Li, Jun Lin, Enze Xie, Chunhua Shen, Xuan Shen

papers.title: VLG-Drive: Unifying Vision-Language and Geometric Priors for Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: A driving planner needs both scene semantics, which vision-language models (VLMs) provide, and spatial structure, which geometric foundation models recover from visual history. We present VLG-Drive, which keeps both models frozen and trains only a fusion interface and a planner from trajectory labels. At each camera-grid cell, the interface fuses the paired VLM and geometry features into one joint token through a geometry-anchored residual, and a command-conditioned planner reads these tokens to predict the ego trajectory. VLG-Drive achieves 31.78 EPDMS on NavHard under perturbed initial states, the highest among the compared methods, and 88.27 PDMS on NavTest from cameras alone. Pointwise fusion outperforms independent VLM and geometry streams on both benchmarks. In closed-loop driving on 420 HUGSIM scenarios, VLG-Drive outperforms all compared planners. These results indicate that a lightweight planner trained on fused features of frozen vision-language and geometric foundation models is an effective alternative to adapting either model for planning.

authors.name: Junge Zhang, Jie Zhu, Yanqi Jia, Xiangyu Xu, Zixun Huang, Wenbin He, Xin Li, Jiachen Li, Liu Ren

papers.title: TACTUS: Unifying Surgical Action Understanding in Time and Space
papers.summary: Advancing surgical automation requires a comprehensive spatio-temporal understanding of how instruments act on tissue throughout an action. Existing surgical benchmarks, however, largely define supervision through task-specific targets, leaving the relationships between action semantics, instrument motion, and tissue interaction incompletely specified. To address this limitation, we introduce TACTUS (Tool, Action, Contact and Trajectory Understanding in Surgery), a new dataset and benchmark that establishes a unified annotation framework for complete surgical actions. The framework jointly specifies tool and action identities, nested action and interaction windows, instrument-specific landmark trajectories, and tissue-region tracks. To construct these annotations at scale, we develop a two-tier pipeline combining human annotation, point tracking, and model-generated spatial prompts. Using this pipeline, we re-annotate 141 videos from five public sources, producing 22,995 action clips spanning 2.9 million frames. The dataset comprises 15,668 Gold clips with human spatial prompts followed by review and re-checking, and 7,327 Silver clips combining human semantic and temporal annotations with model-generated spatial prompts. We further introduce TactusNet, the companion reference network, to benchmark semantic, temporal, and spatial prediction from shared video features. Across TactusNet and 13 published baselines, tool-action accuracy reaches 95.8% with per-head encoder fine-tuning, while the best temporal recall and contact Dice reach 46.6% at temporal IoU 0.7 and 0.351, respectively. Moreover, adding Silver improves the default TactusNet's pair accuracy from 93.8% to 95.5%. Together, these contributions establish a foundation for learning and evaluating the instrument-tissue interactions underlying future surgical automation.

authors.name: Lurui Wang, Hao Ding, Chenhao Yu, Chenyan Jing, Jiru Xu, Ruoqi Zuo, Liwei Mei, Chang Liu, Lalithkumar Seenivasan, Mathias Unberath

papers.title: SPAR: Self-Referenced World-Model Rewards for Physical Alignment in Video Generation
papers.summary: Generating videos with physically plausible dynamics remains challenging despite advances in visual quality. Latent world models offer predictive signals for evaluating physical plausibility, but higher agreement between predicted and observed features may reflect easier-to-predict scene content rather than more plausible dynamics. We propose \textbf{S}elf-Referenced \textbf{P}hysical \textbf{A}lignment \textbf{R}ewards (\textbf{SPAR}), a framework that uses world-model predictions for inference-time physical alignment. SPAR compares each video's prediction error with that of static clips constructed by repeating its own frames, providing a content-matched reference for evaluating generated dynamics.
