Adding charge conjugation symmetry to the operator pool improves the results, and combining different pools with suitable initial states recovers the ground and first excited states over the full mass range. These findings give practical guidelines for applying ADAPT-VQE to lattice field theories beyond $1+1D$.

authors.name: Nico Dichter, Andrea Bulgarelli, Lena Funcke, Stefan K\"{u}hn

papers.title: $QQ\bar Q\bar Q$ Quark System and Gauge/String Duality II: String Breaking
papers.summary: This is the second of two companion papers in which we continue developing the construction of the fully heavy tetraquark system using the gauge/string duality. Here, we extend this construction to model $SU(3)$ gauge theory with two light flavors of equal mass. As an application, we analyze the two lowest Born-Oppenheimer potentials, both analytically and numerically, for rectangular and collinear geometries. Our analysis reveals several critical scales associated with string reconnection and breaking, as well as junction annihilation and pinching. In addition, we find that the string tension is universal, whereas the string breaking distance is not.

authors.name: Oleg Andreev

papers.title: Para-fusion Category and Topological Defect Lines in $\mathbb Z_N$-parafermionic CFTs
papers.summary: We study topological defect lines (TDLs) in two-dimensional $\mathbb Z_N$-parafermoinic CFTs. Different from the bosonic case, in the 2d parafermionic CFTs, there exist parafermionic defect operators that can live on the TDLs and satisfy interesting fractional statistics. We propose a categorical description for these TDLs, dubbed as ``para-fusion category", which contains various novel features, including $\mathbb Z_M$ $q$-type objects for $M\vert N$, and parafermoinic defect operators as a type of specialized 1-morphisms of the TDLs. The para-fusion category in parafermionic CFTs can be regarded as a natural generalization of the super-fusion category for the description of TDLs in 2d fermionic CFTs. We investigate these distinguishing features in para-fusion category from both a 2d pure CFT perspective, and also a 3d anyon condensation viewpoint. In the latter approach, we introduce a generalized parafermionic anyon condensation, and use it to establish a functor from the parent fusion category for TDLs in bosonic CFTs to the para-fusion category for TDLs in the parafermionized ones. At last, we provide many examples to illustrate the properties of the proposed para-fusion category, and also give a full classification for a universal para-fusion category obtained from parafermionic condensation of Tambara-Yamagami $\mathbb Z_N$ fusion category.

authors.name: Jin Chen, Babak Haghighat, Qing-Rui Wang

papers.title: A JT/KPZ correspondence
papers.summary: We point out a correspondence between the Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity and the stationary measure of the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on an interval. By relating the Schwarzian limit of the double-scaled SYK to the weakly asymmetric limit of the open ASEP, we establish that the path-integral measure defining the Euclidean evolution between two end-of-the-world branes in JT gravity can be interpreted as the stationary measure of the KPZ equation on an interval with Neumann boundary conditions. We also establish the match between correlation functions.

authors.name: Masataka Watanabe

papers.title: Topological subregions in Chern Simons theory and topological string theory
papers.summary: The standard, gapped entanglement boundary condition in Chern Simons theory breaks the topological invariance of the theory by introducing a complex structure on the entangling surface. This produces an infinite dimensional subregion Hilbert space, a non-trivial modular Hamiltonion, and a UV-divergent entanglement entropy that is a universal feature of local quantum field theories. In this work, we appeal to the combinatorial quantization of Chern Simons theory to define a purely topological notion of a subregion. The subregion operator algebras are spaces of functions on a quantum group. We develop a diagrammatic calculus for the associated $q$-deformed entanglement entropy, which arise from the entanglement of anyonic edge modes. The $q$-deformation regulates the divergences of the QFT, producing a finite entanglement entropy associated to a $q$-tracial state. We explain how these ideas provide an operator algebraic framework for the entanglement entropy computations in topological string theory \cite{Donnelly:2020teo,Jiang:2020cqo, wongtopstring}, where a large- $N$ limit of the $q$-deformed subregion algebra plays a key role in the stringy description of spacetime.

authors.name: Gabriel Wong

papers.title: Single-valued flat connections in several variables on arbitrary Riemann surfaces
papers.summary: Polylogarithms on Riemann surfaces may be constructed systematically in terms of flat connections that can enjoy various algebraic and analytic properties. In this paper, we present a single-valued and modular invariant connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ on the configuration space $\text{Cf}_n(\Sigma)$ of an arbitrary number $n$ of points on an arbitrary compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ with or without punctures. The connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ generalizes an earlier construction for a single variable and is built out of the same integration kernels. We show that ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ is flat on $\text{Cf}_n(\Sigma)$. For the case without punctures, we relate it to the meromorphic multiple-valued Enriquez connection ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ in $n$ variables on the universal cover $\tilde \Sigma$ of $\Sigma$ by the composition of a gauge transformation and an automorphism of the Lie algebra in which ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ and ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ take values. In a companion paper, we shall establish the equivalence between the flatness of these connections and the corresponding interchange and Fay identities, for arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces.

authors.name: Eric D'Hoker, Oliver Schlotterer

papers.title: Spin chains for ADE quiver theories
papers.summary: The spectral problem of four-dimensional superconformal quiver gauge theories can be mapped to one-dimensional spin chains with restricted Hilbert spaces, where the composition of neighbouring spins follows the path algebra of the quiver. To better understand such spin chains, we compute the one-loop planar dilatation operator for the 4d N=2 ADE quiver gauge theories obtained by orbifolding the N=4 Super-Yang-Mills theory and marginally deforming by independently varying the gauge couplings. This extends previous work which was mainly focused on the Z2 quiver. We characterise the general features of the resulting ADE spin-chain models and construct the 2-magnon Bethe ansatz for holomorphic states. We also evaluate, at large N, the N=2 superconformal index of these gauge theories and use it to study their protected spectrum in specific sectors.

authors.name: Jarryd Bath, Konstantinos Zoubos

papers.title: Quantum channel capacity of traversable wormholes
papers.summary: We formulate the Gao-Jafferis-Wall traversable wormhole protocol as a quantum channel and compute its quantum channel capacity. We show that this capacity is governed by the time derivative of an out-of-time-ordered correlator, hence by operator size growth in the holographic dual, and that its growth is bounded above by the Einstein gravity limit. The channel capacity therefore provides a natural benchmark for quantum simulations of traversable wormholes.

authors.name: Jingru Lu, Zhenbin Yang, Jianming Zheng

papers.title: Supergravity flows, wormholes and their pseudo-Hermitian holographic duals
papers.summary: We find solutions to consistent truncations of supergravity where some real scalars are analytically extended to imaginary values, ensuring the metric remains real-valued. Among the solutions there are Lorentzian traversable wormholes connecting two asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetimes and flows that have a real metric also when uplifted to ten or eleven dimensions. We argue that the holographic duals are pseudo-Hermitian and $PT$-symmetric theories. Wormhole solutions also admit an interpretation as the low-energy theory of two stacks of branes and anti-branes after tachyon condensation. The wormhole is then dual to an entangled state of two copies of the theory that lives on a stack of branes. We present some evidence by computing the mutual information between the theories at each boundary and by identifying the Goldstone bosons associated with the breaking of the two copies of Poincar\'e symmetry to their diagonal subgroup.

authors.name: Jose M. Begines, Ant\'on F. Faedo, Carlos Hoyos, Daniele Musso

papers.title: Generalised Symmetries and Manifest Duality II: Curved Spacetime
papers.summary: We extend the potential-based formulation of self-dual and duality-symmetric gauge theories developed in \cite{Chakrabarti:2025gyt} to curved spacetime. The gravitational coupling is encoded by the same metric-dependent linear map of Sen's formalism. The parent new action retains the higher-form $h$-gauge symmetry, and different gauge choices reproduce either Sen's flux-based formulation or a potential-based description in which the shadow sector decouples directly at the level of the action. We also derive explicit form of the gravitational map for the toroidally reduced theory in $D=4n$ and for a polyform formulation in arbitrary dimension, both of which apply equally to ours as well as Sen's formalism. As non-trivial checks, we reproduce the \'Alvarez-Gaum\'e-Witten gravitational anomalies of the two-dimensional chiral boson without fermionisation, and of the ten-dimensional self-dual five-form. Finally, on $\mathrm{AdS}_5\times S^5$ the physical on-shell action yields the non-vanishing boundary contribution required by holography without adding a boundary term by hand. We also establish a local on-shell identification with the textbook supergravity RR four-form potential.

authors.name: Subhroneel Chakrabarti, Arkajyoti Manna, Madhusudhan Raman

papers.title: What makes spacetime spin in string theory?
papers.summary: Type II string theory in the absence of orientifolds requires the target spacetime $X$ to admit a spin structure. We show that this familiar requirement arises directly from the consistency of the worldsheet GSO projection. The obstruction is a mixed global anomaly between $(-1)^{\text{F}_L}$ and the target space background data, detected by the spin bordism group $\Omega_3^{\mathrm{spin}}(B\mathbb{Z}_2\times X)$. We compute the relevant mixed bordism group and identify the bordism class of the GSO-projected worldsheet theory. For smooth target spaces, vanishing of the anomaly reduces to the condition that $X$ is spin, while for general orbifolds $[\hat{X}/G]$, $\hat{X}$ has to carry a $G$-equivariant spin structure. We also classify all possible theta angles in the worldsheet theory and show that they correspond to all possible continuous and discrete background fields of the target space theory visible in string perturbation theory.

authors.name: Matilda Delgado, Lorenz Eberhardt, Marija Toma\v{s}evi\'c

papers.title: Bootstrapping "black holes" at low impact parameter
papers.summary: We use the stringy dispersion relation to obtain a numerical upper bound on the radius of a uniformly absorptive disk in a six-dimensional gravitational effective field theory. Near the boundary of the allowed region of low-energy couplings, the bound is of order the Schwarzschild radius. The dispersion relation connects those couplings to the partial-wave spectrum. In the calculation, we fix the eikonal contribution in a specified high-energy region at large impact parameter and vary the real parts of the remaining elastic $S$-matrix elements within the bounds imposed by unitarity. The real part of each element sets an upper limit on its absorption probability, so the radius bound applies to any unitary amplitude satisfying the same assumptions. Near the boundary, a strongly absorptive disk of the classical trapped-surface radius is excluded if it must extend down to low collision energies. Raising the minimum energy lifts this exclusion. The angular momentum at the edge of the absorptive core grows approximately as $s^{0.7}$, where $s$ is the squared center-of-mass energy. This is close to the $s^{2/3}$ scaling expected for an edge at a fixed multiple of the Schwarzschild radius in six dimensions. The corresponding dimension-dependent scaling also describes full-amplitude bootstrap results in nine to eleven dimensions. In the extremal spectra, the band's outer edge stays at roughly the same impact parameter as the collision energy increases, about 5-6 EFT cutoff lengths $M_{\rm EFT}^{-1}$ at weak gravity.

authors.name: Diptarka Das, Aninda Sinha

papers.title: Conformal line defects from matter-coupled 5D N=4 gauged supergravity
papers.summary: We study a number of holographic solutions describing conformal line defects within $N=2$ SCFTs from matter-coupled $N=4$ gauged supergravity in five dimensions. For $SO(2)_D\times SO(3)$ gauge group, the gauged supergravity admits two supersymmetric $AdS_5$ vacua with $N=4$ and $N=2$ unbroken supersymmetries. It turns out that only solutions that are asymptotic to the $N=4$ vacuum are possible leading to line defects within the dual $N=2$ SCFT. In gauged supergravity with $SO(2)\times ISO(3)$ gauge group, we find similar solutions with the $N=2$ SCFT appearing in the IR while the UV field theories correspond to six-dimensional $N=(0,2)$ field theories arising from M5-branes wrapped on a hyperbolic space $H^2$. The solution with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry is also uplifted to eleven dimensions via a consistent truncation on $H^2\times S^4$. Finally, for gauged supergravity with $SO(2)\times SO(3)\times SO(3)$ gauge group that admits two $N=4$ supersymmetric $AdS_5$ vacua, we find a solution describing a line defect that interpolates between these two vacua as well as a solution with only one asymptotic $AdS_5$ geometry.

authors.name: Parinya Karndumri

papers.title: Comments on holographic spread complexity
papers.summary: We revisit the holographic proposal relating the growth rate of spread complexity to the radial momentum of a bulk probe, aiming to identify its underlying assumptions and clarify how classical probe dynamics emerges from quantum dynamics. By quantizing AdS probes directly and using the extrapolation dictionary, we provide a more general derivation of the proposal within the probe approximation for the specified class of states. In particular, we discuss a probe analogue of the classical complexity observables appearing in the ``complexity=anything'' (CAny) framework and examine how such an observable can be quantized. Since probe dynamics is not intrinsically tied to the AdS/CFT correspondence, we also examine the proposal in flat and de Sitter spacetimes. In flat spacetime, the physical Hamiltonian does not preserve the coherent-state structure, and spread complexity measures the dispersive broadening of the wave packet rather than classical momentum. In de Sitter space, generic semiclassical wave packets in the static-patch energy representation show the same dispersive behavior. By contrast, coherent states adapted to the principal-series representation can exhibit exponential growth of spread complexity, with a growth rate that has the same time dependence as the classical radial momentum. These examples indicate that a semiclassical limit alone is not sufficient for a momentum--complexity relation.

authors.name: Zhehan Li, Jia Tian

papers.title: Revealing the conformal symmetry of the discrete series scalars in dS${}_2$
papers.summary: On two-dimensional manifolds with nonzero constant Ricci curvature, there exists an infinite sequence of scalar fields with nonzero mass parameter that admit a pair of (anti-)holomorphic currents. After suitably defining the theory in de Sitter space ($\mathrm{dS}_2$), correlation functions of these currents obey global conformal Ward identities. We address the question of how this global conformal symmetry manifests as an action on the scalar field. An essential step is in leveraging an equivalent description of the scalar field in terms of a conformal Killing tensor. Through this, we find a conformal symmetry transformation that acts locally on the conformal Killing tensor, but non-locally on the scalar field. We show that the equation of motion transforms covariantly with respect to these conformal transformations, and further find a traceless stress tensor in both $\mathrm{dS}_2$ and $\mathrm{AdS}_2$, locally defined in terms of the conformal Killing tensor, which generates the global conformal isometry transformations.

authors.name: Lukas W. Lindwasser

papers.title: Magnetic Catalysis and Fermion Mass Generation in de Sitter Spacetime
papers.summary: We consider the dynamics of a charged fermion in de Sitter space in the presence of a uniform background magnetic field, and discuss magnetic catalysis of chiral symmetry breaking using the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. We evaluate the mode functions of the charged fermion field in this background by imposing the Bunch--Davies vacuum condition. The gap equation is solved in the mean-field approximation. We derive analytic expressions for the gap in several limiting regimes, such as the large-magnetic-field and large-curvature limits. We find that the curvature effect restores chiral symmetry, whereas the magnetic field enhances chiral symmetry breaking through the conventional mechanism of magnetic catalysis. The phase structure associated with chiral symmetry breaking is revealed by numerical calculations.

authors.name: Kohei Fujikura, Toshifumi Noumi, Shintetsu Yamazaki

papers.title: Cutting corners: exciting and magical bounds from the cusp bootstrap
papers.summary: An illuminating probe of the dynamics of a line defect is the global geometry of its worldline. For a conformal line defect in a conformal field theory, sharp corners in the worldline, i.e. cusps, host dynamical degrees of freedom characterized in part by a spectrum of scaling dimensions, called cusp anomalous dimensions. We present various general bounds on cusp anomalous dimensions following from unitarity and cutting-and-gluing consistency of different defect geometries. We first establish, for cusps involving conjugate defects, that level crossings upon varying the cusp angle are forbidden between the lightest singlet cusp and any non-singlet cusp, proving that singlet cusps are the lightest. Then, we study line defects arranged in a rectangular geometry, which are subject to bootstrap constraints reminiscent of the spinless modular bootstrap. We find an analytic ``magic" functional that produces an optimal and universal lower bound on the dimension of a right angle bare cusp in terms of the universal defect Casimir energy between the corresponding defect and its conjugate in flat space.

authors.name: Ryan A. Lanzetta, Ian Moult, Yifan Wang

papers.title: Modular flow and the area operator
papers.summary: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, the Jafferis-Lewkowycz-Maldacena-Suh (JLMS) formula relates the boundary modular Hamiltonian to the HRT area operator and the corresponding bulk modular Hamiltonian. In standard discussions of a holographic code built from perturbative excitations on a fixed classical background, the $A/4G$ term dominates over the bulk modular Hamiltonian in the limit $G \to 0$. However, this setup is insufficient to describe the action of boundary modular flows that change the classical background. In contrast, our recent discussion of `large' codes provides a useful framework to obtain a JLMS formula that relates bulk and boundary modular flows acting on appropriate states in the code. Here, one sees that the bulk modular Hamiltonian is not in fact subdominant when the modular flow defined by one state acts on another state peaked around a sufficiently different classical background. Instead, the bulk modular Hamiltonian can be of order $1/G$ and can dominate over the $A/4G$ term. Nevertheless, we show that if the two states have the same classical background except for data conjugate to the HRT area then, under mild assumptions and over a large range of flow parameters, the modular-flowed state is described by a classical background given by the HRT-area flow alone.

authors.name: Xi Dong, Donald Marolf, Pratik Rath

papers.title: Semiclassical reconstruction of the Toda pole lattice via analytic continuation of the Probabilistic Approach
papers.summary: We develop a probabilistic construction of Toda field theory correlators from the Coulomb gas representation. Reinterpreting $n$-point functions of primaries as $w$-moments of random variables with respect to a Gaussian measure, we derive constraints on the Toda momenta and coupling constant. $L^2$ and $L^p$ convergence conditions for the associated random variables, triviality constraints on the correlators, and local integrability conditions for the cross-moments are derived. These constraints define an extended region of convergence for the Toda correlators and provide a systematic, probabilistic interpretation of the Seiberg bounds. We proceed to analytically continue the moment indices by employing a Mellin-Barnes representation of the random variables. The local convergence boundaries become meromorphic local integrability divisors, and, in the semiclassical $b\to0$ limit, these divisors reconstruct the Liouville charge pole lattice. For $A_n$ Toda theory, we show that natural $W_n$-closure conditions in this semiclassical limit select rank-one, Virasoro-like submodules inside the full Toda theory. On these slices, the scalar integrability conditions reduce to Liouville-like divisors and recover the corresponding Toda charge pole lattices.

authors.name: Jacques Distler, Bahaa Elshimy

papers.title: Antipodal Self-Duality for Generalized Fishnets from Integrability
papers.summary: Antipodal self-duality (ASD) is a remarkable property that relates an amplitude to itself, after performing a suitable kinematic map and reversing the letters of the symbol (more precisely, acting with the antipode of the Hopf algebra of the de Rham analogs of multiple polylogarithms). ASD has been seen in only one process in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory, and its physical origin is unknown, motivating a search for ASD in other contexts. Recently, ASD was found to hold for square fishnet integrals in a strongly-deformed version of planar $\mathcal{N}=4$. In this paper, we investigate the properties of polynomials in ladder integrals under the ASD transformation that leaves the square fishnet invariant. Our basic building blocks are determinants of certain matrices of ladder integrals, that are labeled by partitions or Young diagrams, and automatically obey the Steinmann relations. We employ integrability-based representations of such determinants, which are essentially matrix-model integrals, and the theory of symmetric polynomials to find many more ASD quantities -- linear combinations of determinants whose coefficients are expressed using the combinatorics of partitions. As a byproduct, we provide an alternate proof that square fishnet integrals obey ASD.

authors.name: Lance J. Dixon, Claude Duhr, Francesca C. Fernandes, Victor Mishnyakov

papers.title: Black Hole Entropy and Holographic Entanglement Entropy in DGP Brane Gravity
papers.summary: We investigate the relation between gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy in braneworld gravity with gravitational dynamics localized on the brane. We first consider the DGP brane model, in which an Einstein-Hilbert term is included in the brane action, and demonstrate that the gravitational entropy of a braneworld black hole agrees with the holographic entanglement entropy for general stationary spacetimes. We then generalize the brane-localized Einstein-Hilbert term to higher-curvature gravitational theories. For Lovelock gravity and $f(R)$ gravity on the brane, we derive the corresponding expressions for gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy and show that the two entropies also coincide for general stationary spacetimes. These results establish the equivalence between gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy in braneworld gravity for a broad class of gravitational theories and contribute to a deeper understanding of holography in braneworld settings.

authors.name: Takamasa Kanai

papers.title: Graviphoton mixing with KK modes in the 2D effective theory of charged black holes
papers.summary: We study the effects of massive Kaluza--Klein modes on the two-dimensional low-energy effective theory obtained by the $S^2$ reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory on a Reissner--Nordstr\"om black hole background. We retain the first excited ($l=1$) Maxwell Kaluza--Klein modes in addition to the massless sector. The background electric flux mixes the Maxwell Kaluza--Klein scalars with the graviphotons, and tree-level exchange of the massive scalars generates a correction to the graviphoton kinetic term proportional to the square of the black hole charge. Within the leading local approximation, we also perturbatively evaluate the one-loop correction to the graviphoton kinetic term and find no dependence on the black hole charge. We find that near extremality, the charge-dependent tree-level correction becomes parametrically comparable to the classical graviphoton kinetic term.

authors.name: Yoshihiko Abe, Tetsutaro Higaki, Yu Miyauchi

papers.title: What crossing symmetry forbids just above $c=1$
papers.summary: What does a unitary two-dimensional conformal field theory look like just above $c=1$? Using the numerical conformal bootstrap, we study the four-point function of a scalar Virasoro primary $\phi$ such that no primary lighter than $\phi$ appears in its operator product expansion with itself. Slightly above $c=1$, crossing symmetry excludes the interval $0.17\lesssim\Delta_\phi\lesssim1$, although the compact boson realizes every such $\Delta_\phi$ at $c=1$. Combining this exclusion with results from the modular bootstrap, we show that the lightest primary of a compact unitary conformal field theory at $c=1.0005$ or $1.001$ has dimension $\Delta_{\rm gap}<0.17$. Further from $c=1$, the largest excluded central charge at fixed $\Delta_\phi$ has two sharp minima near $\Delta_\phi=1/2$ and $4/7$. At these values it lies within $2\times10^{-7}$ of $c=8/7$, where the $\mathbb{Z}_5$ parafermion and its charge-conjugation orbifold have scalars of exactly these dimensions.

authors.name: Yu Nakayama

papers.title: Imaging the two-sided black hole interior with four-point correlators
papers.summary: We propose a boundary four-point function smeared with wavepackets, which probes local physics behind the horizon of a two-sided AdS black hole. At high frequencies, boundary wavepackets aimed at an interior bulk point travel along geodesics and scatter locally about the bulk point, factorizing the correlator into a flat-space like scattering amplitude. To obtain this configuration, we utilize a non-trivial time ordering of operators, and also use one state-dependent operator insertion moved halfway across the thermal circle. An interesting property of this observable is that it also probes features of nontrivial states: null shocks and matter shells behind the horizon show up as jumps in the observed signal as the bulk point crosses them, thereby imaging the black hole interior.

authors.name: Joydeep Chakravarty

papers.title: Superstars, quantum wormholes and von Neumann algebras
papers.summary: We entangle heavy 1/2-BPS states in two copies of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SU($N$) Super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. Each copy is separately dual to an extremal, supersymmetric, singular black hole geometry, in which the horizon coincides with a singularity. General ideas in the AdS/CFT correspondence suggest that the entanglement between the two copies should lead to some form of connectivity between the two geometries---a kind of wormhole. We use von Neumann algebra methods in the SYM theory to diagnose the possible existence of such wormholes.

authors.name: Vijay Balasubramanian, Ryo Nemoto, Masaki Shigemori

papers.title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
papers.summary: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation. We derive localization identities for these determinants which express their logarithmic derivatives with respect to the spectral parameter in terms of Baxter $Q-$functions evaluated at special points, proving previously conjectured relations. Our derivation uses finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of the underlying integral spectral operators. We identify a sufficient rational closure condition on the symbol of these operators that extends localization to a broader class of spectral problems and determines the evaluation points. Applications include generalized two-dimensional QCD with a quartic gauge-field potential and symbols interpolating between the QCD and Ising cases. We also give a general construction of the spectral operators and establish conditions for the finite-rank reduction on which localization relies.

authors.name: Bercel Boldis, Nikolay Gromov, Gregory P. Korchemsky, Alessandro Testa

papers.title: FLZ integrability in the 't Hooft model
papers.summary: We study the 't Hooft equation describing mesons in large-$N_c$ two-dimensional QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses. Using its Fredholm formulation and the associated Baxter finite-difference equation, we investigate the relations between spectral determinants and canonical Baxter $Q$-functions. We derive special-point identities for the Baxter solutions by exploiting finite-rank commutator relations of the underlying integral operators. We also determine the spectral residues of the inhomogeneous solutions and obtain exact expressions for eigenfunction normalization factors in terms of values at distinguished complex points. These results establish the unit-residue property of the Baxter expressions entering the Fateev-Lukyanov-Zamolodchikov (FLZ) spectral-determinant identities. As a further application, we prove the nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses. We further identify a broader class of integral operators exhibiting the same mechanism, which we refer to as FLZ integrability, and illustrate its applicability to the meson spectral problem in Ising field theory. Our approach reveals a connection between the analytic structure of Baxter equations and the theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators.

authors.name: Alexey Litvinov, Egor Shestopalov, Nikita Slavnov

papers.title: Higher Spin Lagrangians for Black Holes in Arbitrary Dimension
papers.summary: In this paper, we investigate the classical gravitational multipolar structure of rotating objects studying higher-spin Lagrangians coupled to gravity in arbitrary dimensions $D=d+1$. We first consider fields described by totally symmetric tensors with $s$ indices. At finite spin, the minimal coupling depends on both the spin and spacetime dimension. We show that, in the high-spin limit $s\gg 1$, the minimal multipolar expansion becomes dimension independent and it corresponds to the one which reproduces the Kerr solution in four dimensions. Furthermore, we identify a dimension independent relation among the non-minimal coupling coefficients that allows us to reproduce the Myers-Perry multipolar structure in arbitrary dimensions. We then extend our analysis to Lagrangians involving fields with different Young representations, which are allowed in higher dimensions.

authors.name: Francesco Campanella

papers.title: Investigating tidal heating in neutron stars via gravitational Raman scattering
papers.summary: We present a scattering amplitude formalism to study the tidal heating effects of nonspinning neutron stars incorporating both worldline effective field theory and relativistic stellar perturbation theory. In neutron stars, tidal heating arises from fluid viscosity due to various scattering processes in the interior. It also serves as a channel for the exchange of energy and angular momentum between the neutron star and its environment. In the interior of the neutron star, we first derive two master perturbation equations that capture fluid perturbations accurate to linear order in frequency. Remarkably, these equations receive no contribution from bulk viscosity due to a peculiar adiabatic incompressibility which arises in stellar fluid for non-barotropic perturbations. In the exterior, the metric perturbations reduce to the Regge-Wheeler (RW) equation which we solve using the analytical Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi (MST) method. We compute the amplitude for gravitational waves scattering off a neutron star, also known as gravitational Raman scattering. From the amplitude, we obtain expressions for the electric quadrupolar static Love number and the leading dissipation number to all orders in compactness. We then compute the leading dissipation number for various realistic equation-of-state(s) and estimate the change in the number of gravitational wave cycles due to tidal heating during inspiral in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) band. We find that the shear-viscous contribution is small. Even for cold ($T\sim 10^5$K) and weakly compact stars it changes the number of cycles by less than $10^{-2}$, about an order of magnitude below the other conservative 4PN contributions, and it decreases as $T^{-2}$ for hotter stars.

authors.name: M. V. S. Saketh, Zihan Zhou, Suprovo Ghosh, Jan Steinhoff, Debarati Chatterjee

papers.title: Worldvolume Hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm for group manifolds
papers.summary: The Worldvolume Hybrid Monte Carlo (WV-HMC) method [arXiv:2012.08468] is a reliable and versatile algorithm for addressing the numerical sign problem. It resolves the ergodicity issues commonly encountered in Lefschetz thimble-based approaches without requiring explicit evaluation of the Jacobian during configuration generation. In this paper, as a general framework for applying WV-HMC to lattice gauge theories, we extend the algorithm to systems defined on connected compact group manifolds. The key is to introduce a symplectic structure on the tangent bundle of the worldvolume and formulate molecular dynamics on it. The validity of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated using one-site $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ models for purely imaginary couplings.

authors.name: Masafumi Fukuma

papers.title: Parke-Taylor Varieties
papers.summary: Parke--Taylor functions are certain rational functions on the Grassmannian of lines encoding MHV amplitudes in particle physics. For $n$ particles there are $n!$ Parke--Taylor functions, corresponding to all orderings of the particles. Linear relations between these functions have been extensively studied in the last years. We here describe all non-linear polynomial relations between these functions in a simple combinatorial way and study the variety parametrized by them, called the Parke--Taylor variety. We show that the Parke--Taylor variety is equal to the log canonical embedding of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ into $\mathbb{P}^{(n-2)!-1}$ due to Keel and Tevelev by exhibiting a concrete linear isomorphism with the realization in coordinates based on Kapranov's map. We also show that the intersection with the algebraic torus recovers the open part, $\mathcal{M}_{0,n}$. We give an explicit description of this isomorphism. Unlike the realization of the log canonical embedding by using the iterated Kapranov's map, this Parke--Taylor embedding very explicitly respects the symmetry of the $n$ marked points and is constructed in a single-step procedure, avoiding the intermediate embedding into a product of projective spaces.

authors.name: Benjamin Hollering, Dmitrii Pavlov

papers.title: Quantum fields in a cold atomic simulator: relaxation and phase locking in tunnel-coupled 1D bosonic quasi-condensates
papers.summary: We consider a prime example of simulating interacting relativistic QFT with cold atoms: the realisation of the sine-Gordon model by tunnel-coupled quasi-1D Bose gases. While experiments have shown that it can realise the sine-Gordon model in equilibrium, studies of non-equilibrium dynamics have revealed phase-locking behaviour that contrasts with predictions from sine-Gordon field theory. Here, we examine a one-dimensional field-theoretic model of the system and find that the phase-locking behaviour can be understood in terms of the longitudinal harmonic trap, and that the additional degrees of freedom observed in the experiment do not appear to play a significant role. Therefore, the experimental setup provides a good simulator of the sine-Gordon quantum field theory, even out of equilibrium, if the inhomogeneous background induced by the trap is taken into account. Furthermore, our results support the idea that modifying the longitudinal trap to a box shape should result in agreement with standard sine-Gordon dynamics. The main remaining open issues are accounting for 3D corrections and modelling the effect of the boundaries.

authors.name: B. Fitos, G. Tak\'acs

papers.title: Exact general solutions for cosmological scalar field evolution in a vacuum-energy dominated expansion
papers.summary: We derive exact general solutions (as opposed to attractor particular solutions) for the evolution of a scalar field $\phi$ in a universe dominated by a background fluid with equation of state parameter $w_B = -1$, extending earlier work on exact solutions with $w_B > -1$. Straightfoward exact solutions exist when the evolution is described by a linear differential equation, corresponding to constant, linear, and quadratic potentials. In the nonlinear case, exact solutions are derived for $V = V_0\ln \phi$, $V = V_0 \phi^{1/2}$ and $V = V_0/\phi$, and the logarithmic potential also yields an exact first integral. These complicated parametric solutions are considerably less useful than those derived previously for a universe dominated by a barotropic fluid such as matter or radiation with $w_B > -1$. However, we generalize the slow-roll approximation and show that it applies to all sufficiently flat potentials in the case of a vacuum-dominated expansion, while it never applies when the universe is dominated by a background fluid with $w_B > -1$.

authors.name: Patrick Hu, Robert J. Scherrer

papers.title: Spiral Density Waves and Torque Balance in the Kerr Geometry
papers.summary: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in relativistic accretion discs are a key science target for the upcoming LISA mission. Existing models of disc-EMRI interactions typically rely on crude dynamical friction or Newtonian planetary migration prescriptions, which fail to capture the relativistic fluid response induced by the binary potential. In this work we address this gap by providing the relativistic calculation. We apply standard methods from self-force theory, black hole perturbation theory, and relativistic stellar perturbation theory to compute the relativistic analogue of the spiral density wave and torque-balance results underlying planetary migration. Specifically, we calculate the response of a perfect fluid disc to the perturbing potential of an EMRI, consistently incorporating pressure effects. Using a master enthalpy-like variable and linearised fluid theory, we present a set of proof-of-principle calculations that reconstruct the fluid perturbations and relativistic spiral arm structure for a range of spin values in the Kerr geometry. We derive a relativistic torque-balance equation that enables us to compute and compare local torques with the angular momentum advected through the disc, finding striking agreement when applied to our relativistic disc-EMRI solutions. This opens a promising route towards establishing torque-balance relations between integrated disc torques arising from fluid perturbations and the forces acting on EMRIs embedded in matter.

authors.name: Conor Dyson, Daniel J. D'Orazio

papers.title: Time irreversibility and entropy production in non-Hermitian Model A field theories
papers.summary: We develop a systematic framework to quantify irreversibility in scalar Model A field theories with a generic non-Hermitian term driving the dynamics. Using the stochastic path-integral formalism, we perform a controlled small-noise expansion, allowing the computation of the entropy production rate (EPR) and violations of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). We show that the local EPR is entirely determined by the anti-Hermitian part of the linearised Langevin equation. Around steady states, the non-Hermitian component produces linear corrections to FDT violations and contributes quadratically to the EPR. As an illustration of the applicability of our approach, we analyse a minimal non-Hermitian extension of the Ginzburg-Landau $\psi^4$ theory describing a non-reciprocal Ising model at coarse-grained scales, for which we obtain explicit expressions of the local EPR, showing that it localises at interfaces in non-uniform states. Our results provide a general characterisation of TRS breaking in non-Hermitian scalar field theories.

authors.name: Matthias Carosi, Ot Garc\'es, Adri\`a Garc\'es, Demian Levis

papers.title: Finite-density equation of state of hot QCD using the complex Langevin equation
papers.summary: We present the results of continuum-extrapolated lattice simulations of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) above the crossover temperature and for unprecedentedly high baryon densities at the physical point, employing the complex Langevin equation. In particular, we determine the QCD equation of state by computing the baryon density as well as the pressure as functions of the baryon chemical potential and the temperature. Potential issues with wrong convergence of complex Langevin dynamics are under control and we indeed find agreement with previous lattice studies working at smaller chemical potentials, as well as with perturbative hard-thermal-loop calculations at high temperatures.

authors.name: Michael Mandl, D\'enes Sexty, Daniel Unterhuber

papers.title: Quantum integrable matrix models of spinor Bose gases in one spatial dimension
papers.summary: Degenerate spinor Bose gases with repulsive density-density interaction and anti-ferromagnetic spin-spin coupling in one spatial dimension are shown to be described by a quantum integrable matrix extension of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger model, whose fundamental fields are described by an $m\,\times\,n$ matrix of bosonic field operators. The eigenstates of this model are constructed for arbitrarily sized matrix field operators by means of algebraic Bethe-ansatz techniques, and the corresponding Bethe equations governing the spectra of conserved quantities are derived. The approach thus generalizes previously chosen techniques to account for arbitrary spin multiplets and their spin-spin interaction. Focusing on the specific case of the $2\times2$ model, which is shown to correspond to a spin-$1$ Bose gas, a set of integral equations is derived, which describe its equilibrium thermodynamic properties. From these, the ground state phase diagram is computed both, numerically and analytically in the parameter plane spanned by the chemical potential and an external magnetic field. Furthermore, we establish a sufficient condition for interacting bosons in one dimension to obey the Pauli exclusion principle. In particular, we show that in the presence of paired bound states, no two quasiparticle rapidities can coincide, provided that the Lieb parameter satisfies $\gamma>4/3$.

authors.name: Hannes K\"oper, Thomas Gasenzer

papers.title: Cyclic source pairings for Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor spaces
papers.summary: We determine the stable source information carried by the gluing-groupoid algebra of the Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor double. Relative normal residues define supported analytic $K$-classes with specified normal orientations. For a smooth double along a closed submanifold, we compute the full geometric periodic cyclic homology as the parity sum of the compactly supported cohomologies of the ambient manifold and the doubled locus. In the physical model, $K_0\cong\Z^4$ and $HP_0\cong\C^4$, with both odd groups zero. Four explicit cocycles give integral $K$-coordinates and exhaust continuous periodic cyclic cohomology; every periodic cyclic pairing on supported source classes is therefore a linear combination of rank and degree. Finite moments recover $K$-valued normal profiles modulo integral common line twists. A first-jet criterion tests mixed-line triviality and identifies the residue with the torsion cokernel of a generically invertible second fundamental form for pullback quotients. The degree-one Euler modification and the diagonal Coulomb embedding have identical filtered $K$-profiles in every algebraic $SL_2$ representation, while their rank-two Ward connections are respectively indecomposable and split. We give the Euler connection and its transition between both root charts. An elementary holonomy realization shows that the inherited ambient and divisor transverse classes annihilate supported source classes. The relative degree pairing uses an additional choice of opposite defect orientations.

authors.name: Ioannis P. Zois

papers.title: Seven- and eight-loop critical exponents of the three-dimensional Ising model
papers.summary: We determine the critical exponents $\eta$, $\nu$, and the correction-to-scaling exponent $\omega$ of the three-dimensional Ising universality class by resumming the recently computed seven- and eight-loop renormalization-group series in the $\epsilon=4-d$ expansion [O.~Schnetz, \textit{Phys. Rev. D} \textbf{97}, 085018 (2018); O.~Schnetz, \textit{Phys. Rev. D} \textbf{107}, 036002 (2023)]. The resummation combines conformal mapping with a homographic transformation, while the resummation parameters are optimized according to two complementary criteria. This approach yields precise estimates of the critical exponents together with quantitative uncertainty estimates. We find that the error bar on $\eta$ decreases rapidly with increasing loop order, whereas this is the case neither for $\nu$ nor for $\omega$. Unexpectedly, although the estimated values are accurate in absolute terms, their slow convergence with the loop order leads to a slight but systematic tension with the conformal bootstrap estimates that are currently considered as the benchmark. We discuss several possible origins of this behavior and its implications for high-order resummations of perturbative renormalization-group series.

authors.name: D. Shapoval, Yu. Honchar, B. Delamotte, M. Dudka, Yu. Holovatch

papers.title: Sourced stationary Dirac bound states around Kerr black holes
papers.summary: Ultralight bosonic fields can form macroscopic clouds around rotating black holes, whereas the existence of analogous stationary fermionic configurations is constrained by their intrinsic spin. Here we study stationary bound states of massive Dirac fields supported by an external source on Kerr backgrounds, in the test-field approximation, with a kinematic extension to Kerr--Newman, they are not fermionic condensates in the many-body sense. By mapping the Kerr--Dirac system to a globally integrated sourced radial problem, we isolate the boundary constraints dictated by horizon causality. The angular sector shows that for $|m|=1/2$ the regular boundary branches prevent the field density from vanishing on the rotation axis, whereas modes with $|m|\ge3/2$ vanish there, the reconstructed Kerr density is only mildly oblate. Precisely at the kinematic synchronization locus, the Frobenius matrix of the Dirac operator is non-defective and devoid of logarithmic divergences. Regularity on the future horizon nevertheless selects the ingoing solution, and an exact radial flux identity shows that this solution carries a positive flux, which excludes source-free normalizable states at all frequencies. The exclusion of source-free synchronized states demonstrates that a black hole's capacity to support macroscopic stationary fields is governed not merely by superradiant kinematics, but by the interplay between horizon regularity and the positivity of the Dirac flux.

authors.name: Sen Guo, Peng-Yu Chen, Yi-Han Huang, Xin Li, Yu Liang, Kai Lin, Lin Wen, Li-Fang Li

papers.title: Shadow and Polarized Images of Schwarzschild-MOG Black Hole Illuminated by Thick Accretion Disk
papers.summary: Recent EHT polarimetric observations provide a powerful probe of near-horizon physics and modified gravity. We investigate the shadow and polarization images of a static Schwarzschild-MOG black hole illuminated by geometrically thick, optically thin accretion flows. Adopting a phenomenological model and the Hou disk model, and solving null geodesics and relativistic radiative transfer, we study how the MOG parameter, inclination angle, anisotropic synchrotron emission, and flow geometry affect the total intensity and linear polarization. It is found that the MOG parameter mainly enlarges and brightens higher-order photon rings and broadens the shadow, while the inclination angle breaks axial symmetry and enhances polarized emission inside the shadow. The Hou disk model suppresses off-equatorial radiative interference and localizes polarization signals within higher-order rings. Electric vector position angle (EVPA) patterns are mostly azimuthal but vary rapidly near lensed images. These results provide theoretical diagnostics for constraining MOG with EHT/ngEHT polarimetric observations.

authors.name: Cheng Hu, Huan Ye, Hong Lei, Zi-Chao Lin

papers.title: Attractors and initial-condition sensitivity in Horndeski cosmologies
papers.summary: We study whether nearby homogeneous cosmological histories approach or move away from the Genesis and contracting solutions. We also determine how an uncertainty in the scalar velocity at a later stage affects the inferred initial velocity. In the Genesis models, including the gravitational dynamics can substantially change this relation. We find that convergence of homogeneous solutions can occur even around backgrounds with unstable perturbations, and therefore attraction of the background is not sufficient to establish that a cosmological solution is physically viable. In the contracting model, one power-law solution attracts nearby trajectories, whereas another repels them. The strength of these effects depends on how the cosmological state is parametrized. Their evolution through the subsequent bounce is not considered here.

authors.name: Yulia A. Ageeva, Andrey K. Sharofeev

papers.title: Monopole catalysis with massive fermions: the fate of the twisted sector
papers.summary: In the massless limit a fermion scattering on the minimal $SU(5)$ monopole in the lowest partial wave produces an outgoing state with half-integer fermion number in every flavour. This state lives in a twisted sector of the Hilbert space and is now understood as an ordinary fermion attached to a topological line running back to the monopole. In the Standard Model fermion masses and confinement destroy the line at distances greater than the inverse mass scales, causing the twisted state to decay into physical asymptotic states with integer fermion numbers. We study this decay for an incoming lepton or quark of one generation. The cross-section in this partial wave saturates the unitarity bound, $\sigma=\pi/p^2$, and the energy of the outgoing state is shared among the four fermion flavours with a broad Dirichlet distribution, which sets the thresholds and the kinematics. Conservation laws allow exactly two decay channels for each incoming fermion, the helicity flip and its $(B+L)$-violating partner. For an incoming electron the $(B+L)$-violating channel is anti-nucleon synthesis, and we determine the branching ratios in two limits: the two channels are equally likely at high energy, and only the helicity flip remains at low energy, below the anti-nucleon threshold. In between we model the energy dependence. For a quark in a slow proton the $(B+L)$-violating channel is catalysed proton decay, which has no threshold and occurs with a probability close to one. Callan's statistical interpretation of the fractional state emerges in a sharper form: the state is not a superposition of two final states with equal weights, but a single state that decays into them with energy-dependent probabilities, equal only at high energy.

authors.name: Valentin V. Khoze

papers.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
papers.summary: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace, so that states are not described by density matrices in the algebra, and they have no pure normal states, such that the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

authors.name: Markus Fr\"ob, Albert Much

papers.title: Massless neutrinos in a left-right symmetric universe
papers.summary: This comment is a comment stimulated by the 1957 Goldhaber et al. experiment, that detected a massless left-handed electron neutrino with negative helicity. The standard description of this neutrino is by means of a Weyl spinor. It is shown below that this description is incomplete, and in fact one needs a massless Dirac spinor to comply with the requirements of quantum field theory. A Dirac spinor is composed of two Weyl spinors. This in turn raises the necessity to explain the fate of the right-handed electron neutrino, partner of the Goldhaber et al. experiment's one. A possible explanation for its invisibility is suggested here in terms of a left-right symmetric extension of the standard model.

authors.name: Loriano Bonora

papers.title: Flavor Alignment and Operator Sensitivity in a Left--Right Universal-Seesaw Model
papers.summary: We analyse the flavour structure and low-energy operator sensitivity of a parity-related doublet universal-seesaw model with an imposed lepton triality. Degenerate bare singlet masses permit a basis in which light-light tree neutral flavour transitions vanish; the physical heavy masses remain nondegenerate. We connect this alignment property to the axial and scalar differences measured by $B_{d,s}^0\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and reproduce the six-state charged-vector mixing amplitudes for five reference masses. The reference analysis identifies kaon CP violation as the more sensitive flavour probe. Historical kaon data disfavour the lower reference masses, while estimates suggest that dimuon and radiative $B$-decay effects are harder to resolve at present precision. These comparisons use the specified reference spectrum and historical inputs. We also compare charged and neutral resonance rates with published search benchmarks. The vacuum hierarchy entails a cancellation of about $5\times10^{-6}$ at $M_{W_R}=80\,\mathrm{TeV}$. The initially thermal Dirac-neutrino branch has a dataset-dependent extra-radiation tension, strengthened in an illustrative mass-dependent decoupling estimate. For dimuon decays we establish operator selection rules and sensitivity estimates. The numerical flavour results cover meson mixing and charged-vector dipoles. We give no dimuon branching-fraction prediction or global allowed region.

authors.name: Claudio Coriano, Paul H. Frampton

papers.title: Dark vector meson effects on composite dark matter
papers.summary: We extend previous studies of $\mathcal{G}$-parity-odd dark pion dark matter in a QCD-like $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$ gauge theory with electroweakly interacting dark quarks to include the effects of $\rho$ mesons. We show that vector mesons can substantially affect relic abundance calculations through resonant enhancement, significantly affecting the conditions required to reproduce the observed relic abundance. Electroweak interactions further induce mixing between the dark $\rho$ mesons and Standard Model gauge bosons, opening new decay channels for the dark $\rho$ and modifying the effective interactions of the dark pions. We recast existing ATLAS and CMS searches to constrain the model, and perform a collider phenomenology study targeting the future FCC-hh and muon colliders, focusing on the resonant enhancement of cross sections in the $e^+e^-$, $\mu^+\mu^-$, and $W^+W^-$ final states for the latter. We show that the FCC-hh could probe $\rho$ mesons whose mass is up to 40 TeV.

authors.name: Tomohiro Abe, Ryosuke Sato, Ozan Semin, Takumu Yamanaka

papers.title: Discovering Warped Extra Dimensions at Next Generation Dark Matter Detectors
papers.summary: The coming years will see what could be the final push in the search for WIMP dark matter (DM), with direct detection reaching into the neutrino fog and indirect detection reaching TeV-scale thermal relics. We study a class of models that these experiments could discover: DM emerging from a warped extra dimension. In the IR, these scenarios appear generically as a $Z'$-type portal. We show that DM with electroweak couplings and TeV scale masses remains viable and discoverable within such a bottom-up context. However, the models require a 20\% tuning between the DM and $Z'$ masses, a tuning that is relaxed if the DM and $Z'$ are strongly coupled and heavier ($\sim$$10$ TeV). In fact, it is the strongly-coupled $Z'$-type portal which is UV-completed by the framework of a warped extra-dimensional Grand Unified Theory (GUT), where DM stability is a spin-off of suppressing proton decay, resulting in a $\sim$$10$ TeV Kaluza-Klein (KK) scale. We identify a variant of this framework where all gauge fields except a baryon-number gauge boson have suppressed couplings to the DM; this model significantly suppresses the direct detection rate, but it remains discoverable through indirect detection. Further, to address the little hierarchy problem associated with $\sim$$10$ TeV KK scale, inspired by the Super-Composite Higgs, we augment our extra-dimensional GUT setup with supersymmetry. We show that this model also possesses a DM candidate, now with a weakly-coupled and $\sim$${\rm TeV}$ mass $Z'$ mediator. In all cases, a near-term discovery remains possible, for instance with the now online Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO), suggesting that our first hint of extra dimensions could emerge from the high-energy sky.

authors.name: Kaustubh Agashe, Abhishek Banerjee, Kushan Panchal, Nicholas L. Rodd

papers.title: Casimir Experiments as Spin-Force Detectors
papers.summary: Precision Casimir experiments enable highly sensitive probes of short range forces, but have thus far constrained only spin-independent interactions. We show that measurements between reversed polarizations of a magnetically compensated source enable direct searches of axion-mediated monopole-dipole forces. The spin force reverses sign, while the common Casimir, gravitational and electrostatic backgrounds broadly cancel. Compensated sources need no intervening shielding, allowing large probes at micrometer gaps. Casimir experiments could probe the couplings $g_p^e g_s^{N}$ and $g_p^e g_s^{e}$ at $\lambda\sim1-100~\mu{\rm m}$ orders of magnitude beyond existing laboratory searches.

authors.name: Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Hideo Iizuka

papers.title: Charge-resolved four-lepton probes of an $e\mu$-flavour-violating scalar at FCC-ee
papers.summary: We study a real neutral scalar $X$ with a single flavour-off-diagonal coupling $h_{e\mu}=h_{\mu e}\equiv h$. The coupling induces associated production, $e^+e^-\to e^\pm\mu^\mp X$, and the decay $X\to e^\pm\mu^\mp$. The resulting four-lepton final state separates into the charge-balanced channel $e^+e^-\mu^+\mu^-$ and the same-sign same-flavour channels $e^\pm e^\pm\mu^\mp\mu^\mp$. The charge-balanced channel receives a large prompt continuum background, while the same-sign category has a small estimated background under our benchmark assumptions. We analyse the two channels at FCC-ee for $\sqrt{s}=240~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $\mathcal{L}=10.8~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, including a detector simulation. The collider sensitivities are compared with the one-coupling constraints from the electron and muon magnetic moments, muonium--antimuonium conversion, and LEP dilepton data. At $m_X=146~\mathrm{GeV}$, motivated by the largest excess in the CMS $e\mu$ resonance search, the expected 95\% CL reach of the charge-balanced channel, including a 1\% background uncertainty, is $|h|\simeq 1.0 \times 10^{-2}$, while the same-sign channel reaches $|h|\simeq 1.7 \times 10^{-3}$, compared with the cesium-based electron-$g-2$ bound $|h|<1.46\times10^{-2}$. Both channels thus probe couplings below the present bound. The two signal rates are equal before selection; the difference in reach follows from the different backgrounds.

authors.name: Kuldeep Deka, Bharti Rawat, Tripurari Srivastava

papers.title: When heavy vectors meet top partners: HVTP, a unified framework for composite Higgs searches
papers.summary: Vector resonances and top partners are characteristic new states of composite Higgs models: they belong to the same strongly coupled sector, and partial compositeness ties their interactions to the mixings that generate the top mass. Experimental searches, however, usually treat them separately. We provide a common framework for both and release HVTP (Heavy Vectors and Top Partners), a public UFO model for MadGraph in which an electroweak triplet, a hypercharge vector and a colour octet couple to a custodial top-partner multiplet, with all couplings obtained from the exact diagonalisation of the mass matrices. The models and the inputs of our results are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24345218. We translate the latest LHC searches at 13 and 13.6 TeV into the parameter space of the model. In natural scenarios the top partners, which are directly tied to the Higgs mass and to the residual tuning, are lighter than the vector resonances; the vectors then decay mostly into partners and become broad: the standard searches lose much of their sensitivity, while the vectors produce partner pairs at rates that can exceed QCD production. For example, at our benchmark points, with partners near their present limits and an electroweak triplet at about 4 TeV, 73-83% of the triplet decays contain partners, and vector-mediated production reaches up to three times the QCD rate. At the HL-LHC this region can be probed by resonance searches extended to large widths and by partner-pair searches that include resonant production; the latter also reveal the partner spectrum. Composite Higgs models with a non-minimal coset generally also contain a pseudoscalar, which can alter the standard decays of the top partners; we include it in the extension HVTP_eta.

authors.name: Natascia Vignaroli

papers.title: Nuclear deep-inelastic scattering as a BSM probe via SMEFT
papers.summary: Searches for New Physics at the energy frontier have motivated theoretical development of model-independent methods to constrain interactions beyond the Standard Model (BSM) like the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), as well as associated phenomenological analyses. While these approaches are powerful, they are also afflicted by the large space of higher-dimensional operators and the challenge of possible degeneracies among these operators. To help ameliorate these difficulties, processes beyond those at hadron colliders, including deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), have been identified and studied for their ability to contribute added constraining power. In this work, we extend such investigations to charged-lepton DIS involving heavy nuclei, for which we explore the systematics of SMEFT effects for a series of representative cases. In particular, we point out that nuclear effects can reshuffle the luminosities governing partons entering SMEFT-corrected hard interactions, such that the nucleus can serve as an expanded laboratory to explore SMEFT effects complementary to free-nucleon DIS. In particular, we find that nuclear DIS possesses significant constraining power over flavor-isovector SMEFT operator combinations, with reduced nPDF dependence; similarly, improved control over nPDFs would further enhance the SMEFT reach of nuclear DIS observables. We explore projections for future (proposed) facilities like the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh, finding that improvements to nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) can further sharpen the reach of nuclear DIS.

authors.name: Supratim Das Bakshi, T. J. Hobbs, Brandon Kriesten

papers.title: Exotic Portals for Hadronic Processes: The Gluon-Gluon and Gluon-Quark Portals
papers.summary: In this work we explore all possible light exotic (LEX) particles which are accessible through the gluon-gluon ($g$-$g$) and gluon-quark ($g$-$q$) phenomenological portals up to effective dimension six. We present effective models for these new states, which are directly accessible through gluon and quark fusion processes, and which are guaranteed decays involving Standard Model (SM) quarks and gluons. We note many accessible states in particularly unusual SU(3)$_\text{c}$ representations, which contain large Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. We also include some interesting dimension seven operators with highly unusual features. We also consider all potential spin values for our LEX states, looking at Lorentz representations and color selection rules. In this, we find that states in various unusual Lorentz representations are accessible. We also find that certain operator types have restrictions on allowed color representations based on spin.

authors.name: Katherine Schwind, Linda M. Carpenter

papers.title: Quarkonium Energy Correlators in Proton-Proton Collisions: Analytic Calculation and Angular-Momentum Hierarchy
papers.summary: We present the first complete leading-order (LO) analytic calculation of the quarkonium energy correlator (QEC) in $pp$ collisions, for the color-singlet ${}^3S_1^{[1]}$ and the color-octet ${}^1S_0^{[8]}$, ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$, and ${}^3P_J^{[8]}$ channels of $J/\psi$ production. Instead of the high-$p_T$ fragmentation approximation, the calculation retains the full kinematics of the recoil parton, inverts the map from transverse momentum to the rest-frame angle in closed form, and is validated by \textsc{HELAC-onia} in shape and absolute normalization. We also give the analytic counterpart of the $p_T$-weighted variant of the correlator. The LO shape of each channel is organized by the total angular momentum $J$ of the $c\bar c$ pair, as a consequence of the tree-level selection rule that forbids two on-shell gluons from forming a $J=1$ state. This hierarchy is compressed in the central sPHENIX acceptance and exposed by the wider forward coverage at the LHC. In the distribution normalized to the total cross section, much though not all of the scale uncertainty cancels, leaving promising distinctions in the QEC shapes between different $J/\psi$ production channels. The discriminating power of the QEC can be further improved by next-to-leading-order calculations and by utilizing QECs in simultaneous fits with the $p_T$ spectrum and polarization measurements.

authors.name: June-Haak Ee, Christopher Lee, Bianka Me\c{c}aj, Hugo Pereira Da Costa, Bade Sayki

papers.title: Gluon GPDs from hard-exclusive electroproduction of heavy quarkonium at NLO
papers.summary: Gluon tomography of the nucleon through hard-exclusive electroproduction of $J/\psi$ has been one of the key motivations for Electron-Ion Collider. However, the next-to-leading order (NLO) perturbative QCD calculations available in the literature were performed either in the collinear factorization limit where the heavy-quark mass is neglected, or in heavy-quark limit where the heavy quarkonia are approximately point-like. We present a full next-to-leading order collinear factorization for the hard exclusive production of heavy mesons that retains the meson mass as well as full light-cone distribution amplitude. We compare the full NLO result with the special limits and estimate the errors due to potentially-large corrections from $\alpha_s(M)$ and $M^2/Q^2$ at this order.

authors.name: Yuxun Guo, Xiangdong Ji, Yao Ji, Feng Yuan

papers.title: Dijet photoproduction in ep and eA collision in POWHEG
papers.summary: We present the implementation of dijet photoproduction in electron-proton and electron-nucleus collisions in the POWHEG BOX V2 Monte Carlo event generator. The process is computed at next-to-leading order in QCD including both direct and resolved photon contributions and is consistently matched to parton showers using the POWHEG method. The implementation is validated by using POWHEG BOX V2 internal consistency checks as well as by comparing fixed-order results with SHERPA. We compare our predictions to dijet photoproduction data from DESY HERA I and II, finding good agreement within theoretical uncertainties, and provide predictions for both electron-proton and electron-gold collisions at the upcoming BNL EIC, illustrating its potential to further constrain both photon and nuclear parton distribution functions.

authors.name: Alexander Feike, Tom\'a\v{s} Je\v{z}o, Michael Klasen

papers.title: Thermodynamic constraints on warm inflation with the Standard Model
papers.summary: In warm inflation with the Standard Model (SM), an axion-like inflaton dissipates energy into the plasma through QCD sphaleron transitions. Current predictions assume a friction linear in the bias, defined as the free energy released per transition in units of the temperature. The friction, however, has only been simulated at moderate biases in pure SU(2) gauge theory. We show that, during slow roll, energy conservation, the axial anomaly and thermodynamics relate the bias to the quark chemical potentials generated by the transitions, independently of the form of the friction and of the reaction network in the plasma. A bias within the simulated range requires chemical potentials a few times the temperature, which typically lead to Higgs condensation. Conversely, small chemical potentials imply a large bias and, unless the dissipation is very weak, a temperature far above the axion decay constant, which requires a cutoff of the effective description above that temperature. We illustrate that deviations from linearity beyond the simulated range can change the inflationary dynamics qualitatively, so that reliable predictions require a real-time computation of the friction and the noise in QCD at large bias. With high-scale lepton-number violation, the quark chemical potentials also source a $B-L$ asymmetry that exceeds the observed value by many orders of magnitude already during inflation. Finally, we show that the same relation between the bias and the chemical potentials holds for derivative couplings of the inflaton to SM currents. Unless the dissipation is very weak, warm inflation driven by such couplings therefore requires either a temperature far above the decay constant or chemical potentials that typically lead to Higgs condensation.

authors.name: Martin A. Mojahed

papers.title: On the effective atmospheric-scale $\Delta m^2$ in neutrino oscillation
papers.summary: We discuss an effective two-frequency description of the three-generation neutrino oscillation with the key quantity $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$, which unifies the effects of atmospheric-scale $\Delta m^2_{31}$-$\Delta m^2_{32}$ driven oscillations. As a solution to the minimization problem in vacuum, Nunokawa {\it et al.} obtained $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} } = \Delta m^2_{31} - (2E / L) \arctan \left\{ r_{2} \sin 2\Delta_{21} / ( r_{1} + r_{2} \cos 2\Delta_{21} ) \right\}$, where $\Delta_{21} \equiv \Delta m^2_{21} L / (4 E)$ and $r_{i}$ are the mixing-angle dependent constants. Despite the skepticism for the $L/E$ dependence in this formula, we show, in fact, that this is an exact expression, which renders the probability formula also exact. We offer an appealing-to-intuition physical explanation for the $L/E$ dependence that it originates from the nature-designed three generation neutrinos. The way it is buried into $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$ is through the solar-effect renormalization to this quantity. With the physical interpretation of $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$ at hand, we aim at resolving the existing controversies on $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$ in this paper.

authors.name: Hisakazu Minakata

papers.title: Description of the decay $\phi \to \pi^+\pi^-$ in the NJL chiral quark model
papers.summary: The doubly suppressed decay $\phi \to \pi^+\pi^-$ is described in the chiral NJL quark model. This decay occurs in violation of the OZI rule and isotopic invariance. Two possible channels are considered. The first channel involves $\phi-\omega$ mixing and the subsequent decay of $\omega \to \pi^+\pi^-$. In the second channel, the decay occurs via an intermediate $\rho$ meson.

authors.name: M. K. Volkov, A. A. Pivovarov, K. Nurlan

papers.title: Two-loop QCD amplitudes for $pp\to\gamma\gamma$ with a top-quark loop
papers.summary: We revisit the computation of two-loop QCD amplitudes for diphoton production in the quark- and gluon-initiated channels, focusing on contributions involving a closed top-quark loop. We derive analytic expressions for the finite remainders in terms of a set of special functions constructed from the $\epsilon$-expanded components of master integrals. We employ a canonical basis of master integrals for the polylogarithmic sectors, while retaining a noncanonical basis for the elliptic sectors. The analytic cancellation of ultraviolet and infrared poles is established by deriving relations among master integral components. Relations among polylogarithmic components are derived numerically from their differential equations and we utilise a set of finite Feynman integrals, constructed using local numerator insertions and constraints from soft and collinear limits, to derive relations between pole-contributing elliptic master integral components and the polylogarithmic ones. The construction does not rely on a particular choice of noncanonical elliptic master integral basis. The resulting set of special functions is minimal in the polylogarithmic sectors, whereas the elliptic components contributing to the finite part of the amplitudes are potentially overcomplete. The special functions are evaluated numerically by solving systems of differential equations, enabling their computation across the physical phase space. We present a C++ implementation of the corresponding hard functions, suitable for on-the-fly numerical evaluation in cross-section calculations.

authors.name: Souvik Bera, Heribertus Bayu Hartanto

papers.title: Azimuthal Correlations of Heavy-Quark Pairs in Ultraperipheral Collisions
papers.summary: We study azimuthal correlations of $D\bar D$ and $B\bar B$ pairs in Xn0n-selected Pb--Pb ultraperipheral collisions at $\sqrt{s}=5.36~\mathrm{TeV}$. The selection requires neutron emission from the target nucleus and no neutron emission from the photon source. The unpolarized and linearly polarized Weizs\"acker--Williams gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distributions are modeled in the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework and evolved to the hard scale. We keep the full mass dependence of the Born coefficients and the one-gluon soft current. The photon flux includes the neutron selection and is averaged over the target area. We present the transverse-momentum and rapidity dependence of the $\cos(2\phi_h)$ and $\cos(4\phi_h)$ asymmetries. Over the ranges studied, both moments increase with the pair total transverse momentum and decrease with its relative transverse momentum. For the lowest relative transverse momentum interval considered, the $D\bar D$ moments are larger than those for $B\bar B$. In the kinematic region considered, the $\cos(2\phi_h)$ asymmetry is much larger than the $\cos(4\phi_h)$ asymmetry, and the contribution from gluon linear polarization is small compared with the total angular modulation.

authors.name: Qiong Huang, Jing Zhao, Tianbo Liu, Ya-jin Zhou

papers.title: The impact of phase transitions on dilepton production
papers.summary: We calculate dielectron yields at beam energies relevant for the CBM experiment at FAIR and the STAR Beam Energy Scan. The production of intermediate mass dielectrons is expected to increase in presence of a phase transition due to the latent heat. In this work, we use the SMASH+vHLLE hybrid model to quantify this enhancement in two scenarios: with a toy equation of state consisting of the Bag Model and Hadron Resonance Gas, separated by a Maxwell-constructed transition; and with a more realistic equation of state containing a critical endpoint, based on the 3D Ising universality class. We confirm that the dilepton yield increases when the system passes through a first-order phase transition, by about 7% in the realistic scenario.

authors.name: Renan G\'oes-Hirayama, Hannah Elfner

papers.title: Parton Branching evolution in updfevolv: NNLO spacelike evolution in the ZM-VFNS and NLO timelike evolution with heavy-flavour matching
papers.summary: We describe two extensions of the Parton Branching (PB) method as implemented in updfevolv: the next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) spacelike DGLAP evolution of parton densities in the zero-mass variable-flavour-number scheme (ZM-VFNS), and the leading and next-to-leading order (LO, NLO) timelike evolution of fragmentation functions, including the heavy-flavour matching conditions at the quark thresholds. We summarise the timelike PB formalism - momentum sum rule, Sudakov form factor, branching chain and kinematics. We give implementation details needed for the PB formalism to reproduce the semi-analytical solutions of APFEL for all flavours, including heavy quarks at threshold. This note supplements the updfevolv manual and is a technical release note for updfevolv version 2.6.0.

authors.name: H. Jung

papers.title: A Gauge Pathway to an Ultralight Axion through a Hidden Portal
papers.summary: We study a gauge realization of an ultralight axion with a hidden $SU(2)$ interaction, an Abelian vector portal, a charged Higgs and a St\"uckelberg field. The vector absorbs one scalar combination and leaves a physical phase. Its normalization is fixed by the Higgs and St\"uckelberg scales, while hidden confinement generates its mass. Keeping this phase ultralight requires an additional symmetry: the displayed gauge charges alone allow large phase-dependent scalar interactions. We quantify the suppression required of these interactions. Pure-$SU(2)$ lattice results relate the susceptibility to physical confinement scales; one- and two-loop running illustrate the dependence on the chosen high-energy coupling.
