We derive the coherent radiation-era density and exhibit an initial angle giving the reference dark-matter abundance for $F_\chi\simeq10^{17}\,\GeV$ and zero-temperature mass $m_{\chi,0}=3\times10^{-20}\,\eV$. We follow the confined population through number-changing and number-conserving limits and bound its energy contribution. An illustrative inflaton background satisfies the stated vacuum and isocurvature tests, conditional on control of a large portal correction to its potential. Its cold hidden history requires a hidden-to-visible reheating fraction near $5\times10^{-12}$, whose microscopic origin remains an input. A second, gauge-anomaly-free model gives the same physical phase scale using two charged Higgs singlets. These constructions specify conditional cosmological examples and the additional protection and reheating mechanisms needed to complete them.

authors.name: Claudio Corian\o`

papers.title: Z boson production in lead-lead collisions: An investigation Utilizing MRW nuclear TMDs
papers.summary: We investigate $Z$-boson production in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$ within the $k_t$-factorization framework, using four nuclear transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution (TMD) prescriptions, namely LO-MRW, VO-MRW, MVO-MRW, and MKMRW. The aim of this study is to examine how different ordering conditions and normalization treatments influence the theoretical description of this process. We calculate the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions using the parton-level KaTie event generator and compare the predictions with CMS measurements and collinear NLO calculations. This comparison allows us to assess the sensitivity of the predicted distributions to the choice of UPDF prescription.

authors.name: S. Rezaie, R. Kord Valeshabadi, K. Azizi

papers.title: TeV Gamma-Ray Transparency Bounds on Neutrinos and Axions
papers.summary: Multi-TeV gamma rays propagating over cosmological distances measure the extragalactic background light (EBL) through attenuation by electron--positron pair production. This is particularly valuable in the infrared, where the EBL is difficult to measure directly. Since the growing sample of observed multi-TeV photons provides tight constraints on the EBL photon intensity, this, in turn, constrains new particles that radiatively decay into meV--eV photons. We set the first TeV-transparency bounds on active-neutrino electromagnetic transition moments, obtain new constraints on radiatively decaying sterile neutrinos, and derive competitive limits on the axion--photon coupling.

authors.name: Shengyi Liu, Hyeonseok Seong, Chen Sun, Seokhoon Yun

papers.title: Dark Matter Assisted Axion-Magnetic Resonance
papers.summary: An oscillating axion dark matter (DM) background can enhance the conversion of another relativistic axion into photons when traversing a magnetic field. The DM background rotates photon polarization relative the magnetic orientation, which compensates the photon's and the propagating axion's dispersion relation mismatch. We relate this mechanism to Axion Magnetic Resonance (AMR) and apply it to stellar axions in the starburst galaxy M82. We analyze its enhancement to the resulting X-ray signals while accounting for the finite magnetic domain size, dark matter coherence length, DM density morphology, plasma profiles, and the detector response. We derive strong constraints using existing X-ray data from NuSTAR. We show that this resonant conversion can lead to $\mathcal O(10^2)$ enhancement in the photon-axion conversion probability, improving the upper limits on axion's photon coupling over part of the mass range where ordinary conversion is suppressed. We also show that this type of resonance predicts distinctive features in the hard X-ray spectrum, which is moderately favored by the data over the background only model, yet it is currently still consistent with statistical fluctuations.

authors.name: Chen Sun, Si-Yu Wu, Seokhoon Yun

papers.title: Multi-Component Axion Dark Matter Revisited and the Role of Ultralight ALPs
papers.summary: In this work, we revisit the multi-component axion dark matter (DM) scenario and explore the role of ultralight axion-like particles (ALPs). After briefly reviewing maximal axion mixing, we incorporate a stochastic axion mixing mechanism that generalizes it by relaxing the requirement of a uniform hierarchy among the axion decay constants. We find that, depending on the parameters, either the QCD axion or an ALP can dominate the DM abundance after mixing; once axion mass contributions are included, the heaviest ALPs tend to prevail. In a two-component framework, stochastic mixing significantly enlarges the allowed parameter space for the QCD axion decay constant, enabling the QCD axion to constitute the entirety of cold DM. The corresponding ALP mass range remains largely unconstrained by current experiments and is within reach of future searches. In the multi-component case, a larger ALP population leads to the emergence of more ultralight ALPs with large decay constants. These ultralight ALPs represent compelling targets for upcoming axion searches.

authors.name: Hai-Jun Li

papers.title: The relativistic BCS-BEC crossover in closed form: the cutoff as an effective range
papers.summary: At zero temperature the mean-field potential of a Dirac fermion with a pairing gap contains one momentum integral, that of the sum of its two quasiparticle levels. We evaluate it in closed form from a geometric construction: the two levels are distances in a plane, and the momentum line is a finite arc of a fixed ellipse, along which the charge, the scalar density and the pair amplitude, summed over the modes, are combinations of Legendre's three elliptic integrals. As the upper limit of the momentum grows, the integral grows by a quartic term, a quadratic term and a logarithm with a known coefficient. The two powers are absorbed into a constant and into the coupling, and with all momenta integrated what remains is a finite combination of Legendre's integrals and the logarithm of one scale $\lambda$. The gap equation and the density of the relativistic BCS-BEC crossover follow in closed form. Once the coupling has been traded for the scattering length, $\lambda$ takes the place of the cutoff that the literature keeps as a third parameter. We show that it fixes the effective range of the channel of the pair: for a pair of Dirac fermions of mass $m$ with the pairing vertex $\gamma_5$, $r_e=-(4/\pi m)[\ln(2\lambda/m)-1]$. At low density and a fixed $k_Fr_e$ the crossover is that of the two-channel model of a Feshbach resonance with the same scattering length and effective range. In the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model the pion decay constant fixes $\lambda$, the effective range of the pion channel is $-8\pi f_\pi^{2}/(N_cM^{3})$, and the constituent mass $M$ of the quark is the one parameter that remains free.

authors.name: T. G. Khunjua

papers.title: Boosted energy-energy correlators in the small-acoplanarity limit
papers.summary: We study the energy-energy correlator in the hadronic decay of a boosted boson. We focus on the small-acoplanarity region, where the two hadron momenta are nearly back-to-back in the plane transverse to the boson momentum. We derive a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization formula for electroweak and Higgs bosons in this region, expressed directly in boosted-frame variables in terms of hard, soft, and jet functions with a one-dimensional recoil measurement. We verify its singular real-emission terms at next-to-leading order and present resummed predictions up to N$^3$LL for asymmetric $e^+e^-$ colliders. For vector bosons, the azimuthal orientation of the hadron pair about the boost axis is sensitive to the transverse-spin correlation of the produced quarks through the Collins fragmentation function. We study this sensitivity for photon-tagged $Z$ bosons in $e^+e^-\to Z\gamma$ and compare our predictions with simulations using PYTHIA 8 supplemented by StringSpinner.

authors.name: Benjamin Jobilal, Zhong-Bo Kang, Diego Padilla

papers.title: The Sensitivity of Higgs Factories to the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model via Precision Measurements
papers.summary: Precision measurements of Higgs boson couplings at future Higgs factories provide an indirect probe of new particles at mass scales beyond the reach of the high luminosity run of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC). We study this sensitivity in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM), focusing on radiative corrections to the third-generation Yukawa couplings. In particular, supersymmetric threshold corrections to the bottom Yukawa coupling and, in a smaller parameter region, to the tau Yukawa coupling, can remain significant even for multi-TeV superpartner masses. We perform a numerical survey of the MSSM parameter space, using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo, in order to identify models consistent with a 125 GeV Higgs boson and exhibiting potentially observable Higgs-coupling deviations. We find that precision measurements of the bottom Yukawa coupling can probe heavy Higgs masses of order 2-3 TeV and retain sensitivity to gluinos, Higgsinos, and bottom squarks with masses above 5 TeV. The corresponding sensitivity in the {\tau} Yukawa coupling is also present but more limited in parameter space. These results illustrate the characteristic pattern of Higgs-coupling deviations predicted by the MSSM. They demonstrate that precision Higgs measurements can provide sensitivity to supersymmetric physics well beyond the expected direct-search reach of the HL-LHC.

authors.name: Kamal Maayergi, Devin G. E. Walker, Michael Fagundes-Rocha, Michael E. Peskin

papers.title: Triple-Higgs production: a window on the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive study of triple-Higgs production within the $\kappa$-framework as a probe of the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings. At leading order, we derive compact parametrisations of the inclusive $gg\to3h$ cross section in terms of the trilinear and quartic Higgs self-coupling modifiers $\kappa_3$ and $\kappa_4$, the top-quark Yukawa coupling modifier $\kappa_t$, and the anomalous two-top-two-Higgs and two-top-three-Higgs coupling modifiers $\kappa_{2t}$ and $\kappa_{3t}$. These parametrisations allow for a fast and accurate interpretation of current and future LHC measurements. Applying them to LHC Run 2 data and high-luminosity LHC projections, we quantify the impact of $\kappa_t$, $\kappa_{2t}$, and $\kappa_{3t}$ on the constraints on $\kappa_3$ and $\kappa_4$, and derive the first direct constraint on $\kappa_{3t}$ from existing LHC data. We further show that parameter points yielding nearly identical inclusive rates can give rise to different kinematic distributions, demonstrating the potential of differential measurements to resolve degeneracies and enhance the sensitivity of future triple-Higgs searches.

authors.name: John M. Campbell, Giuseppe De Laurentis, R. Keith Ellis, Michelle Gensmann, Ulrich Haisch, Luca Panizzi, Andreas Papaefstathiou, Gilberto Tetlalmatzi-Xolocotzi

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Moduli Stabilization with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ Modular Symmetry
papers.summary: We study the stabilization of the three complex moduli associated with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ modular symmetry by gaugino condensation in $\mathcal N=1$ supergravity models from heterotic string theory, where one-loop threshold corrections fix both the modular weight and the singularity structure of the superpotential. We determine, for each threshold class, the complete parametrization of the consistent superpotential relying on Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ basic modular-invariant ratios and their syzygies, generalizing the insufficient SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$-inspired techniques based solely on polynomials of its absolute invariants. This structure supports a rich landscape of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua. Unlike in the SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$ case, higher-order zeros produce continuous surfaces and curves of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua, while, among the six isolated fixed points, only those with $S_4$ and $D_{12}$ residual symmetries can stabilize all three moduli. We also construct isolated vacua away from fixed points, some of which lie at the moduli values preferred by genus-two modular flavor fits, and examine the suppression of the geometric moduli masses near an enhanced-symmetry point.

authors.name: Miguel Hernandez-Segura, Xiang-Gan Liu, Hans Peter Nilles, Saul Ramos-Sanchez

papers.title: Enhanced spatial resolution and performance for N-body simulation of self-interacting dark matter
papers.summary: Studying the implications of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) on astrophysical objects often requires simulations. N-body simulations are a standard tool but face a few challenges. One is resolving the mean free path in gravothermally collapsing halos. This is necessary to obtain accurate results and is achieved in state-of-the-art simulations by increasing the number of resolution elements. I aim to formulate a numerical scheme that gives an enhanced spatial resolution compared to those methods and allows increasing the resolution without changing the number of resolution elements. The novel scheme that I present is formulated by discarding the classic approach of using kernel functions and computing interaction probabilities. Instead, pairs of particles always interact if their distance is below a specific threshold. Importantly, this distance threshold depends on their relative velocity and the size of the time step. This new formulation no longer requires some of the computations in state-of-the-art schemes and thus helps to increase the performance. Through a variety of test problems with known solutions, I study the accuracy of the new scheme and demonstrate its advantages over state-of-the-art SIDM formulations. Notably, the scheme reduced the computational costs, making the SIDM computations typically much cheaper than gravity. As a consequence, a typical SIDM simulation of isotropic scattering requires only a few percent of its total computational cost for the self-interactions. In conclusion, the new scheme presents an improvement over previous schemes and helps to address current challenges. Besides the enhanced performance, it allows us to achieve a higher accuracy when simulating gravothermally collapsing SIDM halos.

authors.name: Moritz S. Fischer

papers.title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
papers.summary: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum. The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution. The two mesons exhibit qualitatively different light-cone structure, dictated by charge conjugation. The vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA, whose vanishing zeroth moment requires a normalization through its first moment. The decay constants obtained from local matrix elements and from the moments of the LCDAs agree, and approach predictions from nonrelativistic model as the fermion mass increases. For the relatively large masses considered in this work, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, showing that the mesons are dominated by their valence component. Our results demonstrate tensor networks as a practical route to light-cone distributions of ground-state as well as excited hadrons in low-dimensional gauge theories.

authors.name: Juan Hormaza, Wenyang Qian

papers.title: Softer charged-hadron spectra in Ne+Ne than in O+O collisions at the same multiplicity at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV
papers.summary: Charged-hadron spectra measured by the ATLAS Collaboration in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV are compared at the same charged-particle multiplicity instead of at the same centrality, to test whether the shape of the transverse-momentum spectrum at a given multiplicity depends on the size of the colliding system. At equal multiplicity, Ne+Ne collisions have a lower mean transverse momentum $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ than O+O collisions. Without any spectral fit, the published $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ values give a Ne+Ne/O+O ratio of 0.9822 at 3-4% centrality, 6.6 standard deviations below unity even if the O+O systematic uncertainties are taken as uncorrelated between centrality classes. At $0.4 < p_{\rm T} < 2$ GeV the Ne+Ne spectrum is described by the O+O spectrum with the transverse-momentum axis compressed by a single stretch factor, $\lambda_{\rm Ne/O} = 0.969$ in the 3-4% class. It lies 9.5 or 3.3 standard deviations below unity, depending on whether the common part of the O+O systematic uncertainties cancels between centrality classes. This ordering is expected if Ne+Ne collisions have a larger transverse area at the same multiplicity and a larger area gives a softer spectrum. The softening decreases towards peripheral collisions and is the same at forward pseudorapidity. In central collisions the spectral shape follows the centrality class more closely than the multiplicity. The same procedure is tested in Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions.

authors.name: Kishora Nayak

papers.title: Multiscale Zoom-in Lattice Simulation for Inflation
papers.summary: Lattice simulations are a powerful tool for studying the nonlinear evolution of inflationary fluctuations. The exponential expansion, however, makes it challenging to cover a broad range of scales relevant for the dynamics, limiting how many e-folds a single fixed grid can follow. We develop a three-dimensional zoom-in lattice method to follow inflationary fluctuations over a broad range of scales from the adiabatic subhorizon regime through horizon crossing. Every few e-folds, the grid is refined into one or more subgrids, with small-scale power injected and large-scale fluctuations inherited from previous generations. Each zoom shifts the resolved band while keeping its dynamic range fixed. This extends the duration over which lattice simulations can follow inflationary fluctuations from a few e-folds to tens of e-folds. In a Starobinsky benchmark evolved for 50 e-folds, the curvature power spectrum agrees with linear theory. In a model with an oscillatory feature, the zoom-in simulations recover the peak seen in a high-resolution fixed-grid run and show scale-dependent non-Gaussianity.

authors.name: Xinpeng Wang, Angelo Caravano, Leander Thiele, Misao Sasaki

papers.title: Helicity Amplitudes and Quantum Entanglement Analysis in Fully Charm Tetraquark Decays into Double Vector Charmonia or Charmed Mesons
papers.summary: We study helicity amplitudes for the fully charm tetraquark states decays into vector meson pair from single gluon exchange contribution. The decay angular distributions have been given by the cascade decays $T_{4c}\to J/\psi(D_{(s)}^*)+J/\psi(\bar{D}_{(s)}^*)$ along with $J/\psi\to \mu^++\mu^-$ or $D_{(s)}^*\to D_{(s)}+\pi$, showing that spin-0 and spin-2 states can be distinguished. We also find that the spin-0 state decay to vector meson pair exhibits a higher degree of quantum entanglement than that in spin-2 state decays. These findings will help distinguish among different spin-parity states in experiment and explore possible as-yet-undiscovered hadronic structures, thereby shedding light on the internal properties of the double-$J/\psi$ exotic states discovered at the LHC.

authors.name: Kaiwen Chen, Feng-Xiao Liu, Qiang Zhao, Xian-Hui Zhong, Ruilin Zhu, Bing-Song Zou

papers.title: Towards a general subtraction formula for NNLO QCD corrections to processes at hadron colliders: final states with quarks and gluons
papers.summary: We describe the calculation of integrated subtraction terms in the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme for hadron collider processes with quarks and gluons, thereby extending the results presented in Ref.$~$[1]. Although this extension eventually proves to be straightforward, it requires a more careful treatment of certain collinear limits to achieve a compact and physically-transparent final result. We also show that the cancellation of infrared divergences can be organized in such a way that, once soft contributions are removed, it occurs independently for each of the external partons. We consider these results to be important stepping stones on the way to deriving finite remainders of the integrated subtraction terms for fully-general hadron collider processes in the context of the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme.

authors.name: Federica Devoto, Kirill Melnikov, Raoul R\"ontsch, Chiara Signorile-Signorile, Davide Maria Tagliabue, Matteo Tresoldi

papers.title: Thermal Fermion Propagators and Diagonal HTL Effective Action in the Early Universe
papers.summary: Within the minimally extended Standard Model (MESM), with Dirac neutrinos, we study fermion propagation in the electroweak-symmetric plasma, where the Higgs expectation value vanishes. We show that the zero-temperature mass eigenstates do not coincide with the left-handed fermionic quasiparticles identified by the thermal medium, while the right-handed fermions remain diagonal in this basis. At the leading hard-thermal-loop (HTL) order, the left-handed fermion self-energies form flavor matrices containing the CKM and PMNS mixing structures. Diagonalizing flavor matrices, we show that the two members of each left-handed weak doublet possess identical leading-HTL thermal spectra. The eigenvalues are CP-even and are invariant under weak-basis transformations. In this symmetric-phase thermal basis, the leading HTL fermion propagators and electroweak gauge interactions are diagonal, while the flavor structure is transferred to the Yukawa interactions. We further express the HTL effective Lagrangian in this basis, derive the corresponding dispersion relations, and numerically compare the eigenvalues of the complete leading-HTL matrices with the diagonal thermal coefficients obtained in the broken-phase mass basis. This construction provides a diagonal HTL description of fermionic quasiparticles and a systematic framework for resummation and higher-order corrections in the electroweak-symmetric plasma.

authors.name: A. Hataei, S. S. Gousheh

papers.title: An anomaly-free leptophilic $U(1)'_{\ell}$ completion of the Standard Model
papers.summary: We investigate an anomaly-free, family-universal leptophilic $U(1)'_{\ell}$ extension of the Standard Model (SM), in which quarks are neutral under the new gauge symmetry and mixed gauge anomalies are canceled by an SM-vector-like exotic lepton family. A complex singlet scalar breaks $U(1)'_{\ell}$, generating the new gauge-boson mass and contributions to the exotic fermion masses. The residual $Z_6$ gauge symmetry contains a $Z_2$ subgroup protecting the lightest exotic fermion. The specified field content permits Dirac but forbids Majorana masses for ordinary neutrinos, while the exotic neutral sector contains four mixed Majorana states. We calculate the exotic fermion spectrum and tree-level $Z_\ell$ decay widths. For $M_{Z_\ell}=900$ GeV and $g_{\rm eff}=0.10$, opening neutral Majorana-pair channels reduces the combined charged-lepton branching fraction by approximately 10.3% in the first benchmark. A restricted 5041-point scan over two neutral-sector mixing parameters yields reductions of 5.6%--10.8%. Using leading-order CalcHEP calculations, we investigate the resonance signatures in $\mu^+\mu^-\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and $\mu^+\mu^-\to e^+e^-$. At $\sqrt{s}=900$ GeV, the exotic decay channels suppress the visible resonance cross sections by approximately 19.6% and 20.9% for the two benchmarks, respectively. The absolute differential cross sections exhibit similar suppression, while the normalized angular distributions remain nearly unchanged. We also discuss radiatively generated gauge-kinetic mixing, complementary precision observables, and renormalization-group consistency. These results establish a quantitative connection between the anomaly-canceling exotic fermion spectrum and visible leptonic resonance signals, without constituting experimental exclusion limits.

authors.name: Seyit Okan Kara

papers.title: Trilepton Selection and Kinematic Sensitivity for Multiple Weak-Boson Production at Hadron Colliders
papers.summary: We present a detector-level fast-simulation study of the charge-specific processes $pp\to W^+W^-W^+$ and $pp\to W^+W^-W^-$ in the trilepton channel at 8, 14, 27, and 100 TeV. Separate signal regions require exactly three isolated electrons or muons with net charge $+1$ or $-1$, respectively, together with ordered lepton transverse-momentum thresholds, a same-flavour opposite-sign $Z$ veto, missing transverse momentum, and restricted jet multiplicity. For the $W^+W^-W^+$ hypothesis, the expected signal/background yields at reference luminosities of 20 fb$^{-1}$, 3 ab$^{-1}$, 15 ab$^{-1}$, and 20 ab$^{-1}$ are $(1.27,0.186)$, $(180,40.7)$, $(2.81\times10^3,784)$, and $(1.09\times10^4,3.79\times10^3)$, with conditional Asimov significances of 1.84, 7.70, 8.62, and 6.31. For $W^+W^-W^-$, the corresponding signal efficiencies range from $9.0\times10^{-4}$ to $2.95\times10^{-3}$ and the nominal significances are 1.19, 8.02, 8.13, and 6.03. The inclusive charge-channel asymmetry decreases from 0.351 at 8 TeV to 0.166 at 100 TeV; its quoted uncertainty is limited to numerical cross-section integration errors. Exploratory likelihood, neural-network, and boosted-tree classifiers show no stable improvement over rectangular cuts. The projections are conditional on the supplied simulated samples and uncertainty model; important backgrounds and comprehensive detector and theory uncertainties are not included.

authors.name: Ijaz Ahmed, Jamil Muhammad, M. S. Amjad, M. T. Javaid, Farzana Ahmad

papers.title: Impact of a hot local CP-odd domain with chirality imbalance on the QCD-biased axionic domain-wall interpretation of NANOGrav 15-year data
papers.summary: We investigate the influence of the chirality imbalance with local CP-breaking in hot QCD on the generation of a stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) sourced by the axion-like particle (ALP) domain-wall annihilation, induced by the QCD bias $\Delta V$. Such a bias at finite $\theta$ angle, chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$, and temperature $T$ near QCD scale is calculated within a nonlocal Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. We find that the bias $\Delta V$ decreases as $\theta$ approaches $\pi/2$ from either zero or $\pi$, while increases with rising $\mu_5$. We confirm that there exists a $(T,\theta,\mu_5)$ parameter space consistent with the axionic domain-wall interpretation of NANOGrav 15-year data on the nHz gravitational waves. We point out that employing the $\theta$-dependent topological susceptibility to quantify the QCD bias at finite $\theta$ in the previous study is improper, as it violates the general relation $\Delta V(\theta)=\Delta V(\pi-\theta)$.

authors.name: Zhao Zhang, Ruotong Zhao

papers.title: Analyzing Fermionic Dark Matter Scenarios with Anomalous Compact Objects
papers.summary: In this paper, we consider three compact objects (HESS J1731-347, PSR J1231-1411, XTE J1814-338) with anomalous mass-radius relations to analyze the possibility of their being dark matter admixed neutron stars. We try to infer the properties of the dark matter particles, under the assumption of behaving as a free Fermi gas. The main novelty relies on the use of a baryonic equation of state obtained from first principles over the whole density range, which allows the model dependence of the baryonic part of the calculation to be eliminated. Once the possible dark matter admixed neutron star configurations are obtained, we check their stability and whether it is feasible for a neutron star to capture the necessary dark matter fraction. Our analysis shows that our dark matter model favours the dark matter admixed neutron star hypothesis over the pure baryonic neutron star one, with the most favoured dark matter mass of $m_{DM} = 1$~GeV, although the necessary dark matter content cannot be explained in a standard galactic environment.

authors.name: Yaiza Cano, Jose Manuel Alarc\'on

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Transverse-Momentum Subtraction and Semi-Inclusive Deep-Inelastic Scattering at N$^3$LO in QCD
papers.summary: Identified hadron production is essential for the study of nucleon structure and QCD hadronization at high energies. We present the first calculation of unpolarized semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS) at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^3$LO) in perturbative QCD. Our calculation is based on a novel method of two-dimensional transverse-momentum subtraction motivated by QCD factorization of soft and collinear singularities. The N$^3$LO corrections are moderate in general but can be significant in threshold regions, and exhibit excellent perturbative convergence and reduced scale variations. The fully differential framework allows for arbitrary selection cuts and directly enables precision nucleon tomography at the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider, establishing the theory foundation needed to match the anticipated experimental accuracy. Generalization of the method to calculations of polarized SIDIS is also feasible.

authors.name: Liang Dong, Shen Fang, Jun Gao, Hai Tao Li, Ding Yu Shao, Hua Xing Zhu, Yu Jiao Zhu

papers.title: Heavy quark distributions from the Color Dipole Picture
papers.summary: To study charm -quark pair production processes, we utilized the color dipole picture gluon distribution function in a collinear generalized double asymptotic scaling approach at small Bjorken $x$ values ($x{\leq}10^{-2}$). Our results show good agreement with the latest HERA experimental data for reduced cross sections $\sigma_{\mathrm{red}}^{c\overline{c}} (W^2,Q^2)$ across a wide range of $x$ and $Q^2$ values, yielding an effective pomeron intercept. A Hard pomeron intercept with the coefficient $C_{2}=0.29$ in the color dipole model provides comparable results at very low $x$ values ($x{<}10^{-3}$). We demonstrate that the experimental data from HERA in the region $2.5{\leq}Q^2{\leq}2000~\mathrm{GeV}^2$ confirms the symmetry between the saturation and color transparency regions in the scaling variable $\eta$, shifting towards the color transparency region when we incorporate the threshold mass production of $J/\psi$ meson in the color dipole picture.

authors.name: G. R. Boroun

papers.title: Experimental test of symmetron-field based dark energy model using neutron interferometry
papers.summary: We report phase shift measurements of neutron matter waves propagating in vacuum and low-pressure argon gas, using a technique developed for neutron interferometric scattering length measurements. The experiment probes additional phase shifts induced by couplings to scalar fields. Based on the absence of such effects, we derive stringent constraints on scalar symmetron and dilaton fields, both of which represent leading candidates for quintessence dark energy.

authors.name: Andreas Dvorak, Kazuma Obigane, Hartmut Lemmel, Tobias Jenke, Stephan Sponar

papers.title: Rescuing flavor-symmetry-forbidden leptogenesis within the left-right symmetric framework
papers.summary: While the type-I seesaw model provides a unified framework for explaining the origin of neutrino masses and the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, flavor symmetries offer an attractive approach to understanding the observed neutrino mixing pattern. However, in many flavor-symmetry-based type-I seesaw models, either the Dirac neutrino mass matrix $M^{}_{\rm D}$ or the right-handed-neutrino mass matrix $M^{}_{\rm R}$ takes an exactly degenerate form, which prevents the conventional leptogenesis mechanism from working. In this paper, without breaking the original flavor structure dictated by the employed flavor symmetries, we investigate whether such forbidden leptogenesis scenarios can be rescued within the framework of the left-right symmetric model. We show that, in these scenarios, the contribution of the Higgs triplet present in the left-right symmetric model to the CP asymmetries of right-handed neutrino decays can successfully reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry. The leptogenesis mechanism proposed here can also be directly applied in more general type-I+II seesaw models.

authors.name: Yan Shao, Zhen-hua Zhao

papers.title: Revealing precision bounds on neutrino oscillation parameters with quantum estimation theory
papers.summary: Quantum estimation theory provides ultimate precision bounds on parameter estimation, independent of experimental setups. In this article, we apply this theoretical framework to neutrino oscillations, aiming to clarify some subtle issues and reveal the maximum achievable precision of oscillation parameters. First, taking the example of two-flavor oscillations, we clarify how the quantum Fisher information (QFI) depends on the choice of bases when the basis transformation itself involves the parameters in question. Then, for three-flavor oscillations, we compute the QFI matrix for electron and muon neutrino states in the flavor basis and derive analytical expressions and numerical results for both diagonal and off-diagonal elements. The implications of off-diagonal correlations for multiparameter estimation are discussed, including the compatibility of optimal measurements, the Holevo bound, and the spectral analysis of the QFI matrix, from which we show that a single neutrino channel leaves exactly two parameter combinations unconstrained. The quantum Cram\'{e}r-Rao bounds on the precision of oscillation parameters for typical reactor and long-baseline accelerator neutrino experiments are obtained as vacuum, state-level benchmarks, which establish a theoretical reference for the ultimate precision achievable in future neutrino oscillation experiments.

authors.name: Jihong Huang, Tommy Ohlsson, Sampsa Vihonen, Shun Zhou

papers.title: Probing Quadratically Coupled Ultralight Dark Matter with the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna
papers.summary: Ultralight dark matter can interact with Standard Model particles via gravitational and non-gravitational interactions. Through such interactions, it can leave distinctive signals in gravitational-wave experiments. In this work, we investigate signals induced by ultralight dark matter quadratically coupled to the Standard Model in the future space-borne gravitational-wave detector, the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Due to the quadratic nature of the coupling, dark matter signals appear at two distinct frequencies: the frequency corresponding to twice the dark matter mass, and frequencies below the typical dark matter kinetic energy. We analyze both contributions and show that LISA can surpass current constraints from terrestrial and astrophysical probes in certain mass ranges. We also find that dark matter signals in LISA are free from screening effects which significantly limit the sensitivity of terrestrial experiments.

authors.name: Xucheng Gan, Hyungjin Kim, Anna-Malin Lemke, Andrea Mitridate

papers.title: Dark Monopoles, Bounds on Hidden Sectors, and Cosmological Implications
papers.summary: Hidden sectors are a generic prediction of string theory compactifications and result in a promising landscape for dark matter model building. We consider the case of hidden sector magnetic monopoles produced via a thermal phase transition in the early Universe and subsequently diluted by pair annihilation. We show that for symmetry-breaking scales $\gtrsim 100\, \text{PeV}$, the monopole abundance is unacceptably high, overclosing the Universe. Our bounds are robust against variations in the initial fraction of energy density deposited in the hidden sector, exhibiting only a weak power-law dependence on this quantity. The bound is substantially tightened in the case of multiple hidden sectors. The standard cosmology may only be recovered if one of the following is true: the hidden sector(s) are non-existent, the hidden sectors have no monopoles with symmetry-breaking scale above 100 PeV, the maximum temperature of each monopole-producing hidden sector after reheating is below its symmetry-breaking scale, or the monopole abundance is diluted by an additional physical mechanism (such as early matter domination, the Langacker-Pi mechanism, or capture by primordial black holes).

authors.name: Donald Liveoak, Anshuman Maharana, James D. Wells

papers.title: Qubit-qubit-qutrit quantum correlations in $H \to f \bar f V$
papers.summary: We perform an extensive analysis of the quantum correlations carried by the qubit--qubit--qutrit pure state arising in the decay of a massive scalar into a fermion--antifermion pair and a massive gauge boson, $H \to f \bar f V$, specialising to the Higgs boson decay $h \to \tau^- \tau^+ Z$. Working with the exact tree-level spin state and its systematic expansion around the massless-fermion limit, we obtain analytic control over the entire phase space: the bipartite entanglement measures, the genuine $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ entanglement structure (the Miyake classification), as well as the Bell-inequality violations and the non-stabiliserness (magic) are all mapped and reproduced by compact formulas. The bipartite measures exhibit a monogamy-like trade-off between the fermion pair and the fermion--boson pairs. The state is genuinely $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ entangled over almost the entire phase space, most strongly in the collinear regions. We derive, for the first time, semi-analytical expressions for the tight $4 \times 4 \times 2$ Bell inequalities of the $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ system, generalising the optimisation previously available only for three qubits, and find that the local-hidden-variable bound is violated over the entire phase space, reaching within a few per cent of the quantum bound at the upper endpoint of the di-tau mass spectrum. We further extend the stabiliser R\'enyi entropy and the non-local magic to systems with unequal local dimensions, and show that the near-endpoint state carries almost exactly one bit of non-local magic, which peaks at $\log_2 \frac{27}{7} \simeq 1.95$ in the collinear regions. The differential decay rate concentrates precisely in the most nonclassical region of the phase space.

authors.name: Micha{\l} Banacki, Misaki Ohta, Abhyoudai S. Shaleena, Pawe{\l} Caban, Micha{\l} Eckstein, Kazuki Sakurai, Michael Spannowsky, Pawe{\l} Horodecki

papers.title: The near-threshold cross section of $e^+e^- \to \Omega^-\bar{\Omega}^+$: Heavy-flavor rescattering and physics-informed deep learning
papers.summary: Recent precision measurements of the $e^+e^- \to \Omega^-\bar{\Omega}^+$ cross section by the BESIII collaboration provide a valuable opportunity to probe complex hadronic rescattering mechanisms. In this work, we investigate a potential structure near the $D_s\bar{D}_s$ threshold using a coupled-channel framework incorporating $\Omega\bar{\Omega}$, $\Xi\bar{\Xi}$, and $D_s\bar{D}_s$ interactions. The driving potentials are derived from effective Lagrangians respecting heavy quark spin symmetry, chiral symmetry, and hidden local symmetry, and the scattering amplitude is unitarized via the on-shell factorization of the Bethe-Salpeter equation. To go beyond local fits and map theoretical uncertainties, we use a two-step machine-learning framework. First, Simulation-Based Inference with a Mixture Density Network maps the global Bayesian posterior of the effective couplings. Second, to identify the poles, we employ a Cauchy-Riemann Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The network enforces mathematical analyticity by construction, continuing the real-axis determinant into the complex energy plane. At the best fit, no pole is found near the $D_s\bar D_s$ threshold, while a single physical pole is identified at $M=3.1868$ GeV with $\Gamma=1.57$ MeV, sitting 158 MeV below the $\Omega\bar\Omega$ threshold. The corresponding S-matrix residues show an overwhelming coupling to the $\Omega\bar\Omega$ channel, favoring a dynamically generated $\Omega\bar\Omega$ bound state, predicted by the model below the measured energy range.

authors.name: Sara Rahmani

papers.title: Integration-by-parts identities in the presence of measurement delta functions
papers.summary: We derive a convenient form of integration-by-parts (IBP) identities for dimensionally regulated loop integrals that include a measurement constraint imposed by a delta distribution $\delta(\phi(\ell))$, where $\phi$ is a regular and generally non-linear function of the loop momentum. Non-trivial IBP relations can be generated directly by vectors tangent to the hypersurface $\phi=0$, leaving the measurement delta as an overall factor and avoiding derivatives of distributions. This construction provides a systematic route to differential distributions within reverse unitarity for non-linear measurement functions, in particular, for transverse-momentum distributions. We implement the construction and validate it for transverse-momentum distributions in $t\bar tH$ production at leading order and $t\bar t$ production at next-to-leading order in QCD.

authors.name: Saimeng Zhou

papers.title: Energy-independent neutrino dephasing from an ultralight axion-like background
papers.summary: We study neutrino oscillations in an ultralight axion-like particle (ALP) dark-matter background with low-energy derivative couplings $g_i$ diagonal in the neutrino mass basis. In vacuum, these couplings generate an additional relative phase set by the field difference between production and detection, which can vary from event to event as the background oscillates. Averaging over these unresolved variations can then reduce the oscillation contrast. When the field changes little during each flight and the spread of induced phases is small, the leading suppression is quadratic in distance and independent of neutrino energy. Matching published reactor damping limits at representative baselines gives scales near $0.83$ and $0.5~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ for the coupling differences in JUNO and KamLAND, respectively, with $g_2=g_3$ and a local ALP density of $\rho_a=0.4~\mathrm{GeV}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$. These scales vary as $\rho_a^{-1/2}$ and remain nearly mass independent, for instance over $10^{-20}\lesssim m_a/\mathrm{eV}\lesssim10^{-13}$ when the data sample the assumed distribution of the ALP field. We compare two electroweak operators: a dimension-five current involving both neutrinos and charged leptons, constrained by charged-lepton flavor violation, and a dimension-seven operator that selects neutrinos through Higgs fields and allows invisible Higgs decays. For the latter, the Higgs bound on the coupling differences is about two orders of magnitude below the JUNO scale, assuming a single operator valid at the Higgs mass and Standard Model production. At lower energies, we calculate pion and kaon ALP-emission rates and missing-mass spectra and compare them with PIENU and NA62 searches.

authors.name: B. A. Couto e Silva, B. L. S\'anchez-Vega

papers.title: Hidden Sector Relic Abundances from an Effective Planck Mass
papers.summary: Hidden sectors are generic in beyond the Standard Model constructions and string compactifications. We consider models featuring hidden sectors that have dark matter candidates. The relic density is set in part by the energy-injecting inflaton branching ratio $B$ to the sector. We develop a general framework to determine the dependence on $B$ for thermalized hidden sectors by defining an effective Planck mass for the Boltzmann equations for the hidden sector degrees of freedom. We apply this framework to several representative examples, including freeze-out/freeze-in WIMPs and multi-component dark matter. We find that the fractional energy density carried by freeze-out relics (in both single and multi-component models) and monopoles produced from second order phase transitions scale as $B^{1/4}$ and thus may lead to an overclosure problem, even with $B \ll 1$. On the other hand, the energy density of freeze-in relics scales as $B^{5/4}$ and is thus cosmologically irrelevant for sufficiently small $B$. Finally, we discuss the cumulative implications of a large number of hidden sectors.

authors.name: Donald Liveoak, Anshuman Maharana, James D. Wells

papers.title: A unified reduced-mass parametrization of effective chromoelectric interactions in hadrons
papers.summary: We construct a unified effective mass relation in which a common reduced-mass function describes the flavor dependence of chromoelectric pair contributions, with explicit color factors connecting $q\bar q$ and $qq$ pairs. After subtracting fixed spin-weighted chromomagnetic contributions, we jointly fit fourteen spin-averaged meson and baryon masses using constituent quark masses and an additive constant shared by both sectors, obtaining a root-mean-square (RMS) residual of 4 MeV. The fitted saturating form connects the nearly saturated light-flavor contribution with increasing attraction in the heavy-flavor region. In the common saturation limit, the leading chromoelectric contribution acts as a common mass shift for each constituent and can be absorbed into effective constituent masses; the residual pair term accounts for the flavor dependence away from saturation. With the chromomagnetic interaction included, this single parameter set reproduces the ground-state meson and baryon spectra and yields predictions for multiply heavy baryons outside the calibration set. By diagonalizing the sum of the chromoelectric and chromomagnetic mass matrices, we further obtain the ground-state spectra of $cc\bar c\bar c$, $bb\bar b\bar b$, and $bc\bar b\bar c$. The fully charmed tensor mass is ${6505}{(9)(9)}$ MeV, close to recent lattice QCD results, while the upper scalar mass of {${6562}{(9)(12)}$} MeV lies in the mass region near $X(6600)$. The tetraquark masses remain relatively stable under the examined variations of the $qq$ chromomagnetic couplings. The relative $S$-wave rearrangement-decay weights obtained from color--spin recoupling can be used to identify favored decay channels under the stated spatial-overlap approximation.

authors.name: Wen-Nian Liu, Duo-Jie Jia, Fu-Quan Dou

papers.title: Saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at LH$\mu$C
papers.summary: Motivated by recent proposal of high energy $\mu^+$-hadron collider at CERN, LH$\mu$C, which could be a natural extension of the LH$e$C at the end of the HL-LHC stage, we have studied expected gluon saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at DIS; these processes are sensitive to the most basic non-perturbative structure parametrizing hadronic content of small-$x$ gluons, the Weizs\"acker-Williams (WW) TMD gluon distribution. For the nominal center-of-mass energy of LH$\mu$C $\sqrt{s}=5.3$~TeV we have computed a large selection of observables using the ITMD framework in Mote Carlo setting, both for proton and lead target. In the context of future data-driven precise restrictions of the WW TMD gluon distribution, we have computed several azimuthal angle correlations, including the correlations between pairs of jets as well as the outgoing $\mu^+$ and jet plane. We have also computed nuclear modification factors, that show a significant suppression, ranging locally between 30%-40%, depending on the observable.

authors.name: Piotr Kotko, Grzegorz Ziarko

papers.title: Two-loop correction to the complex-bion amplitude in a quasi-exactly solvable sextic oscillator
papers.summary: In this study, a quasi-exactly solvable sextic potential is analyzed by two diagrammatic calculations. At positive coupling, factorization fixes the ground-state energy $E_0$ exactly and forces every perturbative coefficient to vanish. Using only Feynman diagrams, we verify this cancellation explicitly through third order. After continuation to negative coupling, the formal zero mode becomes nonnormalizable. A real instanton remains, but its one-instanton contribution to \(E_0\) vanishes. In particular, the leading shift in energy arises from a complex neutral bion. Taking an exact constrained family, we calculate its local median amplitude through two loops. The direct diagrammatic sum gives $c_{\rm 2L}^{\rm diag}=-0.750000(5)$, in excellent agreement with the exact-WKB value $-3/4$.

authors.name: Adrian M. Escobar-Ruiz

papers.title: Prospect on constraining environment-dependent dilaton model from gravitational redshift measurements
papers.summary: Scalar-tensor gravity represents a natural extension of general relativity. This paper investigates the prospects for constraining the environmentally dependent dilaton through atomic-clock comparisons across media of different densities. Using the scalar Compton wavelength, we assess how the finite size of the surrounding medium and screening by the clock enclosure limit the accessible region. To test the continuous-density approximation for dilute media, we model matter as a periodic lattice of spherical particles and compare an analytic Neumann solution with a three-dimensional finite-element solution on the cubic box. The continuous and discrete models give indistinguishable redshift predictions near the $10^{-20}$ and $10^{-25}$ benchmarks. In the strong-coupling regime, differences become apparent on redshift contours of order $10^{-46}$ or lower. Under the assumed environmental and instrumental conditions, comparisons involving a dense medium identify a window for probing smaller values of $A_2$, offering a gravitational-redshift test complementary to existing fifth-force searches.

authors.name: Li Hu, Rong-Gen Cai, Song He, Li-Fang Li, Tong Liu, Peng Xu, Shao-Jiang Wang

papers.title: Morphological false-vacuum decay in dipolar supersolids
papers.summary: False-vacuum decay between two morphologically distinct supersolid phases via bubble nucleation is studied in a uniform dipolar gas confined to the plane. Starting from a metastable honeycomb state, the formation of stripe phase domains is simulated numerically by means of a stochastic projected extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The speed of bubble growth is analyzed in relation to the multiple speeds of sound of the supersolid, and is found to be set by the slowest of these sounds. The vacuum decay rate is numerically extracted and compared against a minimal effective model for the Coleman bounce solution connecting the two supersolid orders. Our results establish dipolar supersolids as a novel and versatile platform for studying false-vacuum decay. This setting offers a rich structure of metastable states and collective excitations that come into play in the decay. Furthermore, here, in contrast to previous studies, bubble formation occurs directly in the real-space density and can be probed with \textit{in situ} imaging.

authors.name: Wyatt Kirkby, Lauriane Chomaz, Thomas Gasenzer

papers.title: Hadronic and partonic composition of QCD matter across the crossover
papers.summary: We construct a phenomenological equation of state of strongly interacting matter at zero chemical potentials that provides a unified description of lattice QCD thermodynamics in terms of hadronic and partonic degrees of freedom in the temperature range $T=100$-$510$ MeV. The hadronic phase is described by the quantum van der Waals hadron resonance gas, extended by excluded-volume repulsion between mesons, while the quark-gluon plasma is modeled as an ideal gas of quarks and gluons supplemented with a phenomenological interaction term proportional to $T^3$. The two regimes are connected by a smooth crossover switching function. We determine the four model parameters - the meson hard-core radius, the strength of the partonic interaction term, and two parameters of the switching function - by fitting to lattice QCD results for the trace anomaly. In this model, hadronic contributions remain significant up to about $200$ MeV, well above the QCD chiral crossover. We also quantify the crossing contributions generated by the temperature dependence of the switching function. The switching temperature and the hadronic and partonic contributions depend on the chosen equations of state and switching function. The lattice thermodynamic data do not uniquely determine the microscopic composition of QCD matter.

authors.name: Artemiy Lysenko, Mark I. Gorenstein, Marek Gazdzicki, Roman Poberezhniuk, Volodymyr Vovchenko

papers.title: Levy-shaped femtoscopic sources from an exact solution of relativistic hydrodynamics
papers.summary: An important goal of high-energy physics is to better understand the spacetime structure of particle emitting sources created in heavy-ion collisions. For a fraction of a second, a special form of matter, the so-called quark-gluon plasma (QGP), is created, which can be examined with the toolkit of femtoscopy. With the measurement of correlation functions it was determined that L\'evy distributions describe the shape of hadron (pion) emission sources at freeze-out the most accurately; however, analytic solutions of hydrodynamics typically yield Gaussian sources, and power-law tails are usually attributed to the hadronic stage rather than to the fluid dynamics itself. In this article we showcase an exact solution of the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics, which aims to resolve this puzzle by providing L\'evy distributions directly from hydrodynamics. A detailed analysis reveals whether the predictions of this solution are in accordance with observations; in particular, the effective temperatures from angle-averaged transverse mass distributions and the femtoscopic radii from two-particle momentum correlation functions are analyzed.

authors.name: Bence Szentkuti, Mate Csanad

papers.title: Updated T2K measurement of neutrino oscillation parameters with the first data from the Gadolinium-loaded far detector
papers.summary: The T2K experiment presents updated measurements of neutrino oscillation parameters using $21.4(16.3)\times10^{20}$ protons on target (POT) in (anti-)neutrino mode at the far detector, Super-Kamiokande. This analysis uses an additional neutrino dataset of $1.7 \times 10^{20}$ POT compared to the previous result, and for the very first time, data collected with Super-Kamiokande doped with Gadolinium (Gd). Significant improvements were introduced in the far detector selection and systematic error treatment. Both semi-frequentist and Bayesian analyses are presented, including results on $\sin^{2} \theta_{23}$, $\Delta m^2_{32} $, $\sin^{2} \theta_{13}$ and $\delta_{CP}$. Both analyses favor normal mass ordering with a nearly maximal CP-violating phase and are compatible with neutrino maximal mixing, slightly favouring the upper $\theta_{23}$ octant.

authors.name: The T2K collaboration

papers.title: Measurements of $|V_{cd(s)}|$ , decay constants, and form factors in (semi-)leptonic $D_{(s)}$ decays at BESIII
papers.summary: The BESIII experiment accumulated the world's largest charm-meson samples. This proceeding presents recent measurements of decay constants, transition form factors, and CKM matrix elements from (semi-)leptonic \(D^+\) and \(D_s^+\) decays based on these datasets.

authors.name: Medina Ablikim

papers.title: Interference effects in MSSM Higgs boson searches at low $tan\beta$: the $gg\to H\to WW, ZZ, hh$ and $gg \to A \to Zh$ channels
papers.summary: The LHC limits on the heavy neutral Higgs bosons of the minimal supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model, which are particularly relevant at low values of the ratio of vacuum expectation values $\tan\beta$, have been obtained in the narrow-width approximation, without including the interference between the pure Higgs signal and the QCD background. We study the interference of the resonant heavy neutral CP-even $H$ and CP-odd $A$ boson contributions with the non-resonant gluon-fusion amplitudes in the processes $gg\to VV$ with $V=W,Z$, $gg \to hh$ and $gg\to Zh$ at low $\tan\beta$, $1\le \tan\beta \le 6$. We work at leading order but with the exact top-quark mass dependence, and with the longitudinal $VV$ and $Zh$ amplitudes obtained from the Goldstone-boson equivalence theorem that lead to loop form factors similar to those appearing in $gg\to hh$. The lineshapes in the four search channels are governed by a simple complex parameter $\kappa$, the ratio of the resonant to non-resonant amplitudes at the peak. Because the $H$ and $A$ bosons couple weakly to the considered final states, while being broadened by their decays to top quarks, $|\kappa|$ drops to values of a few for masses of $0.5$--$1$ TeV, even though the total widths remain at the percent level. The interference then increases the signal rates by up to tens of per cent, and distorts their lineshapes. For the present ATLAS (and presumably CMS) Run II exclusion limits, the net effect is nevertheless rather modest, except at the high-mass end of the $H\to hh$ contour, but it becomes important for the masses that will be probed at the high-luminosity LHC.

authors.name: Abdelhak Djouadi, John Ellis

papers.title: A pseudoscalar Higgs boson interfering with toponium: a QCD analysis of $\mathbf{gg\to A\to t\bar t}$ near threshold
papers.summary: The CMS and ATLAS collaborations have observed an excess of $t\bar t$ events near threshold that is consistent with the formation of the pseudoscalar toponium state $\eta_t$. A pseudoscalar Higgs boson $A$ with a large coupling to top quarks could contribute part of this excess and the presence of the $A$ boson could be concealed. We point out that, if such a state exists with $M_A$ close to $2m_t$, it necessarily interferes with toponium, since both live in the colour--singlet ${}^1S_0$ channel and share the same Coulomb final--state interaction. Using exact leading--order amplitudes, whose relative phase is fixed by unitarity, and Coulomb resummation applied coherently to the QCD background, the $A$ boson signal and their interference, we show that the line shape is controlled by a single complex number $\kappa$, the ratio of the resonant and non--resonant amplitudes at the peak. Unitarity fixes ${\rm Im}\,\kappa=-1$ exactly when $A$ decays into top quarks, so that the interference reduces the resonant rate by $2/|\kappa|^2$ and produces an exact zero of the ${}^1S_0$ amplitude just above $M_A$. The parameter $\kappa$ does not depend on the $A$ coupling to top quarks and, with the Coulomb--enhanced width we find $|\kappa|\approx1.5$--$1.7$ for $M_A=350$--$380$ GeV and, hence, the $A$ resonance is completely distorted. For an $A$ boson accounting for 50\% (25\%) of the observed excess, it enhances the toponium peak by about 10 to 70\% (5 to 35\%), and the threshold excess differs strongly from the sum of the toponium and $A$ contributions.

authors.name: Abdelhak Djouadi, John Ellis

papers.title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
papers.summary: Agentic systems are increasingly being explored for automating experimental high-energy physics measurements, but the correctness of their results can today be reliably evaluated only via extensive expert review. To address this, we propose a method to perform detailed quantitative evaluations of agent-driven analyses through the use of blind analysis and injection tests, which are critical in a typical expert review. Agents develop a data analysis pipeline on a public dataset, while the evaluation is performed on programmatically generated sealed private datasets where signals are injected and simulation settings varied within realistic detector uncertainties. By requiring agents to provide a single workflow that is evaluated across these "sealed worlds", we are able to test the accuracy and robustness of the workflows. We demonstrate the approach on four tasks built from CMS open data and present it as a way to reliably benchmark scientific work in experimental high-energy physics. At the time of writing, the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, reaches 60% of the score of the expert reference analyses on average, ahead of GPT 6 Astra at 38% and Claude Opus 5.5 at 31%. In individual sessions on one of the tasks, Gemini 4 Argon exceeds the reference. The benchmark is hosted at https://hep-ex-bench.github.io

authors.name: Andrzej Nov\'ak, Yiyang Zhao, Dolores Garcia, Eric A. Moreno, Jeffrey Krupa, V\'ictor Bres\'o-Pla, Samuel Bright-Thonney, Lukas Heinrich, Michael Kagan, Philip Harris

papers.title: Background characterization in the PIKACHU Phase 1 search for two-neutrino double-beta decay of $^{160}$Gd
papers.summary:
We report a background characterization for the search for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u2 eta$) decay of $^{160}$Gd using Ce:Gd$_3$Al$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillators in the PIKACHU experiment Phase 1 at the Kamioka underground laboratory. The experimental backgrounds were investigated through delayed-coincidence analysis and spectral fitting based on GEANT4 simulations. In particular, surface contamination of the crystal was identified through the characteristic distortion of the $^{214}$Po $\alpha$-ray spectrum, leading to an improved background model that reproduces the observed energy spectra. No significant excess attributable to $^{160}$Gd $2
u2 eta$ decay was observed, yielding a lower limit of $T^{2
u}_{1/2} \geq 2.32 	imes 10^{19}$ yr at 90\% C.L. The established background model and analysis framework provide a foundation for future PIKACHU phases aiming to discover $^{160}$Gd $2
u2 eta$ decay.

authors.name: T. Omori, T. Iida, A. Gando, N. Hinohara, K. Hosokawa, S. Ishidate, M. Ishigami, T. Kishimoto, K. Mizukoshi, T. Sako, S. Sugi, M. Yoshino, K. Fushimi, K. Kamada, Y. Shoji, Y. Suga, H. Suzuki, K. Takahashi

papers.title: Transverse Single-Spin Asymmetry Extraction, using both Binned and Unbinned Analysis, including Background Subtraction and Unfolding
papers.summary: The determination of transverse single-spin asymmetries in experiments involving polarized targets and/or beams may encounter challenges when (1) the magnitude of the polarization varies greatly with time, (2) the polarization magnitude is not the same for each spin state, (3) different integrated luminosities occur for different spin states or different target materials, and/or (4) some kinematic variables require unfolding; these are just a few examples. We present general methods of determining the asymmetry based on both binned analysis and unbinned maximum likelihood optimization, incorporating the unfolding of kinematic variables that are smeared by detector effects, and also including the possibility of background subtraction.

authors.name: S. F. Pate, H. Arachchige, C. Kuruppu, D. Nawarathne

papers.title: Constraints on anomalous Higgs boson couplings to vector bosons and fermions using the $\gamma\gamma$ final state in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: Possible anomalous couplings of the Higgs boson to vector bosons and fermions are studied using Higgs boson candidates decaying to a pair of photons. The study is based on proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV collected by the CMS experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. Events with Higgs boson candidates produced via gluon fusion, electroweak vector boson fusion and in association with a vector boson, are categorized using matrix element techniques and multivariate discriminants. The $CP$ properties of the Higgs boson couplings to gluons through loops of heavy particles, as well as the tensor structure of its interactions with two electroweak bosons, are investigated. The results are interpreted in terms of the fractional contributions of anomalous Higgs boson couplings to the total production cross section of each process and are found to be consistent with the standard model expectations.

authors.name: CMS Collaboration

papers.title: Measurement of the branching ratio of the $K^{+}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\nu\bar{\nu}$ decay

authors.name: NA62 Collaboration

papers.title: Evidence for $\eta_{c}(2S)\to p\bar{p}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ and observation of $\chi_{cJ} \to p\bar{p}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$
papers.summary: Using $(2.712\pm0.014)\times 10^9$ $\psi(3686)$ events collected by the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, the $\psi(3686) \to \gamma p\bar{p}\pi^+\pi^-\pi^0$ process is investigated. Evidence for the decay of $\eta_{c}(2S)\to p\bar{p}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ is found with a signal significance of 3.3$\sigma$. The product of branching fractions of $\mathcal{B}[\psi(3686)\to \gamma \eta_{c}(2S)]\times\mathcal{B}[\eta_{c}(2S)\to p\bar{p}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}]$ is determined to be $(3.4\pm0.5\pm0.8) \times 10^{-6}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic. The hadronic decays of $\chi_{cJ} \to p\bar{p}\pi^+\pi^-\pi^0$$~(J=0,1,2)$ are observed, and their branching fractions are measured to be $\mathcal{B}(\chi_{c0}\to p\bar{p}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0})=(4.79\pm 0.01\pm0.40) \times 10^{-3}$, $\mathcal{B}(\chi_{c1}\to p\bar{p}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0})=(2.13\pm 0.01\pm0.17) \times 10^{-3}$, and $\mathcal{B}(\chi_{c2}\to p\bar{p}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0})=(3.72\pm 0.01\pm0.29) \times 10^{-3}$, respectively. Furthermore, the branching fractions for the intermediate processes $\chi_{cJ}\to p\bar{p}\omega$ are updated with significantly improved precision: $\mathcal{B}(\chi_{c0}\to p\bar{p}\omega)=(5.76\pm0.01\pm0.42)\times10^{-4}$, $\mathcal{B}(\chi_{c1}\to p\bar{p}\omega)=(1.85\pm0.01\pm0.13)\times10^{-4}$, and $\mathcal{B}(\chi_{c2}\to p\bar{p}\omega)=(4.51\pm0.01\pm0.33)\times10^{-4}$, respectively.

papers.title: Leakage current evolution in LHCb VELO sensors during Run 1-2 LHC data taking period
papers.summary: Silicon detectors operating in the harsh mixed-hadron radiation environment of modern high-energy physics experiments suffer progressive bulk damage, manifesting macroscopically as a steady rise in leakage current.
