This paper moves beyond that static test to a streaming deployment, in which the correlation structure and the portfolio are both re-estimated on a rolling basis, as a live rebalancing system would actually operate. We introduce two streaming variants -- PCE itself and a joint multi-cut variant, dPCE -- and evaluate both against a Buy & Hold baseline across window lengths, portfolio sizes up to several thousand assets, risk-aversion and transaction-cost settings, and measurement-shot budgets. Streaming PCE and dPCE consistently outperform the passive baseline, including during a market downturn where both lose money but PCE loses markedly less -- evidence that the method's value is not confined to rising markets. PCE also proves the more practical choice at scale, since dPCE's resource requirements and its sensitivity to rebalancing frequency both grow faster with portfolio size. We further report which operational choices -- rebalancing cadence, shot budget, and transaction-cost awareness -- matter most for a real deployment, and which matter less than commonly assumed.

authors.name: Vicente P. Soloviev, Josh Kirsopp

papers.title: Exploiting SU(2) Symmetry for Efficient Quantum State Preparation of Matrix Product States
papers.summary: Quantum computing offers a promising route to simulating strongly correlated systems, particularly for dynamical and spectral quantities whose classical computation can become prohibitively expensive. Fault-tolerant algorithms for these tasks, including real-time dynamics and phase estimation, assume efficient preparation of the initial many-body state, making state preparation an important bottleneck. Matrix product states obtained classically with the density matrix renormalization group can be compiled sequentially into fault-tolerant circuits. We exploit non-Abelian spin SU(2) symmetry in this compilation. By the Wigner-Eckart theorem, only the reduced tensors, which carry the variational information, need generic unitary synthesis. The magnetic structure is restored by Clebsch-Gordan transformations with analytically known angles. We benchmark the method on representative strongly correlated models, including the one-dimensional Hubbard model, quasi-one-dimensional Hubbard geometries, and Anderson impurity models, and perform fault-tolerant resource estimates using the Toffoli count as the primary cost metric. Across the systems considered, exploiting non-Abelian SU(2) symmetry reduces the Toffoli cost roughly threefold relative to U(1)-adapted compilation and by more than an order of magnitude relative to the standard dense compilation method. These results demonstrate how non-Abelian symmetries can substantially reduce the cost of transferring classically tractable many-body ground states to quantum computers, facilitating their use in quantum dynamics and energy estimation.

authors.name: Etienne D'Argenlieu, Alessandro Summer, Fran\c{c}ois Jamet, David P. Tew, Lachlan P. Lindoy

papers.title: Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson simulation of the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model
papers.summary: The Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard (JCH) model describes the interaction of light and matter in coupled optical cavities and provides a framework for studying their quantum dynamics. In this work, we design a Trotterized quantum circuit to investigate the real-time dynamics of the JCH model using Bosonic Qiskit and a Matrix Product State (MPS) backend. We simulate single-polariton transport and benchmark site occupations against exact diagonalization results. We then extend the simulations to the two-excitation sector under a hard-core photon constraint, examining excitation transport and symmetry properties. Finally, we study the dependence of bipartite entanglement entropy on the inter-cavity photon-hopping strength. The results illustrate how hybrid qubit-boson circuits, simulated with matrix product states, can be used to study light-matter lattice dynamics. This work provides a numerical benchmark for extending hybrid simulation approaches to more complex interacting and open light-matter systems.

authors.name: Nabaraj Khatri, Dilip Ojha, Rajib Tripathi, Kismat K. C, Ashish Khanal

papers.title: Dirac Propagation for Simulating Fermionic Observables under Particle-Number-Conserving Unitaries
papers.summary: Simulating the dynamics of interacting fermions remains a central computational challenge across physics and chemistry. We introduce Dirac propagation, a classical method that simulates local observables in fermionic systems subject to particle-number-conserving unitaries. We show that, in the operator expansion, strings with weights above the total particle number can be discarded without incurring any error in the final expectation value. This exact cutoff bounds the number of retained strings polynomially in the number of modes at fixed particle number, including for interacting dynamics. The formalism combines a compact representation with explicit expressions for interacting gates and exact treatment of number-conserving fermionic Gaussian and Clifford unitaries. This framework offers an approach to simulating fermionic many-body dynamics and classically benchmarking fermionic quantum circuits.

authors.name: G Arnav Naidu, Matteo D'Anna, Adri\'an P\'erez-Salinas, Jannes Nys, Juan Carrasquilla

papers.title: Iterative Petz Protocols for Quantum State Recovery
papers.summary: Noise is omnipresent in quantum systems, and thus, approximately reversing this noise is a central challenge towards quantum technologies. The Petz map provides a physically admissible recovery channel, but its performance depends critically on the choice of reference state. Here, we introduce and investigate the iterative Petz recovery (IPR) protocol, an adaptive multicopy strategy that begins from an unbiased reference state and uses each recovered output to construct the Petz map for the next iteration. We establish the stability of the protocol and develop a tomography-assisted finite-copy implementation with explicit control of error propagation and fidelity loss. For qubit depolarizing noise, we derive an exact recurrence for the fidelity of every pure input. For single-axis Pauli noise, we derive an exact recurrence for the six-state Pauli average and compare it numerically with the Haar average. We further benchmark finite-copy IPR against measure-and-prepare strategies based on local and collective measurements, revealing the associated finite-resource tradeoffs.

authors.name: Lea Lautenbacher, Felix Ahnefeld, Susana F. Huelga, Martin B. Plenio

papers.title: Polynomial Master Equations of Open Quantum Systems and an Analysis on the Critical Solutions
papers.summary: The dynamics of open quantum systems exhibits in general a non-Markovian behavior, lying typically beyond the description of first-order differential equations. Traditional methods commonly turned to first-order integro-differential equations, which allowed for the standard interpretation of non-Markovianity as having its origin in the global history of the system evolution. We examine the possibility of an alternative, locally deterministic interpretation [arXiv:2607.09651] of the working of its dynamical hysteresis, where the evolution of a system is determined by its local behavior alone. The present work elaborates on our systematic method in deriving non-Markovian linear differential equations associated with matrix polynomials of higher order. Our methods will be demonstrated with exact analyses on two illustrative examples: one built upon the simplest non-trivial model concerning a two-qubit system, and another involving an unbounded Hamiltonian defined on an infinite-dimensional quantum system. We also analyze the critical parameters at which qualitative changes are observed in the system dynamics, and reveal how our polynomial equations account for the phenomena.

authors.name: Miku Ishizaki, Jaeha Lee

papers.title: Class-resolved sifting for quantum key distribution with photon pairs hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial variables
papers.summary: Photon pairs hyperentangled in polarization and transverse spatial variables can carry two key bits per pair in entanglement-based quantum key distribution. We develop class-resolved sifting for such sources: every detected pair is assigned to a class according to which degrees of freedom were measured in compatible bases, and error and key rates are estimated separately in each class. Applied to previously reported data from a two-crystal spontaneous parametric down-conversion source read out in intermediate fractional-Fourier planes, the method recovers the key yield of independent sifting and turns the comparison between classes into a quantitative consistency test for cross-dependencies between the two degrees of freedom. The measured dependence lies below the spatial-polarization coupling predicted for the source, at the edge of the present statistical sensitivity. Resolving the data by polarization-analyzer setting, we find an approximately twofold dependence of the spatial error on the polarization setting in one readout arm, attributable to the measurement apparatus rather than to the source and relevant to basis-dependent side channels. We compare the hyperentangled protocol with a single 4-dimensional system measured in two mutually unbiased bases. Fundamentally, both yield the same key per detected pair and obey the same entropic bound, but they differ in their tensor-product structure: hyperentanglement factors the bases into separate two-outcome measurements, which are simpler to implement and allow errors to be attributed to each degree of freedom, whereas a single variable gives access to non-product bases that can increase the noise tolerance. For the present source, whose polarization coherence is limited by partial which-crystal erasure, a single-variable spatial encoding would yield more key only if its four-outcome readout kept the symbol error within a few percent.

authors.name: Murilo H. Magiotto, Millena B. Novaes, Wesley B. Cardoso, Ardiley T. Avelar, Guilherme L. Zanin, Rafael M. Gomes

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Superradiant Criticality and Thermal Emission in the Open Dicke Model
papers.summary: Near the superradiant phase transition of the Dicke model, the lowest-frequency excitation softens and its losses can no longer be treated as a weak perturbation. We develop a finite-temperature theory of this transition in the open system, with no restriction on the strength of the system-bath coupling. The cavity mode and the atomic ensemble are coupled to independent reservoirs, the first at zero temperature and the second at temperature $T$, and we assume that the spins remain thermalized with their reservoir. We find that the reservoirs do not shift the temperature-dependent critical coupling for a broad class of spectral densities, while the polariton becomes overdamped in a finite interval of couplings around it. As expected, raising the temperature moves the transition to stronger couplings, and in the superradiant phase we find a faster decoupling of light and matter. The theoretical framework developed here yields the reflection and thermal emission spectra for arbitrary parameters in both the normal and the superradiant phase, and provides a basis for comparison with experiments on systems displaying ground-state condensation. We also identify conditions under which the system behaves, at specific frequencies, as both a perfect absorber and a perfect emitter.

authors.name: Gabriele Orlando, Samuel Napoli, Salvatore Savasta, Omar Di Stefano

papers.title: Robust growth of $\alpha$-tantalum on sapphire at room temperature using atomically thin titanium seed layer
papers.summary: Tantalum (Ta) based superconducting circuits have attracted attention for their low microwave loss. However, reproducible growth of high-quality $\alpha$-phase Ta films remains challenging because film properties are highly sensitive to growth conditions. We present a robust, room-temperature route for $\alpha$-Ta growth on sapphire substrates using an ultrathin Ti seed layer, which significantly widens the accessible deposition parameter space. We compare this approach to Ta films grown at high temperature without a seed layer and at room temperature with a Nb seed. We assess films using structural and surface characterization and quantify microwave loss with coplanar-waveguide (CPW) resonators measured in the quantum regime. We obtain two-level-system (TLS)-limited quality factors comparable to the state of the art for Ta-on-sapphire CPW resonators with similar geometries. In addition, temperature-dependent measurements reveal that high-temperature-grown films and films subjected to extended buffered-oxide etch treatment exhibit additional temperature activated loss, highlighting the role of growth route and post-processing in microwave performance. Our results establish ultrathin seed-layer engineering as a reliable alternative route to reproducible, low-loss $\alpha$-Ta films and motivate closer study of the interfacial mechanisms that govern Ta phase formation.

authors.name: Anand Kamlapure, Lucas Hak, Kishore Kumar Thiyagarajan, Hozanna Miro, Marc Beekman, Matvey Finkel, Leonardo DiCarlo

papers.title: Classical algorithms for sparse random Hamiltonians via free probability
papers.summary: The search for quantum advantage in average-case problems is a pressing open question in physics and computer science. The widest conjectured example of such an advantage is in simulation of quantum many-body systems, where sign problems and entanglement growth cause the breakdown of many classical methods. Nonetheless, theoretical evidence for or against such an advantage remains scarce. Here, we investigate this in sparse random non-local Hamiltonians. We design a classical algorithm for such Hamiltonians that enables accurate computation of spectral fluctuations, thermal values, and time-ordered and out-of-time-order correlation functions. For any subexponential precision $\varepsilon$, our algorithm runs in time $(1/\varepsilon)^{2+o(1)}$, nearly identical to a quantum simulation. Crucially, this applies even at late evolution times, low temperatures, and near critical points, where existing classical methods require exponential time. Rather than directly simulating a quantum state or operator, our algorithm first computes the model's mean behavior and then a short hierarchy of instance-dependent corrections. These corrections predict long-time behavior based on short-time data using free probability theory.

authors.name: Matthew Ding, Robbie King, Thomas Schuster

papers.title: A Koashi--Imoto Criterion for Holevo-Rate Visible Compression
papers.summary: For a finite memoryless quantum source whose encoder knows the sequence of classical labels, we determine when the Holevo rate is achievable with shared classical randomness and no shared entanglement. In the maximal Koashi--Imoto decomposition of the signal ensemble, this occurs exactly when each signal is pure on the quantum part of every sector it occupies. For qubits, this means that the signals are all pure or commute pairwise. If any occupied quantum part is mixed, every code with sufficiently small mean local error has rate bounded away from the Holevo information, uniformly in blocklength. To prove the converse, we apply Fawzi--Renner recovery to a hypothetical sequence of visible codes approaching the Holevo rate at vanishing local error, then invoke a decoupling bound of Baghali Khanian and Winter for blind compression.

authors.name: Anthony M. Polloreno

papers.title: On the concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls
papers.summary: We show that the Gaussian uniquely maximizes the $L^2$ concentration of the ambiguity function on every centered ball, up to time-frequency shifts and multiplication by a unimodular constant. The proof relies on ideas from quantum information theory.

authors.name: Fabio Nicola

papers.title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
papers.summary: The celebrated Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.

authors.name: Andrew Osborne, Rhine Samajdar, Andrew A. Houck

papers.title: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times
papers.summary: Following the real-time dynamics of correlated electrons to extended times, at all interaction strengths, remains an open challenge. We address it with an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation (td-gGA). The method extends the Gutzwiller approximation by auxiliary ghost orbitals. It adds more of them whenever the correlations that build up during the dynamics exceed a threshold. This is computationally far more efficient than keeping their number fixed. As a demonstration we take the interaction quench of the half-filled Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. For this paradigmatic problem, numerically exact nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) serves as the reference. A previous td-gGA study with a fixed set of 6 ghost orbitals per spin largely reproduced the available DMFT data. It lacked, however, an error estimate that would support predictions beyond them. With up to 16 ghost orbitals per spin, adaptive td-gGA agrees with DMFT wherever DMFT data are available, from the weak-coupling prethermal regime to the strong-coupling collapse-and-revival regime. At strong coupling it remains converged up to three and a half times as long as the DMFT data. Near the crossover between the two regimes, the system relaxes to thermal values that agree with DMFT. Resolving the dynamics in the number of ghost orbitals shows how the sharp dynamical transition of the Gutzwiller approximation turns into this smooth crossover. In the extended time window at strong coupling, we observe that the oscillation frequency is renormalized as predicted by our second-order strong-coupling expansion. With its built-in error estimate, adaptive td-gGA offers a systematically improvable route to the extended-time dynamics of driven and multi-orbital correlated systems, especially when combined with tensor-network or quantum solvers for the embedding problem.

authors.name: Yong-Xin Yao

papers.title: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
papers.summary: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the non-Abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons, provides a microscopic description of strongly interacting matter, including hadron structure and dynamics. Real-time dynamics and finite-density properties of these systems remain challenging for conventional Monte Carlo methods because of sign problems. Quantum simulation provides a complementary approach, although circuit depth and noise limit digital implementations and non-Abelian gauge-matter interactions remain difficult to engineer in analog systems. Here we realize a non-Abelian lattice gauge model with dynamical matter in an analog cold-atom simulator and directly observe its hadronic dynamics using site- and spin-resolved quantum gas microscopy. This realization is enabled by harnessing two hyperfine states and site-occupation configurations of 87Rb atoms to jointly encode both matter and gauge fields. We tailor resonant tunneling in a spin-dependent optical superlattice to implement a gauge sector of a truncated one-dimensional SU(2) quantum link model with independently tunable mass and gauge coupling. Leveraging this control, we track the conversion of an initially mesonic state into baryonic or vacuum-like configurations through slow mass ramps. Near resonance, we observe coherent oscillations between mesons and baryon-antibaryon pairs and characterize the conversion efficiency as a function of mass, gauge coupling and net baryon density. Our realization establishes an atomic platform for non-Abelian gauge dynamics, opening a route to microscopic studies of nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly interacting matter.

authors.name: Tian-Yi Wang, Wei-Yong Zhang, Tie-Jin Zhong, Ming-Gen He, Zhao-Yu Zhou, Hui Sun, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, Jian-Wei Pan

papers.title: Low-Degree Torus Approximations of the AND Function and $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ Circuits
papers.summary: Torus polynomials, real polynomials evaluated modulo one, were proposed by Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao as a route to $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ lower bounds. We prove degree upper bounds for torus polynomials approximating a function on every input. First, for every $\epsilon\in(0,1/4)$, $\mathsf{AND}_n/2$ has an $\epsilon$-approximating torus polynomial of degree $O(\log(n/\epsilon))$, improving the previous $O(\log^2(n/\epsilon))$. This is optimal up to constant factors for inverse-polynomial error, by a lower bound of Krishan and Vishwanathan, and refutes two superlogarithmic-degree conjectures of Krishan and Sarma. Second, for every Boolean function $g$ computed by a depth-$d$, size-$s$ $\mathsf{AC}^0[m]$ circuit, $g/2$ has an $\epsilon$-approximating torus polynomial of degree at most $C_m^d(\log s)^{\max\{1,\mu-1\}d}\log(1/\epsilon)$, where $\mu$ is the number of distinct prime factors of $m$ and $C_m$ depends only on $m$. This improves the bound $(\log s)^{O_m(d^2)}(\log(1/\epsilon))^{O_m(d)}$ of Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao, making the exponent of $\log s$ linear in the depth and the dependence on $\log(1/\epsilon)$ linear. Both proofs sample terms of a Fourier expansion and approximate them by low-degree torus polynomials. A torus approximation of degree $D$ can be written as a linear combination of at most $(n+1)^D$ parities, called a periodic Fourier representation, which is known to give a non-adaptive measurement-based quantum computation with linear side-processing using one qubit per parity. Hence every $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ function can be computed with quasipolynomially many qubits and inverse-polynomial error probability on every input. Conversely, we prove that a periodic Fourier representation with $r$ parities and error probability $\epsilon$ gives a torus approximation of degree $O(\log(r/\epsilon))$, so the two notions are equivalent.

authors.name: Shuhei Osaki, Ryuhei Mori

papers.title: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions
papers.summary: We investigate the out-of-equilibrium scaling behaviors induced by periodic driving protocols in quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions at zero temperature. We consider two paradigmatic one-dimensional systems: the quantum Ising chain subject to periodic longitudinal fields and the Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, equivalent to a quantum Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Within a renormalization-group (RG) framework, we develop a dynamic scaling theory for both finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, identifying scaling variables associated with the driving amplitude and period. We distinguish between protocols that break the global ${\mathbb Z}_2$ symmetry by coupling to the order parameter and those that preserve it. These two classes of driving exhibit distinct scaling behaviors, with power-law exponents determined by the RG dimensions of the corresponding perturbations. We verify the proposed dynamic scaling theory through numerical simulations of both smooth single-frequency and discontinuous square-wave periodic drivings.

authors.name: Andrea Pelissetto, Davide Rossini, Ettore Vicari

papers.title: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on generalized Bethe trees
papers.summary: We completely classify the generalized Bethe trees $B(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1})$ that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. We prove that such a tree exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if it is a path or a uniform subdivision of either $B(2,3)$ or $B(1,2,3)$. We also determine all transferring pairs and the minimum transfer times.

authors.name: Koushik Bhakta, Bikash Bhattacharjya

papers.title: Conformality lost in Anderson localization in infinite dimensions, and regained in finite dimensions: a phenomenological theory of the Anderson transition in high dimensions
papers.summary: We show that the recent works on Anderson localization when the number of spatial dimensions $d\to\infty$ can be framed into the scenario dubbed it conformality lost [Kaplan et al., Phys. Rev. D 80, 125005 (2009)], which occurs when two fixed points of the RG collide and become complex. This framing makes it natural for a two-parameter scaling flow \`a la Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) to control all the observables of the theory as conjectured in [Vanoni et al., PNAS 121, e2401955121 (2024)]. We also use this as a starting point for an $\epsilon$ expansion of the RG equations in $\epsilon=1/d\ll 1$, and find phenomenological RG equations which fit the numerical results in dimensions $d\gtrsim 4$.

authors.name: Antonello Scardicchio, Carlo Vanoni

papers.title: Exact solution of the Bose-Fermi mixture along the unnesting line
papers.summary: A one-dimensional model of a Bose-Fermi mixture with contact repulsions is exactly solvable via nested Bethe ansatz. That formal solution is here simplified along a special line where the Bethe-ansatz equations can be unnested. The model solution is expressed in terms of the known solutions for the Lieb-Liniger model and the Yang-Gaudin model of attractive spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ fermions in the balanced case. We find explicit analytical results for the ground-state energy, the velocities of excitations, and the Drude weights at weak and strong interactions. At weak interactions, the special line corresponds to the parameter values where the isolated systems of free fermions and weakly interacting bosons have equal velocities.

authors.name: Soham Chandak, Aleksandra Petkovi\'{c}, Zoran Ristivojevic

papers.title: The Capacity of Conference Key Agreement over GHZ Networks
papers.summary: $K$ users share independent GHZ states, each held by a subset of the users, and want a common secret key, using local operations and public classical communication (LOCC). We show that the conference key capacity, the largest number of secret key bits per copy of the resource, equals the key capacity of the classical source obtained by measuring every GHZ state. Measuring first is therefore optimal, even when the users keep quantum memory and communicate over any number of rounds. The capacity also equals the GHZ distillation capacity, the largest number of GHZ states shared by all users obtainable per copy.

authors.name: Hua Sun

papers.title: Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Inhomogeneous Quenches
papers.summary: Entanglement asymmetry is a powerful probe of symmetry breaking and its dynamical restoration following quantum quenches. While extensively studied for homogeneous initial states, its evolution from inhomogeneous initial configurations remains largely unexplored. We investigate a spin-$1/2$ XX chain whose two halves are initially prepared in tilted ferromagnetic states with different tilt angles. Combining generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) and the quasiparticle picture with exact fermionic correlation-matrix calculations, we study the dynamics of entanglement asymmetry. We find good agreement between the two approaches for generic initial configurations and observe the quantum Mpemba effect, whereby states with stronger initial symmetry breaking can restore the symmetry faster. This effect now depends on the subsystem position: while the homogeneous behavior is recovered when the subsystem lies entirely within one of the initially tilted halves, the entanglement-asymmetry curves for subsystems straddling the interface can exhibit multiple crossings or no crossings at all. A notable exception occurs for subsystems entirely within an initially non-tilted half. In this case, GHD predicts vanishing asymmetry, but the exact dynamics generates a small, nonzero asymmetry that can develop a plateau before decaying toward zero. This feature reveals contributions beyond the leading-order hydrodynamic description.

authors.name: Ma\"elle Olivier, Filiberto Ares, Pasquale Calabrese

papers.title: Anomalous front propagation in many-body quantum transport with memory-dependent resetting
papers.summary: We introduce an exactly solvable framework for non-Markovian quantum many-body dynamics based on stochastic resetting with memory. Applicable to arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonians, including interacting systems, our framework provides an exact representation of the dynamics with memory in terms of the corresponding reset-free evolution, which can be accessed either analytically or numerically. We demonstrate the power of this approach by studying domain-wall melting in a one-dimensional chain of noninteracting fermions, obtaining exact analytical results for the density profile, the local structure of the front edge, the extreme-value statistics of the rightmost fermion, and the integrated current. Remarkably, memory transforms ballistic transport into logarithmically slow propagation without arresting spreading. While the macroscopic density profile retains its original scaling function, the front edge broadens as $\sqrt{\ln t}$ rather than $t^{1/3}$ at late times and develops a qualitatively different edge structure. Furthermore, the extreme-value statistics change from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian, while both the mean and variance of the integrated current grow logarithmically in time. Our predictions are in excellent agreement with numerical simulations. These results reveal how memory can fundamentally alter quantum many-body transport and its fluctuations.

authors.name: Gabriele de Mauro, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar

papers.title: The gap persistence theorem for quantum multiparameter estimation
papers.summary: One key aspect of quantum metrology, measurement incompatibility, is evident only through the simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters. The symmetric logarithmic derivative Cramer-Rao bound (SLDCRB), gives the attainable precision, if the optimal measurements for estimating each individual parameter commute with one another. As such, when the optimal measurements do not commute, the SLDCRB is not necessarily attainable. In this regard, the Holevo Cramer-Rao bound (HCRB) plays a fundamental role, providing the ultimate attainable precisions when one allows simultaneous measurements on infinitely many copies of a quantum state. For practical purposes, the Nagaoka Cramer-Rao bound (NCRB), or Nagaoka--Hayashi Cramer-Rao bound (NHCRB), is more relevant, as a lower bound when restricted to measuring quantum states individually. The interplay between these three bounds dictates how rapidly the ultimate metrological precisions can be approached through collective measurements on finite copies of the probe state. In this work we investigate this interplay. For full rank probe states, we prove that if the SLDCRB or HCRB cannot be saturated with measurements on a single copy of the probe state, then they cannot be saturated for any finite number of copies of the probe state. We demonstrate that these results do not necessarily hold for rank deficient states. As an application of this result, we show that it is impossible to saturate the HCRB for several physically motivated problems, including the simultaneous estimation of phase and phase diffusion. Finally, for practical purposes it is more relevant to study the rate at which the NHCRB converges to the HCRB. We prove that given $M$ copies of the probe state, the NHCRB converges to the HCRB at rate of at least $1/\sqrt{M}$.

authors.name: Lorc\'an O. Conlon, Jun Suzuki, Ping Koy Lam, Syed M. Assad

papers.title: Minimum Hilbert--Schmidt distance for pure states of Schmidt rank two
papers.summary: The Hilbert-Schmidt norm is not contractive under general completely positive trace-preserving maps. This fact alone does not decide whether distance from the separable set decreases under a restricted class of entanglement transformations. For bipartite pure states with two nonzero Schmidt coefficients, we give a self-contained derivation of the minimum distance and its closest separable state. We prove global optimality of the boundary construction previously conjectured by Witte and Trucks and show that the result is unchanged by embedding the state in larger local Hilbert spaces. An explicit product-state decomposition certifies separability, and the embedded optimizer also minimizes distance over the full PPT set. The squared distance has a simple branch above a golden-ratio threshold and a cubic branch below it. A bound on the physical cubic root gives a direct proof that both the distance and its square are non-increasing under deterministic LOCC transformations between pure states of Schmidt rank at most two. Unrestricted two-qubit PPT optimization independently verifies the formulas, while Rust Gilbert iterations give separable upper bounds.

authors.name: Palash Pandya

papers.title: Asymmetry Amplification by a Nonadiabatic Passage through a Critical Point
papers.summary: We propose and solve a minimal model of dynamic passage through a second-order phase transition in the presence of symmetry breaking interactions and no dissipation. Our model generalizes the Hamiltonian dynamics of the Painleve'-2 equation to the case with many degrees of freedom, while maintaining the integrability property. The evolution eventually leads to a highly asymmetric state, no matter how weak the symmetry breaking parameter of the Hamiltonian is. This suggests a potential mechanism for strong asymmetry in the production of quasi-particles with nearly identical characteristics. The model's integrability also yields exact exponents for the scaling of the density of the nonadiabatically excited quasi-particles.

authors.name: Bhavay Tyagi, Fumika Suzuki, Vladimir A. Chernyak, Nikolai A. Sinitsyn

papers.title: Quantum state engineering of light using intensity measurements and post-selection
papers.summary: Quantum state engineering of light is of great interest for quantum technologies, particularly generating non-classical states of light, and is often studied through conditioning approaches. Recently, we demonstrated that state engineering approaches can be applied in intense laser-atom interactions to obtain measurement statistics which resemble optical "cat" states by using intensity measurements and classical post-selection of the measurement data. Post-processing of the finite-size sampled data set allows to select specific events, here the processes which are energy conserving, corresponding to measurement statistics of non-classical states of light. However, to fully realize the potential of this method for quantum state engineering, it is crucial to thoroughly investigate the role of the involved measurements and the finite-size nature of the post-selection scheme. We illustrate this by analyzing the post-selection approach recently developed for high harmonic generation, which enables the generation of optical cat states bright enough to induce non-linear phenomena. These findings provide significant guidance for quantum light engineering and the generation of intense optical cat states with potential applications in non-linear optics and quantum science.

authors.name: J. Rivera-Dean, Th. Lamprou, E. Pisanty, M. F. Ciappina, P. Tzallas, M. Lewenstein, P. Stammer

papers.title: Bare-ancilla fault-tolerant syndrome extraction: General extensions of distance-three codes and structural criteria for graph codes
papers.summary: The reliability of quantum computation critically depends on the performance of quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs). Performance of QECCs can be severely degraded by hook errors, which effectively reduce the code distance. We develop a systematic framework for bare-ancilla syndrome extraction in $[[n,k,3]]$ stabilizer codes. It provides a criterion for a specific single ancilla fault model and jointly searches for suitable stabilizer generators and data-ancilla interaction orders to correct hook errors. We call such stabilizer generator sets bare-ancilla codes (BACs). We also present two constructions that enlarge the set of valid BACs while preserving minimum distance, either by keeping the number of logical qubits fixed or by increasing it. Under the correlated-data error model, $3177$ $[[7,1,3]]$ graph codes are found to be BACs out of $3379$ and all $335415$ $[[8,1,3]]$ graph codes are BACs. We tested $500$ $[[7,1,3]]$ and $1000$ $[[8,1,3]]$ graph codes in the presence of anisotropic and depolarizing noise. The number of data-ancilla interactions is an important predictor of the pseudo-threshold of these graph codes. In the analyzed codes, the BAC, which works with the bare ancilla method, usually performs well or better than the flag method, particularly for depolarizing noise. Notably, we report new bare ancilla codes, namely $[[6,1,3]]$ and $[[7,1,3]]$ with improved code rate compared to the bare code used in the work of Muyuan Li \emph{et al.} and Maheshwari \emph{et al.} respectively.

authors.name: Harsh Gupta, Mainak Bhattacharyya, Ritik Jain, Ankur Raina

papers.title: Hong-Ou-Mandel interference of more than 10 indistinguishable atoms
papers.summary: When two indistinguishable bosons interfere at a beam splitter, they both exit through the same output port. This foundational quantum-mechanical phenomenon, known as the Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) effect, has become a cornerstone in the field of quantum information. It also extends to many indistinguishable particles, resulting in complex interference patterns. However, despite of its fundamental and applied interest, the many-particle effect has only been observed in notoriously lossy photonic systems, but a realization with atomic systems has remained elusive until now. Here, we demonstrate HOM interference with up to 12 indistinguishable neutral atoms in a system with negligible loss. Our single-particle counting clearly reveals parity oscillations, a bunching envelope and genuine multi-partite entanglement, defining features of the multi-particle HOM effect. Exploiting HOM interference, we demonstrate a Heisenberg scaling of metrological sensitivities achievable with the generated quantum states. Our technique holds the potential to scale to significantly larger numbers, with wide-ranging applications from high-precision atom interferometry to multi-particle Bell tests.

authors.name: Martin Quensen, Mareike Hetzel, Luis Santos, Augusto Smerzi, G\'eza T\'oth, Luca Pezz\`e, Carsten Klempt

papers.title: Hardware-tailored logical Clifford circuits for stabilizer codes
papers.summary: Quantum error correction is the art of protecting fragile quantum information through suitable encoding and active interventions. However, it is notoriously difficult to manipulate encoded quantum data without causing uncorrectable errors. Here, we introduce a mathematical framework for constructing hardware-tailored circuits that implement any desired Clifford unitary on the logical level of any given stabilizer code. We formulate this task as a discrete optimization problem that minimizes the number of CZ gates while naturally incorporating a parameterization of all Clifford stabilizers. Despite the intrinsic difficulty of the circuit compilation problem, our methods scale to at least $16$ physical qubits. Because our circuits require very few CZ gates, they provide excellent starting points for constructing fault-tolerant implementations using flag gadgets. Using a brute-force search, we develop several such flag gadgets, including weakly fault-tolerant logical Hadamard circuits for the $[[8,3,2]]$ code that require an unprecedentedly small number of physical two-qubit gates. Our work introduces both the mathematics and software for compiling hardware-tailored logical Clifford circuits. From a broader perspective, we turn away from the standard generator decomposition and instead focus on the holistic compilation of entire logical circuits, leading to significant savings in practice.

authors.name: Eric J. Kuehnke, Kyano Levi, Joschka Roffe, Jens Eisert, Daniel Miller

papers.title: Correlations and quantum circuits with dynamical causal order
papers.summary: Requiring that the causal structure between different parties is well-defined imposes constraints on the correlations they can establish, which define so-called causal correlations. Some of these are known to have a "dynamical" causal order in the sense that their causal structure is not fixed a priori but is instead established on the fly, with for instance the causal order between future parties depending on some choice of action of parties in the past. Here we identify a new way that the causal order between the parties can be dynamical: with at least four parties, there can be some dynamical order which can nevertheless not be influenced by the actions of past parties. This leads us to introduce an intermediate class of correlations with what we call non-influenceable causal order, in between the set of correlations with static (non-dynamical) causal order and the set of general causal correlations. We then define analogous classes of quantum processes, considering recently introduced classes of quantum circuits with classical or quantum control of causal order---the latter being the largest class within the process matrix formalism known to have a clear interpretation in terms of coherent superpositions of causal orders. This allows us to formalise precisely in which sense certain quantum processes can have both indefinite and dynamical causal order.

authors.name: Rapha\"el Mothe, Alastair A. Abbott, Cyril Branciard

papers.title: Real-time adaptive quantum error correction by multi-agent learning
papers.summary: Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, yet existing approaches rely on static assumptions about noise that break down in realistic hardware where error channels drift over time. We introduce a unified framework that separates QEC into two learning timescales: offline code discovery and online adaptation. Offline, Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) autonomously discovers complete QEC cycles as explicit quantum circuits, with separate agents responsible for encoding, syndrome extraction, and error recovery, and without prescribing a code family or circuit ansatz. Online, a lightweight adaptive layer, termed Bandit Retraining for Adaptive Variational Error Correction (BRAVE), realigns the discovered code with the drifting error channel through a transversal single-unit rotation, while a bandit controller decides from the syndrome record when an update is worth its cost. Updates are applied during operation, without decoding the logical state or retraining the MARL stack, and follow drifts on timescales of order $0.1$ s and longer. This yields a "discover once, adapt online" strategy that combines the flexibility of learned codes with real-time adaptation to non-stationary noise. At sufficiently high sampling rates relative to noise drift, our method reduces logical infidelity by up to 3.1-fold for qubit codes and 3.4-fold for qutrit codes compared to the strongest static alternative at each error rate, including a perfect code using two more physical units, while substantially extending robustness to noise fluctuations. These results establish a paradigm in which QEC is no longer static but dynamically optimized for realistic quantum hardware.

authors.name: Manuel Guatto, Francesco Preti, Michael Schilling, Tommaso Calarco, Francisco Andr\'es C\'ardenas-L\'opez, Felix Motzoi

papers.title: Dynamical quantum codes and logic gates on a lattice with sparse connectivity
papers.summary: We introduce several dynamical schemes that take advantage of mid-circuit measurement and nearest-neighbor gates on a lattice with maximum vertex degree three to implement topological codes and perform logic gates between them. We first review examples of Floquet codes and their implementation with nearest-neighbor gates and ancillary qubits. Next, we describe implementations of these Floquet codes that make use of the ancillary qubits to reset all qubits every measurement cycle. We then show how switching the role of data and ancilla qubits allows a pair of Floquet codes to be implemented simultaneously. We describe how to perform a logical Clifford gate to entangle a pair of Floquet codes that are implemented in this way. Finally, we show how switching between the color code and a pair of Floquet codes, via a depth-two circuit followed by mid-circuit measurement, can be used to perform syndrome extraction for the color code.

authors.name: Dominic J. Williamson, Bence Het\'enyi

papers.title: Decoding Multimode Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Codes with Noisy Auxiliary States
papers.summary: In order to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computing, we make use of quantum error correction schemes designed to protect the logical information of the system from decoherence. A promising way to preserve such information is to use the multimode Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) encoding, which encodes logical qubits into several harmonic oscillators. In this work, we focus on decoding the measurements obtained from Steane-type quantum error correction protocols for multimode GKP codes. We propose a decoder that considers the noise present on the auxiliary states, more specifically by tracking the correlations between errors on different modes spreading throughout the error-correction circuit. We show that leveraging the correlations between measurement results and the actual error affecting the multimode GKP state can decrease the logical error probability by at least an order of magnitude, yielding more robust quantum computation.

authors.name: Marc-Antoine Roy, Thomas Pousset, Baptiste Royer

papers.title: Rotational Asymmetry beyond Phase Rigidity in Non-Hermitian Eigenfunctions
papers.summary: Phase rigidity, the standard measure of eigenvector nonorthogonality, vanishes at an exceptional point (EP). We show that this collapse need not imply phase spreading and can mask persistent phase organization. Using quantum and classical relative entropies linked by the Holevo bound and the phase--Fourier entropic uncertainty relation, we uncover rotational asymmetry within this organization. In both a classical microcavity and quantum hydrogen, phase entropies peak and Fourier entropies dip on a broad parameter scale. Near the EP, one branch gains rotational asymmetry while the other loses it despite common rigidity loss. Changes in quantum rotational asymmetry dominate those in classical asymmetry, consistent with the weak-pattern scaling of the uncertainty gap. This hidden phase organization predicts testable probe-induced splitting axes relevant to EP sensing and allows distinct rotational asymmetries at fixed geometric imaginarity. Rotational asymmetry thus reveals non-Hermitian eigenfunction structure beyond nonorthogonality.

authors.name: Kyu-Won Park, Soojoon Lee, Kabgyun Jeong

papers.title: Approximate Decoherence, Recoherence and Records in Isolated Quantum Systems
papers.summary: Using the framework of decoherent histories, we study which past events leave detectable records in isolated quantum systems under the realistic assumption that decoherence is approximate and not perfect. Using tools from quantum state discrimination, we establish asymptotically for a large class of (pseudo-)random histories how the strength of decoherence changes the number of reliable records, i.e., we quantitatively answer the question: when can approximate decoherence be approximated by exact decoherence? In addition, we reveal a clear decoherence structure for long histories based on a numerically exact solution of a random matrix model that, as we argue, captures generic aspects of decoherence. In particular, we observe strong recoherences for maverick histories that are statistical outliers with respect to Born's rule. From the perspective of the Many Worlds Interpretation, our results reveal a "branch selection problem" and shed light on the emergence of Born's rule and the theory confirmation problem.

authors.name: Philipp Strasberg, Joseph Schindler, Jiaozi Wang, Andreas Winter

papers.title: Detailed, interpretable characterization of mid-circuit measurement on a transmon qubit
papers.summary: Mid-circuit measurements (MCMs) are critical components of the quantum error correction protocols expected to enable utility-scale quantum computing. MCMs can be modeled by quantum instruments (a type of quantum operation or process), which can be characterized self-consistently using gate set tomography. However, experimentally estimated quantum instruments are often hard to interpret or relate to device physics. We address this challenge by adapting the error generator formalism -- previously used to interpret noisy quantum gates by decomposing their error processes into physically meaningful sums of "elementary errors" -- to MCMs. We deploy our new analysis on a transmon qubit device to tease out and quantify error mechanisms including amplitude damping, readout error, and imperfect collapse. We examine in detail how the magnitudes of these errors vary with the readout pulse amplitude, recover the key features of dispersive readout predicted by theory, and show that these features can be modeled parsimoniously using a reduced model with just a few parameters.

authors.name: Piper C. Wysocki, Luke D. Burkhart, Madeline H. Morocco, Corey I. Ostrove, Riley J. Murray, Tristan Brown, Jeffrey M. Gertler, David K. Kim, Nathan E. Miller, Bethany M. Niedzielski, Katrina M. Sliwa, Robin Blume-Kohout, Gabriel O. Samach, Mollie E. Schwartz, Kenneth M. Rudinger

papers.title: The emergence of classical stochasticity
papers.summary: We examine the emergence of classical stochasticity for a quantum system governed by a Pauli-type master equation. It is well-known that while such equations describe the evolution of probabilities, they do not automatically justify reasoning based on the assumption that the system exists in a definite state at intermediate times. On the other hand, we show that this assumption is crucial for the standard calculation of stochastic times such as the persistent time and the time of first arrivals. It is also curious to point out that the standard derivation of the Pauli master equation based on the Fermi Golden Rule actually proceeds by assuming that the system remains in a definite state as the starting point to derive the transition rate to a different state. By studying the so-called ultradecoherence limit, we show that the Pauli master equation can also be arrived at without such an assumption. Instead, that the system exists in a definite state has to be justified by a different argument. We then consider examples of single particles, bosons, and fermions in the ultradecoherence limit to illustrate how classical stochasticity may emerge from quantum mechanics.

authors.name: Xuan Du Trinh, Isma\"el Septembre, Hai-Chau Nguyen

papers.title: Scalable testing of quantum error correction
papers.summary: The standard method for benchmarking quantum error correction is Monte Carlo sampling. However, direct estimation of rare logical failures through unconditional Monte Carlo sampling can be prohibitively expensive, even with efficient simulators such as stim. In this paper, we present a scalable approach that combines stratified fault injection with extrapolation. Our insight is that some of the fault space can be sampled efficiently, after which extrapolation is sufficient to complete the testing task. As a result, our tool scales to distance 17 for a physical error rate of 0.0005 with a two-hour time budget on a desktop, while Monte Carlo sampling using \stim observed 0 logical errors at distance 13 with the same time budget. At distance 17, ScaLER estimated a logical error rate of $1.51 \times 10^{-11}$ with high confidence.

authors.name: John Zhuoyang Ye, Jens Palsberg

papers.title: Scalable quantum resources with short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains
papers.summary: The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range or power-law couplings that decay too quickly for this purpose. We demonstrate that two spin-$\tfrac12$ chain models -- a staggered nearest-neighbor XXX chain and a long-range XXZ chain -- develop an effective OAT nonlinearity when projected onto the symmetric sector. We show that these dynamics generate metrologically useful spin-squeezed states and Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger coherences that ensure violation of many-body Bell inequalities. We confirm the accuracy of this mapping by comparing it to the exact dynamics and demonstrate that the generated correlations can be read out using a single probe qubit. The resulting dynamics can be simulated with analog and digital quantum simulators.

authors.name: Marcin P{\l}odzie\'n, Jan Chwede\'nczuk

papers.title: Fermionic entanglement and quantum correlation measures in molecules
papers.summary: We analyze fermionic entanglement and correlation measures in the ground and the low temperature thermal state of the water molecule as a function of the internuclear distance in the context of the full configuration interaction approach. The aim is to obtain a general entanglement based characterization of the electronic eigenstates. We consider first the spin-up - spin-down partition and the associated Schmidt decomposition, examining the total up-down entanglement of the electronic wave function. We then consider the one- and two-body entanglement derived from the one- and two-body reduced density matrices (DMs), which measure the deviation of the state from a Slater determinant (SD). All blocks of these DMs are examined. We also introduce and analyze new measures like the up-down two-body mutual information, which measures the up-down correlation at the two-body level, and two types of two-body negativities, the latter detecting and measuring the "inner" entanglement of the reduced two-body DMs, i.e., their deviation from a convex mixture of SDs. Finally, the dissociation limit is also analyzed, considering both the exact ground state (GS) as well as the thermal state in the zero temperature limit, representing the projector onto the "GS band" of almost degenerate lowest lying eigenstates.

authors.name: J. Garcia, J. A. Cianciulli, R. Rossignoli

papers.title: Learning Cut Distributions with Quantum Optimization
papers.summary: The probabilistic nature of quantum computation can be an asset rather than an obstacle for combinatorial optimization. In this work, we tackle the problem in which the sampled distribution itself is the object being optimized. This perspective is especially natural for fairness, coverage, and robustness objectives, where success is determined by the least-protected components rather than by average or best performance. We develop this idea by learning graph cut distributions. The resulting framework turns Fair Cut Cover into a native quantum distribution-learning problem and uses quantum circuits as trainable generators of cut distributions. We prove that standard QAOA at depth one achieves higher Fair Cut Cover values than optimal Semidefinite programming plus Gaussian hyperplane rounding on complete graphs with at least four vertices. We further establish a separation on a family of high-girth graphs using published QAOA evaluations, compare against a classical column-generation heuristic in numerical experiments, and examine finite-sampling and noise effects in quantum hardware implementations. These results suggest a broader role for this type of quantum algorithms: not merely finding good bitstrings, but learning useful combinatorial distributions for worst- and average-case-aware optimization.

authors.name: Bao Bach, Cameron Ibrahim, Reuben Tate, Jad Salem, Stephan Eidenbenz, Ilya Safro

papers.title: Coherence Transfer in Quantum Networks
papers.summary: Detecting coherence transfer in complex quantum networks is challenging under uncharacterized experimental conditions and with limited access to the system. Here, we use the coexistence of static and dynamic coherence to derive a nonlinear criterion for coherence transfer. The criterion applies even when the verification capabilities of checkpoint nodes are uncharacterized. It requires only minimal one-network output analysis, up to the number of output state dimensions. Each output requires only two-setting measurements of state populations, regardless of the network size. The criterion is general for both spatial and temporal networks, including those with multiple coherence sources, and applies to quantum transport in solid-state nanostructures. Experimentally, using entanglement swapping, we transfer polarization-entangled pairs in four- and six-photon entanglement networks. The criterion provides experimental evidence of coherence transfer in multiphoton entanglement networks. Our findings provide a practical tool for investigating the presence, role, or function of coherence transfer in quantum networks.

authors.name: Chun-Yang Lin, Yu-Cheng Li, Shih-Hsuan Chen, Sheng-Yan Sun, Ching-Jui Huang, Kuan-Jou Wang, Che-Ming Li

papers.title: Quantum Fisher Information and Separable Energy Minima in Spin Systems
papers.summary: We develop a general method to bound the minimum energy of spin Hamiltonians over separable states with fixed single-particle reduced density matrices. The method uses a two-particle optimization and identifies conditions under which the resulting bound is tight. For ferromagnetic Ising and Ising-like interactions on any regular graph, we obtain an exact separable-energy minimum expressed through the quantum Fisher information (QFI) of the local state; a symmetric separable state attains the optimal correlation on every bond. For fully connected ferromagnetic Ising-like systems, ground-state correlations give a lower estimate of this single-particle QFI with a rigorous O(1/N) finite-size error. Further exact results relate symmetric-separable minima of antiferromagnetic Ising-like and XY-like models to local expectation values, and ferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg chains to quantum fidelity. We also derive bounds for separability across fixed partitions into contiguous blocks.

authors.name: G\'eza T\'oth, J\'ozsef Pitrik

papers.title: ffsim: faster simulation of fermionic quantum circuits
papers.summary: We present ffsim, an open-source software library for fast simulation of fermionic quantum circuits. ffsim exploits conservation of particle number and the z component of spin, symmetries present in a wide range of fermionic systems, to dramatically reduce memory usage and simulation time compared to general-purpose quantum circuit simulators. Compared to FQE, a library with similar functionality, ffsim differs in software design and is faster on a representative set of simulation benchmarks. Beyond state vector evolution by basic fermionic gates, ffsim offers a number of additional features including variational ansatzes, Hamiltonian time evolution via Trotter-Suzuki product formulas, efficient sampling of Slater determinants, seamless integration with Qiskit and PySCF, and comprehensive documentation. We demonstrate ffsim's capabilities on scientific applications, including a 64-qubit Hubbard model with 8 electrons. ffsim's source code and documentation are available via https://github.com/Qiskit/ffsim.

authors.name: Kevin J. Sung, Inho Choi, Mirko Amico, Bartholomew Andrews, Esra Ayantuna, Hrishikesh Belagali, Yukio Kawashima, Ryan LaRose, Wan-Hsuan Lin, David Omanovic, Samuele Piccinelli, Javier Robledo Moreno, Abdullah Ash Saki, James Shee, Soyoung Shin, Sabyrzhan Tasbolatov, Minh C. Tran, Kento Ueda, Haimeng Zhang, Mario Motta

papers.title: Unified entropy entanglement
papers.summary: The unified entropy as a generalization of the von Neumann entropy exhibits distinct diversity which contains the Tsallis entropy, the R\'{e}nyi entropy, the von Neumann entropy as special cases. The unified-($r,t$) entropy entanglement with $01$ and $qs\geq1$ and show that it is also an entanglement monotone and that both of them are monogamous. Going further, we present a global multipartite entanglement measure (GlMEM) based on the unified entropy and it has two subclasses which are classified by the parameters $(q,s)$ and $(r,t)$. Consequently, from the view of the complete multipartite entanglement measure theory, we show that one of them is a complete multipartite entanglement monotone and is not only completely monogamous but also tightly completely monogamous, but the other one is even not complete. We also explore the genuine entanglement measures induced by the unified entropy and the relations with the bipartite entanglement and the global entanglement are discussed, respectively.

authors.name: Wenxue Ren, Binghao Li, Ruiqun Niu, Yu Guo, Shuanping Du

papers.title: Minimum-Length Permutation-Invariant Qudit Codes from Edge-Colorings of Complete Graphs
papers.summary: We study permutation-invariant quantum codes in the symmetric subspace $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathbb{C}^q)$ of $n$ qudits of local dimension $q$. For every integer $q\ge 2$, we construct a permutation-invariant code with parameters $((4,q,2))_q$. Thus four physical qudits suffice to encode one logical qudit with distance two in the symmetric sector for every local dimension. We also show, using a self-contained decoupling and rank argument, that no permutation-invariant code of dimension $q$ and distance at least $2$ exists in $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathbb{C}^q)$ for $n\le 3$. Hence four qudits are necessary and sufficient. The construction has simple representation-theoretic and combinatorial descriptions. On $\mathrm{Sym}^4(\mathbb{C}^q)$, the distance-two Knill--Laflamme conditions split into root and Cartan parts. By restricting supports to the even-entry occupation layer, all root-error conditions vanish automatically. The remaining Cartan conditions reduce to linear balancing constraints on packets of occupation vectors. These packets admit a natural graph-theoretic interpretation in terms of the vertices and edges of the complete graph $K_q$: for odd $q$, they are organized by the midpoint rule, while for even $q$, they are organized by a decomposition of $K_q$ into perfect matchings. In this way, the existence of minimum-length $((4,q,2))_q$ permutation-invariant codes is reduced to a parity-dependent edge-coloring problem on $K_q$.

authors.name: Eric Kubischta, Ian Teixeira

papers.title: Fourier analysis of quantum neural network with non-linear data embedding
papers.summary: Fourier analysis has become a crucial tool for understanding the expressivity of Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) models, as well as an important indicator of barren plateaus. While existing literature has only studied angle-embedded VQCs in a noiseless environment, here we develop the Fourier analysis of VQCs with non-linear data embedding, with particular focus on amplitude embedding, as it provides a naturally compact encoding scheme. We first investigate a difference in the domain of input features that leads to a distinct expressivity of the zero-frequency Fourier coefficient. Assuming that the unitaries generated from the parameter space forms at least a unitary 2-design, we derive that, in integer-valued frequencies, the mean of the Fourier coefficients is concentrated at zero, and the variance is upper bounded by an inverse power-law function with respect to the infinity norm of the frequency. A numerical evidence of exponentially decaying pattern with respect to the frequency magnitude is also established, providing a frequency-perspective of viewing VQC model expressivity and its trainability. When a noise channel with unitary Kraus operators and probabilities $\{p_k\}$ is taken into account, the variance is further suppressed by a factor $\left(\sum_kp_k^2\right)^{Q}<1$ for $Q$ as the number of channel instances applied. Furthermore, we demonstrate and validate the analytical results through simulations, both noiseless and noisy, and contrast its expressivity against the angle-embedded Fourier features. We also examine the model's performance where target functions contains non-integer frequencies. Our results establish a rigorous Fourier framework for amplitude-encoded VQCs, offering both theoretical guarantees on expressivity, hence trainability scaling in the frequency domain, as well as practical simulations for deployment on noisy quantum devices.

authors.name: Haiyue Kang, Martin Sevior, Muhammad Usman

papers.title: Quantum Computing Algebra (QCA), the theory and implementation
papers.summary: We present a real geometric algebra framework designed for the direct translation of the Dirac formalism into geometric algebra representations. Unlike previous approaches based on positive-definite signatures, QCA employs a split-signature construction that enables a natural realization of quantum states and operators while simplifying computational implementation. We further present an implementation of QCA using the \textit{GAALOP} software and show how quantum gates and multi-qubit systems can be efficiently represented and generated computationally. As an application, we demonstrate the use of QCA in quantum game theory, where the real-algebraic formulation provides computational advantages for modeling entangled strategies and quantum interactions. The proposed framework establishes a practical bridge between the abstract formalism of quantum computation and efficient geometric algebra implementations.

authors.name: Jaroslav Hrdina, Dietmar Hildenbrand, Oliver Rettig

papers.title: From spectral structure to sensing limits in quantum thermometry
papers.summary: The precision of a quantum thermometer is fundamentally constrained by the spectral structure of the probe itself, and a systematic mapping between the configurations of energy levels and thermometric performance provides relevant information to design optimized devices. In this work, we establish such a mapping by analyzing a broad class of quantum systems, ranging from finite spin ensembles and degenerate atoms to confining potentials, quantum walks, and continuous-spectrum models. We derive exact scaling laws for the quantum Fisher information, revealing two distinct high-temperature universality classes: finite-spectrum probes exhibit a $T^{-4}$ decay, while unbounded or continuous spectra yield a slower $T^{-2}$ decay. At low temperatures, we show that sensitivity, though universally exponentially suppressed, can be enhanced arbitrarily by engineering degenerate excited states or a quantum walk on a fully connected topology. By contrast, specific quantum walk topologies provide a distinct enhancement mechanism based on gap engineering, whereby an optimal network size yields an optimized $T^{-2}$ low-temperature scaling. Furthermore, power-law spectra enable tunable scaling of thermometric performance with system size, offering a design principle for optimal probes in specific temperature windows. Our results contribute to transform spectral information into a resource for quantum thermometry, providing both fundamental bounds and practical guidelines to tailored temperature sensing.

authors.name: Youssef Aiache, Simone Cavazzoni, Abderrahim El Allati, Paolo Bordone, Matteo G. A. Paris

papers.title: A loss-limited optimum for fixed uniform multi-pass quantum sensing per absorbed photon
papers.summary: Multi-pass schemes send a photon through a sample several times to learn more about it. When the sample rather than the light is scarce, the natural figure of merit is the information gained per photon the object absorbs. We show that three properties fix the loss-limited optimum of every fixed scheme in which a single photon passes repeatedly and uniformly through the sample and is detected once at the end: a payoff that grows as the square of the pass number, the same survival probability on every pass, and no dose from a photon already lost. They force a single trade-off function $h(x)=x^2/(e^x-1)$, where $x$ is the number of passes times the loss per pass. Its maximum, 0.648, sits at $x_{\rm opt}=1.594$. The multi-pass optima of Koppell and Kasevich and of Yu et al. are two instances, and the loss-limited ceiling of interaction-free interrogation is a third when its payoff is counted as conclusive detections. Phase sensing of a weakly absorbing object is optimal at $m_{\rm opt}=x_{\rm opt}/(\epsilon+\alpha)$ passes; the absorption $\alpha$ and the parasitic loss $\epsilon$ enter the optimum only through their sum, but the damage counts only $\alpha$. N00N states and their loss-robust generalisations do worse per absorbed photon, and optimising over photon and pass number returns a single recycled photon; Gaussian probes and chains tailored pass by pass lie outside this class and can exceed its ceiling by a bounded factor. Absorption estimation gains nothing, for any scheme. Above the crosstalk crossover of the mode sorter, detecting a faint companion below the Rayleigh limit costs the companion a dose independent of its faintness; below it, and under direct imaging at any separation, the dose grows without bound as the companion fades. Among single photons and path-entangled number states, the gentlest measurement of a fragile sample is also the simplest: a single photon, recycled.

authors.name: Christoph F. Wildfeuer

papers.title: Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios with Agent-like Observers on Quantum Computers
papers.summary: The Wigner's friend thought experiment raises the question of whether quantum theory can be applied consistently to systems that include observers. Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios include spatially separate observers sharing entanglement. In the Local Friendliness (LF) framework, these scenarios lead to experimentally testable inequalities derived from Absoluteness of Observed Events and Local Agency, assumptions weaker than those needed for Bell inequalities. Their violation therefore has stronger implications, but LF tests are more experimentally challenging because they require an observer implemented as a quantum system. Drawing from the literature on artificial intelligence, we implement the "friend" with explicit agent-like functionality in a reversible quantum circuit. The agents store measurement outcomes, condition subsequent operations on stored information, and, in the most structured case, use Born-rule probabilities to bet on outcomes of their own future observations based on past observations. We study the circuits through ideal simulations, simulations using an IBM-device noise model, and experiments on the IBM processor ibm_marrakesh. Ideal simulations reproduce the maximal quantum violation of an LF inequality up to finite-shot fluctuations, while hardware runs show positive LF violations for all agents. These results are a step towards more sophisticated agent-like observer models in LF experiments on quantum computers. By focusing on functionality rather than size alone, this approach complements tests of quantum theory in the macroscopic regime and opens a direction for studying agents whose use of quantum theory is implemented within coherently controlled quantum dynamics.

authors.name: Joshua Laux, Eric G. Cavalcanti

papers.title: Indistinguishability Theory for Identical Particles with Invariant Degrees of Freedom
papers.summary: Identical particles have dynamically invariant labels in all setups where their degrees of freedom can be partitioned into two parts, which we call internal and visible, with the visible part subject to unitary evolution, while the dynamically invariant internal part accounts for the partial distinguishability of particles. We give the explicit form of the visible state in terms of the indistinguishability function, generalizing the standard symmetrization/antisymmetrization postulate for bosons/fermions with internal modes. The indistinguishability function on the symmetric group accounts for the permutation symmetry of the dynamically invariant label state and gives a self-contained description of the symmetry spectrum of the visible state. It is shown that the indistinguishability of single particles emitted independently from a stable source is completely characterized by the projective measures on the symmetry spectrum. We reveal a hierarchy of successive upper bounds on the projective measure of indistinguishability in terms of marginal projective measures. We point out an experimentally feasible way to get the upper bounds on the indistinguishability of an arbitrarily large number of single photons by direct experimental readout of their marginal projective measures. We also analyze the indistinguishability of coherent superpositions and convex mixtures and resolve a recently posed problem.

authors.name: Valery Shchesnovich

papers.title: Anomalous Hardening of a Fluctuation-Induced Gap
papers.summary: In a mean-field picture, a gap opened by quantum fluctuations grows with them. This can fail if the fluctuating mode is critical and its displacement compensates its coupling to the degenerate states. A single parameter sets the gap response: above a universal threshold, the gap hardens as the critical fluctuations weaken. Whenever the parameter is nonzero, overcompensation beyond the critical point drives a secondary phase transition. In a quantum Rabi ring with synthetic flux, exact diagonalization shows the gap of a photonic Landau level rising by 15% as the critical variance falls by 25%.

authors.name: Shu He, Liwei Duan

papers.title: Quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization
papers.summary: We introduce a quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization. Quantum dynamics based on quantum annealing (QA) or the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is used to engineer the transition kernel. Increasing the annealing time in QA or the number of layers in QAOA enables transitions to explore distant configurations while suppressing large energy changes. The Hamming-space delocalization originates from operator spreading, whereas the energy-space localization arises from a dynamically generated correlation. For optimization, we propose quantum-echo local optimization. For the ferromagnetic Ising chain, increasing the annealing time or circuit depth yields a nearly quadratic improvement in the dependence of the mean first-passage time on the inverse optimality gap compared with random single-spin flips. For the random Ising model, increasing these parameters initially improves optimization performance, whereas further increases degrade performance in QA and lead to saturation in QAOA. Quantum-echo greedy descent substantially improves the performance, highlighting the complementary roles of quantum dynamics in exploration and greedy descent in exploitation. These results establish quantum-echo dynamics as a framework for engineering structured transition kernels and provide a route to using finite-resource quantum many-body dynamics as a computational primitive for iterative optimization.

authors.name: Tatsuhiko Shirai

papers.title: Analytic construction of dimension-dependent steering witnesses from generalized equiangular measurements
papers.summary: In this work, we construct a dimension-dependent family of generalized equiangular measurements (GEAMs) that gives explicit steering witnesses in every prime dimension $d$. The construction consists of \(d-1\) mutually unbiased measurements and an additional normalized family of \(2d-1\) Hermitian operators, which is a $(1,2d-1)$-POVM {(POVM denotes a positive, operator-valued measure).} For odd prime dimensions, we reduce the noncentral operators to three-dimensional invariant subspaces and solve the central operator in a two-dimensional subspace. We combine complementary Gershgorin bounds from two unitarily equivalent matrix representations to obtain a fully analytic asymmetric interval for {a parameter} that guarantees positivity. The {qubit and qutrit cases} are treated separately. Finally, using a maximally entangled realization and the local-hidden-state bound for GEAMs, we obtain an explicit steering inequality and a sufficient criterion for quantum violation in every prime dimension.

authors.name: Adam Rutkowski, Katarzyna Siudzi\'{n}ska

papers.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
papers.summary: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length $T$, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on $[0,T]$. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on $O(n\log n)$ windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range $O(\log N)$, has expected error $O(N^{-b}+T^{-1})$ while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.

authors.name: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

papers.title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
papers.summary: A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs.
