For an impurity injected into the Fermi sea we have the following: at infinite coupling the average impurity momentum relaxes completely in the thermodynamic limit, while at finite coupling relaxation remains incomplete. The closed-form matrix elements turn the spectral representation of the average impurity momentum into explicit finite sums over eigenstates. We evaluate the post-injection dynamics, resolve the quantum-flutter oscillations and the approach towards the diagonal-ensemble value, and map the stationary momentum as a function of the injection momentum and the coupling. Finally, we analyse the thermodynamic limit and its asymptotics as an integral over Fredholm determinants.

authors.name: Felipe Taha Sant'Ana

papers.title: Covalent Welding of Two-Dimensional Molecular Sheets into Ultra-Stiff, Super-Tough Polymeric Networks
papers.summary: Since the inception of macromolecular science, polymers have been constructed from zero-dimensional monomers, a paradigm that funnels all stress through discrete one-dimensional chains. Driven by conformational entropy, polymer chains inevitably coil in three-dimensional space, precluding effective stress transfer, thereby compromising the ultimate mechanical performance. Two-dimensional (2D) molecular sheets, with intrinsic in-plane rigidity, could in principle circumvent this constraint. Yet in existing assemblies, where stress transfers efficiently within each molecular sheet but poorly between them, their exceptional properties fail to translate to the macroscale. Here, we demonstrate a 2D highly oriented molecular network (2D HOMN), an ultra-stiff, super-tough polymeric material constructed by the solid-state covalent welding of assembled 2D polyaramid sheets with flexible linkers pre-grafted at their peripheries. Enabled by efficient intersheet load sharing and energy dissipation, the welded films rival the modulus and strength of Kevlar 29 fibers, reaching 69.8 and 3.9 GPa, with impact toughness up to an order of magnitude beyond Kevlar composites. This designed intersheet covalent connectivity further renders the 2D HOMN impermeable to gas molecules and ions, resilient to radiation and efficient in thermal transport. This work establishes 2D molecular motifs as heterogeneous monomeric building blocks and provides a general strategy for constructing multifunctional polymeric networks.

authors.name: Xiaoli Gong, Guohu Luo, Jiaxin Wu, Jiayu Chen, Zhengqiao Yin, Zhipeng Yan, Jingran Chen, Bowen Tang, Le Tang, Yuxiao Wu, Guanling Wu, Li Peng, Qihang Wang, Yinglong Hu, Yue Zhu, Yuan Yu, Keyan Liu, Xiaozhou Liu, Huanhuan Wu, Yakai Lin, Yifei Xu, Zhiliang Pan, Hao Ma, Man Li, Hongjun Zhang, Dacheng Wei, Youpeng Zhang, Yao Fu, Yongxiang Hu, Yuwen Zeng

papers.title: Curvilinear nanomagnets of non-trivial geometric topology
papers.summary: In this Chapter, we focus on the question of how the global geometric characteristics given by the topology of the sample's shape are reflected in the properties of the magnetization field of the given curvilinear nanoarchitecture. We start with a brief introduction to differential geometry and topology, giving their connection to the specific properties of the vector field represented by the magnetization field defined at the specific manifold. Then we discuss modern fabrication and characterization techniques that make analysis of a sample's topology not only an interesting theoretical concept but also a directly accessible and practically relevant topic. The main attention of the Chapter is dedicated to the theoretical and experimental analysis of nanostructrures with the topology different from the extended films beyond the in-depth studied topic of tubes of the constant radius. In particular, toroidal, spherical, and non-orientable manifolds are considered.

authors.name: Vagson L. Carvalho-Santos, Luke A. Turnbull, Na\"{e}mi Leo, Oleksandr V. Pylypovskyi

papers.title: Neural-network-inferred initial guesses for photoelastic force inversion
papers.summary: The inversion of contact forces between closely packed photoelastic disks has become a standard tool in the granular research community. The process iteratively fits the image generated by a forward model to the experimental image, and the correct convergence of the iteration depends critically on the initial guess of the force vectors. In this work, we train a convolutional neural network to infer a force vector from the image in the vicinity of individual contacts. This method, called Contact-Region Inference of Forces, or CRIF, provides the initial guess for the iteration. When tested with synthetic disk images, our approach substantially improves the accuracy of fitting results in comparison to that from the $G^2$ method in the widely adopted PeGS pipeline [Rev. Sci. Instrum. 88, 051808 (2017)], particularly for disks with many contacts and large forces involving high fringe orders. In addition, we extend the method to disks with a built-in axisymmetric residual stress, which often arises when photoelastic disks are submerged in fluids. Finally, on an experimental packing, fits started from the CRIF guess satisfy force reciprocity at strong contacts where fits started from $G^2$ do not.

authors.name: Jr-Jiun Lin (JC), Jih-Chiang (JC), Tsai

papers.title: Angular Momentum Hall Effect of Axial Ferrons in Ferroelectrics
papers.summary: Phonon thermal and angular-momentum (AM) Hall effects are known in non-ferroelectric insulators, yet whether terahertz soft modes of displacive ferroelectrics, i.e., ``ferrons", share them remains open. We report axial ferrons that hold polarization-momentum locking in uniaxial ferroelectrics and show that both effects exist: a longitudinal temperature gradient drives a transverse AM flow without any field, whereas an out-of-plane magnetic field switches on the thermal Hall response. Two competitive channels emerge for the AM Hall effect: self-radiated magnetic fields hybridize two branches into circular modes whose momentum-locked Berry curvature deflects opposite magnetic moments to opposite edges, while temperature-gradient-induced mode quantum coherence adds a magnetic-moment dipole that leads to an opposite transverse AM current. An out-of-plane magnetic field breaks the exact polarization-momentum locking and yields a polarization Hall current. Numerical calculations show these effects are significant in both LiNbO$_3$ and van der Waals ferroelectrics. Edge magnetization or polarization accumulation can switch adjacent magnets or ferroelectrics, enabling low-power magnetoelectric functionality by thermal current in the future.

authors.name: Xiyin Ye, Tao Yu

papers.title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
papers.summary: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.

authors.name: Miguel A. L. Marques, Irene D'Amico, Stefano Pittalis

papers.title: Magnetoelectric response to a N\'eel domain wall in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films: Spontaneous currents, vortex pinning, and vortex-antivortex nucleation
papers.summary: We study the superconducting response induced by a N\'eel domain wall in a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The combined action of the magnetic texture and broken inversion symmetry generates a magnetoelectric coupling that induces spontaneous equilibrium currents. To establish the basic response to a continuously rotating magnetic texture, we first consider a periodic harmonic cycloid as an analytically tractable reference problem. Near Tc, this reference problem illustrates how the magnetoelectric coupling modifies the superconducting order parameter, while below Tc it provides a simple setting for describing the phase response, Pearl screening, and the interaction with a vortex. We then turn to the main problem of this work, a single N\'eel domain wall, and derive analytical expressions for its equilibrium phase profile, spontaneous current, magnetic field, and vortex-wall interaction energy.We show that the N\'eel wall acts as an extended magnetoelectric source and produces a vorticity-selective pinning landscape controlled by the competition between the wall width and the effective screening length. We further demonstrate that sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling can render a bound vortex-antivortex pair energetically favorable relative to the vortex-free state, even in the absence of an applied magnetic field. Our results provide an analytical framework for understanding magnetoelectric vortex pinning and vortex-antivortex nucleation by N\'eel domain walls in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films.

authors.name: P. J. F. Cavalcanti, M. D. Croitoru, A. I. Buzdin

papers.title: Contribution to the GdTe$_3$ magnetic phase diagram from electronic transport measurements
papers.summary: Magnetic phase diagrams of the three antiferromagnetic (AFM) transitions of GdTe$_3$ that occur at zero magnetic field at $T_{N1}=12$ K, $T_{N2}=10.5$ K and $T_1=7$ K are investigated by means of resistance measurements in a magnetic field oriented along the three crystallographic directions. With the magnetic field applied in the basal plane we found re-entrance of an intermediate phase which may be a result of the coupling between the $T_{N2}$ AFM and the charge density wave with possibly a ferroaxial order. A spin flop transition is also observed at a temperature that presumably converges towards a triple point in vicinity of 2.5-3.0 T and $T$ between $T_1$ and $T_{N2}$. Our results help complete a complex phase diagram of GdTe$_3$ and advance a method for investigating magnetic ordering via transport measurements -- a technique applicable to many other compounds.

authors.name: A. A. Sinchenko, P. D. Grigoriev, A. Hadj-Azzem, E. Pachoud, E. Lorenzo, P. Monceau

papers.title: Continuum model for disconnection structures of hetero-interfaces
papers.summary: Hetero-interfaces, as planar defects between dissimilar materials, accommodate the lattice misfit through networks of line defects of disconnections (a combination of structural ledges/step and dislocation characters). We develop a continuum model that predicts the hetero-interface structures, including disconnection networks, the interface inclination and misorientation angles. The model is based on the interfacial energy minimization with respect to all possible disconnection modes, subject to the interface structure constraint of the generalized Frank-Bilby equation that describes the lattice correspondence across the interface including both dislocation and step characters of disconnections and the inclination and misorientation angles. Numerical simulations are performed to determine the equilibrium configurations of three different types of hetero-interfaces: the $\alpha$/$\beta$ (orthorhombic/monoclinic) interface in ZrO$_2$, $\alpha$/$\beta$ hetero-interfaces in Ti and Au/Pd (001) twist-misfit interfaces. Comparisons with experiments, atomistic simulations and theoretical predictions show that our continuum model provides excellent predictions of the hetero-interface structures including disconnection networks and inclination, misorientation angles. Furthermore, systematic analysis reveals the functional dependence of hetero-interface structural properties on inclination and misorientation angles.

authors.name: Luchan Zhang, Xiaoxue Qin, Dongsong Tao, Jian Han, David J. Srolovitz, Yang Xiang

papers.title: Classifying exact local-equilibrium solutions of the Boltzmann equation
papers.summary: We provide a complete classification, in a \(d\)-dimensional Euclidean space, of all hydrodynamic states and external forces for which a local equilibrium distribution constitutes an exact solution to the Boltzmann kinetic equation. We demonstrate that the temperature \(T\) must be spatially uniform, that the velocity field is the sum of a rigid translation, a radial expansion or compression, and a rigid rotation, and that the external acceleration must be conservative, though time-dependent within a reference frame that translates and rotates along with the fluid. The density profile is then determined by the external potential, while its temporal dependence is governed by any temperature function \(T(t)\) that can be generated through an appropriate adjustment of the external acceleration. We recover the classic ``harmonic breather'' and obtain solutions involving static forces that exhibit algebraic cooling, similar to Haff's law, despite the occurrence of elastic collisions. Our classification identifies the exceptional circumstances under which local equilibrium is exact and provides rigorous criteria for evaluating kinetic and hydrodynamic approximations.

authors.name: Nagi Khalil, Jorge Bravo-Gadea

papers.title: On fluctuation properties of the cumulative current in gTASEP on open chains
papers.summary: We present preliminary results of our numerical study of the fluctuation properties of the cumulative current, JT, in the generalized totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (gTASEP) on open chains with Liggett boundary conditions. GTASEP is the ordinary TASEP (a model of 1D- traffic on a single track, having many diverse applications), where an additional term controlling clustering of the particles is added. Extensive numerical simulations are performed to determine the dependence of the second scaled cumulant C2 of the time integrated current, JT, on the system size, L, in the long-time limit, allowing for comparison between open and periodic geometries. Preliminary results for C2 in the maximum current phase show agreement with theoretical predictions about the Kardar-Parizi-Zhang universality of the gTASEP on a segment.

authors.name: N. C. Pesheva, N. Zh. Bunzarova, E. K. Mitsova, A. M. Povolotsky

papers.title: Odd Viscosity-Driven Phase Separation in Chiral Active Mixtures
papers.summary: Binary mixtures of active particles spinning in opposite directions can spontaneously separate into homochiral domains, yet the mechanism behind this robust demixing remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a two-fluid hydrodynamic theory that generalizes odd viscosity to multicomponent systems. We show that cross parity-violating viscosities, which couple the stress of one chiral species to the strain rate of another, can destabilize the homogeneous mixture, while odd viscosity within each homochiral domain governs the interfacial stability and dynamics. Microscopic measurements of stress and velocity correlations yield viscosity estimates that predict spontaneous demixing followed by domain coarsening. These findings identify odd viscosity as a route to programming phase behavior and domain morphology in chiral active mixtures.

authors.name: Xiaoyi Wu, Tzer Han Tan, Hongbo Zhao

papers.title: Spin-Group versus Magnetic-Group Selection Rules for Nonlinear Photocurrents in Compensated Ferrimagnets
papers.summary: Optical excitation offers a contact-free, ultrafast route to charge and spin currents, with symmetry determining which nonlinear photocurrents are allowed and whether they carry charge, spin, or both. Spin-group symmetry describes the limit without spin-orbit coupling (SOC), whereas magnetic-group symmetry accounts for SOC. We show that the two descriptions yield different selection rules for both charge and spin photocurrents in the multiferroic compensated ferrimagnet GaFeO$_3$. Without SOC, only linear shift and circular injection currents are allowed, with identical components for charge and spin, so every charge current is spin polarized along the moments. SOC leaves these charge currents nearly unchanged, activates magnetic linear injection and circular shift charge currents, and enables pure spin currents polarized perpendicular to the moments. Ferroelectric switching reverses the linear shift and circular injection charge currents and their spin polarization. These findings establish the importance of magnetic-group symmetry for a complete description of nonlinear charge and spin photocurrents in compensated ferrimagnets.

authors.name: Fu Li, Vikrant Chaudhary, Weiyi Pan, Hongbin Zhang, Harish K. Singh

papers.title: Constrained Allen-Cahn phase-field topology optimization of flexoelectric devices
papers.summary: Topology optimization provides an effective approach to exploring performance-oriented designs for miniature devices. In this work, a phase-field framework for constrained topology optimization of microscale flexoelectric devices is developed using a continuum model under the assumption of infinitesimal deformations. The material distribution is optimized at the device level with the output voltage as the objective. The framework also accommodates objectives based on capacitance or stored electrostatic energy. Manufacturing variations are incorporated through a worst-case objective over the prescribed geometric realizations, with spectral constraints imposed to maintain the structural connectivity. The framework is applied to two-dimensional pressure and bending sensors and a three-dimensional thin-film device. The optimized nominal output voltages reach approximately 4.8 times the initial value for the pressure sensor and 2.5-3.4 times the initial values for the bending sensors. The voltage gains arise primarily from increased mechanically induced source charge, with capacitance reduction providing an additional contribution that varies with the device configuration. Erosion analyses of representative designs further show that structural connectivity is well preserved when structural members become locally narrower, with the output voltage remaining close to that of the nominal configuration. Combined with specific microfabrication processes, this optimization framework is expected to provide a numerical basis for configuration screening and prototype development of flexoelectric devices.

authors.name: Hao Zhen, Sheng Mao

papers.title: Comparative Molecular Dynamics Study of Initial Oxide Film Growth on Al, Mg, and Ti Using a Universal Neural Network Potential
papers.summary: Spontaneous formation of an oxide film, which may be passive, is found in many metals such as Al and Ti. We report direct computational observation of oxide film formation on the three major light structural metals, Al, Mg, and Ti, with molecular dynamics (MD) using a universal neural network potential (NNP). O2 molecules were supplied during MD simulations to replenish O consumed by the metal. Al and Ti formed a 1-2 nm thick film within a few ps of the simulation with O2 gas pressure of 102-103 atm. The film thicknesses of all metal oxides continued to increase proportionally to the logarithm of simulation time, consistent with Cabrera-Mott theory. Al and Ti oxides grow at the surface, while Mg oxide grows into the Mg metal. Al, Mg, and Ti are approximately 4.4, 4.3, and 5.2-fold coordinated, respectively, in the oxide.

authors.name: Yoyo Hinuma, Taisuke Hasegawa

papers.title: A macroscopic-atom spectral theory of grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys
papers.summary: Predicting grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys remains challenging because existing spectral approaches require alloy-specific atomistic calculations to resolve segregation-energy distributions and correlations across non-equivalent boundary sites. Here, we develop a transferable macroscopic-atom spectral theory that predicts the joint segregation behavior of multiple species from physically interpretable elemental descriptors. The theory is founded on the finding that local strain and bond deficit account for 91\% of the site-to-site co-variation of 40 solutes in a density-functional-theory (DFT) Al polycrystal. Linked to atomic size and surface enthalpy, these coordinates allow prediction of individual segregation spectra and their cross-species correlations, which determine whether species compete for or share grain-boundary sites. A closed-system formulation unifies host-element redistribution and dilute-solute segregation, couples metallic and light-element sublattices, and accounts for bulk compound formation and solute pairing. Calibrated using binary spectra only, the theory predicts unseen-host spectral means with a correlation coefficient of 0.81, outperforms embedded-atom spectra against DFT benchmarks, and ranks site competition across 870 solute pairs with a Spearman coefficient of 0.90. Without fitting to multicomponent observations, it reproduces 11 of 12 equilibrium Fe ternaries and 49 of 55 Mg ternaries. Predictions recorded before simulations of an 82,699-atom polycrystal identify site competition as the baseline behavior and metal-metalloid pair chemistry as a source of deviations requiring atomistic resolution. These results establish a physically grounded route to screening grain-boundary chemistry in multicomponent alloys, including steels and high-entropy alloys.

authors.name: Dennis Boakye, Chuang Deng

papers.title: Reversible Self-Assembly of a P-Ir(100)-P Trilayer on Ir(111)
papers.summary: Adsorbate-induced surface reconstructions offer a route to engineer low-dimensional materials with atomic arrangements and electronic properties fundamentally different from those of their parent substrates. Here, we demonstrate how phosphorus adsorption on Ir(111) drives the formation of an incommensurate P-Ir-P trilayer, in which a square Ir(100)-like atomic lattice emerges from the underlying hexagonal crystal. This transformation illustrates how strong adsorbate-substrate interactions can stabilize unconventional atomic coordination within an ultrathin metallic structure. Remarkably, the process is reversible, allowing the system to switch between distinct structural phases through phosphorus deposition and thermal annealing. The resulting trilayer exhibits a two-dimensional, semimetal-like electronic structure dominated by Ir 5d states. Our findings establish adsorbate-driven symmetry transformation as a strategy for engineering atomically thin transition-metal compounds with structural and electronic properties inaccessible through conventional surface growth.

authors.name: M. Bassotti, J. Sivianes, J. Dai, M. Tallarida, P. Angulo-Portugal, A. A. Makarova, J. Iba\~nez-Azpiroz, D. Yu. Usachov, A. Verdini, F. Schiller

papers.title: Intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect in ferroaxial metals with high-order rotation axes
papers.summary: The low-field Hall resistivity of non-magnetic metals has an intrinsic quantum contribution that derives from the field-corrected Berry curvature and intrinsic magnetic moment of the Bloch states near the Fermi surface. However, its effect is usually overshadowed by the classical Lorentz-force contribution. Here we show that for the longitudinal Hall effect, which occurs in ferroaxial crystals when the applied magnetic field lies in the Hall plane, the Lorentz force contribution vanishes for the eight ferroaxial groups with a 3,4 or 6-fold rotation axis. This provides an opportunity to measure the quantum correction in isolation, but so far all measured instances of the effect fall in the remaining five ferroaxial groups of lower symmetry, where the Lorentz force dominates the signal. We compile a list of candidate ferroaxial metals with such high-order rotation axis and compute the Hall effect from first principles for representative candidates, identifying Ni$_3$P with $\sigma^{\rm H}_{xzx} = 28.4$ S/m/T as a promising material to unambiguously measure the intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect.

authors.name: Eleni Chatzikyriakou, Stepan Tsirkin, Fernando Pe\~naranda, Oscar Pozo, Ivo Souza, Fernando de Juan

papers.title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
papers.summary: Heat flow across the core-mantle boundary (CMB) depends on the lattice thermal conductivity ($\kappa_{\mathrm{latt}}$) of lowermost-mantle minerals, yet calculated CMB values for MgO differ severalfold, and high-temperature estimates of the conductivity increase across the bridgmanite-post-perovskite transition range from about 20 to 50%. Direct solutions of the linearized phonon Boltzmann transport equation (LBTE) require thousands of density functional theory (DFT) force evaluations per thermodynamic state. Here we replace these evaluations with phase-specific, fine-tuned MACE potentials for MgO, MgSiO3 bridgmanite (Pv), and MgSiO3 post-perovskite (PPv). The potentials reproduce DFT energies, forces, stresses, pressure-volume relations, and compressed-state phonons for all three phases. For MgO at 0 GPa, replacing MACE forces with DFT forces in otherwise identical transport calculations changes $\kappa_{\mathrm{latt}}$ by 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K. PPv is 44-55% more conductive than Pv at the same pressure and temperature and strongly anisotropic, with $\kappa_{[100]}/\kappa_{[010]}$ ranging from 1.7 to 2.1. The quasi-harmonic phase boundary has a Clapeyron slope of $(7.4 \pm 0.1)$ MPa/K and intersects a model geotherm at 116.2 GPa and 2660 K, where the transition raises the silicate conductivity by 47%, to 8.6 W/(m K). Heating in the basal thermal boundary layer lowers the MgO and PPv conductivities to 37.3 and 6.7 W/(m K) at the CMB, where Hashin-Shtrikman bounds of 9.5-11.4 W/(m K) for an Fe-free aggregate of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO encompass the 10 W/(m K) used in earlier heat-flow estimates. The density-temperature parameterizations provide an intrinsic end-member reference for lower-mantle thermal models.

authors.name: Amrendra Kumar Tiwari, Sandro Jahn

papers.title: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes
papers.summary: We measure how much the left-to-right species order $W_t$ of interacting particles on the integer lattice reveals about their initial configuration. For distinct species under long-range swaps, deleting stronger particles gives coordinates with independent Poisson increments. For a finitely supported initial law, the mutual information between any function $U$ of the initial configuration and $W_t$ is $C_U/t+O(t^{-3/2})$ as $t\to\infty$, where $C_U$, which may vanish, is determined by the means of Gaussian order statistics and the conditional means of the initial compressed coordinates given $U$. On consecutive sites with a uniform initial order, we compute the coefficient of the $t\log(1/t)$ term in the short-time information loss for arbitrary species counts. For three particles in this setting, repeating the weaker rather than the stronger species triples the long-time $t^{-1}$ coefficient, although both compositions have the same composition entropy and initial-order entropy. These long-time coefficients are the same whether equal particles block or push each other, but the nonuniform limiting output law is reversed. In the ordinary multispecies totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP), two distinct particles at fixed sites with a uniform initial order instead give $t^{-1/2}$ decay.

authors.name: Eunghyun Lee

papers.title: Zone-folded Goldstone mode of the field-induced spin supersolid in the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet
papers.summary: The field-induced spin supersolid of the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet with single-ion and exchange anisotropy has so far been characterized only by static observables, among them a two-peak transverse structure factor. We compute its dynamic spin structure factors, and those of the neighboring phases, by stochastic analytic continuation of stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo data on a $16\times16$ lattice at inverse temperature $\beta=32$, at one field in each of the supersolid, the $m_z=1/2$ Ising plateau and the canted $XY$ phase. The supersolid has a single Goldstone mode, which the checkerboard folds onto both the ordering wave vector $\mathbf{Q}=(\pi,\pi)$ and $\mathbf{q}=(0,0)$, so that it appears in both spin channels at both points with one velocity $v=1.36\pm0.01$. The canted phase shows half of this pattern and the plateau none, the latter carrying instead a gapped magnon band and a two-magnon longitudinal continuum. Exactly at $\mathbf{Q}$ and $(0,0)$ the finite-lattice spectra are governed by a rotor tower of the condensate in the transverse channel and an Ising doublet of the checkerboard in the longitudinal one, both present at $\mathbf{Q}$ in the supersolid. Three parameter-free comparisons with the stiffness and the uniform susceptibility of the same runs, for the velocity, the sound-mode weight and the thermal decay of the rotor tower, tie the continued spectra to raw Monte Carlo observables. The folded Goldstone mode is the dynamical fingerprint of the supersolid.

authors.name: Sibin Yang, Pinaki Sengupta

papers.title: Long-Range Hydrodynamic Communication in Active Matter
papers.summary: Directed transport in active matter is typically achieved by introducing geometric asymmetry, such as ratchets or gears, that rectify the stochastic motion of active particles. Here we demonstrate a fundamentally different route in which persistent mechanical motion emerges without any geometric bias. A symmetric passive rotor placed at the center of a circular domain undergoes spontaneous unidirectional rotation driven solely by the hydrodynamic flow generated by a boundary-confined flocks of Marangoni swimmers, despite the absence of direct physical contact. While individual swimmers produce intermittent torque reversals arising from transient hydrodynamic backflow, increasing the size of the flock establishes coherent circulation that stabilizes the rotor dynamics. Particle image velocimetry (PIV) reveals that the collectively generated flow transmits momentum over macroscopic distances, converting local active forcing into robust mechanical transport. Together with a minimal flow superposition model, our results identify the suppression of reverse-torque events as a collective signature of hydrodynamic coupling between active swimmers and a passive body, providing a contact-free mechanism for remote mechanical actuation in active matter.

authors.name: Abhishek Thakur, Bibaswan Ghosh

papers.title: Confinement-induced Transitions of Chiral Active Particles and Dumbbells
papers.summary: We present a coherent framework for the stochastic description of a chiral Active Brownian Particle (cABP) and a chiral Active Brownian Dumbbell (cABD) in a harmonic trap. On the one hand, we employ the Martin-Siggia-Rose path integral formalism, using the passive Brownian motion as a reference state around which activity is accounted for as a perturbation series in the self-propulsion speed. This method is suited best to calculate the exact time-dependent correlation functions. On the other hand, we use the Fokker-Planck equation, which works best to obtain the steady-state probability distribution. We discuss in detail the transitions from a trap centered distribution for low activity/strong confinement to a ring-shaped distribution for high activity/low confinement and the effect of chirality, i.e. the active angular velocity. For the dumbbell, a series of such transitions occurs and the correlation functions yield information about the particle's conformation and orientation. This establishes the combined framework as a powerful tool to investigate stochastic active particle systems.

authors.name: Mike Brandt, Falko Ziebert, Carsten Littek

papers.title: Local Thermodynamic Reconstruction of Impurity Entropy
papers.summary: Resolving the thermodynamic entropy associated with a local impurity in a spatially extended interacting quantum bath remains a numerical challenge. We develop a Local-Maxwell approach that reconstructs the impurity entropy from local observables in worldline quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. By integrating their temperature responses along the impurity coupling, the method avoids separate estimates of extensive entropies. For nonnegative worldline expansions with bounded local couplings, we establish bath-size independent bounds on all factorial moments of the impurity vertex count. For even vertex counts, the Maxwell estimator variance remains bounded as the coupling approaches zero. The transverse-field Ising benchmark reproduces exact free fermion results, while an interacting XXZ chain demonstrates up to several hundredfold improvement in statistical efficiency over conventional extensive thermodynamic integration. In a three-channel XXZ impurity junction, we reveal entropy recovery upon cooling and a nonmonotonic coupling dependence of the finite-temperature entropy contrast. These results establish local thermodynamic reconstruction as an efficient approach to impurity entropy in interacting quantum baths.

authors.name: Hang Su

papers.title: Investigating competing order in the Kanamori-Hubbard model with the multiorbital multichannel fluctuating field theory
papers.summary: The multichannel fluctuating field (MCFF) approach treats selected collective fluctuations in interacting quantum lattice models nonperturbatively, but has so far been applied only to single-band systems. Here, we extend MCFF theory to multiorbital systems, accounting for the orbital structure of charge and spin instabilities. We apply it to the half-filled two-orbital Kanamori-Hubbard model with repulsive intra-orbital interaction $U$, and both positive and negative Hund's coupling $J$, addressing the competing orders and their interplay. The ability to selectively retain individual fluctuation channels and control their interplay allows us to disentangle their respective contributions and identify the mechanisms underlying competing instabilities. The model features a simple competition between charge density wave and antiferromagnetic fluctuations in the vicinity of $J=U$, and a more intricate competition between antiferromagnetic, orbital, and spin-orbital fluctuations near $J=0$, where the model acquires a higher SU(4) symmetry. The proposed multiorbital extension thus provides a computationally inexpensive and efficient framework for exploring how orbital and spin character shape competing collective fluctuations.

authors.name: Laura Torchia, Erik Linn\'er, Massimo Capone

papers.title: Nanoparticles with a BANG: Detonation-Driven Synthesis of Metals and Metal Oxides
papers.summary: Bristol Accelerated Nanoparticle Generation (BANG) method is a solvent- and capping-agent-free nanoparticle synthesis. Previous work was limited mostly to gold, silver and copper particles. Here, the method is extended to ten further elements, including Pb, Bi, Tl, Mn, Fe, Zn, Pt, Ni, Cd and Pd. Detonation in air favoured metal formation for less oxophilic metals, whereas detonation of silver azide under nitrogen suppressed detectable silver oxide formation while retaining locally identified hexagonal close-packed (HCP) Ag alongside face-centred cubic (FCC) Ag. The outcome of the synthesis can be modified by changing the detonation environment, while the highly non-equilibrium conditions provide access to phases that are difficult to obtain using conventional synthetic routes. BANG is a broadly applicable, highly non-equilibrium nanoparticle synthesis method whose products are governed by precursor chemistry and atmosphere, with potential access to kinetically trapped phases and direct supported-particle deposition.

authors.name: Jan Maurycy Uszko, Robert Maty\'a\v{s}, Naoto Shirahata, Stephen J. Eichhorn, Avinash J. Patil, Simon R. Hall

papers.title: Topological Anderson Superconductor in Landau Levels
papers.summary: There is much interest in two-dimensional superconductors with odd integer values of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Chern number $C_{\rm BdG}$, often termed topological superconductors, as these are predicted to harbor Majorana zero modes. Because a magnetic field produces Landau levels (LL) with nonzero Chern numbers, it is natural to ask if a conventional two-dimensional superconductor of spinful fermions with Rashba spin-orbit coupling can be driven topological by application of a magnetic field. Self-consistent solutions of the BdG equations for an on-site attractive interaction produce a phase diagram consisting almost everywhere of superconducting states with even integer values of $C_{\rm BdG}$, transitioning from one value to another as parameters such as the chemical potential are varied. We predict that introducing Anderson-type on-site disorder, which broadens as well as mixes LLs, produces, in the transition region, states wherein topological superconductivity percolates. This topological Anderson superconducting state provides another example where disorder can produce topologically nontrivial states.

authors.name: Uddalok Nag, Koji Kudo, J. K. Jain

papers.title: Energy transport from an active medium
papers.summary: We study the energy current through a harmonic chain whose left end is coupled, via a short-range contact potential, to a medium of overdamped run-and-tumble particles moving on a ring, while the right end is attached to a zero-temperature Langevin reservoir. The activity is parametrized by the propulsion speed $v_0$ and the persistence time $\tau$. Using nonequilibrium response theory at weak system-medium coupling, we predict the stationary current and simulations reproduce it over a large part of the $(v_0,\tau)$ plane. That includes the possible nonmonotonicity of the current as function of $v_0$ and $\tau$, and occurrence of resonances with the normal modes of the chain, most significantly at large $\tau$ and small $v_0$. There is a critical propulsion speed $v_c$ at which the ring-crossing frequency of the particles leaves the phonon band: for $v_0v_c$ it decays as $(v_0^2\tau)^{-1}$. We also explain where the theoretical prediction fails, especially due to an oscillatory instability originating from a sufficiently strong negative friction induced on the leftmost oscillator. Finally, the persistent medium produces strongly non-Gaussian velocity statistics and long-range, oscillating velocity correlations in the bulk of the chain.

authors.name: Simon Krekels, Christian Maes, Ion Santra

papers.title: Polar Streams through Active Condensation in Flocks
papers.summary: Two of the most paradigmatic phenomena in active matter are flocking, where particles align to move collectively, and motility-induced phase separation, where self-propulsion causes particles to condense even without attractive interactions. Here, using experiments on self-propelled Janus colloid dimers, we show that flocks can phase separate to form polar streams. These structures are elongated dense clusters of particles that flock along the stream's long axis, in contrast to the well-known transverse bands that form close to the flocking transition. We use particle-based simulations and hydrodynamic theory obtained through coarse-graining to identify the underlying mechanism, which we call active nematic condensation: Denser regions of the flock develop stronger polar and hence nematic order, which leads to further particle fluxes into the dense region. These results reveal a generic mechanism whereby flocks can condense into streams. Our findings uncover that flocks can be shaped by nematic order, which is usually not accounted for in the standard Toner-Tu equations. More broadly, our work shows that collective motion and phase separation can not only coexist but also cooperate in active matter.

authors.name: Lauritz Hahn, Xinyu Dou, Ziqi Zhou, Jie Zhang, Marin Bukov, Ricard Alert

papers.title: Multistable Thermoelectric Josephson Automata
papers.summary: Multistable systems can store and process information, yet their elements usually only burn the drive energy. Here, we build an automaton whose elements actively convert heat into electrical power. Heat alone stabilizes the states at zero bias, and each state routes generation and dissipation to different junctions. The elements, gap-asymmetric superconducting tunnel junctions, deliver up to 2.6 pW at either polarity under fixed heating and support a magnetic-field-tunable Josephson current. Two junctions sharing a heated island split the bias hysteretically and, even at zero bias, lock into opposite voltages encoding the sweep direction. With a load and current bias, the automaton accesses states spanning junction polarity combinations, including zero voltage; the magnetic field sets which are available and the bias history selects the occupied one.

authors.name: Filippo Antola, Margherita Cervi, Angelo Greco, Alessandro Braggio, Giorgio De Simoni, Francesco Giazotto

papers.title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
papers.summary: Native vacancy populations in transition-metal nitride coatings reflect vacancy formation, association, and depth-dependent stability. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compare these effects in rocksalt TiN and CrN in bulk and at (001) surfaces, within phase-stability-constrained chemical potential ranges. In TiN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ is favoured under N-poor and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ under N-rich conditions; in CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ remains preferred throughout its stability range. Association energies are referenced to corresponding isolated vacancies where positive values mean association lowers the energy and negative values favour separation. Mean bulk association energies for mixed metal-nitrogen pairs are $+0.132$ eV in TiN and $+1.053$ eV in CrN. At (001) surfaces, $V_\mathrm{N}$ in TiN prefers the surface and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ the first subsurface layer. In CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ has similar formation energies at the surface and first subsurface layer, with a slight preference for the latter; $V_\mathrm{Cr}$ slightly prefers the second subsurface layer. Surface cluster energies are referenced to separated vacancies at their preferred depths. The compact $2V_\mathrm{Ti}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ cluster in TiN has favourable association in bulk ($+0.217$ eV per vacancy) but unfavourable association at the surface ($-0.346$ eV per vacancy). By contrast, $2V_\mathrm{Cr}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ in CrN remains stabilised, with its association energy decreasing from $+1.188$ to $+0.431$ eV per vacancy. CrN's stronger association occurs without larger structural distortions and is accompanied by distinct Cr-centred magnetic responses.

authors.name: Barsha Bhattacharjee, Emilia Olsson

papers.title: Signatures of Kitaev quantum spin liquid states in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ revealed by nitrogen-vacancy spin-noise spectroscopy
papers.summary: Bond-dependent magnetic interactions, strong spin-orbit coupling, and quantum fluctuations in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ make it an archetypical candidate for exotic Kitaev quantum spin liquid (QSL) states. While electronic transport, neutron scattering, optical and tunneling spectroscopies were used to probe global QSL signatures in large scale $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ samples, nanoscale evidence of local QSL behavior via a non-invasive experimental probe is still missing. Here, we use diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spin-noise spectroscopy to probe QSL states in {\alpha}-RuCl3 nanoflakes with thicknesses ranging from 8 to 150 nm over a temperature range of 4.3-250 K. Our measurements reveal a pronounced decrease in the NV spin-lattice relaxation time ($T_{1}$) below ~100 K in proximity to the $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ flakes, indicating enhanced GHz-frequency magnetic fluctuations. This temperature scale is consistent with the energy scale associated with Kitaev interactions (~8 meV) and the emergence of low-energy fractionalized excitations. Below 50 K, thicker (> 90 nm) flakes exhibit a distinct bi-exponential $T_{1}$ decay, unlike the single-exponential behavior observed for off-flake and thinner (8 nm) flake measurements, suggesting an increasingly heterogeneous magnetic noise environment. These results establish NV spin-noise spectroscopy as a local, non-invasive probe of low-energy spin dynamics in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ nanoflakes and open a route to testing predicted noise signatures of fractionalized excitations in atomically thin QSL candidates.

authors.name: Jitender Kumar, Sehrish Iqbal, Himani Saraswat, Benjamin Hammons, Tianlin Li, Ariel Smooha, Rupak Timalsina, Arnab K. Pariari, Sy-Hwang Liou, Xia Hong, Markus H\"ucker, Amit Finkler, Abdelghani Laraoui

papers.title: Anharmonic enhancement of thermal conductivity in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$: A consistent picture from molecular dynamics and Wigner transport
papers.summary: Anharmonicity limits heat conduction in crystals, but its role in amorphous solids, where heat is carried mainly by tunneling between quasi-degenerate vibrations, remains unsettled. Here we disentangle the contributions of structural disorder, quantum statistics, and anharmonicity to the thermal conductivity of amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ (aGST), the prototypical phase-change memory material. Using a single machine-learned potential trained on first-principles data, we compare classical equilibrium and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (MD), which include anharmonicity to all orders, with harmonic Allen-Feldman theory and the anharmonic Wigner transport equation, both of which include quantum statistics. Four MD approaches agree on a conductivity of 0.171-0.181 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, about 16% above the harmonic Allen-Feldman value for the same model, and the Wigner formulation bridges the two: with classical statistics, it agrees with MD to within 5%. We trace this anharmonic enhancement to vibrational couplings that grow with the frequency difference between modes, so that anharmonic broadening opens additional channels for heat conduction. A comparison with silica, alumina, and disordered carbons reveals three regimes, in which anharmonicity reduces, barely affects, or enhances the conductivity. The predicted glass-like increase of the conductivity with temperature is consistent with thermoreflectance measurements. These results show that anharmonicity has no universal effect in disordered solids, and can promote rather than limit heat transport in strongly disordered materials.

authors.name: Luiz Felipe C. Pereira, Kamil Iwanowski, Michele Simoncelli, Omar Abou El Kheir, Marco Bernasconi, Riccardo Mazzarello, Francesco Mauri

papers.title: A model colloidal gel former for the measurement of inter-particle forces
papers.summary: Tracking of particle coordinates in colloidal model systems is an established technique. Recently, an emulsion system has been introduced where not only the coordinates, but also contacts and compressive forces between the droplets can be determined [Dong et al. J. Chem. Phys. 156 214907 (2022). Here we develop this system to control both the density mismatch and refractive index contrast between the emulsion droplets and the solvent. The former is important in minimizing sedimentation due to gravity and the latter is necessary for 3d imaging with confocal microscopy. By mapping our system carefully to computer simulation, we quantify interdroplet forces and packing geometries in depletion gels and probe the relationship between local structure and compressive stress. The simulations also provide ensemble measurements of the attractive part of the force between droplets and related quantities such as the stress tensor. Finally, we implement an improved measure of local stress in our experiments, which can be directly compared with the corresponding quantity in simulations. We find that locally rigid minimum energy clusters are associated with regions of higher stress in the gel network.

authors.name: Rui Cheng, Kristian Thijssen, Abraham Mauleon Amieva, Tanniemola B. Liverpool, Malcolm A. Faers, Robert L. Jack, C. Patrick Royall

papers.title: Classification of spin space groups and crystal magnetic orders
papers.summary: Spin space groups (SSGs) describe magnetic crystals in the limit of negligible spin-orbit coupling, where spatial and spin rotations decouple. Although algebraic enumerations of SSGs exist, their abstract mathematical approaches obscure the physical meaning of the resulting classifications, leaving the direct correspondence between SSGs and real-space magnetic orders unestablished. Here, we present a physically motivated framework for enumerating and classifying SSGs based on their translation holonomy---the image of the spatial lattice translation group under the spin homomorphism. The three classes of abelian images in $SO(3)$ divide SSGs into three basic translation types. Translation holonomy constrains the spin operations associated with point-group elements, yielding a complete enumeration of SSGs organized by a physical hierarchy. Within this framework, translation holonomy classifies SSGs and magnetic orders into 17 universal spin-lattice types, each with unambiguous Bragg-peak geometries and polarization signatures in neutron diffraction. Beyond organizing known magnetic orders, this framework directly predicts four universal physical phenomena: (i) exact magnetization compensation enforced by certain spin-lattice types; (ii) an exact group-theoretic criterion for the emergence of noncommuting Brillouin zones; (iii) a new type of 3Q magnetic order with vanishing octupoles; and (iv) the realization of strictly collinear momentum-space spin textures protected by reflection-staggered coplanar spin lattices. We also construct a spin space group database organized according to this physical hierarchy.

authors.name: Zheng Zhang, Peiyuan Wang, Y. X. Zhao

papers.title: Compositionally Tunable Synthesis of High-Entropy Transition Metal Dichalcogenides Exhibiting Above-Room-Temperature Magnetism
papers.summary: As silicon-based electronics approach their physical limits, low-dimensional magnetic materials have attracted increasing attention for next-generation electronic and information technologies. Realizing these opportunities requires two-dimensional (2D) materials with robust and tunable room-temperature magnetism. Here, we report a two-step synthesis strategy for fabricating 2D high-entropy transition metal dichalcogenides (HE-TMDs) incorporating magnetic elements beyond conventional groups 4-6. High-entropy layered double hydroxides (HE-LDHs) are first synthesized via hydrothermal coprecipitation, enabling atomic-level mixing of diverse transition metals across groups 4-12. Subsequent chalcogenization yields 2D HE-TMDs while preserving homogeneous elemental distribution. This approach circumvents the constraints of solid-state reaction, chemical vapor transport methods, enabling the synthesis of compositionally complex and structurally controlled 2D magnets. Representative (VCrFeCoNi)S2-x exhibits robust magnetism above room temperature, demonstrating the potential of this high-entropy design strategy for expanding the compositional and functional diversity of 2D magnetic materials.

authors.name: Chen Zhang, Xiahua Zhong, Dejia Kong, Wenhu Wang, Christopher T. Nelson, Mingfeng Chen, Xiaoqing He, Benjamin J. Lawrie, Hsin-Yun Chao, Alex L. Melendez, Peixin Liu, Benjamin G. Gibson, Xiaodong Yan, Xi Wang, Liangbo Liang, Zheng Gai, Huan Zhao, Yingchao Yang

papers.title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
papers.summary: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). (c) In the third approach, we retain the parent-crystal lattice intact but spatially pattern the on-site mass parameter, which controls the topology of the parent insulating system, such that it assumes two topologically distinct values on the fractal network and its complement (patterned fractal lattices). By numerically diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonians and computing appropriate topological invariants or local markers, corroborating the bulk-boundary correspondence through gapless modes at outer or inner boundaries, we establish Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topology on the Cantor set using all three approaches, Haldane topology on the hexaflake [using (a) and (b)] and Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet [using (c)], and strong $Z_2$ topological insulating phases on the tiled Menger sponge from methods (a), (b), and (c). These findings complement and substantially extend the previously reported realization of Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpi\'nski carpet using methods (a) and (b) [Phys. Rev. B 110, L241302 (2024)].

authors.name: Aiden Mains, Danile Salib, Christopher Leong, Bitan Roy

papers.title: Antiferromagnetic phase of MnTe2: spin-order-induced renormalization of phonon Raman spectrum
papers.summary: Recently, two modes of spin wave excitations (magnons) were detected in Raman scattering spectra of MnTe2. It is an unconventional magnet that features a pyrite-type crystal structure hosting a non-collinear, non-coplanar antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin order below the N\'eel temperature. In this brief communication, the focus is primarily on the effect of spin ordering on lattice dynamics (phonons) that has been established through temperature (5 - 300 K), linear polarization angle (0 deg - 360 deg) and external magnetic field (up to 16 T) dependent measurements. It has been found that below the magnetic transition temperature, the frequencies of four out of five Raman-active lattice vibrations (i.e., Eg and three Tg phonon modes) revealed significant departure from the mechanism of the three-phonon anharmonic decay described by Klemens model. Here, we propose a new model considering spin-phonon coupling to explain frequency renormalization of the phonon part of the Raman spectrum upon the para-/antiferro- (PM/AFM) magnetic phase transition change in MnTe2. Through employing Green's function formalism, we show that a simple two-sublattice collinear antiferromagnet approach follows well both spin ordering induced hardening and softening of phonon modes observed in AFM phase of MnTe2 upon cooling. Additionally, the detailed temperature and field dependences of the energy for both magnon modes are presented. In addition to unexpected twofold anisotropy of the higher energy magnon mode (approx. 3.5 meV) unveiled in crossed configuration, our magneto-optical measurements revealed a subtle, yet definite softening trend for the lower energy mode (approx. 2.6 meV). Although the precise reasons for these effects remain unclear, we put forward a symmetry reduction in the local atomic surroundings as a possible mechanism for discussion.

authors.name: Taras Palasyuk, Ashutosh S. Wadge, Eduard E. Zubov, Igor Antoniazzi, Gayatri, Andrzej Wi\'sniewski, Wojciech Szuszkiewicz, Daniel Jastrzebski, Ryszard Diduszko, Adam Babi\'nski, Maciej R. Molas, Micha{\l} Wierzbicki, Cezariusz Jastrzebski

papers.title: Systematic and accurate anharmonic formation free energies of metastable defects via a constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force framework
papers.summary: Computing the formation free energies of metastable defects at finite temperature remains challenging due to anharmonicity, the multiplicity of basins and the frequent occurrence of migration events. Using the previously introduced constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force method (BABFc), we establish a practical thermodynamic integration framework for computing restricted anharmonic formation free energies associated with individual metastable defect basins. We demonstrate that BABFc can be exploited as a robust, systematic and numerically efficient tool for addressing a long standing bottleneck in atomistic materials science: the finite temperature thermodynamic characterization of metastable defects in complex, highly anharmonic energy landscapes. The proposed workflow requires only a reference local minimum and a confinement strategy and does not rely on defect specific collective variables. It therefore provides a general route to assign well-defined free energies to individual metastable basins, even when these basins are separated by low barriers and embedded in a dense landscape of competing configurations. In this setting, BABFc enables stable, bias corrected free energy estimates with statistical accuracies at the meV/atom level and a very low failure rate, including for systems containing approximately one thousand atoms. We demonstrate this capability through thousands of independent free energy calculations covering hundreds of four-interstitial and four-vacancy configurations in bcc $\alpha$-Fe over a broad temperature range, using both a traditional empirical potential and a data driven force field.

authors.name: Clovis Lapointe, Anruo Zhong, Manuel Ath\`enes, Mihai-Cosmin Marinica

papers.title: Accessing Excitation of Many-body Systems via Single-Mode Approximation within Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations
papers.summary: We extend the single-mode Approximation (SMA) into quantum Monte Carlo simulations to provides an efficient and fast method to obtain the dynamical dispersion of quantum many-body systems. Based on stochastic series expansion (SSE) and its projector algorithms, the SMA + SSE method can simply extract the dispersion of the dynamical dispersion in the long wave-length limit and the upper bound of the dispersion elsewhere, without external calculations and high technique barriers. Meanwhile, numerical analytic continuation methods require the fine data of imaginary time correlations and complex programming. Therefore, our method can approach the excitation dispersion of large systems, e.g., we take the two-dimensional Heisenberg model on a $512 \times 512$ square lattice. We demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our method with high precision via additional examples. We also demonstrate that SMA combined with SSE goes beyond spin-wave theory with numerical results. We further illustrate that SMA is able to extract useful information in strongly correlated systems with competing states.

authors.name: Yan Liu, Kemeng Wu, Shutao Liu, Yan-Cheng Wang, Jie Lou, Zheng Yan, Yan Chen

papers.title: Spin Current Generation Controlled by the N\'{e}el State in a Compensated Ferrimagnet
papers.summary: Compensated ferrimagnets, which break sublattice and time-reversal symmetries in the ground state, exhibit an isotropic ferromagnet-like spin splitting despite a vanishing net magnetization, in contrast to altermagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting. We investigate how isotropic spin splitting manifests in spin transport by analyzing the spin Seebeck effect and spin pumping in a junction between a compensated ferrimagnet and a normal metal. We show that compensated ferrimagnets generate a sizable spin Seebeck signal, with a sign that can be reversed by switching between the two N\'{e}el states. Furthermore, we demonstrate that spin pumping exhibits a N\'{e}el-state-dependent resonance splitting, which is absent in conventional antiferromagnets. These results identify spin pumping as a natural readout mechanism for compensated ferrimagnets and establish them as promising magnetization-free building blocks for spintronic memory devices.

authors.name: Xin Theng Lee, Takahiro Misawa, Mamoru Matsuo, Takeo Kato

papers.title: Time arrow in open-boundary one-dimensional stochastic dynamics: effects of discrete thermal kicks over temperature interface
papers.summary: Does nonequilibrium characteristics exhibit in one-dimensional open-boundary stochastic systems? We introduce a discrete-timestep stochastic model, where the particle dynamics follows a discrete overdamped stochastic equation, and thermal kicks are presented over discrete timesteps. These thermal kicks are derived from a position-dependent temperature profile with a sharp interface. The discrete characteristic and the It\^{o}-type stochastic scheme make our model distinct from the conventional discussions of an overdamped colloidal model. Under the open-boundary condition, one cannot observe any net probability current in the nonequilibrium steady state (NESS). On the other hand, the nonequilibrium nature of this system can be extracted through the asymmetry in forward and backward transition probabilities, as is reported in this work through the simulation and theoretic analysis. In particular, our result shows prominent time irreversibility near the temperature interface. We propose a hidden-gyration scenario that demonstrates the source of irreversibility, while the collapse of gyrations on the one-dimensional coordinate accounts for the absence of probability current.

authors.name: Chi-Lun Lee, Yu-Syuan Lin, Pik-Yin Lai

papers.title: Voltage-tunable Josephson diode at zero applied field
papers.summary: We report a gate-tunable Josephson diode effect in hybrid nanowire junctions consisting of a spin-orbit-coupled semiconductor core coated with epitaxial ferromagnetic insulator and superconductor shells. The wires display a hysteretic superconducting window as a function of axial magnetic field. In the superconducting regime, the devices exhibit nonreciprocal supercurrent transport, with the diode efficiency showing a strong dependence on back-gate voltage. The effect persists at zero applied magnetic field in a remanent magnetization state following a controlled demagnetization procedure. These findings demonstrate a voltage-controlled Josephson diode in a single junction and suggest a route toward probing intrinsically broken inversion and time-reversal symmetries in hybrid materials.

authors.name: Sjoerd Telkamp, Junting Zhao, Saulius Vaitiek\.enas

papers.title: Hidden universality in large-deformation soft contact
papers.summary: Large-deformation soft contact mediates how biological and robotic systems interact with their environments, underpinning embodied intelligence, wearables, human-machine interactions and tactile sensing. The same coupling between contact area and remaining thickness shapes the response of physical interaction interfaces in wearable sensors and soft robots. Yet predictive theories remain confined to small strains or specific geometries, and a general law for nonlinear soft contact has remained elusive. Here we reveal hidden universality in large-deformation soft-body contact: after normalization by a simple geometric correction, diverse force-displacement responses collapse onto a master curve. By extending the method of dimensionality reduction into the nonlinear regime, the framework yields analytical solutions for contact force and radius. Finite element analyses and experiments across canonical geometries, non-axisymmetric structures and irregular gummy candies validate the scaling law up to 50% compression. These results establish a universal principle for nonlinear soft contact and a mechanics-guided route to wearable devices, tactile systems and soft robotics interactions beyond empirical calibration.

authors.name: Tong Mu, Changhong Linghu, Ruozhang Li, Shizhuo Weng, Jingyi Yu, Yanju Liu, Jinsong Leng, K. Jimmy Hsia, Huajian Gao

papers.title: Intrinsic spin accumulation in the magnetic spin Hall effect
papers.summary: The magnetic spin Hall effect is a time-reversal-odd phenomenon in which spin current is induced by the charge current. In the presence of a spin-orbit coupling and/or noncolinear magnetism, however, spin current is not uniquely defined. Instead, we study an intrinsic response of spin to an electric field gradient that describes the spin accumulation at the boundaries of magnetic systems. We derive a generic formula expressed by Bloch wave functions and apply it to a minimal model for representative altermagnets, RuO$_{2}$ and MnF$_{2}$. Our results show that the intrinsic spin accumulation can be nonzero in magnetic insulators in sharp contrast to the magnetic spin Hall conductivity.

authors.name: Atsuo Shitade

papers.title: Design of Chalcopyrite-Inspired Tellurides for Solar Cells: A First-Principles and Coupled FDTD-CHARGE Device Study
papers.summary: The defect-chalcopyrite tellurides XGa$_2$Te$_4$ (X = Cd, Zn) are evaluated as photovoltaic absorbers by combining first-principles calculations with coupled optical and electrical device simulations. Density functional theory (PBEsol) yields tetragonal $I\bar{4}$ structures with negative formation energies and phonon spectra free of imaginary modes. Both compounds have direct band gaps at $\Gamma$ of 1.046 and 1.032 eV (PBEsol) and 2.21 and 1.895 eV (HSE06), with absorption coefficients above $10^5$ cm$^{-1}$ in the visible. Wannier-Mott estimates give exciton binding energies of 18.85 and 26.81 meV, comparable to $k_BT$ at 300 K, and Bohr radii of 3.43 and 2.30 nm. Constant-relaxation-time Boltzmann transport gives Seebeck coefficients up to ~255 $\mu$V K$^{-1}$ near 350-400 K. Mulliken-electronegativity estimates place both band edges outside the water redox potentials at pH 0, with hydrogen-evolution driving forces of 0.83 and 0.60 eV but oxygen-evolution margins of only 0.16 and 0.07 eV. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) optical simulations coupled to drift-diffusion (CHARGE) electrical simulations of FTO/IGZO/XGa$_2$Te$_4$/CuAlO$_2$/Pt cells reveal a small conduction-band spike at the front junction (+0.15 and +0.33 eV), reflection losses governed by interference in the front oxide stack, electron collection confined to ~0.5 $\mu$m from the junction, and a fill-factor loss in the CdGa$_2$Te$_4$ device caused by the CuAlO$_2$ hole contact. Because the imported optical constants retain the PBEsol absorption edge, the simulated photocurrents exceed the detailed-balance limit; absolute efficiencies are therefore treated as upper bounds, whereas the identified loss mechanisms and design trends are robust. These results identify CdGa$_2$Te$_4$ and ZnGa$_2$Te$_4$ as candidate thin-film absorbers and define the contact engineering required to exploit them.

authors.name: Md H. S. Rifat, Tanvir Khan, Ababil Hossain Fahad, Md Arafat Hossain Shourov, Md Sahat Bin Sayed, K. M. Mehedi Hassan

papers.title: Observation of topological phases without crystalline counterparts
papers.summary: The center-of-mass position of a nonlinear soliton in a lattice is commonly attributed to the interplay between nonlinearity and lattice confinement. Here, we reveal its geometric origin by establishing an exact relation between the soliton position and an intrinsic Zak phase. Unlike the Zak phase of a linear Bloch band, this intrinsic Zak phase arises from the nonlinear self-consistent band of the lattice reconstructed by the soliton density. We construct a composite periodic function to define this phase and demonstrate that its topological winding during nonlinear Thouless pumping dictates the quantized soliton displacement. Our results establish band geometry as a fundamental descriptor of nonlinear soliton position in a lattice and provide a geometric framework for their topological transport.

authors.name: Mou Yan, Yu-Liang Tao, Yichong Hu, Zhenxing Cui, Jiong-Hao Wang, Gang Chen, Yong Xu

papers.title: Nanoindentation induced plasticity in equiatomic MoTaW alloys by experimentally guided machine learning molecular dynamics simulations
papers.summary: Refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCA) exhibit exceptional strength and thermal stability, yet their plastic deformation mechanisms under complex contact loading remain insufficiently understood. Here, the nanoindentation response of an equiatomic MoTaW alloy is investigated through a combined experimental and atomistically resolved modeling approach. Spherical nanoindentation experiments are coupled with large scale molecular dynamics simulations employing a tabulated low dimensional Gaussian Approximation Potential (tabGAP), enabling near DFT accuracy. A physics based similarity criterion, implemented via PCA of load-displacement curves, is used to identify mechanically representative experimental responses for quantitative comparison with simulations. Indentation stress-strain curves are constructed yielding excellent agreement in the elastic regime between experiment and simulation, with reduced Young's moduli of approximately 270 GPa. Generalized stacking fault energy calculations reveal elevated unstable stacking- and twinning-fault energies in MoTaW relative to pure refractory elements, indicating suppressed localized shear and a preference for dislocation-mediated plasticity. Atomistic analyses demonstrate a strong crystallographic dependence of plastic deformation, with symmetric {110} slip activation and four-fold rosette pile-ups for the [001] orientation, and anisotropic slip, strain localization, and enhanced junction formation for [011]. Local entropy and polyhedral template matching analyses further elucidate dislocation network evolution and deformation-induced local structural transformations. Overall, this study establishes a direct mechanistic link between fault energetics, orientation-dependent dislocation activity, and experimentally observed nanoindentation behavior in RCCA.

authors.name: F. J. Dominguez-Gutierrez, T. Stasiak, G. Markovic, A. Kosinska, K. Mulewska

papers.title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
papers.summary: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. In the MAGNDATA database, 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. With the $k$ index fixed to its experimental value, about nine structures are generated per material on average. We perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. The characteristic energy scale among oriented SSA structures is only approximately 0.29 meV per magnetic atom, about 300 times smaller than that of distinct SSA structures. These results demonstrate that oriented SSG-based enumeration, combined with the two-step calculations for SSA and oriented SSA structures, provides an efficient and robust route for large-scale magnetic-structure prediction.

authors.name: Takuya Nomoto, Kohei Shinohara, Hikaru Watanabe, Ryotaro Arita

papers.title: Depth-resolved magnetization dynamics in Fe thin films after ultrafast laser excitation
papers.summary: We performed time-resolved x-ray resonant magnetic reflectivity measurements on a laser-excited ferromagnetic Fe thin film to simultaneously probe the transient magnetic and structural depth profiles with nanometer spatial and femtosecond temporal resolution. Our results show that during the first picoseconds after optical excitation, the magnetization of the Fe layer is strongly inhomogeneous, especially in the vicinity of the buried interface. By comparing our experimental results to predictions based on the microscopic three-temperature model and simulations of laser-induced spin-currents, we demonstrate that local and non-local angular momentum transfer phenomena take place simultaneously. After a few picoseconds, the magnetization relaxes back to equilibrium while the total thin film thickness starts oscillating periodically, with a maximum dilation of approximately 1.3% of the entire thin film thickness due to laser-induced stresses.

authors.name: Valentin Chardonnet, Marcel Hennes, Romain Jarrier, Renaud Delaunay, Nicolas Jaouen, Marion Kuhlmann, Cyril Leveill\'e, Clemens von Korff Schmising, Daniel Schick, Kelvin Yao, Xuan Liu, Gheorghe S. Chiuzb\u{a}ian, Jan L\"uning, Boris Vodungbo, Emmanuelle Jal

papers.title: A Generalized Coherent State Framework for Many-Body Density of States
papers.summary: We develop a general framework to calculate the many-body density of states (DOS) of isolated and interacting quantum systems. Based on the generalized coherent state formalism and the Simon-Lieb bounds for a quantum partition function, our method provides a general method of calculation for the DOS in high-dimensional irreducible sectors. This framework further provides rigorous bounds for the ground state energy in each sector and enables the calculation of microcanonical observables across the entire spectrum. Using the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) model as a test bed, we validate our framework by successfully identifying quantum phase transitions (QPTs) and excited-state quantum phase transitions (ESQPTs) across spin sectors. We then study the ferromagnetic transverse field Ising chain with power law interactions, where the hamiltonian ceases to be block diagonal in irreducible sectors. We generalize our coherent states to explicitly track the permutation symmetry group. For the strongly long range interacting case, we demonstrate that the DOS in highest-spin sectors is qualitatively identical to that of LMG-type Hamiltonians in the thermodynamic limit. Unlike existing model-specific numerical or analytical techniques, our formalism relies on general underlying symmetries, making it broadly applicable. It establishes a versatile and computationally efficient bridge between algebraic structure and many-body thermodynamics.

authors.name: Deniz Coskun, R. Chitra

papers.title: Endowing phase-field fracture models with custom strength criteria
papers.summary: By now, several approaches have been proposed to endow phase-field fracture models with the ability to describe crack nucleation under multiaxial stress states. These include techniques for splitting the free energy, direct modifications of the phase-field driving or resisting forces, and the introduction of additional internal variables, such as plastic strains or other nonlinear strains. In this paper, we propose a fundamentally different strategy for incorporating arbitrary elastic domains into phase-field fracture models, formulated within the energetic framework of generalized standard materials. The proposed approach relies on letting the dissipation potential depend on the current state of the material. In this way, the elastic degradation and the strength criterion remain two distinct and independently controllable aspects of the material response, while the governing equations directly descend from a local stability condition and energy balance. Simple yet representative models are presented and thoroughly discussed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The resulting evolution of the elastic domain is investigated in both strain and stress spaces under proportional and non-proportional loading paths, with the latter highlighting the path dependence of the dissipated work. Moreover, numerical simulations demonstrate a range of crack nucleation processes under multiaxial loading conditions for various analytical strength surfaces. The present work paves the way for future developments and applications in several directions, including crack propagation studies and dedicated numerical solution strategies.

authors.name: Roberto Alessi, Matteo Brunetti, Roshan Udaram Patil, Jacinto Ulloa

papers.title: Atomic-scale visualization of the toroidal order in a trimeric Dy(III) single-molecule toroic
papers.summary: Single-molecule toroics (SMTs) offer a unique platform for next-generation quantum devices utilizing head-to-tail spin alignments in the compounds. Presence of toroidal moments in SMTs has been essentially based on magnetometry and ab initio calculations. Here, we report observation and probe of the toroidal moment in [Dy3(OH)(teaH2)3(paa)3]Cl(OMe) [teaH3: triethanolamine; paaH: N-(2-pyridyl)-acetoacetamide] from mapping of Dy3+ magnetic susceptibility tensors by polarized neutron diffraction (PND). Neutron diffraction under variable magnetic fields demonstrates field-induced magnetization along the c-axis with toroidal moments anti-parallelly stacked, providing definite proof of the toroidal moment. Magnetometry studies confirm the toroidal ground state. For the first time, the combined use of PND, variable-field neutron diffraction, ab initio calculations, and magnetometry is introduced as a robust and quantitative methodology to probe molecular-scale toroidal magnetism. This integrated approach overcomes limitations of earlier indirect methods, establishes a benchmark framework for investigating SMTs, and provides valuable insights for the design of molecular quantum materials.

authors.name: Michael J. Jenkins, Madalynn G. Marshall, Jie Xing, Muthu Satheeshkumar, Brandon D. Watson-Sanders, Xiaoping Wang, Christina M. Hoffmann, Gopalan Rajaraman, Huibo Cao, Rongying Jin, Zi-Ling Xue

papers.title: Mean-field theory of myopic self-avoiding fractional Brownian motion
