papers.summary: Myopic self-avoiding fractional Brownian motion (FBM) is a stochastic process in which an ensemble of particles is driven by fractional Gaussian noise while being repelled by the gradient of the time-integrated ensemble density [J. House et al., Phys. Rev. E 112, 034119 (2025)]. Depending on the anomalous diffusion exponent $\alpha$ characterizing the noise, the process features two dynamical regimes: an interaction-dominated regime ($\alpha \alpha_c$) where FBM correlations prevail. In the interaction-dominated regime, the mean-squared displacement grows as $\langle r^2(t) \rangle \sim t^{4/(d+2)}$ regardless of $\alpha$, while for $\alpha > \alpha_c$ the standard FBM scaling $\langle r^2(t) \rangle \sim t^{\alpha}$ is recovered. Here, we develop an analytical mean-field theory of myopic self-avoiding FBM, based on a Fokker-Planck approach to the interaction-dominated regime. This allows us to derive closed-form polynomial solutions for the probability density. To compare with computer simulations, we develop an efficient radial binning algorithm that significantly reduces the computational complexity, making large-scale three-dimensional simulations feasible. Extensive simulations in one, two, and three dimensions confirm the analytical predictions. We also discuss the application of the process to the self-organization of serotonergic axons (fibers) in vertebrate brains, where FBM paths with self-avoidance provide a natural framework for understanding spatial heterogeneities of fiber densities.

authors.name: Rashad Bakhshizada, Skirmantas Janu\v{s}onis, Ralf Metzler, Thomas Vojta

papers.title: Graphene Josephson diodes from asymmetric disorder
papers.summary: Josephson diodes are non-reciprocal superconducting devices characterized by different switching currents depending on the current flow direction. They recently attracted considerable theoretical and experimental attention, in view of their possible application as rectifying elements in the field of superconducting electronics, and as probes to investigate symmetry breaking mechanisms in mesoscopic systems. In this work, we show that graphene Josephson junctions provide rectification of supercurrent with an efficiency exceeding 20%. The effect appears applying a mT out-of-plane magnetic field and is enhanced close to the nodes of the Fraunhofer interference pattern. Our findings are consistent with a theoretical model that considers long-range scattering potentials in the junction as the symmetry-breaking mechanism, which yields supercurrent rectification in highly transparent junctions. While graphene stands out as an ultra-clean transmission medium, our work shows that unavoidable residual disorder is sufficient to promote this effect.

authors.name: Ivan Villani, Luca Chirolli, Matteo Carrega, Alessandro Crippa, Elia Strambini, Francesco Giazotto, Vaidotas Miseikis, Camilla Coletti, Fabio Beltram, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Stefan Heun, Sergio Pezzini

papers.title: Facet-Driven Electronic Modulation in Self-Aligned Phosphorus Nanoarrays
papers.summary: Two-dimensional (2D) materials often require specific substrate terminations for epitaxial stabilization, yet the search for suitable templates has largely focused on low-index metal surfaces, which may not provide the optimal conditions for the growth of new phases. Here, we show that crystal-facet engineering on curved Cu surfaces enables the stabilization, within a single preparation step, of two distinct phosphorus surface phases with different electronic properties. Hexagonal phosphorus adlayer forms on Cu(111) terraces, whereas a previously unreported skewed-square P overlayer is stabilized on Cu(513) facets. By combining complementary microscopy and spectroscopy techniques with theoretical calculations, we show the quasi-semiconducting character of the P-derived electronic states of the skewed-P overlayer, in contrast to the case of hexagonal phosphorene. The coexistence of these two competing structures gives rise to electronic P band modulation overlayer across the substrate while, locally, self-aligned nanoarrays of alternating hexagonal and skewed-square phosphorus terraces form. These results establish crystal-facet engineering as a practical route for discovering and stabilizing emergent 2D phases on high-index substrates.

authors.name: M. Bassotti, M. Tallarida, J. Dai, S. Salaverria, P. Angulo-Portugal, L. Fernandez, A. El-Sayed, J. E. Ortega, A. A. Makarova, Dimas G. de Oteyza, D. Yu. Usachov, A. Verdini, F. Schiller

papers.title: Stacking-Directed Polarization and Excitonic Engineering in MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
papers.summary: The stacking-dependent polarization and excitonic response of MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ heterostructures were investigated using GW+BSE many-body perturbation theory. While homobilayer MoS$_2$ exhibited a switchable interlayer dipole driven by registry-induced symmetry breaking, the MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ hetero-interface remained pinned by the intrinsic chemical potential mismatch between sulfur and selenium. In 2L-MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ trilayers, the stacking sequence enabled a deterministic control of photogenerated electrons between the central and bottom MoS$_2$ layers, governed by internal electric fields and quasiparticle band-edge shifts of 60--70~meV. Our calculations predicted a 36~meV interlayer excitonic shift, in remarkable agreement with recent experiments. These results elucidate the microscopic link between atomic registry and many-body interactions, establishing transition metal dichalcogenide trilayers as a potential platform for sliding ferroelectricity and programmable optoelectronic functionalities.

authors.name: Mohammed El Amine Miloudi, Oliver K\"uhn

papers.title: Magnetoelectric flat band induced by a $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ charge density wave in monolayer CrSe$_2$
papers.summary: We investigate the electronic and magnetic properties of the polar $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ charge-density-wave (CDW) phase of CrSe$_2$ using ab initio calculations. The CDW introduces a polar distortion out of the van der Waals plane that couples to the spin-polarized Cr d states resulting in a remarkably flat electronic band exactly at the Fermi level. We provide a microscopic understanding of the origin of the flat band by analyzing in detail the structural reconstruction, the effects of orbital hybridization, crystal-field splittings, spin-orbit coupling and electronic correlations. Our calculations show that due to the polar nature of the CDW distortion, an electric field can act as an external switch to induce the CDW phase, providing a way to manipulate strong correlations in the system.

authors.name: Pablo Savino, M. del Carmen Fuente Santiago, Jan Phillips, Javier Corral Sertal, Adolfo O. Fumega, Santiago Blanco-Canosa, Victor Pardo

papers.title: Cyclic machines in contact with thermal and athermal baths: the role of Poisson shot noise
papers.summary: We study stochastic models of a microscopic active heat engine, comprised of an overdamped Brownian particle trapped in a harmonic potential, and in simultaneous contact with thermal (passive) and athermal (active) baths. The interaction with the active bath is modeled as a stochastic force described by Poisson shot-noise (PSN) having a specified amplitude distribution. With analytical calculations and numerical simulations, we study the thermodynamic performance of this machine with cyclic protocols that are analogous to two-stroke and Stirling-like engines. For specific parameter ranges, the thermodynamic behavior is that of a hybrid machine, operating as a heat engine with respect to the thermal (passive) bath and as a refrigerator with respect to the PSN (active) bath, or vice versa. Focusing on the parameter region where the overall performance is that of an engine, we show that the average total extracted work per cycle divided by average total heat intake from the hot baths per cycle may surpass the Carnot efficiency associated with the temperature of the passive baths. Applying the second law for active heat engines, we focus on a bonafide efficiency (bounded by Carnot's efficiency) that incorporates an information-theoretic metric~$\mathcal{I}$ ---which we call {\em quasistatic divergence}--- quantifying how distinguishable are the engine's statistics in the quasistatic limit with respect to a continually changing equilibrium distribution. We analyze, with theory and numerical simulations, how the PSN shot rate and the degree of non-Gaussianity in the particle position distribution influence the efficiency of the engine, and explore the correlation between non-Gaussianity and efficiency. Our findings reveal optimal PSN shot rates maximizing the engine's efficiency and an intriguing non-bijective relation between efficiency and kurtosis.

authors.name: Rita Majumdar, Costantino Di Bello, Ralf Metzler, Rahul Marathe, \'Edgar Rold\'an

papers.title: Universal scaling of the spin Hall effect
papers.summary: We study the spin Hall (SH) effect for the Dirac electrons in terms of the spin and magnetic-moment accumulation coefficients $-\Gamma^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy}$. We take short-range nonmagnetic impurities into account within the self-consistent $T$-matrix approximation. Similarly to the universal scaling for the anomalous Hall (AH) effect, we find three distinct regimes by changing the electric conductivity $\sigma^{yy}$; the superclean regime with $-\Gamma^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy} \propto \sigma^{yy}$ owing to the skew scattering, moderately dirty regime with almost constant $-\Gamma^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy}$, and dirty regime with a scaling relation $-\Gamma^{00} g_{s(m)z}^{\phantom{s(m)z} xy} \propto (\sigma^{yy})^{0.6}$ whose exponent differs from that of the AH conductivity. Our results construct a unified theory of the SH effect without any ambiguity of spin current.

authors.name: Atsuo Shitade, Naoto Nagaosa

papers.title: Short-range spin correlations and temperature-driven interlayer exchange crossover in the van der Waals magnet CrCl$_3$
papers.summary: We investigate the evolution of spin correlations and the nature of the multi-stage magnetic transition in the quasi-two-dimensional easy-plane van der Waals magnet $\rm CrCl_3$. By combining broadband magnetic resonance spectroscopy and DC SQUID magnetometry on mechanically exfoliated microflakes with non-local dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) calculations, we analyze both long- and short range magnetic order in CrCl$_3$. Experimentally, SQUID and magnetic resonance measurements confirm the presence of the crossover to a spin polarized phase with the subsequent transition into an antiferromagnetic ground state upon cooling, but show robust short-range correlations at temperatures far above the magnetic ordering temperatures. Theoretically, we show the existence of highly stable local magnetic moments at room temperature, with a giant room temperature lifetime $\tau$ of 130--300 ps due to a wide Mott bandgap. Below room temperature, a rapid growth of the in-plane correlation length $\xi$ signals the formation of strong short range magnetic order consistent with the experimental observations. We also obtain a temperature-driven crossover of the interlayer exchange interaction, which changes from positive (ferromagnetic) at high temperatures to negative (antiferromagnetic) in the low-temperature ordered phase.

authors.name: T. B. Mazitov, M. I. Panin, A. S. Pakhomov, M. V. Bakhmetiev, E. O. Chiglintsev, A. I. Chernov, A. A. Katanin

papers.title: Memory-Retaining RG Fixed Points in Nonlinear PDEs
papers.summary:
Self-similar solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) are often interpreted as fixed points of renormalization-group (RG) transformations. Let $\xi$ denote a similarity variable and $\eta$ a dimensionless physical scale. In conventional RG descriptions, asymptotic coarse graining leads to memory loss, whereby $\eta$ disappears from the fixed-point solution. Here, we develop an RG framework in which fixed points take the general form $\eta^{\alpha}\Gamma(\xi/\eta^{ eta})$, where the surviving scale $\eta$ remains embedded in the asymptotic solution. While the case $ eta=0$ with $\alpha
eq 0$, corresponding to anomalous scaling via amplitude renormalization $\eta^{\alpha}$, is well understood within RG theory, self-similar solutions with $ eta
eq 0$ are known in second-kind self-similarity but have lacked a general RG formulation. We develop a nonperturbative RG framework for nonlinear PDEs that extends RG fixed-point theory to the $ eta
eq 0$ class by treating physical scales as dynamical variables of the RG flow. This framework identifies which scales remain asymptotically relevant and leads naturally to three classes of RG fixed points: memory-loss, memory-retaining I, and memory-retaining II. In the first class, scale information disappears asymptotically; in the second, it survives only in multiplicative amplitude factors such as $\eta^{\alpha}$; and in the third ($ eta
eq 0$), it remains embedded in the similarity profile $\Gamma$ itself. We illustrate the framework using conservative diffusion, the Barenblatt diffusion equation, a modified density-dependent diffusion model, and a three-scale fatigue-crack-growth problem. These examples show how RG flows determine both the surviving scales and the asymptotic self-similar solution, providing a unified RG formulation for memory retention and second-kind self-similarity with $ eta
eq 0$.

authors.name: Ko Okumura

papers.title: Local magnetic correlations and light-sensitive centers in the Cr2AlC MAX phase
papers.summary: Cr2AlC MAX phase is synthesized by high-pressure solid-state annealing and investigated as a candidate platform for optically responsive magnetism. Structural characterization confirms the formation of the Cr2AlC phase, while magnetic and optical-magnetic properties are examined by superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) magnetometry, electron spin resonance (ESR), and first principles calculations. SQUID magnetometry identifies Cr 2AlC as a weak, field-linear metallic paramagnet dominated by Pauli-like susceptibility of itinerant Cr-derived states. Its non-monotonic temperature dependence is described by an additional contribution from antiferromagnetically coupled Cr-Cr dimers, whereas the low-temperature Curie-like upturn originates from only a trace population of localized Cr centers. Under red-light illumination, SQUID magnetometry does not reveal an intrinsic macroscopic optomagnetic response. In contrast, ESR at 4 K shows a reversible light-induced reduction of a local magnetic signal, but the optically modified spin population corresponds only to several tens of ppm of the Cr sublattice. Ab initio Bethe-Salpeter equation (ai-BSE) calculations combined with the maximally localized Wannier function analysis suggest that optical excitation can redistribute spin polarization between neighboring Cr sites with the opposite local moments. The combined experiment-theory approach therefore establishes the hierarchy of magnetic contributions in Cr 2AlC and identifies the microscopic origin of its local optical sensitivity.

authors.name: Malgorzata Wierzbowska, Anna Basa, Kazuhiro Marumoto, Jiaxi Wang, Katarzyna Gas, Maciej Sawicki, Kacper Sierakowski, Karel Carva, Michal Bockowski

papers.title: Electrothermal control of spin-reorientation transition in Co/Fe_3GaTe_2 heterostructures
papers.summary: Electrical control of magnetic anisotropy in van der Waals (vdWs) magnets is a key step toward reconfigurable two-dimensional spintronics, yet how a conventional metallic ferromagnet competes with a van der Waals magnet across a direct interface has remained largely unexplored. Here we demonstrate reversible thermal and electrothermal control of a spin-reorientation transition in Co/Fe_3GaTe_2 (FGaT) heterostructures. As Joule heating weakens the FGaT anisotropy, the heterostructure switches from an out-of-plane- to an in-plane-dominated state at a reorientation temperature of approximately 311 K, well below the Curie temperature, consistent with an exchange-mediated anisotropy competition between the Co overlayer and FGaT. An electrically driven device shows a closely matching loop evolution within an 80-100 mW power window, reversibly over five measurement cycles, consistent with an electrothermal origin. In a Co-free FGaT device, Kerr microscopy traces the switching to a power-tunable domain nucleation barrier and demonstrates power-thresholded, field-assisted magnetization reversal at a threshold near 15 mW. These results demonstrate electrothermal anisotropy competition as a route to heat-assisted and device-level control of vdWs magnetism.

authors.name: Po-Wei Chen (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan, Department of Physics, The University of Osaka, Toyonaka, Osaka, Japan, Institute of Physics, Academia Sinica, Taipei, Taiwan), Ming-Hsien Hsu (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Cheng-Ying Hsiao (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Ming-Yang Ho (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Masahiro Haze (Institute for Solid State Physics, The University of Tokyo, Kashiwa, Chiba, Japan), Yan-Ru Chu (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Yu-Cheng Shao (National Synchrotron Radiation Research Center, Hsinchu, Taiwan), Po-Chun Chang (Department of Physics, Tamkang University, New Taipei City, Taiwan), Chen-Yu Ou (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Ruei Chen (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Ko-Fan Chen (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan), Chung-Ting Ke (Institute of Physics, Academia Sinica, Taipei, Taiwan), Chao-Hung Du (Department of Physics, Tamkang University, New Taipei City, Taiwan), Yukio Hasegawa (Institute for Solid State Physics, The University of Tokyo, Kashiwa, Chiba, Japan), Wen-Chin Lin (Department of Physics, National Taiwan Normal University, Taipei, Taiwan)

papers.title: End-State-Controlled Quantum Transport in Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Artificial Quantum Materials
papers.summary: Artificial quantum materials based on atomically precise graphene nanostructures provide an ideal platform for exploring quantum phenomena arising from localized electronic states. Here, we develop a real-space theoretical framework to elucidate the microscopic origin of interface states in graphene architectures composed of $n$-triangulenes and armchair graphene nanoribbons (AGNRs). By continuously tuning the coupling between graphene building blocks, we reveal the evolution of triangulene zero-energy modes and AGNR end states into compact localized node orbitals at three-arm junctions. For the chiral bipartite junctions considered here, the number and sublattice character of these node orbitals follow a general counting relation, $N_{node,\delta}=|N_{es,t,A(B)}-N_{tri,0,B(A)}|$, where $N_{es,t}$ is the total number of AGNR end states contributed by the three AGNR arms and $N_{tri,0}$ is the number of triangulene zero-energy modes. The resulting node-orbital chirality is determined by the dominant constituent: when $N_{es,t}>N_{tri,0}$, they inherit the sublattice chirality of the AGNR end states ($\delta=A(B)$), whereas for $N_{tri,0}>N_{es,t}$ they inherit that of the triangulene zero-energy modes ($\delta=B(A)$). Using experimentally synthesized triangulene nanographenes as representative examples, we further identify their low-energy zero-mode structure and investigate its manifestation in tunneling transport within an extended Anderson framework. Finally, we demonstrate that these node orbitals can serve as elementary building blocks for constructing artificial graphene nanoribbons with highly tunable flat subbands near the Fermi energy. The resulting compact localized states exhibit controllable degeneracy and strongly anisotropic quantum transport.

authors.name: David M T Kuo

papers.title: Circular phonon dichroism in $d$-wave altermagnets
papers.summary: Altermagnets, a new class of collinear antiferromagnets, exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting and offer compelling advantages for antiferromagnetic spintronics. However, the magnetic order is intrinsically difficult to read out, which hinders practical applications. We propose finite-momentum circular phonon dichroism as a direct probe that distinguishes the two opposite out-of-plane N\'eel vector configurations in two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnets. Combining Onsager reciprocity with $C_{2z}$ lattice symmetry, we find that the dichroic signal reverses sign when the N\'eel vector is flipped for the in-plane phonon wave vectors. Moreover, a channel-resolved decomposition identifies the circular phonon dichroism originates from the interband coherent transitions. Representative finite-momentum cuts show pronounced dichroic asymmetric ratio, with $|\eta_{\mathrm{CPD}}|=36\%$. Our work reveals that the circular-ultrasound absorption can distinguish the two opposite out-of-plane N\'eel vector configurations of $d$-wave altermagnets.

authors.name: Ding Li, Tao Qin, Jianhui Zhou

papers.title: Uncertainty-quantified $J$-integral computation for quasicontinuum and finite element methods
papers.summary: The $J$-integral is a fundamental concept in fracture mechanics, quantifying the energy release rate that drives crack propagation. This work presents a rigorous implementation and validation of the $J$-integral within the multiscale three-dimensional (3D) quasicontinuum (QC3D) method, along with an uncertainty quantification analysis applicable to both QC3D and conventional FE methods. We compute the 3D $J$-integral under plane-strain assumptions, utilizing continuum mechanics fields (stress and strain energy density) derived from the underlying interatomic potential through the Cauchy--Born rule. Our implementation is comprehensively validated against both linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM) theory and the virtual crack extension (VCE) method for three regimes of increasing complexity: small-strain elasticity, and nonlinear deformation without and with atomic relaxation in the region near the crack tip. Excellent agreement is demonstrated in all cases. Further, we introduce a novel Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) framework to statistically assess the uncertainty in $J$-integral results for a given mesh and integration domain in QC3D and conventional FE methods. Our implementation's predictive capability is demonstrated through a QC3D simulation of a three-point bending test on silicon, where the computed critical energy release rate is shown to be in excellent agreement with the Griffith criterion. This work establishes a reliable and efficient framework for evaluating crack driving forces in multiscale fracture simulations with quantified uncertainty, enabling large-scale fracture simulations while resolving atomistic mechanisms at the crack tip.

authors.name: Sai Harshith Badi, Stephen M. Whalen, Ronald E. Miller, Ellad B. Tadmor

papers.title: Activity-induced response amplification and instability near jamming in a Wishart--Ginibre model
papers.summary: We study the linear mechanical response of a disordered contact network using an additive Wishart--Ginibre model: a passive Wishart operator is perturbed by an independent real Ginibre coupling of strength \(\alpha_0\). The observable is the mean-square static displacement response per degree of freedom, normalized by the variance of the applied isotropic forces, rather than a shear compliance. In the large-matrix limit, the Hermitized Dyson equation gives \(J=(1-q)^{-3}/[1-(\alpha_0/\alpha_c)^2]\) on the stable side, where \(q<1\) is the Wishart aspect ratio and \(\alpha_c=(1-q)^{3/2}\). Thus the random coupling amplifies the response up to the onset of linear instability. At the unshifted isostatic point \(q=1\), the limiting spectrum enters the right half-plane for every nonzero \(\alpha_0\), so there is no stable isostatic susceptibility at nonzero activity. Direct matrix calculations show response amplification away from the threshold and a broadened stability crossover at finite size. Near marginality, a single singular value often carries much of the inverse trace, including in unstable realizations for which that trace is not a steady response.

authors.name: Hisao Hayakawa

papers.title: Scanning Gate Microscopy Modulation of Supercurrent in Graphene Josephson Junctions
papers.summary: Graphene Josephson junctions (JJs) represent an excellent platform for quantum technologies, thanks to the combination of high carrier mobility, ballistic transport, and gate-tunable critical currents, preserved even under quantizing magnetic fields. Investigating the spatial distribution of supercurrent flow could be crucial for elucidating transport mechanisms and advancing the engineering of these devices. In this work, we employ a scanning gate microscope to investigate supercurrent transport in hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated graphene JJs. We study the supercurrent modulation as a function of tip voltage bias and tip-to-sample distance and provide a complete characterization of the tip-induced modulation. Our experimental results are quantitatively consistent with numerical simulations and pave the way toward local mapping and manipulation of gate-tunable superconducting phenomena with unprecedented spatial resolution.

authors.name: Ivan Villani, Samuele Fracassi, Niccol\`o Traverso Ziani, Maura Sassetti, Matteo Carrega, Vaidotas Miseikis, Camilla Coletti, Fabio Beltram, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Sergio Pezzini, Stefan Heun

papers.title: Synthesis and structural validation of close-to-stoichiometric NiTe$_2$ single crystals
papers.summary: We report the synthesis of close-to-stoichiometric NiTe$_{2}$ single crystals via chemical vapor transport together with precise structural characterization. A combined analysis using powder and single crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD) was performed to determine lattice parameters and structural details. High-resolution single crystal XRD reveals no evidence of interstitial nickel, confirming a close-to-stoichiometric composition. This work establishes a reliable benchmark for the crystal structure of NiTe$_{2}$, offering a reference for future studies on its physical properties.

authors.name: T. Tirasutt, L. H. Tjeng, A. C. Komarek

papers.title: Chiral bosonic mean-field Ansatz and spin dynamics in spin-1 Kitaev magnets
papers.summary: The Kitaev model is a paradigmatic system for realizing quantum spin liquids, but its higher-spin extensions are not exactly solvable, and their spin dynamics is less well understood than in the spin-$1/2$ case. We reexamine a previously introduced triplet-pairing $\phi_t=\pi/2$ phase pattern for the antiferromagnetic $S=1$ Kitaev model and extend the analysis to weak symmetric off-diagonal exchanges $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$. Using a bond-operator formulation of Schwinger-boson mean-field theory, we calculate the dynamical spin structure factor for the triplet $0$-flux and $\pi/2$-flux states. At the pure Kitaev point, the $\pi/2$-flux Ansatz yields a flatter spectrum, consistent with its weakly dispersive spinon bands, and suppresses longer-range spin correlations more strongly than the $0$-flux Ansatz. Spectral flatness provides a consistency check for short-ranged spin correlations but is not, by itself, a diagnostic of time-reversal symmetry breaking. Three-spin correlations reveal staggered chirality in the mean-field state, which breaks time reversal but preserves combined inversion and time reversal. At the pure Kitaev point, the $\pi/2$-flux Ansatz also captures the dominant low-energy features of the exact-diagonalization spectra better than the $0$-flux Ansatz. For representative weak perturbations along $\Gamma'=\Gamma$, we obtain gapped solutions within the constrained $\pi/2$-flux manifold. These results support the triplet $\pi/2$-flux chiral bosonic Ansatz as a useful mean-field description of spin dynamics near the antiferromagnetic $S=1$ Kitaev limit with weak off-diagonal exchanges.

authors.name: Daiki Sasamoto, Arnaud Ralko, Jaime Merino, Joji Nasu

papers.title: Doping-driven Mott transition from steady-state density functional theory
papers.summary: We describe the doping-driven Mott transition in the Hubbard model within the framework of steady-state density functional theory, or i-DFT. In order to access the many-body spectral function in i-DFT, an approximation to the exchange-correlation (xc) bias at arbitrary density and current is required. By making use of Fermi-liquid theory, we derive conditions on the xc bias of i-DFT in terms of the quasiparticle weight, thus establishing a clear connection between i-DFT and Fermi-liquid theory. The Fermi liquid conditions are then employed to guide the construction of an approximation to the xc bias functional. Numerical results obtained with this functional demonstrate that the doping-driven Mott transition can indeed be captured with i-DFT. More generally, our i-DFT approach to calculate spectral functions establishes an explicit form for the functional relationship between the many-body spectral function and the ground state electronic density.

authors.name: David Jacob, Stefan Kurth

papers.title: Geometric Propulsion of a Scallop with Control-Dependent Hydrodynamics
papers.summary: We study a force-free single-hinge swimmer driven by two controls. When its axial hydrodynamic connection depends only on the opening angle, we show that the mean displacement per cycle vanishes in the periodic state at any driving rate. An independent control of the hydrodynamic response removes this restriction. For a factorized connection, the displacement at arbitrary driving rate is an integral of a measurable shape moment against the hydrodynamic modulation; in the slow-driving limit it reduces to a curvature flux which, at fixed potential and connection, is independent of the shape mobility. A reflecting harmonic model illustrates how thermal fluctuations modify this flux without generating it, and a hinged-bead model with variable passive slip gives a quantitative opening--closing test of the mechanism. We distinguish these propulsion results from the leading shape-sector dissipation, which depends on the mobility and is governed by a thermodynamic metric.

authors.name: Hisao Hayakawa

papers.title: Interferometry reveals spin-singlet fractional quantum Hall edges in graphene
papers.summary: The edge modes of spin-singlet fractional quantum Hall (FQH) phases are manifestations of multicomponent topological order and SU(2) spin symmetry. An archetype is the spin-unpolarized state at $\nu$=2/3, whose edge is expected to host spatially coexisting yet counter-propagating charge and neutral spin modes. Despite efforts, its edge properties, including spin coherence and spin-charge separation, have remained elusive owing to the difficulty of resolving spins in FQH edge transport. Here, we develop a spin-sensitive probe of graphene FQH edges by using a p-n junction to interface a target FQH state with a probe integer quantum Hall (QH) state of opposite polarity. An Aharonov-Bohm (AB) interferometer forms along the interface, when the target and probe edge channels carry the same spin. We identify the spin-unpolarized and polarized edges of the $\nu$=2/3 states at lower and higher magnetic fields, respectively, through spin-dependent interference. A novel multiparticle AB interference between two electrons of opposite spin emerges from spin-charge separation and recombination on the unpolarized edge, featuring a spin swap. Our results establish edge transport as a probe of spin-singlet topological orders, with implications for parafermion platforms in graphene-superconductor hybrids.

authors.name: R. Ayache, K. Kim, M. Kuiri, Q. Benichou, H. Chakraborti, L. Pugliese, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, H. -S. Sim, P. Roulleau

papers.title: Foundations of Many-Body Theory of Quantum Unified Statistics: Green functions and Linear Response Theory
papers.summary: We develop a comprehensive many-body theory for systems of particles obeying quantum unified statistics, or quons. After exploring the properties of the Fock space of this system, we formulate a systematic S-matrix expansion and a generalized Wick's theorem. A consistent Green-function formalism is constructed at both zero and finite temperatures, accompanied by a generalized Wick's theorem appropriate for infinite-statistics operator algebras. Within this framework, we establish diagrammatic rules for interacting quon systems. Employing the random phase approximation, we derive the dielectric function and reveal the emergence of anomalous plasmon modes that have no direct counterpart in conventional Bose or Fermi systems. We further analyze the ground-state energy, energy-loss function, generalized Thomas-Fermi screening wave vectors, and Friedel oscillations, elucidating how infinite statistics qualitatively modifies collective behavior and screening properties.

authors.name: M. Beyrami, M. N. Najafi, H. Esmaili, M. Dournama, H. Mohammadzadeh

papers.title: Projective representation theory of spin space groups
papers.summary: Spin space groups provide the symmetry framework for magnetic crystals with weak spin-orbit coupling, but extracting their physical consequences requires a general theory of irreducible representations. The central difficulty is that spin space groups are represented projectively: their factor systems can render lattice translations noncommuting, induce nonsymmorphic actions in momentum space, and modify the projective structure of little cogroups. These effects lie beyond conventional space-group representation theory. Here, using Mackey's theory of group extensions, we develop a unified constructive framework for all collinear, coplanar, and noncoplanar spin space groups, including antiunitary symmetries and general factor systems. A central result is a canonical decomposition of the relevant factor system $\nu$ into a translational factor $\sigma$, a mixed factor $\gamma$ coupling translations to point-group operations, and a point-group factor $\alpha$. This decomposition makes transparent how ordinary representation theory is modified: $\sigma$ determines the projective translation algebra and the appropriate Brillouin zone, $\gamma$ controls the momentum-space group action and can make it nonsymmorphic, and $\alpha$ contributes to the factor systems of little cogroups. On this basis, we construct all projective irreducible corepresentations by induction over momentum-space orbits. The framework identifies which nonsymmorphic momentum-space symmetries can be realized by spin space groups and how they reconstruct high-symmetry momenta. It reveals Brillouin spaces that are compact flat manifolds, Weyl points of the same chirality locked by projective translation symmetry, and spin space group symmetry-enforced Zak phases as well as Chern insulators. Our results establish the representation-theoretic foundation for systematic studies of weak-spin-orbit-coupled magnetic materials.

authors.name: Zheng Zhang, Peiyuan Wang, Y. X. Zhao

papers.title: Lattice in Line: Optimized DMRG ordering for complex lattice geometries
papers.summary: The density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) is a one-dimensional tensor-network technique, but it is not limited to one-dimensional systems: it can be applied to periodic 2D and 3D clusters and molecules, provided their sites are first enumerated along a line; a step one may call ``lattice compilation''. This paper discusses three proxy loss functions for finding this optimal enumeration: the graph bandwidth $B$ (maximum interaction range), the cutwidth $C$ (maximum number of bonds crossing a cut), and the average interaction range $R$. Constructing the Hamiltonian MPO (matrix-product operator) for a large set of clusters that are of interest in frustrated magnetism, I find that $C$ determines the peak SU(2) Heisenberg MPO bond dimension and $R$ the average one. Targeting $(C,R)$ lexicographically yields the best energies. Targeting $B$ indirectly reduces $C$, but not as efficiently as targeting $C$ directly. Otherwise, the value of $B$ itself is largely irrelevant in the sense that good DMRG energies can have large $B$. To perform the optimization, classic heuristics (e.g.\ reverse Cuthill--McKee) prove unreliable even for small clusters, and I find that a QUBO formulation improves them only marginally. Instead I propose a staged optimization built on Boolean satisfiability (SAT) and constraint-programming (CP) solvers, CP-SAT of Google's OR-Tools (a hybrid of CP propagation and SAT clause learning) and the SAT solvers CaDiCaL and Glucose. This approach yields significantly better orderings together with rigorous bounds. The corresponding \textit{Lattice in Line} code is available at https://github.com/spinflip/lattice_in_line and was designed with extensive use of the Fable 5 large language model.

authors.name: Roman Rausch

papers.title: Arrested phase separation and amorphous patterns in charged binary fluids
papers.summary: Frustration generated by competing interactions can stabilise patterns with tunable lengthscales which evade indefinite coarsening and macroscopic phase separation. Here we investigate a charged binary fluid in which the tendency toward phase separation is opposed by screened electrostatic repulsion. Combining analytics and numerical simulations, we identify a regime of arrested phase separation characterised by finite-wavelength instability. The resulting states include droplet and labyrinthine phases in two dimensions, and droplets, concentric shells and tubular structures in three dimensions. Surprisingly, some of these structures are amorphous morphologies that emerge reproducibly from different initial conditions. Free-energy estimates suggest that these disordered structures may be thermodynamically stabilised by frustration, rather than being kinetically trapped. Our results identify a simple mechanism through which the competition between phase separation and screened electrostatics can generate equilibrium amorphous microphases with glassy features.

authors.name: Logan H. Grant, Ana Bensabat, Eva Posp\'i\v{s}ilov\'a, Joost de Graaf, Alexander Morozov, Giuseppe Negro, Ciprian G. Pruteanu, Tyler N. Shendruk, Davide Marenduzzo

papers.title: Categorical classification of non-Fermi liquids in 2+1 dimensions
papers.summary: A defining feature of non-Fermi liquids is a lack of the quasiparticle peak on the Fermi surface in the spectral function, which is usually realized by coupling a finite density of fermions with critical collective fluctuations. However, these features of the two- and three-point vertex functions are qualitatively the same across many non-Fermi liquids, which has made it difficult to classify them beyond the definition by negation. We point out that the four-point function in the pairing channel contains rich information that positively differentiates distinct types of non-Fermi liquids. Using the generalized notion of fixed points that captures scale-dependent universal pairing interaction, we provide a non-perturbative classification of 2+1-dimensional non-Fermi liquids. In the large Fermi momentum limit with fixed dimensionless couplings, metals coupled with long-wavelength critical fluctuations are classified into seven superuniversality classes. Each of them exhibits a unique phase diagram in the space of temperature and bare four-fermion coupling. The present work generalizes the earlier perturbative classification to strongly interacting non-Fermi liquids by leveraging kinematic constraints.

authors.name: Shubham Kukreja, Dawson M. Willerton, Sung-Sik Lee

papers.title: Electron-electron interactions mediated by vibrations: Implications for chirality-induced spin selectivity
papers.summary: Molecular vibrations that modulate both electronic hopping and spin--orbit coupling (SOC) have been proposed as an ingredient of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS). We study a four-site bridge coupled to a single Peierls mode that modulates both terms, with amplitudes $g$ and $\chi$. An exact Lang--Firsov transformation yields the transformed Hamiltonian in closed form; in the antiadiabatic limit, it reduces to a purely fermionic model with instantaneous vibration-mediated interactions, whose two-body part separates into $g^2$, $\chi^2$, and $g\chi$ channels, the last containing a Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction (DMI) and correlated hopping. For a common SOC axis, local spin rotations mix these channels, so that the DMI is not separately gauge invariant; the invariant content lies in the components $g_\parallel$ and $g_\perp$ of the Peierls coupling parallel and perpendicular to the static bond. For spin-independent injection and extraction, the acceptor polarization $P_A$ is odd in both components, vanishes on two nodal lines, and reverses with the handedness of the bridge. We also prove that, for a common SOC axis and a single irreversible exit, a single electron transferred through an empty bridge acquires no long-time polarization, at any coupling strength. Donor--bridge--acceptor simulations with a half-filled bridge and the mode treated explicitly obey the symmetry rule. At weak coupling, $P_A$ scales as $g_\parallel g_\perp\simeq g\chi$, and, for the transfer rates considered, on-site Coulomb repulsion enhances it by a factor of about three. Within the model, a long-time polarization of the transferred charge is thus a many-electron effect: it requires spin exchange between the transferred electron and the other bridge electrons.

authors.name: Leonardo Celada, Rocco Bellusci, D. K. Andrea Phan-Huu, Alessandro Chiesa, Stefano Carretta

papers.title: Quantum effects on the Peierls stress for screw dislocations in {\alpha}-Fe
papers.summary: The large discrepancy between the Peierls stress calculated using atomistic methods and that measured in experimental studies is well known. Despite significant research efforts over the past decades, our understanding of this mismatch remains limited. This work presents a multiscale study on the kinetics of screw dislocations in {\alpha}-Fe at 0.7K, employing the phonon description of temperature and using the Concurrent Atomistic-continuum (CAC) method as the simulation tool. Our simulations are shown to preserve the Bose-Einstein distribution of phonon modes and reproduce the nucleation and propagation of kink pairs. Large-scale CAC simulations with dislocation line lengths ranging from 0.1 to 2.1 microns, a typical range of lengths for screw dislocation lines, are performed, providing a quantitative and mechanistic understanding of the phonon-dislocation in {\alpha}-Fe. The experimentally measured Peierls stress in {\alpha}-Fe has been successfully reproduced, and the quantum effects on Peierls stress are quantified. Dependencies of phonon-dislocation interactions on dislocation line length and specimen size are explored and discussed.

authors.name: Jiaqi Sun, Yang Li, Boyang Gu, David McDowell, Youping Chen

papers.title: Interface Invariants of Rhombohedral Graphene with Layer-dependent Potentials and Couplings
papers.summary: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.

authors.name: Yuelong Li

papers.title: Collineations of particles as a tool to study nucleation and crystallization processes in liquids
papers.summary: We suggest several methods that can be used for identification of crystal nuclei in the studies of the nucleation and crystallization processes in multicomponent systems and in situations when the forming crystalline phase is different from the FCC, HCP or BCC lattices. The approaches are based on consideration of collineations of particles. They allow finding nuclei and separating them from each other. We demonstrate the methods by considering two systems. For a single-component system, we perform a comparison between the results derived from the collineations and those obtained using the coarse-grained bond-orientational order parameters. Further, we illustrate the methods by considering the crystallization process in a Wahnstr\"{o}m binary $BA_2$ system forming a rather complex crystal structure.

authors.name: V. A. Levashov

papers.title: Geometric Structure of Defects in General Teleparallel Geometry
papers.summary: We develop a curvature-free geometric framework for the description of topological defect structures. In conventional metric-affine models, dislocations are associated with torsion, disclinations with curvature, and point defects with non-metricity. However, this identification leads to a structural overlap in the defect classification, while curvature-squared metric formulations may also involve higher-order field equations. In this work we reformulate the defect variables within general teleparallel geometry, characterized by the vanishing of the total curvature, $R^a{}_b = 0$, while allowing nontrivial torsion and non-metricity. Within this setting, a reduced set of effective defect variables is constructed from selected components of the non-Riemannian field strengths. The torsion trace is adopted as an effective Burgers-type variable, the second trace of non-metricity as an effective Frank-type variable, and the first trace of non-metricity as a point-defect variable, while the scalar torsion component remains as an additional independent sector. The resulting structure defines a constrained geometric field system that admits a metric formulation. Quadratic Lagrangians constructed from torsion and non-metricity lead to second-order field equations in the teleparallel metric formulation considered here, without requiring curvature-squared terms. The framework provides a reduced geometric classification of effective defect fields and clarifies their underlying variational structure.

authors.name: Muzaffer Adak, Ertan Kok, Mehmet Orhan

papers.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
papers.summary: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $\lambda$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $\lambda \ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $\lambda \ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.

authors.name: Sergey Matveev

papers.title: GeoCANO: A Geometry-Conditioned Adaptive Neural Operator for Physical-Field Prediction on Varying Domains
papers.summary: Industrial design requires repeated evaluation of candidate configurations. Integral performance measures alone do not resolve critical local phenomena, while high-fidelity simulation remains costly. Existing physical-field surrogates often couple geometry representation and coordinate evaluation through prescribed mesh topologies, limiting reuse across resolutions. We propose the Geometry-Conditioned Adaptive Neural Operator (GeoCANO), which maps a sampled complete three-dimensional geometry to a coordinate-dependent field function. An attention-based encoder extracts a geometry state from unordered surface coordinates. A multiresolution axis-factorized hash encoding and query-wise sparse mixture-of-experts decoder enhance multiscale expressiveness. GeoCANO constructs the field representation before introducing output coordinates, allowing one geometry encoding to be reused across regions without rebuilding the graph for each output topology. We evaluated GeoCANO on transonic aerodynamic-field prediction over complete aircraft configurations using a Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes dataset of 10,484 wing-body-nacelle geometries. For unseen configurations within the sampled design family, GeoCANO outperformed baselines in complete-surface prediction, high-gradient pressure reconstruction, and pressure-drag recovery. It reduced pressure-coefficient mean absolute error by 77.9% relative to the strongest baseline and retained an advantage over a finite range of wall-normal distances. Ablation studies showed that geometry-modulated coordinate encoding achieved comparable accuracy with substantially fewer parameters than conventional three-dimensional hash encoding. Routing analysis indicated spatially structured, query-dependent expert specialization. These results demonstrate a reusable continuous-coordinate representation for rapid physical-field evaluation over varying geometries.

authors.name: Biao Chen, Xinrui Zhou, Xianlin Jin, Jing Wang, Jifa Zhang, Chen Zhai, Wei Liu, Miao Zhang

papers.title: Automated classification of modal displacements
papers.summary: The bending, torsional, or coupled character of a mode shape helps determine the dynamic behaviour of aerospace and civil structures. In vibration testing, it is assigned by inspecting mode shape plots, and depends on the analyst. This work proposes four indices to describe the motion of a mode from a few sensor vectors: a bending score, a torsion score, a twist share and an in-plane ratio. They are assessed on the first eight finite element modes of a tapered plate with a swept trailing edge. They are applied to identified XB-2 wing modes and to the published modes of the Sheraton Universal Hotel, a reinforced concrete (RC) building. On the plate, the twist share separates bending, coupled and torsion modes. The XB-2 modes include one bending and three coupled modes (one dominated by in-plane bending and two by out-of-plane bending). The coupled mode dominated by in-plane bending (15.25 Hz, in-plane ratio 1.33) was not investigated in earlier campaigns on the wing. On the RC building, all five modes are bending (twist share below 0.0005). The twist share and the in-plane ratio indicate the type of each mode. Hence, modes are classified without visually inspecting the mode shapes. Code and processed data are openly released.

authors.name: Gabriele Dessena, Marco Civera, Saray Undiano Ech\'aniz, Oscar Bonilla-Manrique

papers.title: InterGS+: Inter-Frame Gaussian Splatting Compression with Geometry-Aware Transformer Prediction and Adaptive Residual Coding
papers.summary: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides real-time photorealistic rendering, but representing each frame as irregular Gaussian primitives with high-dimensional attributes creates substantial storage and transmission cost. Exploiting temporal redundancy is challenging because Gaussian primitives do not preserve fixed identities across frames. We propose InterGS+, a lightweight post-hoc inter-frame codec that jointly improves temporal prediction and residual representation. Current-frame geometry is coded with G-PCC and reconstructed before prediction, enabling consistent temporal neighborhoods at encoder and decoder. Attributes are predicted using lightweight KNN and bilateral predictors together with a geometry-aware transformer for spherical-harmonic (SH) appearance, with per-Gaussian mode selection. Residual coding is adapted to each attribute: SH innovations are coded in a shared PCA domain using vector quantization with refinement, opacity and scale in activated gamma-companded domains, and rotation as canonicalized quaternion innovations using vector quantization and refinement. On MPEG dynamic sequences, InterGS+ achieves average BD-rate reductions of 45.48% over G-PCC Amd. 1 and 7.78% over InterGS-Lite, with corresponding BD-PSNR gains of 9.98 dB and 1.10 dB. Average decoding complexity is 0.049 ms/Gaussian, demonstrating efficient streamable dynamic 3DGS compression.

authors.name: Muhammad Talha, Zhu Li, Joel Jung

papers.title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Parameter-Varying Systems With Noisy Data
papers.summary: This paper proposes a tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme for unknown discrete-time linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems using offline noisy input-scheduling-state data. We establish a multi-trajectory simplified LPV fundamental lemma yielding a collective Hankel representation of finite-horizon trajectories. Constraining the Hankel coefficients to a scaled simplex uniformly bounds the noise-induced predictor mismatch but may exclude relevant constrained lifted trajectories. A convex-hull coverage condition for admissible receding-horizon continuations restores the required representability. LPV data-consistency and robust positively invariant sets provide tube-tightening ingredients computed directly from noisy data. The online problem is a quadratic program, for which recursive feasibility, closed-loop constraint satisfaction, and practical input-to-state stability are established. Numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

authors.name: Chi Wang, David Angeli

papers.title: Heterogeneous Risk-Sensitive Evolutionary Learning in Coordination Games: Polarization, Welfare Loss, and Intervention for Efficiency
papers.summary: We study evolutionary learning in coordination games in a finite population of agents with heterogeneous risk attitudes, modeled using the entropic risk measure (ERM). The population consists of two subpopulations, each with a fixed risk attitude. Under risk-sensitive best response with mutations (BRM), we characterize the long-run outcomes of the learning process. In particular, we characterize when a polarized state, in which the two subpopulations choose different actions, is uniquely stochastically stable in terms of agents' risk attitudes and the subpopulation sizes. Notably, this polarized state is strictly Pareto dominated by the payoff-dominant equilibrium under both expected payoffs and agents' own ERM-adjusted payoffs. Moreover, its welfare, measured by average expected payoff, is always lower than that of the payoff-dominant equilibrium and can also be lower than that of the risk-dominant equilibrium. Thus, heterogeneity of risk attitudes in learning alone can lead to an inefficient long-run outcome. To mitigate such inefficiency, we propose intervention mechanisms to modify agents' risk attitudes in learning. We show that a sufficiently large intervention share (the fraction of agents modified) and sufficiently high intervention intensity (the increase in their risk parameter) ensure that the payoff-dominant equilibrium is uniquely stochastically stable. However, greater intervention intensity cannot compensate for an insufficient intervention share, and a larger intervention share cannot compensate for insufficient intervention intensity.

authors.name: Solaleh Mohammadi, Yiman Fong, Kaiqing Zhang

papers.title: Adaptive Robust Optimisation for Frequency-Constrained Market Clearing Problem
papers.summary: This paper formulates the day-ahead market clearing as a two-stage adaptive robust optimisation problem in which the first stage determines unit commitment, energy dispatch, and reserve procurement, while the second stage represents worst-case balancing actions under simultaneous uncertainty in renewable generation, load, and HVDC converter outages. Frequency security is enforced explicitly through inertia and fast frequency response constraints at the synchronous-area level, with HVDC lines allowed to provide emergency power support within their available headroom. The resulting min--max--min problem is solved by a column-and-constraint generation algorithm and applied to an eight-country North Sea test system comprising three synchronous areas, sixteen onshore bidding zones, and five offshore wind farm hubs connected through a meshed HVDC grid. We compare the Home Market (HM) and Offshore Bidding Zone (OBZ) designs on this infrastructure across different uncertainty scenarios. The results first demonstrate the value of robustness, where deterministic solutions that ignore uncertainty are severely vulnerable to worst-case realisations. Comparing the two designs, we find that OBZ's offshore zone boundaries make line congestion visible to the day-ahead market, enabling targeted reserve procurement that raises day-ahead costs but substantially reduces real-time load shedding, yielding a net reduction in total system cost that grows with the severity of localised offshore uncertainty. When both designs face the identical worst-case contingency, HM cannot distinguish an offshore converter trip from normal operation and thus fails to hedge against it, while OBZ considers the risk at the day-ahead stage. This advantage can be seasonal, scaling with the ratio of offshore wind output to HVDC line capacity and diminishing when onshore generation dominates the supply mix.

authors.name: \"Ozlem Mahmuto\u{g}ullar{\i}, Hakan Ergun

papers.title: A concave-convex approach to bit depth allocation for linear MMSE estimation in wireless sensor networks with correlated noise
papers.summary: Nodes in a wireless sensor network (WSN) are generally powered by batteries, and therefore energy efficiency is crucial. The bit depth used to quantize the sensor signal samples heavily influences energy consumption, as it strongly impacts the amount of information to be transmitted between the sensor nodes. Bit depth allocation problems seek to assign a bit depth to each sensor signal to optimize network resources, such as energy or bandwidth, together with algorithmic performance. We study a general bit depth allocation problem for linear minimum mean squared error (MMSE) estimation in WSNs with spatially correlated noise and a communication energy model depending linearly on the sensor bit depths. This model follows from common configurations in digital communications with orthogonal multiple-access schemes. After relaxation to real variables, we formulate the resulting non-convex problem as a difference of convex (DC) problem, and develop an algorithm based on the concave-convex procedure (CCP) to find a local optimum. We show that the convex problem involved in each CCP iteration can be efficiently solved with a worst-case complexity that is linear in the number of sensors. Additionally, we show that our approach is more computationally efficient than previously proposed bit depth allocation algorithms and generic optimization methods, and it achieves significant energy savings.

authors.name: Fernando de la Hucha Arce, Marian Verhelst, Alexander Bertrand

papers.title: Your bids are showing: re-identifying power plants in anonymized market data, and a differentially private alternative
papers.summary: ERCOT publishes every generator's hourly offer curve 60 days after the operating day. Market monitors, researchers and traders use these records to study the merit order and check for withholding. PJM publishes the same kind of data with unit names replaced by codes, on the view that masking keeps offers confidential. We test that view on ERCOT data from 2024 to 2026, where names are public and so provide ground truth, by masking the records under PJM's published rules. Public EIA and EPA data match 25% of the masked units we can score (32% of their capacity) to their plant, and 45% fall within the top five guesses. PJM's feed carries the same fields, so we expect masking to fail there too. Publishing exact fuel-group totals instead does not help. An attacker who knows the other units in a group recovers one unit's high-price offers exactly, and an outsider who knows only the target's outage dates reaches a correlation of 0.77, most of it from a few renewable and hydro units that offer at very high prices (0.32 over fossil units). We propose a differentially private release: monthly totals by fuel group and price bin, with Gaussian noise calibrated under zero-concentrated differential privacy so that each unit's whole year of offers is protected. It publishes an unbiased noisy layer and derives a monotone supply curve and shares from it at no extra privacy cost. At $\varepsilon=10$ per unit-year the market supply curve stays within 11% of the truth, the implied clearing price within \$3.0/MWh, and the attacker's correlation falls to 0.23. Whether an analysis still works depends on one ratio, how much the true quantity varies month to month against the noise, which predicts the accuracy of totals to within 0.05. The clearing price, supply slope and combined-cycle capacity remain usable, but no monthly release, private or exact, can answer questions about single hours or single units.

authors.name: Nikhil Ravi

papers.title: Gaussian Process Data-Driven Hamiltonian for Probabilistic Safe Set Construction
papers.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability is a general framework for verifying the safety of nonlinear systems, but it relies on an accurate dynamics model. The data-driven Hamiltonian (DDH) framework avoids system identification by lower-bounding the Hamiltonian directly from state-control-velocity data. However, it requires a Lipschitz bound on the unknown dynamics which is hard to certify from finite data, and as a single global constant this bound makes the computed safe sets conservative. We propose the Gaussian process data-driven Hamiltonian (GP-DDH), a fully data-driven framework that constructs safe sets with probabilistic guarantees under a GP prior on the dynamics. Furthermore, we suggest two methods to choose the confidence parameter $\beta$, both mathematically guaranteed to underbound the Hamiltonian. The computed safe set lies inside the true one with posterior probability at least $1-\Delta$ for any $\Delta\in(0,1)$. Numerical experiments show that GP-DDH recovers a bigger volume of the true safe set than DDH while still correctly providing a conservative approximation, even when DDH is given a Lipschitz constant computed from the true dynamics.

authors.name: Seungseok Oh, Junho Kim, Jason J. Choi, Namhoon Cho

papers.title: Modeling Lunar Power Harvesting and Battery Recharging In The Presence of Random Pointing Error
papers.summary: In our work, we establish a lunar power beaming environment between a low-lunar orbiter and a circular solar panel mounted on top of a lunar vehicle located at the Lunar South Pole. Due to the random nature of the pointing errors, various upper bounds reflecting the severity of these errors are considered. Although harvested power is modelled stochastically in the literature, we extend this randomness to battery-storage analysis by deriving PDFs of state of charge, accumulated battery capacity and energy, and end-to-end efficiency for both battery charging modes. Then, our derivations are verified with extensive Monte Carlo simulations. Hence, our derivations provide a mathematical model that enables prediction and helps us understand the randomness of the corresponding variables. For the given pointing error levels, we quantify the differences between charging modes in these battery metrics. Our work explains the stochastic nature of these battery metrics in a realistic lunar environment. Regarding the end-to-end efficiency metric, which is the ratio of the stored electrical energy to the transmitted electrical energy, we observed that slow-charging efficiency is immune to pointing errors, and this mode can utilize only one-sixth of what the link can deliver under a mild pointing error.

authors.name: Bar{\i}\c{s} D\"onmez, Yanni Jiwan-Mercier, Julien Magn\'e, Guillaume Blanchette, Paolo Pino, S\'ebastien Loranger, G\"une\c{s} Karabulut Kurt

papers.title: Federated Policy Gradient for Dynamic Consensus: Gradient Dominance and Topological Bounds
papers.summary: This paper presents a federated optimization framework for dynamic consensus in homogeneous multi-agent systems. The underlying problem is challenged by the communication graph's spectral properties, which induce spatial heterogeneity and complicate decentralized control even when the dynamics of the agents are completely known. The problem is addressed in this paper by bridging distributed control theory with federated policy gradients. Accordingly, a comprehensive optimization landscape for dynamic consensus is established through a modal decomposition formulation. Specifically, a parameterized suboptimality bound is characterized that explicitly decouples the true aggregate policy gradient from the network covariance mismatch. Building on this formulation, sufficient conditions based on the graph's Laplacian spectrum are derived to recover exact gradient dominance, which guarantees convergence to the global consensus policy and establishes a lower bound on the achievable dominance coefficient. Furthermore, a Federated model-free consensus algorithm is proposed that utilizes zeroth-order exploration alongside a bisection-based discount factor annealing mechanism, successfully eliminating the need for an initial stabilizing policy. This approach achieves linear global convergence for policy optimization subroutines while maintaining strictly bounded outer iterations until dynamic consensus is achieved. Through extensive simulation studies and comparative feasibility analyses across diverse network topologies, it is demonstrated that the proposed federated approach consistently outperforms existing model-based and data-driven separation-based techniques.

authors.name: Maryam Babazadeh

papers.title: Barrier-Based Safety Filtering for Quadrotor Flight in Cluttered Environments Under Acceleration Limits
papers.summary: Accurate trajectory tracking alone does not guarantee safe quadrotor flight when the reference passes near obstacles or the available control authority is limited. This paper presents a safety-filtered trajectory-tracking framework for a quadrotor operating at a fixed altitude in obstacle-cluttered environments. A nominal tracking controller is combined with high-order control barrier constraints and an acceleration-constrained quadratic program. The safety filter preserves the nominal acceleration whenever it is admissible and modifies it only when the prescribed obstacle clearance is threatened. The analysis establishes nominal exponential tracking, forward invariance of the safe region under compatible initial conditions and continued quadratic-program feasibility, and bounded tracking error during safety intervention. Numerical experiments using an idealized planar translational model with single and multiple stationary circular obstacles show minimum clearances of $0.000$--$0.001$~m under the safety filter, compared with $-1.594/-1.421$~m under nominal control. Tracking RMSE increases from $0.618$ to $0.950$~m across reference-speed scales $0.6$--$1.6$, illustrating the effect of reference speed on tracking accuracy under safety constraints. Additional tests examine how acceleration limits affect control effort and feasibility. These findings inform safety-filter design for UAV trajectory tracking under limited control authority.

authors.name: Andi Rahmadiansah

papers.title: Active road noise control using networked mean-square learning and lightweight conditional compensation experts
papers.summary: Multichannel active road noise control (ARNC) requires effective noise reduction (NR) under causality and computational constraints. A computationally efficient method is proposed that separates linear control from condition-dependent nonlinear residual compensation. A finite impulse response (FIR) baseline filter is obtained through networked mean-square learning that can be made adaptive, while a multi-resolution FIR mixture-of-experts (MRF-MoE) module provides possibly nonlinear corrections. Training comprises baseline initialization, sample-graph-regularized expert and router optimization, and joint refinement. Target channels are treated as nodes in a connected network for mean-square error minimization, whereas training windows define a graph for regularizing routing probabilities. Each expert combines short-time dense and long-tail low-rank FIR filtering, and causal single-expert routing reduces inference computation. Compared with WaveNet-VNN under the same configuration, the proposed method reduces estimated inference cost by 96.3% while achieving higher NR on the test set.

authors.name: Xingzhao Huang, Hengzhi Zhou, Yu Shi, Ming Wu, Bin Liao, Yijing Chu

papers.title: Model Order Detection with Parameter Estimation Guarantees for the Matrix Pencil Method
papers.summary: Detecting the model order and estimating the parameters of sums of damped complex exponentials in noise is challenging when poles are closely spaced, the sample size is small, or the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is low. We propose REECAP, a matrix pencil (MP) algorithm for joint model order detection and pole estimation. The algorithm computes candidate poles using an overestimated working rank and classifies them using a score derived from their associated eigenvectors. The model order is then estimated by counting the retained candidates. The score measures the eigenvector energy concentration in coordinates corresponding to the dominant right singular subspace of the data Hankel matrix. Under a suitable rank condition, we derive a deterministic sufficient condition guaranteeing that a candidate whose score exceeds a certain threshold lies within a prescribed tolerance of at least one signal pole. This establishes a theoretical connection between eigenvector energy concentration and pole-estimation accuracy. Extensive simulations demonstrate improved model order detection and frequency estimation performance relative to conventional MP order detection methods, recent structure-aware MP methods, and information-theoretic criteria (ITC), across a broad range of scenarios, including clustered frequencies, low SNR in the threshold region, and small sample sizes. Runtime comparisons further demonstrate substantial computational savings, and moderate sensitivity to noise model mismatch, compared to the evaluated structure-aware and information-theoretic methods.

authors.name: Yehonatan-Itay Segman, David Sadka, Ronen Talmon

papers.title: Iterative Identification of Aperiodic Sampled-Data Systems via Affine LPV Models Scheduled by the Sampling Interval
papers.summary: This paper proposes a method for identifying a control-oriented model of a stable continuous-time linear system from aperiodically sampled input-output data. Rather than recovering the continuous-time matrices, the method directly identifies a discrete-time linear parameter-varying (LPV) state-space model that depends affinely on the measured normalized sampling-interval variation, a structure obtained from the first-order expansion of the zero-order-hold discretization. The resulting model is directly usable in control design for aperiodic sampled-data systems. An initial LPV estimate, including approximate first-order terms, is derived from a standard LTI subspace model through sampled-data relations. The method then iteratively alternates state-sequence reconstruction and LPV parameter refitting. Numerical examples show that the identified model retains high validation accuracy over a wide range of sampling-interval variations where a fixed LTI model degrades. Already at initialization, the state-space LPV structure substantially outperforms an LPV-ARX regression with the same scheduling variable, and the iterative refinement brings the model close to a state-measured benchmark, a practical upper-bound reference.

authors.name: Hiroshi Okajima, Yohei Hosoe

papers.title: Wireless-OptSG: A Versatile Multi-Agent Optimization Framework for Wireless Resource Allocation
papers.summary: 6G wireless networks are expected to accommodate heterogeneous service requirements across diverse deployment scenarios, giving rise to physical-layer resource allocation problems with scenario-dependent objectives and constraints. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and agent systems can interpret wireless-domain specifications and incorporate execution feedback into optimization. However, translating language-level reasoning into feasible, high-quality resource allocations remains challenging, since candidates need to satisfy precise mathematical constraints throughout iterative search. This work proposes the Wireless Optimization Solution Generator (Wireless-OptSG), a versatile multi-agent framework for physical-layer resource allocation. Wireless-OptSG organizes optimization as a feedback-driven candidate search guided by a static meta-prompt and an evolving optimization history. In a nested outer-inner loop, parallel agents explore solution trajectories and periodically exchange high-quality records to guide candidate generation. Feasible initialization uses executable optimization primitives, while a tiered repair pipeline restores feasibility and solution-dependent context improves retained-record informativeness. Experiments on four representative tasks under perfect and imperfect channel state information show that Wireless-OptSG achieves performance comparable to scenario-specific state-of-the-art (SOTA) solvers, exceeds SOTA in some settings, and consistently outperforms generic baselines, demonstrating its potential as a transferable optimization framework for future wireless networks.

authors.name: Wenhe Zhang, Xin Li, Hanzhi Chen, Chau Yuen

papers.title: Damping Ratio and Convergence Rate Analysis for Inverter-Based Power Systems via Root Locus
papers.summary: As more renewables enter the grid, it becomes insufficient to rely solely on the center of inertia frequency to analyze the transient performance, especially for oscillation behaviors. Motivated by this, we study the transient frequency performance of inverter-based power systems. Two key performance criteria are considered: the damping ratio and the convergence rate, which are determined by the angles and the real parts of the closed-loop poles, respectively. By decomposing the network system into a set of scalar feedback systems, we show that the closed-loop poles can be analyzed using the root locus of a scalar feedback system as the gain varies from the smallest nonzero eigenvalue to the largest eigenvalue of the scaled Laplacian matrix of the interconnection network. Based on this, we derive sufficient conditions that ensure desired damping and convergence performance. Our analysis shows that the worst-case damping ratio and convergence rate occur when the gain equals the largest and the smallest nonzero eigenvalues of the scaled Laplacian, respectively. This result significantly simplifies the performance assessment. We further provide guidelines for tuning the inverter parameter. Numerical simulations are included to illustrate and validate the proposed approach.

authors.name: Dan Wang, Wei Chen, Yan Jiang, Shinji Hara

papers.title: Strategic Beam Brainstorming for Generative Site-Specific Beamforming
papers.summary: A novel plug-and-play candidate beam selection strategy is proposed for generative site-specific beamforming (GenSSBF), a paradigm that draws on a learned conditional channel distribution to generate multiple plausible beams. Under a limited probing budget, realizing the full potential of GenSSBF requires identifying which candidate beams are worth probing. To this end, the marginal probing value is first derived to guide strategic candidate probing by quantifying each beam's additional gain beyond those already selected. Based on this criterion, two algorithms are developed without retraining the generator: 1) Greedy candidate probing (GCP) selects all candidate beams from a locally generated pool prior to over-the-air probing, requiring only a single feedback round; 2) Adaptive candidate probing (ACP) exploits reference signal received power (RSRP) feedback after each probe to update channel hypothesis weights and guide the next beam selection, without increasing the asymptotic complexity. Simulations across three ray-tracing scenarios under noiseless and noisy probing reveal that: 1) candidate complementarity is key to efficient beam brainstorming; and 2) ACP is particularly beneficial when initial sensing leaves substantial channel uncertainty and subsequent feedback is reliable.

authors.name: Zihao Zhou, Zhaolin Wang, Yuanwei Liu

papers.title: Net-Gain-Optimized Constellation Shaping for the 5G NR DFT-s-OFDM Uplink: Probabilistic, Geometric, and Joint Designs
papers.summary: Constellation shaping improves the achievable information rate of coded modulation. On the single-carrier uplink waveform of 5G New Radio, discrete Fourier transform (DFT)- spread orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), the same shaping can also raise the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). A higher PAPR forces more power amplifier back- off and reduces the link budget. Prior work characterized this penalty for fixed probabilistically and geometrically shaped constellations, but did not turn the trade-off into a design objective. We optimize constellation shaping (CS) to maximize the net-gain, i.e., the sum of the communication gain and the PAPR gain, at the fixed spectral efficiency of 4 bits per channel use for 64-QAM. We apply it to probabilistic shaping (PS), geometric shaping (GS), and a joint scheme that combines both. As the coded block error rate cannot be evaluated inside a gradient loop, we use the achievable information rate as a surrogate for the communication performance and the PAPR surrogate as differentiable cost functions for the optimizer. The learned constellations are then validated on a complete DFT-s-OFDM link-level chain. Conventional Maxwell-Boltzmann PS yields a negative net-gain, but net-gain-aware optimization removes this deficit in every method.
