GS converts it into a substantial gain, as it not only improves the communication performance but also lowers the PAPR below the uniform 64-QAM reference, achieving the largest net-gain among the CS methods studied.

authors.name: G\"unther Lindorfer, Andreas Springer

papers.title: Online outlier-resilient data-driven moving horizon estimation for linear discrete-time systems
papers.summary: This paper addresses data-driven state estimation for linear systems of which online output measurements may be corrupted by sparse outliers of arbitrary magnitude. Using only offline input-state-output data without explicitly identifying a system model, we propose an outlier-resilient data-driven moving horizon estimation scheme, termed OORD-MHE, based on Willems' fundamental lemma. The scheme employs a truncated-quadratic loss on the output residuals, parameterized by a truncation threshold, to mitigate the influence of online outliers. We establish sufficient conditions under which the resulting estimation error remains uniformly bounded. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed OORD-MHE scheme generates accurate state estimates in the presence of sparse online outliers.

authors.name: Jingshi Yao, Zenghong Huang, Xiaojie Li, Xunyuan Yin

papers.title: CRISP: Sparse Risk-Calibrated Front-End Allocation and Fusion for Low-Resolution Snapshot GNSS Positioning
papers.summary: Low-resolution global navigation satellite system snapshot receivers face strong coupling among automatic gain control compression, coarse quantization, and waveform distortion from nonlinear interference mitigation. This paper presents Cross-Risk Interference-Resilient Snapshot Positioning, denoted CRISP, an aided single-snapshot architecture that allocates and fuses complementary pre-correlation processors over a bounded position-clock search region under a shared direct position estimation solve budget. On a pre-frozen baseband descriptor partition, offline calibration estimates uncentered second-order position-error cross moments and solves cardinality-constrained simplex programs along east, north, and up axes, retaining validation-screened multibranch combinations while assigning single matched processors elsewhere. An online reliability gate screens the same quantized snapshot to route unfamiliar waveforms toward single-branch protective operators. We characterize profiled contrast shifts after nonlinear suppression and derive a conditional finite-sample excess-risk bound across disjoint splits alongside an exact same-snapshot gating risk identity. Across 17 568 simulated 2-ms GPS L1 C/A trials, CRISP reduces core positioning root-mean-square error by 13.84%, > 100-m gross errors by 41.32%, and multi-geometry error by 12.23% over Snapshot-FD at 1.43 core and 1.51 overall solves per snapshot.

authors.name: Zhihan Zeng, Kaihe Wang, Zhongpei Zhang, Li-Ta Hsu

papers.title: Integrated Semantic Sensing and Communications: Target Attribute Inference and Beamforming Design
papers.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is expected to become a key enabling paradigm for future 6G networks, supporting emerging applications that require a comprehensive understanding of sensed targets. As a step toward this goal, we consider an ISAC system with semantic sensing capability that determines what the sensed target is, where it is located, and how large it is. However, the accurate retrieval of these attributes, including target class, location, and size, is challenging due to the highly nonlinear relationships between the received signals and different attributes. In addition, new beamforming strategies are also required to balance multi-user communication and semantic sensing performance. To address the first challenge, we develop a physics-guided inference model that leverages signal propagation priors and a unified Transformer backbone to effectively characterize the highly nonlinear relationships between received ISAC signals and multiple attributes. As for the second challenge, we develop a multi-stage training framework for the optimization of beamformers and model parameters, aiming to improve semantic sensing performance while guaranteeing multi-user communication requirements. Simulation results show that under the same multi-user communication rate requirements, the proposed scheme can provide more than 12% performance gains across classification, localization, and size estimation tasks compared with existing methods and achieve 91.21% classification accuracy using only two OFDM frames, demonstrating the feasibility of accurate semantic sensing with low measurement overhead.

authors.name: Haobo Zhang, Shuhao Zeng, Boya Di, Hongliang Zhang, Harald Haas, Lingyang Song

papers.title: DBFM: Dual-Band Flow Matching for ECG Super-Resolution
papers.summary: Long-term ECG monitoring is increasingly supported by wearable and portable devices, where limited power and transmission capacity motivate acquisition at lower sampling rates. ECG super-resolution (SR) aims to reconstruct high-sampling-rate signals from low-sampling-rate recordings for clinical analysis. A recent diffusion-based approach, DiSR-ECG, has demonstrated powerful reconstruction performance, particularly in cross-dataset evaluation. However, its iterative sampling during inference incurs high computational cost when processing large volumes of long-term ECG data. To reduce this cost while maintaining reconstruction accuracy, we propose Dual-Band Flow Matching (DBFM), a generative framework for ECG SR. DBFM decomposes ECG signals into low- and high-frequency components and separately learns their source-to-target transport using conditional flow matching. This dual-band formulation enables frequency-specific reconstruction, while one-step inference substantially reduces computational complexity. Experimental results show that DBFM achieves performance comparable to or better than DiSR-ECG while reducing inference FLOPs by approximately 98.7\%. These results demonstrate that DBFM enables computationally efficient ECG SR without compromising reconstruction quality.

authors.name: Fan-Yi Hsu, Kuan-Chen Wang, I Chiu, Kai-Chun Liu, Ping-Cheng Yeh, Yu Tsao

papers.title: Stability and periodic switching in feedback systems with sector-bounded hybrid integrators
papers.summary: We study stability of piecewise linear systems composed of the feedback interconnection of a linear time-invariant process and a sector-bounded hybrid integrator. Exploiting the observation that for such systems state-dependent switching sequences asymptotically exhibit periodic behaviour, we develop a spectral approach to stability analysis as an alternative to sufficient Lyapunov-based methods. We formulate a conjecture that asymptotic periodicity holds irrespective of the initial conditions and system stability, and provide a description of the limit system and propose an algorithm to obtain its parameters. We establish this rigorously for second-order linear-time invariant processes. Based on spectral properties of the resulting periodic limit system, we derive sufficient stability conditions. The results provide a novel viewpoint for accurate stability analysis of general state-based piecewise linear systems.

authors.name: Sebastiaan van den Eijnden, Kai Wulff, Christoph Weise, Johann Reger

papers.title: Dual-Pilot Design for OCDM Channel Estimation
papers.summary: Channel acquisition in orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) over doubly-dispersive channels incurs a large pilot overhead, since delay and Doppler jointly shift the symbols in the chirp domain and separating them requires repeated pilots, each protected against the complete coupled displacement. This letter proposes a dual-pulsone pilot design that reduces this overhead in two steps. First, a pulsone occupies fewer chirp-domain bins than alias-free Doppler estimation requires, deliberately allowing Doppler wrapping. Second, a phase-offset pulsone is placed within the same protected region to observe a complementary part of the displacement, further reducing the shared guard. The phase offset also resolves the wrapping ambiguity, enabling low-complexity delay-Doppler estimation. Simulations show competitive estimation and BER performance, with the lowest complexity and highest payload efficiency among the considered OCDM estimators.

authors.name: Ayoub Ammar Boudjelal, Huseyin Arslan

papers.title: Overparameterized Simulation-Error Minimization for Nonlinear System Identification: Horizon-Uniform Landscape and Identifiability
papers.summary: Simulation-error minimization is a standard criterion in nonlinear system identification, but its landscape is nonconvex and its conditioning can degrade geometrically with the data horizon N. We propose to lift the trajectory with a free, softly penalized per-step correction, which yields a fit loss that gradient descent provably minimizes: under a rank condition on the output map and a bound on the one-step Jacobian, it satisfies a Polyak-Lojasiewicz inequality with an explicit constant independent of N. A zero-loss model leaves the physical parameter undetermined. Identifiability is restored by a minimal-correction selection principle: under structural identifiability, the global minimizer of the penalized loss returns the true parameters for every positive penalty weight, and under noise and unmodeled dynamics the parameter error grows at most linearly with the mismatch. The resulting estimator, gradient descent on the fit loss followed by a homotopy in the penalty weight, reconciles fit and selection, with a local convergence guarantee. In experiments, it recovers the parameters on long records of expanding and chaotic systems on which single shooting fails.

authors.name: Cesare Donati, Constantino Lagoa

papers.title: Interference-Free In-Symbol Pilots for High-Mobility DFT-s-OFDM Uplink
papers.summary: The 5G New Radio (NR) uplink uses discrete Fourier transform spread orthogonal frequency-division multi- plexing (DFT-s-OFDM) for its low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). Its demodulation reference signal (DMRS) occupies whole symbols, although channel estimation only needs channel samples. Since existing designs cannot place pilots inside a data symbol without interference on the data, or on both data and pilots, NR keeps whole DMRS symbols, which wastes spectral efficiency (SE), and adds more of them as the channel varies faster, lowering the SE further. We develop a technique that places pilots free of data interference inside the data symbols, for frequency-domain channel estimation in every symbol. Using the Zak transform, we show that leaving a set of equally spaced pre- DFT samples empty frees one column of the Zak grid of the DFT output. The data values of the pilot subcarriers are relocated into this column by adding a constant over a few subcarrier combs, which preserves the energy and keeps the NR DFT sizes. The receiver undoes it linearly with comb sums, without decisions or side information, and a symbol loses as few as one data sample beyond its pilots. Since the pilots raise the PAPR, we keep them few per symbol and hop their positions across symbols, so that a two-dimensional estimator over the slot resolves long delay spreads at high Doppler. On 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels, pilots in every symbol achieve a higher effective SE than all NR DMRS configurations from pedestrian to high- speed-train velocities, at a PAPR close to plain DFT-s-OFDM.

authors.name: Ayoub Ammar Boudjelal, Huseyin Arslan

papers.title: Waveform Randomization for Secure ISAC Against Informed Eavesdroppers
papers.summary: We study waveform-level protection of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) against a UAV-mounted eavesdropper (Eve) that knows the waveform construction and the phase-key generation rules. The novelty of this work is a systematic, budget-explicit attack analysis: instead of relying on undisclosed design details, we quantify what an informed Eve can learn and reconstruct, and how much computation this takes. We protect the sensing reference with Fourier-curve modulation, phase keys, and tangent Artificial Noise (AN), with burst- specific information shared over secure backhaul. We compare three key-generation rules against offline Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based sequence identification and online Adam and phase-aware expectation-maximization (EM) key recovery, under complete or partial nominal-sequence knowledge. A power- domain model couples residual key error with imperfect AN removal and predicts coherent delay locking. Results show that reusable key structure permits sequence identification even when demodulation fails, position-dependent keying raises recovery difficulty, and seed-expanded keying resists the evaluated clas- sifier within the learning budget. Waveform simulations under multipath, clutter, and echo accumulation confirm the sensing impact.

authors.name: Zexin Fang, Bin Han, Shuangyang Li, Hans D. Schotten

papers.title: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Forward Scatter Radar
papers.summary: Forward Scatter Radar (FSR) enhances the detection of low-observable targets by exploiting the increased radar cross section that occurs when a target crosses the transmitter-receiver baseline. Conventional FSR typically uses single-input single-output (SISO) architectures with limited localization capability, while recent single-input multiple-output (SIMO) systems enable non-coherent angular estimation. This paper introduces a multiple-input multiple-output FSR (MIMO-FSR) framework for joint estimation of target direction of departure (DoD) and direction of arrival (DoA) from non-coherent, amplitude-only measurements. By exploiting antenna arrays at both the transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX), the proposed approach enables two-dimensional angular localization without phase synchronization among TX/RX array elements. We establish the underlying operating principle under ideal signal separability and then develop practical frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) and time-division multiplexing (TDM) implementations. For each scheme, dedicated signal models and processing methods compensate for distortions caused by frequency offsets and target motion, respectively. We also derive analytical expressions for angular resolution, ambiguity conditions, and output-map distortions. Extensive numerical simulations for short- and long-baseline scenarios reveal operational limits and trade-offs between the two multiplexing schemes. Finally, proof-of-concept outdoor experiments using software-defined radio platforms validate the proposed framework. The results demonstrate joint DoD-DoA estimation and support the feasibility of MIMO-FSR for future active, passive, and integrated sensing and communications applications.

authors.name: Abdollah Ajorloo, Stefano Amato Ciciretti, Fabiola Colone

papers.title: Automated Design and Evaluation Pipeline for Optimal Control Transcriptions in Model Predictive Control
papers.summary: The computational burden of Model Predictive Control represents a bottleneck limiting its widespread deployment in real-time applications. The selection of the optimal control transcription strategy for a given MPC formulation is a key driver of computational efficiency. Identifying performant MPC transcriptions requires significant effort and domain knowledge. We propose an automated pipeline for the design and evaluation of performant optimal control transcriptions for a given MPC formulation. Custom multi-objective design metrics, such as computation time or closed-loop performance, can be specified and are minimized by the pipeline. As a transcription method, a pseudospectral Legendre-Gauss-Radau method is employed. We show that it incorporates forward Euler integration and implicit collocation methods of low and high order in one formulation, leveraging the pipeline to evaluate both numerical approaches. Furthermore, different mesh configurations can be parameterized. To identify the optimal configuration of the transcription, a Bayesian Optimization framework is applied. The pipelines improvements in MPC performance are demonstrated through On-Orbit Servicing scenarios involving spacecraft motion planning and closed-loop control.

authors.name: Fabio Schneider, Peter K\"otting, Renato Loureiro

papers.title: Perfect Scores, Misplaced Explanations: A Controlled Study of Explainability in Audio Deepfake Detection
papers.summary: What if an explanation achieves perfect scores but it is uninterpretable? We show that this happens when explaining audio deepfake detectors. Using an optimization-based method, we explain a state-of-the-art wav2vec2-based detector. The explanations achieve optimal scores on standard explainability metrics, i.e. fidelity and faithfulness. Visual inspection, however, reveals unintuitive and uninterpretable patterns. To understand this discrepancy, we run a controlled perturbation study in which we modify known frequency regions of the speech signal. Although we propose a model that is able to obtain close-to-optimal results with respect to the metrics, the explanations locate the manipulated region only when it is fixed across samples, and mostly fall to chance level when it varies. We further show that the signal used to fill the removed regions largely determines the explanation and its localization, without being reflected in the metrics.

authors.name: David Combei, Dan Oneata, Francesco Paissan, Cem Subakan, Horia Cucu, Adriana Stan

papers.title: Robust inverse dielectric design of skin phantoms for implantable wireless link evaluation
papers.summary: Skin phantoms support reproducible evaluation of implantable wireless links, yet published complex permittivities of skin predict different propagation losses. We formulate a robust inverse design to determine a homogeneous phantom permittivity that minimizes the largest channel-loss difference across selected skin reference models, incidence angles and both transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic polarizations. Computed candidates and analytical lower bounds bracket the optimal mismatch and constrain the critical depth. Across seven frequencies from 5 to 500 GHz, the minimax mismatch at 1.3 mm ranges from 1.13 to 13.72 dB. For a 3 dB tolerance, suitable permittivities exist at every investigated depth at 5 GHz, while critical depths at the other frequencies range from 0.23 to 1.01 mm. Only one of seven material cases from the literature meets a 6 dB tolerance at 1.3 mm. These results translate channel-loss tolerances into quantitative design criteria for skin phantoms used in implantable wireless link evaluation.

authors.name: Andreas Prokscha, Ali Alhaj Abbas, Samar Elmaadawy, Mandana Jalali, Yamen Zantah, Josep M. Jornet, Daniel Erni, Thomas Kaiser

papers.title: Contract2Reach: Discretization-Induced Contractive Dynamic Programming for High-Dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) enable undiscounted Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis for high-dimensional systems, but their performance can be sensitive to hyperparameter choices and the underlying system dynamics. We introduce Contract2Reach, which recasts undiscounted finite-horizon reachability as a sequence of contractive fixed-point problems solved by backward time marching. Our formulation combines discretized temporal and spatial derivatives to construct a contractive mapping without introducing a discount factor. Under standard assumptions, we prove that the exact scheme converges to the unique viscosity solution as both the temporal and spatial step sizes tend to zero. Unlike PINNs, our training fits rollout-based value targets via a single regression, without backpropagating through spatial value gradients. In the neural implementation, adaptive zero-level-set sampling and conservative target combination address high-dimensional sample sparsity and false positives, respectively. Experiments on a parameterized vertical drone, a 13D quadrotor, and a 40D publisher-subscriber system show competitive performance against PINNs-based baselines. Boundary evaluations on the vertical drone and publisher-subscriber systems demonstrate improved fidelity and reduced learning-rate sensitivity, revealing errors that volume-based metrics can miss.

authors.name: Jaeyoung Lee, Donggun Lee, Jason J. Choi, Namhoon Cho

papers.title: Embodied Intelligence for Spectrum Map Construction in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
papers.summary: Accurate spectrum map construction by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for intelligent resource management in low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs). Although various construction approaches have been investigated, their performance often degrades under extremely sparse sampling because purely data-driven models may not capture the underlying propagation physics. To address these challenges, an embodied intelligence framework is proposed, which synergistically integrates closed-loop perception-cognition-execution (PCE) coupling and embodied exploration to achieve precise and efficient spectrum construction. Based on this framework, a corresponding embodied cognition and decision network (ECDNet) with three tightly coupled modules is designed. Specifically, by leveraging distance-aware convolutions, the semantic bridge, and adaptive feature alignment mechanisms, ECDNet establishes the bidirectional information flow between construction and decision-making. Simulation results show that ECDNet achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.787 dBm at 4.00% sampling under the non-revisiting spiral protocol. Furthermore, a practical UAV-based spectrum construction platform is developed and field-deployed to provide prototype-level evidence that the sensing, cognition, and action modules execute as a closed loop on size, weight, and power constrained UAV edge devices.

authors.name: Hongtao Liang, Yiyao Wan, Jiahuan Ji, Lingda Meng, Fuhui Zhou, Qihui Wu

papers.title: QoS-Constrained Sum-Rate Maximization in RIS-Assisted Pinching-Antenna NOMA Systems
papers.summary: This paper investigates a two-user downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system jointly assisted by a single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) and a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). To maximize the achievable sum rate under quality-of-service (QoS) constraints, the pinching antenna (PA) positions, RIS phase shifts, and power allocation coefficients are jointly optimized. The resulting non-convex optimization problem is addressed using an alternating optimization (AO) framework, where power allocation is obtained in closed form, while RIS phase shifts and PA positions are optimized through majorization-minimization (MM) and sequential quadratic programming (SQP), respectively. Numerical results show that the proposed architecture achieves higher sum rates than conventional-antenna and PASS-only benchmarks. Moreover, the MM- and SQP-based optimization stages achieve performance comparable to semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and grid-based exhaustive search, respectively, while the AO algorithm exhibits rapid convergence.

authors.name: L\"utfullah \"Ozkan, Saliha B\"uy\"uk\c{c}orak

papers.title: Mask-Based Speech Enhancement for Spatial Audio: Effects of Signal Representation and Channel-Specific Masking
papers.summary: Speech enhancement for spatial audio needs to improve speech quality and intelligibility while preserving the spatial characteristics of the acoustic scene. Time-frequency masking provides an effective approach for speech enhancement, but its performance and spatial fidelity may depend strongly on the signal representation in which the mask is applied. This work systematically compares time-frequency masking in the microphone, beamformer, and first-order Ambisonics domains in simulated reverberant acoustic scenes. Both an ideal ratio mask (IRM) and a lightweight deep-learning-based mask estimator are considered, with performance evaluated in terms of speech reconstruction, perceptual quality, intelligibility, reverberation preservation, and binaural spatial-cue preservation. The results show that channel-specific masking in the beamformer domain provides the highest speech quality and intelligibility, while channel-specific masking in the Ambisonics domain better preserves the spatial characteristics of the residual interference. Reducing the spatial representation from third- to first-order Ambisonics substantially reduces the performance gap between the beamformer and Ambisonics domains due to the lower spatial resolution of the resulting beamformers. Furthermore, a shared mask across first-order Ambisonics channels achieves speech enhancement performance close to that of channel-specific masking while requiring only a single mask-estimation network. These results demonstrate that the choice of signal representation and masking strategy should be considered jointly, and indicate that first-order Ambisonics with shared masking provides a practical compromise between speech enhancement performance, spatial fidelity, and computational complexity.

authors.name: Sheli Hendel, Boaz Rafaely, Dorothea Kolossa

papers.title: Compositional Reachset-Conformant Modeling for Managing Uncertainty in the Development of Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.summary: The development of cyber-physical systems (CPS) proceeds through iterative design revisions, and compliance with safety requirements must be re-established after every revision, typically based on a system model. Conventional models, however, predict only the most likely behavior, leading to model-plant mismatch that often surfaces only during late-stage testing, when redesign is most expensive. This article presents reachset-conformant modeling as a framework for managing uncertainty throughout the development process: instead of a single trajectory, a reachset-conformant model predicts a set of behaviors, calibrated from data to conservatively enclose the true system behavior with a statistical guarantee. Safety properties established on the model therefore transfer to the realized system. Beyond a practical introduction to reachset-conformant identification and its benefits for CPS development, our main theoretical contribution is a closure result: reachset conformance is preserved under serial composition, parallel composition, and feedback interconnection, and hence under any architecture assembled from these primitives. Subsystem models identified independently from local measurements can thus be substituted into the system architecture, and the interconnected model inherits a coverage guarantee from the subsystem guarantees. We complement this result with update strategies that adapt the uncertainty sets after design changes without restarting the identification workflow. Experiments on an automotive brake-system test bench demonstrate that a) a single model covers all operating conditions and hardware variants, b) late-stage modifications are absorbed by uncertainty set updates, c) a black-box hydraulic unit is conservatively abstracted from input-output data alone, and d) independently identified subsystem models form a conformant model by construction.

authors.name: Laura L\"utzow, Francesco Pio Urbano, Tobias D\"user, Matthias Althoff

papers.title: From Safety-Driven Redundancy to Value-Driven Architecture: An ODD-Based Rationalization Framework for Level 4 Autonomous Vehicles
papers.summary: Level 4 autonomous vehicles require fault-tolerant architectures that preserve critical driving functions under sensing, computing, communication, power, and actuation failures. As these systems progress toward industrial scalability, architectural complexity, validation burden, integration effort, and lifecycle cost become increasingly relevant. This study proposes an Operational Design Domain (ODD)-based, safety-constrained systems-engineering framework for architecture rationalization. ODD-specific capabilities, physical fault assumptions, post-fault operational policies, and spatial sensing requirements are propagated through an integrated safety-feasibility gate. Architecture transformations, including removal, relocation, functional reassignment, and consolidation, are evaluated only within the resulting safety-feasible design space, followed by lifecycle-cost sensitivity and robust multiobjective Pareto analysis. A generic, synthetically parameterized Level 4 architecture is used as a demonstrative computational case study. Within this modeled design space, direct ablation showed limited rationalization potential, whereas directional redistribution and functional consolidation generated a broader set of safety-feasible candidates. Under the illustrative lifecycle-cost model, the best nominal candidate achieved a 5.55% normalized cost reduction and remained cost-reducing across all 5,000 sampled points in the prescribed uncertainty domain. The analysis identified 15 non-dominated architecture-policy solutions representing seven physical transformations. The results support capability-based, policy-conditioned, and lifecycle-aware architecture rationalization under the stated assumptions, with safety retained as a non-compensatory feasibility constraint. The reported transformations are design candidates rather than validated production architectures.

authors.name: Tiago Sim\~ao Ferreira (Federal Institute of Minas Gerais - IFMG), Farzad Fallahi (University of Luxembourg)

papers.title: Continuous Time Identification of Linear Systems: Extended Version
papers.summary: We consider a problem to develop a framework for model identification adhering to the tenets of neuromorphic computation, without resorting to neural networks as the mathematical substrate. In particular, all computations take place in continuous time. We are naturally led to adaptive observers, where the main technical obstacle is the possible mismatch between the unknown plant order and the observer order. The key concept that informs the proposed framework is an overparameterized model, an input-output equivalent model that provides a suitable parameterization in the overmodeled case, with theoretical extensions also addressing the undermodeled case. A discrete algorithm orchestrates successive experiments to incrementally learn the model order, while a standard parameter adaptation law learns the parameters.

authors.name: Fatima J. Ghadieh, Mireille E. Broucke

papers.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Can Decide the Outcome
papers.summary: Quantum machine learning is proposed to detect grid cyberattacks, but no study we could read tests quantum and classical detectors under white-box, transfer, and black-box attacks and random label flips in one protocol. We compare two quantum and six classical detectors on public grid-attack data under equal tuning budgets. Our main finding: evaluation choices can decide the outcome. On these data, seven choices each changed a reported result with model families fixed. Row-level splits inflate our best score by 0.31 macro-averaged F1 over held-out files, where matched-dimensionality classical and quantum models barely clear chance. Under its own white-box attack the quantum kernel's score falls from 0.56 to 0.01 (chance 0.50), while a transferred attack in the same run leaves 0.52. Trees admit no gradient-based white-box attack, so their attacked scores are upper bounds. These attack results use eight-dimension detectors under row-level splits. On gas-pipeline and simulated-grid data, neither quantum detector is more accurate or consistently more robust; three of the seven choices reproduce fully on gas data with one pressure feature log-scaled (two within noise), and none of the four checked on the grids does. Benchmarks should hold out whole files and give every model its own attack where possible. We release code and checklist.

authors.name: Md Rezwanul Islam, ASM Shihavuddin

papers.title: Directed brain-body graphs across timescales
papers.summary: Simultaneous brain and body recordings combine signals sampled at very different rates with processes that act on timescales from milliseconds to minutes. Placing all signals on one time grid can distort the directed relationships estimated from them. Unmeasured common influences can also make one signal appear to drive another. We introduce rate-matched Granger causality (RMGC), which estimates directed predictive relationships without a common sampling grid. Each relationship receives a robustness value, the strength of the weakest common influence found within a specified class that can reproduce it. A neural extension tests for nonlinear relationships. In a controlled benchmark, RMGC recovered more true relationships than four established methods and an autoregressive model on a common grid (92\% at a false-positive rate of 5\%). Given the same signal features, the common-grid model matched this recovery but had more than twice the false-positive rate, and it reversed the relationship from respiration to heart rate. The robustness value never overstated the strength of the driver behind a spurious relationship, even for drivers outside the searched class. It separated true from spurious relationships better than predictive strength did. In overnight sleep recordings and two awake datasets, many brain--heart relationships could be reproduced by common drivers no stronger than measured respiration. Robustness values only partly identified those that appeared when respiration was omitted, particularly during wakefulness. Surrogate analyses showed elevated background rates in one awake dataset. The approach applies to other signals recorded at different rates or as events, provided that influences act with a delay.

authors.name: Lu\'is A. Alexandre, Karolina Finc

papers.title: Geometric Control Analysis of an Internally Actuated Flying Wing
papers.summary: This paper presents a rigorous geometric accessibility and controllability analysis for a fixed-wing Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS) actuated solely by an internal moving mass, a momentum wheel, and external thrust. This configuration eliminates traditional control surfaces, which in turn reduces the combinatorial set of computational fluid dynamics (CFD) studies necessary for high-fidelity modeling of flight through unsteady flow fields. Using Lie bracket computations and the strong Lie Algebra Rank Condition, it is shown that the full nonlinear dynamics are generically small-time locally accessible, with singular configurations explicitly characterized and shown to be immediately escapable by direct mass actuation. The stronger property of small-time local controllability is shown to hold for the attitude subsystem at equilibrium points, using Sussmann's condition. A key contribution is the explicit treatment of the time-varying inertia tensor via the Huygens-Steiner Theorem, which introduces nontrivial coupling between the control vector fields. The momentum wheel provides direct yaw authority that, combined with inertia variation from the moving mass, generates a full-rank accessibility Lie algebra. A nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (MPC) is derived with consideration of flight envelope constraints and is applied to track different trajectories under unperturbed and perturbed flow field conditions.

authors.name: Jonathan Becker, Ella M. Atkins

papers.title: CRAB-H: Task-Centric Certification for Healthcare Autonomous Systems
papers.summary: This paper introduces CRAB H as a task-centric certification methodology for healthcare autonomous systems. CRAB H extends the ARC governance architecture by introducing the task as a first-class governance object, represented through Task Requirement Profiles TRP H. Each profile defines the cognitive capabilities, governance constraints, evidentiary requirements, and operational assumptions necessary for the safe execution of a specific healthcare activity. Rather than asking whether a robot achieves a sufficiently high benchmark score, CRAB H asks whether demonstrated capabilities satisfy the requirements of the task. Certification becomes a comparison between demonstrated capability and required capability. A reliability-gated assurance allocation mechanism routes cognitive dimensions that cannot be reproducibly evaluated to LEA operational requirements rather than discarding them. Governance integrity is preserved: unreliable dimensions are governed, not ignored. The Capability Margin is defined as the threshold-based conjunction of per-dimension compliance determinations, not as a subtracted scalar preserving non compensatory governance logic appropriate for safety-critical healthcare deployment

authors.name: Tord Johan Eide, Einar Holt

papers.title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
papers.summary: Multi-agent trajectory optimization poses two coupled challenges: effectively exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling favorably to large teams of agents. Sampling-based methods are natural candidates for the exploration challenge but scale poorly with problem dimension. Moreover, their off-the-shelf integration into distributed optimization introduces a fundamental trade-off: sampling either fails to address the constraint-induced non-convexity or its search space grows with neighborhood size. We address this gap by introducing a $\underline{D}\text{istributed}$ $\underline{S}\text{ampling-based}$ $\underline{T}\text{rajectory}$ $\underline{O}\text{ptimization} \ \text{(DS-TO)}$ architecture built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling. Under this splitting, each agent samples only in its own control space, independent of neighborhood size, while still remaining exposed to both the constraint-induced non-convexity and the decisions of other agents. The resulting algorithm is fully decentralized, requiring only neighborhood communication, with all local updates executed in parallel across agents. Efficient variations, including parallel Jacobi updates within each agent's subproblem and single-step constraint linearization, further reduce computation. Experiments on 2D and 3D tasks with up to 1024 agents demonstrate improved exploration and constraint satisfaction over state-of-the-art derivative-based distributed optimization, and superior scalability to existing distributed sampling methods.

authors.name: Minchan Jung, Dimitrios S. Georgiou, Augustinos D. Saravanos, Evangelos A. Theodorou

papers.title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation
papers.summary: Differentiable simulation enables gradient-based optimization in learning and control problems involving collisions, but its gradients are least reliable at the moment of impact, when the velocities jump. A fixed-step simulator detects a collision only after the bodies overlap, and some differentiable simulators correct for this with a linear estimate of the time of impact. In this paper, we study impacts between ellipsoids. We show that the gradient error of this estimate grows with the obliqueness of the collision, the curvature at contact, and the time step, and that ignoring spin adds a further error. Subsequently, we find the time of impact with continuous collision detection on the Perram Wertheim contact function and differentiate through the touching condition rather than the search. This gives exact gradients at any step size. We demonstrate our method on an optimal control problem and a system identification problem. In both, exact gradients recover the optimal control and the true parameters, while the linear estimate does not, even when it accounts for spin.

authors.name: Shamak Dutta, Biswadip Dey

papers.title: DAA for an Autonomous Delivery Drone: Maneuver Selection Policies for Near-Collision Risk Avoidance
papers.summary: Detect-and-avoid (DAA) systems for autonomous drones operating in shared airspace must select avoidance maneuvers under conditions that differ markedly from those assumed by conventional DAA architectures designed for crewed aircraft. Limited on-board sensing capabilities restrict detection of collision risk to near distances (sub-km), the time available for decision-making is severely limited, uncertainty in the predicted closest point of approach (CPA) and the time to reach it is substantial, and the maneuver envelope of a small uncrewed aircraft at low altitude is tightly constrained. This paper presents and compares two maneuver-selection strategies that address these challenges: (1) a purely geometric approach, steering in the direction away from the intruder at CPA, and (2) a method that also takes into account the known sources of uncertainty in the intruder's location, and steers away from a plane expected to contain the intruder's location distribution at CPA. Performance is evaluated using the risk ratio metric on a large dataset of simulated near-collision encounters with crewed intruders. Results indicate that both strategies are feasible (i.e., computable in closed form from an onboard track estimate), and that the second strategy substantially outperforms the first.

authors.name: Franco Callari, Ishay Kamon, Anthony Narkawitz, Pradeep Yarlagadda, Amir Navot

papers.title: Multi-User Linear Precoder Optimization for Obfuscation-Aided Mixed Regular and Wiretap Coding
papers.summary: Physical-layer security has attracted considerable research interest with the development of quantum computing. One prominent approach is wiretap coding, which exploits the channel advantage of a legitimate receiver over an eavesdropper to achieve secure communication. However, under unfavorable channel conditions, wiretap coding can significantly reduce the achievable rate compared to regular channel coding. Mixed coding alleviates this limitation by using wiretap coding to protect a short secret required for obfuscation, while the obfuscated payload is encoded using regular channel coding. In this work, we propose a generalized obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system based on the multi-user (MU)-linear precoding (LP) architecture that unifies existing approaches employing different obfuscation functions. We then formulate the corresponding precoder optimization problem, abstracting the obfuscation function through a minimum secrecy rate constraint. Numerical simulations using a geometric two-user line-of-sight (LoS) channel demonstrated how the minimum secrecy rate requirement determines the operating point of mixed coding between regular and wiretap coding. Subsequent beampattern analysis revealed a key synergy between mixed coding and precoding: Mixed coding enables individual beam shaping for the two coding layers. Finally, spatial analysis showed that mixed coding offers the largest sum-rate gains when users are positioned at similar angles.

authors.name: Bastian Loss, Ahmad Nimr, Gerhard Fettweis

papers.title: Sequences for Flat-Top Beams
papers.summary: Flat-top beams have numerous applications in radar and communication systems. Sequences with diverging merit factors can approach the ideal omnidirectional beams but do not directly apply to flat-top beams, which require simultaneous control of passband ripple and stopband leakage. To bridge this gap, we study the asymptotic behavior of both quantities of flat-top beams by using tools of Fourier analysis. We establish contrasting results for sequences with finite or infinite alphabets. For sequences with finite alphabet, including binary and quaternary ones, their passband ripple and stopband leakage cannot simultaneously vanish as the sequence length grows to infinity. For sequences with infinite alphabet, however, both requirements are satisfied simultaneously by the generalized step-chirp (GSC) sequences if and only if the length-bandwidth product $N\gamma$ goes to infinity and the distance of the step size $a$ from $\{0,1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$ goes to zero. Besides, both quantities vanish at rate $O((N\gamma)^{-1/2})$ if $a\in \{1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$.These results broaden the scope of classical sequence design beyond full-band spectral flatness and provide a theoretical foundation for flat-top beam synthesis.

authors.name: Cheng Du

papers.title: Convex computation of cost bounds for data-driven nonlinear optimal control
papers.summary: The paper addresses the optimal control problem of an input-affine polynomial system with an unknown (state-dependent) input matrix affecting the control effectiveness. Under assumptions on the existence of a data set and the Lipschitz continuity of the unknown part {of the dynamics}, an uncertainty set is constructed and used to adapt the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation towards a data-driven formulation. We solve it for the best-case scenario, thus giving a lower bound on the best cost achievable by means of a feedback control policy. After relaxing it into a moment-SoS hierarchy of semidefinite programs, a control law is extracted from the primal on moments and compared with other benchmark methods in a numerical application.

authors.name: Oumayma Khattabi, Matteo Tacchi-Benard, Sorin Olaru

papers.title: Low-Power Spiking Neural Network Acceleration with Differential Time Representation: A Modular Hardware Framework
papers.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer promising energy efficiency, making them well suited for energy-constrained applications. Much of their energy savings stems from the sparse encoding of spike trains. We show that spike trains can be represented more efficiently using Differential Time Representation (DTR), which requires fewer bits than Address-Event Representation (AER) or equidistantly sampled 1-bit spike trains. To support multiple input spike trains, we provide a rigorous proof that DTR sequences can be merged with low complexity. We also provide a set of modular hardware streaming components using this representation that can be flexibly connected to construct custom accelerator architectures for specific SNNs. Tailoring the hardware architecture to the selected SNN is streamlined by a Python framework combining the modular hardware components into a full SNN implementation. We use the framework to generate three accelerators for the Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD), Spiking Speech Commands (SSC), and PSMNIST benchmarks, each in a throughput-optimized parallel variant and a resource-reduced time-multiplexed variant. We report results for FPGA and ASIC implementations, the latter synthesized with a fully open-source flow targeting the predictive ASAP7 PDK. On the SHD dataset, the ASIC implementation reaches 92.46% classification accuracy, while sustaining $\approx{}$12,027 inferences per second at 20.37$\mu{}$J per inference, exceeding the neuromorphic Loihi processor by 109$\times$ in throughput and 1.8$\times$ in energy efficiency. The corresponding FPGA implementation achieves $\approx{}$6,023 inferences per second without using DSP blocks. Across all three datasets, the synthesized ASICs reduce energy per inference by 27-37$\times$ relative to their FPGA counterparts, demonstrating that competitive SNN accelerators can be realized entirely within an open-source design flow.

authors.name: Daniel Windhager, Lothar Ratschbacher, Bernhard A. Moser, Michael Lunglmayr

papers.title: An exponential-rate consensus-based algorithms for estimation from relative measurements: implementation and performance analysis
papers.summary: In this work we address the problem of optimal estimating the position of each agent in a network from relative noisy vectorial distances with its neighbors. Although the problem can be cast as a standard least-squares problem, the main challenge is to devise scalable algorithms that allow each agent to estimate its own position by means of only local communication and bounded complexity, independently of the network size and topology. We first propose a synchronous consensus-based algorithm that is guaranteed to have exponentially convergence rate to the optimal centralized least-squares solution. We then extend this algorithm to more realistic asynchronous implementations via the use of local memory variables. We show that exponential convergence is still guaranteed under both uniform persistent communication and randomized persistent communication protocols. We finally complement the analytical results with some numerical simulations.

authors.name: Ruggero Carli, Andrea Carron, Luca Schenato, Marco Todescato

papers.title: Extended Set-based Tasks for Multi-task Execution and Prioritization
papers.summary: The ability of executing multiple tasks simultaneously is an important feature of redundant robotic systems. As a matter of fact, complex behaviors can often be obtained as a result of the execution of several tasks. Moreover, in safety-critical applications, tasks designed to ensure the safety of the robot and its surroundings have to be executed along with other nominal tasks. In such cases, it is also important to prioritize the former over the latter. In this paper, we formalize the definition of extended set-based tasks, i.e., tasks which can be executed by rendering subsets of the task space asymptotically stable or forward invariant using control barrier functions. We propose a formal mathematical representation of such tasks that allows for the execution of more complex and time-varying prioritized stacks of tasks using kinematic and dynamic robot models alike. We present an optimization-based framework which is computationally efficient, accounts for input bounds, and allows for the stable execution of time-varying prioritized stacks of extended set-based tasks. The proposed framework is validated using extensive simulations, quantitative comparisons to the state-of-the-art hierarchical quadratic programming, and experiments with robotic manipulators.

authors.name: Gennaro Notomista, Mario Selvaggio, Francesca Pagano, Mar\'ia Santos, Siddharth Mayya, Vincenzo Lippiello, Cristian Secchi

papers.title: A Note on Emergent Behavior in Multi-agent Systems Enabled by Neuro-spike Communication
papers.summary: In this note, we show emergent behavior can arise even when the agents interact solely through spikes. Rather than exchanging real-valued states, each agent encodes its own state by bio-inspired neuromorphic amplifiers and transmits signed spikes, so that each firing carries a single bit and the traffic is intermittent and asynchronous. We model the resulting network as a hybrid system and introduce a coordinate that is invariant under the spike-induced jumps, which reduces the convergence analysis to a flow dynamics without jumps. On this coordinate, we prove that the agents practically synchronize and collectively follow the blended dynamics that characterizes an emergent behavior, and we derive explicit ultimate error bounds for synchronization and for the expected behavior. The bound reveals a certified accuracy--threshold trade-off and yields closed-form tuning rules under a minimum-threshold or prescribed-accuracy constraints. A distributed median solver is tested using neuro-spike communication.

authors.name: Hyeonyeong Jang, Donghyeon Song, Jin Gyu Lee, Hyungbo Shim

papers.title: Direct-to-Cell Satellite Communications: Task-Oriented Paradigm for 6G Closed-Loop Autonomous Operations
papers.summary: Direct-to-cell (D2C) satellite communications have emerged as a crucial alternative to terrestrial communications in the sixth generation (6G) mobile networks due to their wide-area coverage capability. Unlike human-oriented communications, future 6G robot-oriented D2C satellite communications in autonomous operations place greater emphasis on the ultimate task completion than on the intermediate stage of data transmissions. Such a difference renders it crucial to evaluate the performance of each stage in a systematic manner and consider a multistage integrated optimization. Motivated by this, we model the system with a sensing-communication-computing-control (SC3) closed loop and analyze it from an entropy-based perspective, from which a task-oriented system design method is developed. Furthermore, to manage the complexity of the closed-loop network, we decompose it into fine-grained functional structures and investigate the key challenges of collaborative sensing, collaborative computing, and collaborative control. A case study is presented to compare the proposed task-oriented scheme with conventional communication-oriented schemes, showing that the proposed method has better performance in system-level control cost. Finally, several open issues are outlined for future research and practical implementation.

authors.name: Daohong Shen, Wei Feng, Yunfei Chen, Yongxu Zhu, Jinxia Cheng, Dapeng Wang, Shi Jin

papers.title: Soft projections for robust data-driven control
papers.summary: We consider data-based predictive control based on behavioral systems theory. In the linear setting this means that a system is described as a subspace of trajectories, and predictive control can be formulated using a projection onto the intersection of this behavior and a constraint set. Instead of learning the model, or subspace, we focus on determining this projection from data. Motivated by the use of regularization in data-enabled predictive control (DeePC), we introduce the use of soft projections, which approximate the true projector onto the behavior from noisy data. In the simplest case, these are equivalent to known regularized DeePC schemes, but they exhibit a number of benefits. First, we provide a bound on the approximation error consisting of a bias and a variance term that can be traded-off by the regularization weight. The derived bound is independent of the true system order, highlighting the benefit of soft projections compared to low-dimensional subspace estimates. Moreover, soft projections allow for intuitive generalizations, one of which we show has superior performance on a case study. Finally, we provide update formulas for soft projectors enabling the efficient adaptation of the proposed data-driven control methods in the case of streaming data.

authors.name: Andr\'as Sasfi, Jaap Eising, Florian D\"orfler

papers.title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Time-Invariant Systems
papers.summary: This paper presents a tractable tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme that uses only a single finite noisy input-state trajectory of an unknown discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) system. A simplex constraint is imposed on the Hankel coefficient vector, yielding explicit polyhedral bounds on the prediction mismatch induced by bounded measurement noise. Using certified initial and terminal robust positively invariant (RPI) sets, we derive a tube-tightened formulation whose online optimization problem is a strictly convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting controller guarantees recursive feasibility, robust satisfaction of input and state constraints, and practical input-to-state stability of the closed loop with respect to measurement noise. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness, robustness, and closed-loop performance of the proposed method.

authors.name: Chi Wang, David Angeli

papers.title: Submodular Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Effective Online Distributed Task Allocation
papers.summary: This paper studies online distributed multi-agent task allocation with submodular team utilities. Since each agent selects one action from a local categorical distribution, feasible joint actions form a partition matroid over agent-action pairs. The classical Multilinear Extension relaxation, based on independent Bernoulli sampling, does not align with categorical execution under partition-matroid constraints. To remedy this, we propose the Partition Multilinear Extension (PME), which equals the expected stage utility under factorized categorical policies. We prove that submodular difference rewards provide unbiased PME marginal-gradient information and a stagewise policy-gradient estimator. Building on this connection, we propose SubMAPG, a centralized-training, decentralized-execution framework using masked categorical policies and difference-reward signals. For projected stochastic-gradient ascent in the PME marginal space, we establish a stagewise 1/2-approximation guarantee and sublinear dynamic regret under slowly varying environments. We instantiate SubMAPG on graph neural network policy models that effectively handle open systems with time-varying agents and tasks. Experiments on cooperative coverage and multi-target tracking showcase superior performance compared with standard MARL that does not leverage submodular rewards, online submodular optimization, and greedy baselines.

authors.name: Jing Liu, Yangyang Yang, Luca Ballotta, Fangfei Li, Yang Tang, Ruggero Carli

papers.title: AdaPTwin: Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Predictive Digital Twin for Proactive Radio Resource Management in Vehicular Networks
papers.summary: The highly dynamic nature of vehicular networks necessitates proactive and site-specific radio resource management (RRM) for safety-critical services. While Network Digital Twins (NDTs) have emerged as a promising enabler, physics-based ray tracing is time-consuming, challenging accurate RRM under strict latency constraints. We propose AdaPTwin, an adaptive multi-fidelity predictive NDT framework for proactive and latency-aware RRM in vehicular networks. Unlike single- and multi-fidelity NDTs with fixed fidelity levels, AdaPTwin selects the NDT fidelity by constrained optimization under a per-slot latency budget. The framework adopts a hierarchical cloud-edge architecture: fidelity selection is performed periodically in the cloud, whereas the proactive RRM loop runs at the edge in every slot. The edge loop predicts the channels between vehicles and roadside units (RSUs) through trajectory forecasting, using a Transformer with continual learning, and look-ahead ray tracing with NVIDIA Sionna over a dynamically updated 3D scene of buildings, roads, and vehicles. A joint RSU beamforming and vehicle-RSU association problem is then solved to maximize the proportionally fair sum rate using a scalable multi-start iterative coordinate descent algorithm. AdaPTwin is assessed in a simulation-based evaluation in which a high-fidelity reference NDT, rather than field measurements, provides the accuracy reference. Comparisons with reactive, single-fidelity, and non-adaptive predictive NDTs and the stochastic 3GPP model show that AdaPTwin adapts to the evaluated traffic densities and urban layouts, where fixed-fidelity DT frameworks either lose accuracy or overrun their deadline. In the evaluated scenarios, AdaPTwin achieves up to 70% sum-rate gain and 80% outage probability reduction compared with a non-adaptive predictive multi-fidelity NDT while meeting the per-slot deadline.

authors.name: Armin Makvandi, Md. Zoheb Hassan, Md. Jahangir Hossain

papers.title: Sensor-Stack Limits on Contactless In-Bed Body Position: A 20-Subject Multimodal Radar + Thermal LOSO Characterization
papers.summary: Contactless in-bed body-position inference can be limited by the sensor representation the host receives rather than by the classifier. We characterize a bedside 60 GHz frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar that reports only on-device constant-false-alarm-rate (CFAR) point clouds, together with a low-resolution thermal array (24x32 nominal, 24x16 effective), on 20 subjects under leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) evaluation. Two tasks share the cohort: 273 operator-directed in-bed posture holds (148.7 minutes) and a per-second bed-presence timeline (8,817 scored seconds). The cohort is a friends-and-family convenience sample (13 minors, ages 5 to 68, six families), and every session used the same bed in one room with the subject uncovered, so the figures describe this setup rather than a population. Bed presence reaches a 0.871 per-subject median balanced accuracy (95% CI 0.796 to 0.910). For four-class posture, nested LOSO, in which every selection and fitting step sees training subjects only, gives 0.646 balanced accuracy (per-subject median 0.683). Prone recall is 0.45 at a precision of 0.42, so prone is not usefully detected. Version 1 reported 0.674 for a stacked ensemble picked on the folds it was scored on; this version replaces that figure with a nested estimate and corrects the bed-presence accounting and the description of the recording setting. Thermal resolves left versus right (lateral swaps of 35 to 42% with radar alone, 8% with thermal alone). The supine-versus-prone breathing cue shows up in the CFAR output only as a group shift (Cohen's d = 0.61), with a clean per-hold peak in 8.4% of holds. The next hardware test is raw range-FFT access, not further classifier tuning on CFAR detections.

authors.name: Dovy Paukstys

papers.title: HAPS-Complemented Terrestrial Networks
papers.summary: We consider a downlink multicell multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system in an urban region, with a focus on improving the capacity of cell-edge user equipments (UEs). These UEs typically experience lower rates than near UEs because of shadowing, path loss, and inter-cell interference (ICI). To address this issue, we integrate a high-altitude platform station (HAPS) with the terrestrial network as a relay for edge-UE transmissions. We assume that the HAPS operates in full-duplex (FD) mode and exploits its large physical size to enhance passive self-interference (SI) suppression by separating its transmit and receive antennas. In the proposed scheme, each terrestrial base station (BS) forwards edge-UE data to the FD-HAPS, which then relays the data to the intended edge UEs. To design beams at both BSs and HAPS, we formulate an {edge-UE} sum-rate maximization problem under total transmit-power and minimum quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a centralized algorithm based on successive convex approximation (SCA) and alternating optimization (AO) for fast convergence. Simulation results show that relaying information via FD-HAPS significantly improves the capacity of cell-edge UEs compared with a terrestrial-only network.

authors.name: Animesh Yadav, Halim Yanikomeroglu

papers.title: Learning Regularization Structure for Biosignal Template Estimation
papers.summary: Objective: To estimate event-related templates of biosignals accurately from a small number of events. Methods: We design a template estimation algorithm that minimizes Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) over a convolution kernel defining a Tikhonov penalty, learning its structure and magnitude from the data, and extend SURE to temporally correlated noise. We compare the resulting estimator, SURE(kernel), with established estimators in simulations and on auditory EEG, P300 (ten subjects), and ECG recordings. Results: In simulations, SURE(kernel) was the most accurate method at moderate and high noise levels and, at moderate noise, for every number of events tested; at low noise, generalized cross-validation was the most accurate. On real data with five events per class, SURE(kernel) was the closest of the compared estimators to the full-data references on the auditory EEG and in all ten P300 subjects. On ECG, averaging was closest; SURE(kernel) stayed within 3% of it, whereas generalized cross-validation and Empirical Bayes were 38% and 40% farther. On P300, SURE(kernel)'s template-implied event probabilities were less overconfident than those of averaging, at similar detection performance. On both EEG datasets, absolute accuracy at five events remained limited. Conclusion: Learning the regularization structure from the data, with a correction for correlated noise, can make templates estimated from few events more accurate than those of established estimators. Significance: The method yields more accurate templates when few events can be recorded, as in personalization or when collecting data from each user is costly, with better-calibrated event probabilities at similar detection performance.

authors.name: Yonathan Murin, Alexandre Gramfort

papers.title: Topology-Aware Congestion Pricing: Demand Robust Routing using the Forman-Ricci Curvature
papers.summary: Congestion pricing is widely used to improve transportation network efficiency where individual decentralized route choices can lead to system-level inefficiencies. Pigouvian tolls achieve the system optimum but depend on demand and can lose effectiveness under demand shifts, particularly on structurally critical bottleneck edges. We propose a topology-aware regularization of the Beckmann potential governing the (Wardrop) equilibrium by augmenting precomputed Pigouvian tolls with an offline structural penalty derived from Forman--Ricci curvature (FRC), which captures bottleneck structures. We prove that the resulting equilibrium is well-defined, that stronger regularization reduces flow on penalized edges, and that efficiency loss depends on how closely the structural penalty approximates optimal Pigouvian tolls. Experiments on eight real-world networks under targeted and uniform demand perturbations show reduced bottleneck flow with near-optimal efficiency. FRC achieves reductions comparable to edge betweenness at substantially lower computational cost, making it a practical, robust complement to classical congestion pricing.

authors.name: Sheryl Paul, Samuel Williams, Kexin Wang, Ruolin Li, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh

papers.title: Calibrating Generative Flows through Regional Probability Matching
papers.summary: Generative models for scientific simulation must reproduce the frequencies of rare states as well as their structure. We developed generalized mass-preserving coupled flow matching (G-MPCF), which assigns regions of Gaussian noise the probability masses of corresponding regions in weighted observations. Conditional sampling within matched regions preserves the prescribed target distribution while changing the velocities used to train the flow, without modifying the underlying generative model architecture. On a rare-mode benchmark, an analytic coupling reduced relative score error by 95.0% and numerical integration error by 89.9% compared with independent pairing. On CIFAR-10 with a 100:1 class-probability ratio, G-MPCF reduced corrected class-mass error by 44.6% relative to minibatch optimal transport and improved mean image fidelity at matched computational budgets. These results show how the construction of training pairs can improve the reproduction of prescribed population frequencies by generative flows.

authors.name: Yubo Huang, Xiongyu Hu, Xin Lai, Zixi Wang, Liao Jian, Jingzehua Xu, Yong Ren, Chuan He

papers.title: CoRE: Relating Fine-Grained Chest X-ray Findings in Anatomical Context
papers.summary: Chest X-ray interpretation depends on both the anatomical location of findings and their relationships with other abnormalities. However, relations defined over global finding labels do not explicitly distinguish the same finding across anatomical locations. We propose CoRE(Co-occurrence-guided Region Evidence), a framework that incorporates relationships among findings and anatomical context into fine-grained chest X-ray prediction. It groups anatomical region-finding labels by co-occurrence and uses these groups to guide shared representation learning through visual prompt tuning on a frozen vision transformer. The predictions are supplemented by an anatomically supervised region-evidence stream through region-matched logit residuals. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR with Chest ImaGenome annotations show that CoRE improves region-finding classification over standard and relation-aware prompt-based baselines. Quantitative evaluations on MS-CXR and the Chest ImaGenome gold standard show improved finding localization, supported by qualitative comparisons. CoRE also improves finding-level classification on mapped finding labels in external VinDr-CXR and CheXpert datasets without target-domain adaptation. These results demonstrate the value of jointly modeling finding relationships and anatomical context for fine-grained chest X-ray analysis.

authors.name: Minjun Kim, Jong Hak Moon

papers.title: Kinematic Total-Body 3D PET Video Reconstruction with 33-ms Frames via Hierarchical List-Mode EM and Validation-Adaptive Space-Time Regularisation
papers.summary: Kinematic PET is introduced as an imaging task focused on visualisation of early radiotracer delivery and rapid multi-organ motion without gating. The proposed kinematic video reconstruction method uses 33-ms frames (~30 frames per second), initialised with 3D expectation maximisation (EM) time of flight (TOF) list-mode reconstruction, followed by cycles of a 2-stage update. These 2 stages are i) a hierarchical EM (HEM) update using multiple temporal pooling levels, and ii) a validation-adaptive space-time (VAST) regularisation update. HEM combines frame-specific EM corrections with corrections estimated from higher-count temporal blocks, slowing noise amplification for the ultrashort frames. VAST mixes each 3D target patch in a frame with source patches sampled nearby in space and time. It selects the candidate that best matches the mean of the corresponding patches in the two adjacent frames, with the unchanged patch also eligible. Optional temporal block sum correction uses the initial EM temporal sum as a reference to reduce loss of spatial detail. HEM+VAST was evaluated with a dynamic digital phantom, and demonstrated on human FDG data acquired on a Siemens Biograph Vision Quadra (28 - 58 s post-injection). At a background spatial coefficient of variation of 10%, the temporal full width at half maximum of the fastest phantom bolus was 151 ms with HEM+VAST, compared with 86 ms for the ground truth. The video frame rate FDG images reveal vascular and organ detail, radiotracer bolus passage and respiration-related multi-organ motion. Kinematic PET could complement conventional dynamic PET by supporting the development of image-derived physiological biomarkers and motion estimation for quantitative reconstruction. Future work should compare HEM+VAST with prior 4D PET reconstruction methods at the same 33-ms frame duration and matched noise levels.

authors.name: Andrew J. Reader, Gary J. R. Cook, Paul K. Marsden, Sarah-May Gould, Alexander Hammers, Simon R. Cherry

papers.title: Grid-Forming AI Data Centers: Coordinated Grid Support Control from IT Loads and Energy Storage
papers.summary: To exploit the grid-support capability of AI data centers (AIDCs), this paper proposes a grid-forming (GFM) control scheme which coordinates the IT loads and energy storage (ES) in the AIDC. First, the framework of a grid-connected AIDC is presented, with the multi-stage power conversion from the grid to the IT loads presented. A dual GFM scheme is then proposed for the back-to-back converters to provide grid support through coordinated power adjustments from IT loads and ES. In addition, an aggregated power response model is established to characterize the IT-load flexibility considering multiple IT servers executing diverse tasks. Time-domain simulations of a 100 MW grid-connected AIDC demonstrate that the proposed control scheme can effectively support the grid.

authors.name: Xuechun Zhang, Zhiyi Zhao, Fei Teng, Zhen Wang

papers.title: Connections Between Instrumental Variable, Pseudo-Linear Regression, and Prediction Error Methods in Terms of Their Minimized Criteria
papers.summary: This paper explores the connections between the criteria directly or indirectly minimized by Prediction Error (PE), Instrumental Variable (IV), and Pseudo-Linear Regression (PLR) algorithms for the identification of output-error models. By definition, PE methods aim to minimize the variance of the prediction error. In contrast, the correlation functions appearing in the stationarity conditions of IV and PLR algorithms are not the gradients of any underlying loss function involving a signal variance. Nevertheless, if the true system lies in the model set, we show that one IV algorithm minimizes asymptotically the variance of an unmeasurable signal called the equivalent prediction error. This signal was introduced previously to analyze the bias distribution of PLR schemes. It turns out that, regardless of whether the true system lies in the model set, some iterative IV and PLR algorithms aim to minimize the prediction error variance and can therefore be interpreted as indirect PE algorithms.

authors.name: Bernard Vau, Henri Bourl\`es

papers.title: Data-driven model reduction: An identification perspective using Generalized Bases of Orthonormal Functions
papers.summary: This paper proposes a data-driven model order reduction approach based on system identification concepts. A revised equation error formulation is introduced, in which the model is parameterized using Generalized Bases of Orthonormal Transfer Functions (GBOFs). The generalized reduction problem is formulated in the Hambo frequency domain associated with the GBOF transform. The frequency-domain fit of the reduced-order model is adjusted through the selection of the basis poles. A fit indicator depending on these poles is introduced, providing valuable heuristic guidance for their selection.

authors.name: Bernard Vau, Henri Bourl\`es

papers.title: How to Receive Focused Beams in Near-Field MIMO? Analytical Combiners and Array Size Optimization
papers.summary: This paper investigates receive combining for near-field beamfocusing in line-of-sight channels with antenna array misalignment. We propose and evaluate two analytical combiners: analog ANF-AC and digital ANF-DC. Beyond focusing the beam toward the transmitter, ANF-AC benefits from the proposed phase-flip corrections (PFCs), while ANF-DC additionally exploits Dirichlet-kernel-based amplitude tapering. ANF-AC closely matches theoretically optimal analog equal-gain combining (EGC), with an SNR gap below 0.006 dB. Similarly, ANF-DC matches optimal digital maximum-ratio combining (MRC). We then leverage the analytical properties of these combiners for link-level evaluation and optimization, deriving a closed-form expression for the optimal transmitter-receiver array-size trade-off that maximizes received SNR with analog combining. We also show that the optimized analog receiver performs within 0.84 dB of its fully digital MRC-equivalent counterpart. These results demonstrate that optimized analog combining (with potentially lower implementation complexity and cost, particularly at higher frequencies) can get close to the fully digital performance. Beyond the theoretical insights presented, the analytical tractability and EGC-like / MRC-like performance of our combiners enable accurate network-level mathematical studies of beamfocusing, such as coverage, capacity, and interference analysis and optimization toward efficient 6G+ near-field MIMO communication systems.

authors.name: Phinehas Chinthalagattu, Vitaly Petrov, Emil Bj\"ornson

papers.title: Planar Formation Control with Minimal Sensing and No Common Orientation: An Almost-Global Result
papers.summary: Formation control based on geometric constraints often requires either rigid interaction graphs or a common orientation reference. This paper investigates whether a prescribed planar formation can instead be achieved using only $N-1$ pairwise interactions while preserving global rotational freedom. To this end, a guiding-vector-field-inspired framework is developed in which each selected distance relation is represented by a parameterized circular manifold and the remaining geometric freedom is coordinated through relative virtual phases, based on which, a distributed controller is then constructed. The closed-loop system is shown to possess only the desired equilibrium set and a degenerate undesired equilibrium set corresponding to collapse of the central edge. The latter is proved to form a saddle-type equilibrium manifold with a measure-zero stable set, yielding almost-global convergence to the desired formation. In addition, the controller admits an implementation under mutually misaligned local frames using locally expressed relative measurements and scalar phase information.

authors.name: Jingyi Zhao, Yuhu Wu, Hector Garcia de Marina

papers.title: S$2$SCORE: A Textless Unified Evaluation Metric for Speech-to-Speech Translation Systems
papers.summary: Evaluating speech-to-speech translation (S$2$ST) systems requires assessing multiple dimensions of translated speech, including semantic adequacy, speaker similarity, and acoustic naturalness. Existing approaches are largely text-based, relying on ASR transcripts and primarily assessing semantic adequacy, while other dimensions require separate metrics. We propose S$2$SCORE, a unified text-free evaluation framework that jointly models these dimensions within a multi-task architecture and produces a human-calibrated overall quality score. S$2$SCORE is trained using supervision derived from established evaluation models, enabling scalable learning without direct human annotations. Evaluated across five language pairs, S$2$SCORE shows strong agreement with human judgments, independent reference metrics, and the training supervision metrics, indicating robust generalization. The reference-free variant, S$2$SCORE-QE, consistently outperforms S$2$SCORE-REF and achieves stronger semantic adequacy prediction than BLASER~$2.0$.

authors.name: Lalaram Arya, Mrinmoy Bhattacharjee, S. R. Mahadeva Prasanna

papers.title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models
papers.summary: Speech language models (LMs) generate speech as sequences of discrete tokens, requiring tokenizers that preserve both acoustic detail and linguistic content at a low bitrate. Semanticenhanced tokenizers may discard acoustic detail, whereas acousticoriented tokenizers retain acoustic variation that hinders language modeling. Unified tokenizers combine both, but encoding them within a single feature space can cause interference, and existing methods typically align acoustic features to fixed targets from a frozen semantic teacher. We propose Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization (BiSAT), a unified framework with separate acoustic and semantic branches coupled by a shared-index mechanism. During training, each branch has its own encoder, codebook, and decoder, and at every frame a shared index minimizes the combined quantization error across both branches. BiSAT thus learns acoustic and semantic representations in separate continuous spaces while producing a single discrete code stream, jointly optimizing both encoders without fixed semantic teachers. Built on BiSAT, BiSAT-TTS pairs an autoregressive text-speech LM with a conditional flow-matching acoustic decoder for zero-shot text-to-speech. Reconstruction, frozen-code understanding, and diagnostic analyses show that BiSAT preserves accessible linguistic and acoustic structure in a low-bitrate single stream, generalizes strongly to in-thewild and out-of-domain speech, and learns complementary paired codebooks. BiSAT-TTS matches or surpasses state-of-the-art speech LM-based TTS baselines with less training data, demonstrating that accessible code structure, not reconstruction quality alone, benefits autoregressive speech modeling. The audio demos are available at https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo.

authors.name: Y. Lu, L. Wang, S. Okada

papers.title: On the Effect of Bounded Rationality in Mixed Duopoly Markets
papers.summary: Nash equilibrium is a common solution concept that captures strategic interaction in market analysis.
